paper.title: Critiquing Menstrual Pain Technologies through the Lens of Feminist Disability Studies

works.title: Drone Arena
works.description: In a three-day drone challenge at KTH, teams moved from aiming for seamless control to treating small drones as fragile, wilful and crash-prone, and used intimate bodily interactions to probe what their drone could do.
works.description_zh: 在 KTH 举办的三天无人机挑战赛中，各团队从追求无缝操控，转向把小型无人机视为脆弱、任性、容易坠毁的存在，并通过亲密的身体互动去试探无人机能做什么。
works.idea_en: Shaping a machine's behaviour needs perception-action loops you can feel; programming becomes a bodily negotiation rather than pure instruction.
works.idea_zh: 塑造机器的行为，需要能被亲身感受的感知—行动回路；编程于是成为一种身体上的协商，而不只是下达指令。
works.method: Observation, interviews, field notes, video and inspection of each team's code from the Drone Arena challenge (Crazyflie nano-drones with an external positioning system), analysed through bricolage.
works.method_zh: 对 Drone Arena 挑战赛的观察、访谈、现场笔记、录像以及各团队代码的检视（Crazyflie 微型无人机配合外部定位系统），以拼贴式方法分析。

paper.title: Shaping and Being Shaped by Drones: Programming in Perception-Action Loops

works.title: EchoVision
works.description: Visitors lift a bat-shaped mixed reality mask, make a sound with their voice and see waves of light travel over the people and objects around them, a simulation of bat echolocation.
works.description_zh: 观众举起一副蝙蝠形状的混合现实面具，用嗓音发出声音，便会看到光波在周围的人与物上扫过，模拟蝙蝠的回声定位。
works.idea_en: Using one's own voice to 'see' turns a familiar place strange and makes perception feel like an active, bodily act.
works.idea_zh: 用自己的声音去“看”，让熟悉的地方变得陌生，也让知觉被感受为一种主动的身体行为。
works.method: Smartphone-based HoloKit headset in a custom mask; LiDAR scene reconstruction and microphone input trigger expanding echo shaders.
works.method_zh: 定制面具内的智能手机 HoloKit 头显；激光雷达重建场景，麦克风输入触发扩散的回声着色效果。

paper.title: Seeing with Sound: Demonstrating "EchoVision", a Mixed Reality Simulation of Bat Echolocation

works.title: Five Political Provocations for Soma Design: A Relational Perspective on Emotion and Politics
works.description: Five provocations on the politics of soma design — ways of knowing, the self, felt ethics and right action, the pursuit of happiness, and justice and the emotional labour of transformation.
works.description_zh: 关于身体设计之政治的五条“挑衅”：认识方式、自我、被感受的伦理与正当行动、对幸福的追求，以及正义与转化中的情绪劳动。
works.idea_en: Felt experience is shaped between bodies and by society; designing for the soma therefore means designing within politics.
works.idea_zh: 被感受的经验在身体之间、由社会塑造；因此为身体设计，就是在政治之中设计。
works.method: Conceptual paper combining soma design, political theory and Sara Ahmed's The Cultural Politics of Emotion (with Pasko Kisić-Merino and Pedro Sanches).
works.method_zh: 结合身体设计、政治理论与 Sara Ahmed《情绪的文化政治》写成的概念性论文（与 Pasko Kisić-Merino、Pedro Sanches 合著）。

paper.title: Five Political Provocations for Soma Design: A Relational Perspective on Emotion and Politics

works.title_zh: 身体设计的五条政治挑衅：情绪与政治的关系视角

works.title: GravField
works.description: Participants wearing mixed reality headsets move together while an 'object jockey' live-codes virtual ropes, springs and magnetic fields between their bodies; distance, formation and synchrony between the bodies generate music and visuals.
works.description_zh: 佩戴混合现实头显的参与者一起移动，一位“物件 DJ”在他们身体之间实时编写虚拟的绳索、弹簧与磁场；身体间的距离、队形与同步生成音乐与视觉。
works.idea_en: Virtual objects with felt 'digital physics' can nudge a group into moving together without choreography, while leaving each person their agency.
works.idea_zh: 带有可感“数字物理”的虚拟物件，可以在没有编舞的情况下引导一群人一起移动，同时保留每个人的能动性。
works.method: Co-located HoloKit AR headsets tracking head poses, mapped to live-coded parameters (weight, elasticity, force) and sound; studied through video, interviews, soma trajectories and field notes.
works.method_zh: 同地协作的 HoloKit 增强现实头显追踪头部姿态，映射到实时编码的参数（重量、弹性、力）与声音；通过录像、访谈、身体轨迹与田野笔记进行研究。

paper.title: Nudging the Somas: Exploring How Live-Configurable Mixed Reality Objects Shape Open-Ended Intercorporeal Movements

works.title: Haptic Source-Effector
works.description: Instead of strapping actuators to each body part, a single magnetic coil moved across the scalp stimulates the sensorimotor cortex, and the user feels touches and forces in the hands, arms, legs, feet and jaw.
works.description_zh: 不再在每个身体部位绑执行器，而是用一个在头皮上移动的磁线圈刺激感觉运动皮层，让用户在手、手臂、腿、脚和下颌感到触碰与力。
works.idea_en: Touch can start at the brain and still be felt out in the limbs, which shows how the felt body is assembled centrally and projected outward.
works.idea_zh: 触觉可以从大脑开始，却仍在四肢中被感受到；这显示了被感受的身体是在中枢组装、再投射出去的。
works.method: Transcranial magnetic stimulation with a robot-positioned coil; first study mapped about 15 sensations across the body, second tested them in VR.
works.method_zh: 经颅磁刺激，线圈由机械装置定位；第一项研究在全身映射出约 15 种感觉，第二项研究在 VR 中测试它们。

paper.title: Haptic Source-Effector: Full-Body Haptics via Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation

works.title_zh: 触觉源效应器：经无创脑刺激的全身触觉

works.title: How to Train Your Drone
works.description: Three people sharing a home spent a month shaping what their drones could sense and how they responded, forming intimate, individual human-drone couplings.
works.description_zh: 三位合住的人用一个月时间，塑造各自无人机能感知什么、如何回应，形成了亲密而各不相同的人机配对。
works.idea_en: Thinking of a drone's umwelt, its own sensory world, opens a design space where human and machine come to understand each other somatically.
works.idea_zh: 把无人机的“环世界”（umwelt，即它自己的感知世界）纳入思考，就打开了一个人与机器在身体层面相互理解的设计空间。
works.method: Drones whose sensing and behaviour can be trained through bodily interaction, deployed for a month in a shared household; umwelt used as a design metaphor within soma design.
works.method_zh: 可通过身体互动训练其感知与行为的无人机，在合住家庭中部署一个月；在身体设计中把“环世界”用作设计隐喻。

paper.title: How to Train Your Drone: Exploring the umwelt as a design metaphor for human-drone interaction

works.title: Mechanical Sympathy
works.description: Drawing on How to Train Your Drone, the paper proposes mechanical sympathy, the feel a person develops for a machine's agency, oscillations and aesthetic possibilities, as a design concept for somaesthetic relations with machines.
works.description_zh: 以 How to Train Your Drone 为案例，论文提出“机械共感”作为设计概念：人对机器的能动性、振荡与审美可能性逐渐养成的一种体感，用于建立与机器之间的身体美学关系。
works.idea_en: Like a driver who feels an engine, people can cultivate appreciative, idiosyncratic relationships with machines that complement technical understanding.
works.idea_zh: 就像驾驶者能感觉到引擎一样，人可以与机器培养出欣赏性的、个人化的关系，补充技术层面的理解。
works.method: Descriptive and reflective accounts of design strategies and of co-creators living with the drones, distilled into three qualities: machine agency, oscillations and aesthetic pursuits.
works.method_zh: 对设计策略和共同创作者与无人机共处的描述性、反思性记录，提炼出三种品质：机器能动性、振荡与审美追求。

paper.title: Articulating Mechanical Sympathy for Somaesthetic Human-Machine Relations

works.title: PneuMa
works.description: Soft pneumatic wearables that move parts of the body in everyday moments: pushing an ear forward to listen ('Pardon?'), lifting a hand to wave, or drawing the hands away from the keyboard to take a break.
works.description_zh: 在日常时刻移动身体部位的柔性气动可穿戴装置：把耳朵向前推以便倾听（“Pardon?”），抬起手挥别，或把双手从键盘上拉开提醒休息。
works.idea_en: Being gently moved by a bodily extension raises awareness of one's own movement habits, so actuation can serve attention to the body rather than replace it.
works.idea_zh: 被身体延伸装置轻轻带动，会提高人对自身动作习惯的觉察；执行机构因此可以服务于对身体的关注，而不是取而代之。
works.method: Inflatable actuators on the ear, hand and arm triggered by context; a field study with 12 participants analysed thematically (bodily awareness, perception of scenarios, anticipating movement).
works.method_zh: 在耳朵、手和手臂上按情境触发的充气执行器；对 12 名参与者进行田野研究并作主题分析（身体觉察、对情境的感知、对动作的预期）。

paper.title: PneuMa: Designing Pneumatic Bodily Extensions for Supporting Movement in Everyday Life

works.title: Sentient Clit: The Pussification of BioTech
works.description: Video performances, lab experiments and digital art around growing clitoral tissue by 3D bioprinting stem cells from menstrual fluid, centring pleasure rather than reproduction.
works.description_zh: 以视频表演、实验室实验与数字艺术，探讨用经血中的干细胞进行 3D 生物打印、培育阴蒂组织的可能，把愉悦而不是生殖放在中心。
works.idea_en: Biotech can be designed around felt pleasure: asking who owns an organ that can sense opens questions of consent and sentience.
works.idea_zh: 生物技术可以围绕被感受的愉悦来设计：追问一个能够感知的器官归谁所有，会引出关于同意与感知能力的问题。
works.method: Primary cell culture from a menstrual cup to petri dish, 3D bioprinting and distribution of the work through social platforms such as OnlyFans.
works.method_zh: 从月经杯到培养皿的原代细胞培养、3D 生物打印，并通过 OnlyFans 等社交平台传播作品。
works.title_zh: 感知之花：生物科技的柔性变革

works.title: Shape-Changing Car Seats
works.description: With a car manufacturer, the team co-designed touch patterns for a shape-changing driver's seat: re-engaging in driving, disengaging, saying farewell and being held while turning.
works.description_zh: 团队与一家汽车制造商共同为形变驾驶座设计触摸模式：重新投入驾驶、从驾驶中抽离、道别，以及转弯时被“托住”。
works.idea_en: Touch on large, heavy parts of the body can link somatic experience to the rational tasks of driving, so the car's intelligence is felt rather than displayed.
works.idea_zh: 对身体大块、较重部位的触摸，可以把身体经验与驾驶的理性任务连起来，让汽车的智能被感受到，而不是被显示出来。
works.method: A low-fidelity inflatable prototyping tool on a racing seat, used in a soma design workshop with the manufacturer's designers.
works.method_zh: 装在赛车座椅上的低保真充气原型工具，用于与制造商设计师进行的身体设计工作坊。

paper.title: Exploring the Somatic Possibilities of Shape Changing Car Seats

works.title: Shared Bodily Fusion
works.description: In the game 'Hidden Touch', one player's touch on the other's body is turned by a shared EMS system into a muscle movement in the partner, fusing two bodies through a mediating computer.
works.description_zh: 在游戏“Hidden Touch”中，一名玩家对另一人身体的触碰，被共享的肌肉电刺激系统转化为对方的肌肉动作，借由中介的计算机把两个身体融合起来。
works.idea_en: Touch that makes another's body move brings back the pushing and pulling of playground games, and makes the partner's body felt as partly one's own to move.
works.idea_zh: 能让对方身体动起来的触碰，找回了游乐场游戏中推拉的身体互动，也让对方的身体被感受为部分可由自己驱动。
works.method: Touch-sensing on the skin mapped to EMS on the partner's forearm; study with 27 participants mapping experiences across threshold, tolerance and precision.
works.method_zh: 皮肤上的触碰感测映射到对方前臂的肌肉电刺激；27 人研究沿阈值、耐受与精度三个体验空间描绘玩家经验。

paper.title: Shared Bodily Fusion: Leveraging Inter-Body Electrical Muscle Stimulation for Social Play

works.title: SplitBody
works.description: While a person concentrates on a mental task such as writing, EMS automates a repetitive movement in the background, like stirring a pot, and their mental workload drops.
works.description_zh: 当一个人专注于写作等脑力任务时，肌肉电刺激在后台自动完成重复动作，比如搅拌锅里的汤，他们的心理负荷随之下降。
works.idea_en: The design splits attention from movement; it works, which raises the soma-design question of what is lost when the body keeps moving without the mind attending to it.
works.idea_zh: 这个设计把注意与动作分开；它确实有效，这也提出一个身体设计的问题：当身体在心不在焉时继续动作，我们失去了什么。
works.method: EMS electrodes drive a repetitive arm movement during a cognitively demanding multitask; workload, performance and user experience compared with and without EMS.
works.method_zh: 在高认知负荷的多任务中，肌肉电刺激电极驱动重复的手臂动作；比较有无电刺激时的负荷、表现与体验。

paper.title: SplitBody: Reducing Mental Workload while Multitasking via Muscle Stimulation

works.title: Voicing Discomfort, Communicating Breakdowns: Design Exploration of Felt Ethics in a Body-Based Workshop
works.description: A soma-design workshop with interaction designers that explores ethics through the discomfort felt in interpersonal bodily interaction, and how participants make that discomfort shared.
works.description_zh: 一个面向交互设计师的身体设计工作坊：通过人与人身体互动中的不适来探讨伦理，并观察参与者如何让这种不适被共同承认。
works.idea_en: Ethical breakdowns are first felt as discomfort; giving people ways to voice it keeps bodies safe and design honest.
works.idea_zh: 伦理上的裂缝最先表现为身体的不适；给人说出它的方式，能保护身体，也让设计保持诚实。
works.method: Body-based workshop grounded in soma design and the ethics of care, analysed from video recordings and post-workshop interviews (with Arife Dila Demir, Joo Young Park and Rob Comber).
works.method_zh: 以身体设计与关怀伦理为基础的工作坊，依据录像与事后访谈进行分析（与 Arife Dila Demir、Joo Young Park、Rob Comber 合著）。

paper.title: Voicing Discomfort, Communicating Breakdowns: Design Exploration of Felt Ethics in a Body-Based Workshop

works.title_zh: 说出不适，沟通裂缝：身体工作坊中被感受的伦理设计探索

works.title: Wings Against the Veil of Light
works.description: Butoh dancers wearing wings made of zippers and rulers chirp like crickets by rubbing them together, enacting how light pollution makes male crickets call at the wrong time.
works.description_zh: 舞踏舞者佩戴用拉链和尺子做成的翅膀，通过摩擦发出蟋蟀般的鸣声，演绎光污染如何让雄蟋蟀在错误的时间鸣叫。
works.idea_en: Butoh's practice of 'emptying the human shell' becomes a way to feel another species' body from inside.
works.idea_zh: 舞踏“清空人的躯壳”的修习，成为从内部感受另一物种身体的方式。
works.method: Site-specific performance at The Contemporary Austin, choreographed by Rosemary Candelario from a cricket butoh score adapted from Hijikata's bug notation.
works.method_zh: 在奥斯汀当代美术馆的场域表演，由 Rosemary Candelario 编舞，舞谱改编自土方巽的昆虫舞踏谱。

works.title: Auto-Paizo Games
works.description: Three games in which a player uses one hand to play against their other hand, whose movements are taken over by electrical muscle stimulation, so the body is both the input and the output of the game.
works.description_zh: 三款游戏中，玩家用一只手与另一只手对战，而后者的动作由肌肉电刺激接管；身体既是游戏的输入，也是输出。
works.idea_en: Most movement games pull attention to a screen; making the body the play material keeps attention on the body, and playing against oneself makes the familiar body strange.
works.idea_zh: 大多数体感游戏把注意力拉向屏幕；把身体作为游戏材料，能让注意力留在身体上，而与自己对战则让熟悉的身体变得陌生。
works.method: EMS on the forearm of the 'computer' hand, the other hand tracked as input; field study with 12 participants and thematic analysis.
works.method_zh: 在“计算机”那只手的前臂施加肌肉电刺激，另一只手被追踪作为输入；对 12 名参与者进行田野研究并作主题分析。

paper.title: Auto-Paizo Games: Towards Understanding the Design of Games That Aim to Unify a Player's Physical Body and the Virtual World

works.title: Biomenstrual: Menstrual Care for More-than-Human Bodies
works.description: Workshop participants made biodegradable menstrual artefacts from biomaterials that can be composted, returning the nutrients in menstrual blood to soil.
works.description_zh: 工作坊参与者用生物材料制作可堆肥的月经用品，把经血中的养分还给土壤。
works.idea_en: Menstrual care can extend to soil and other species when the body is understood as more-than-human.
works.idea_zh: 当身体被理解为超越人类的，月经照护就可以延伸到土壤与其他物种。
works.method: Research through Design with three workshops and 20 participants, making tools and biomaterial artefacts.
works.method_zh: 以设计为研究，举办三场工作坊、20 位参与者，制作工具与生物材料物件。

paper.title: Feminist Posthumanist Design of Menstrual Care for More-than-Human Bodies

works.title_zh: 生物月经：面向超越人类身体的月经照护

works.title: Boards Hit Back
works.description: An interactive wooden training dummy for martial arts was designed with and by a martial arts expert, and the process changed both the expert's practice and the expert.
works.description_zh: 一个用于武术训练的互动木人桩，由一位武术专家参与并主导设计，这个过程同时改变了这位专家的修习与这位专家本人。
works.idea_en: Estrangement in soma design lets practitioners break habits and cultivate new ones, fused with thought and feeling.
works.idea_zh: 身体设计中的陌生化让修习者打破旧习惯，培养新的、思与感交融的习惯。
works.method: Soma design process around a sensor-equipped wooden dummy, reported through a phenomenological first-person account of the practitioner.
works.method_zh: 围绕一个装有传感器的木人桩进行身体设计，并以修习者第一人称的现象学叙述来报告。

paper.title: Boards Hit Back: Reflecting on Martial Arts Practices Through Soma Design

works.title: Corsetto
works.description: Corsetto is a robotic garment worn by audience members during a live opera performance; it enacts haptic gestures that echo the singer's upper-body movements, adding a felt 'fourth voice' to Morton Feldman's Three Voices.
works.description_zh: Corsetto 是观众在现场歌剧演出中穿着的机器人服装；它施加与歌手上身动作相呼应的触觉姿态，为莫顿·费尔德曼的《Three Voices》加上一个被感受到的“第四声部”。
works.idea_en: Haptic gestures on the torso can bridge inner and outer sensation, so listening to a voice becomes a shared intercorporeal experience.
works.idea_zh: 躯干上的触觉姿态可以连通内在与外在的感觉，让聆听一个嗓音成为共享的身体间经验。
works.method: Soft robotic (likely fluidic fibre) actuators in a corset-like garment play composed haptic gestures synchronised with a live singer; audience experiences were studied with micro-phenomenological interviews.
works.method_zh: 类似束衣的服装中装有软体机器人执行器（可能是流体纤维），播放与现场歌手同步的触觉姿态编排；以微观现象学访谈研究观众体验。

paper.title: Corsetto: A Kinesthetic Garment for Designing, Composing for, and Experiencing an Intersubjective Haptic Voice

works.title: Embodied Embroidery
works.description: The first author, a woman with an invisible disability, tried other women's masturbation techniques on her own body and articulated each felt experience as an embroidered piece.
works.description_zh: 第一作者是一位有隐性残障的女性，她在自己身上尝试其他女性的自慰方式，并把每一种身体感受以刺绣作品表达出来。
works.idea_en: Embroidery can articulate felt pleasure where words fail, turning first-person sexual experience into shareable design knowledge.
works.idea_zh: 在语言无力之处，刺绣可以表达被感受到的愉悦，把第一人称的性经验变成可以分享的设计知识。
works.method: First-person somaesthetic study guided by first-person perspective, intersubjectivity and articulation, with handmade embroidery as the articulation medium (pictorial).
works.method_zh: 以第一人称视角、主体间性与表达为指引的第一人称身体美学研究，以手工刺绣作为表达媒介（图文论文）。

paper.title: Embodied Embroidery: Somaesthetic Interaction Design for Women's Masturbation

works.title: Embodied Telepresent Connection (ETC)
works.description: A VR artwork where two people meet as ethereal, glowing bodies and 'touch' each other through visual and sound effects rather than any device on the skin, with subtle biosignals in the scene.
works.description_zh: 一件 VR 艺术作品：两个人以空灵、发光的身体相遇，通过视觉与声音效果而非皮肤上的任何装置“触碰”彼此，场景中还带有细微的生物信号。
works.idea_en: Social touch in VR need not imitate physical tactility; an ephemeral, suggested touch can still carry play and intimacy.
works.idea_zh: VR 中的社会触碰不必模仿实体触感；一种短暂的、被暗示的触碰依然能承载嬉戏与亲密。
works.method: Pseudo-haptic visual and audio feedback at virtual contact points between networked avatars; developed in soma design-inspired workshops with 14 HCI experts and shown to 300+ visitors.
works.method_zh: 在联网化身的虚拟接触点给出伪触觉的视觉与声音反馈；通过有 14 位人机交互专家参与、受身体设计启发的工作坊发展，并向 300 多名观众展出。

paper.title: Ethereal Virtual Touch for Embodied Telepresent Connection: Applying Pseudo-haptics in Social Virtual Reality

works.title: Felt Ethics: Cultivating Ethical Sensibility in Design Practice
works.description: Argues that ethical judgment in design is also felt, and describes practices that cultivate designers' bodily ethical sensibility during design work.
works.description_zh: 主张设计中的伦理判断也是被感受的，并描述在设计工作中培养设计师身体性伦理感受力的实践。
works.idea_en: Ethics is not only reasoning after the fact; discomfort and care felt in the body during design are ethical signals worth attending to.
works.idea_zh: 伦理不只是事后的推理；设计中身体感到的不适与关切，就是值得注意的伦理信号。
works.method: Analysis of soma design and HRI design processes, identifying practices of felt ethical attention.
works.method_zh: 分析身体设计与人机器人交互设计过程，识别出被感受的伦理关注实践。

paper.title: Felt Ethics: Cultivating Ethical Sensibility in Design Practice

works.title_zh: 被感受的伦理：在设计实践中培养伦理感受力

works.title: Fused Spectatorship
works.description: Spectators hand control of both hands to an EMS system and watch their own hands play a game; many could not tell whether they were watching or playing.
works.description_zh: 观众把双手的控制交给肌肉电刺激系统，看着自己的手玩游戏；许多人分不清自己是在观看还是在玩。
works.idea_en: When one's own hands act without one's intention, spectating and playing merge, and the felt line between observing one's body and being it blurs.
works.idea_zh: 当自己的手在没有意图的情况下行动，观看与游玩便融合了；观察自己的身体与成为这个身体之间的感受界线变得模糊。
works.method: EMS on both forearms driven by game logic in three competitive and collaborative games; study with 12 participants yielding four spectator experience themes and four spectator types.
works.method_zh: 由游戏逻辑驱动双前臂的肌肉电刺激，设计了三款竞争与协作游戏；12 人研究得出四个观众体验主题与四种观众类型。

paper.title: Fused Spectatorship: Designing Bodily Experiences Where Spectators Become Players

works.title: Intercorporeal Biofeedback for Movement Learning
works.description: A strong concept: biofeedback shared between trainer and trainee, so that both can see or feel one body's inner activity and learn the movement together.
works.description_zh: 一个强概念：在教练与学员之间共享的生物反馈，让双方都能看到或感受到一个身体的内在活动，从而一起学习动作。
works.idea_en: Movement is learned between bodies; biofeedback works best when it supports that intercorporeal exchange instead of a lone user and a screen.
works.idea_zh: 动作是在身体之间学会的；生物反馈最有效的时候，是支持这种身体间的交流，而不是一个人对着屏幕。
works.method: Strong concept articulated from several training-technology design cases, with its design qualities (with Annika Waern).
works.method_zh: 从多个训练技术设计案例中提炼的强概念及其设计品质（与 Annika Waern 合著）。

paper.title: Intercorporeal Biofeedback for Movement Learning

works.title_zh: 用于动作学习的身体间生物反馈

works.title: JIZAI ARMS
works.description: A wearable back unit with six sockets holds detachable robot arms that the wearer or another person can control, and arms can be passed between wearers as a social exchange.
works.description_zh: 一个背部可穿戴单元带六个接口，可安装可拆卸的机械臂，由佩戴者或他人控制；机械臂还可以在佩戴者之间传递，成为一种社交交换。
works.idea_en: Extra limbs are not only personal tools; exchanging an arm with someone makes the extended body a shared, social body.
works.idea_zh: 额外的肢体不只是个人工具；与他人交换一只手臂，让延展的身体变成共享的、社会性的身体。
works.method: Designed by human-augmentation researchers with product designers and manufacturers; arms are driven by small motors and teleoperated, likely through a miniature replica arm used as a controller.
works.method_zh: 由人类增强研究者与产品设计师、制造商共同设计；机械臂由小型电机驱动，很可能通过一个缩小的复制臂作为控制器进行远程操控。

paper.title: Social Digital Cyborgs: The Collaborative Design Process of JIZAI ARMS

works.title: JumpMod
works.description: A backpack moves a weight up and down along the wearer's back at the right moment of a jump, making them feel they jumped higher, landed softer or were pulled down.
works.description_zh: 一个背包在跳跃的恰当时刻沿佩戴者背部上下移动一块重物，让他们觉得自己跳得更高、落地更轻，或被往下拉。
works.idea_en: The felt height of a jump is built from momentum sensed in the body, so shifting weight at the right time rewrites the experience of one's own movement.
works.idea_zh: 跳跃的“高度感”来自身体感受到的动量；在恰当时刻移动重量，就能改写人对自身动作的体验。
works.method: Untethered backpack with a motor-driven mass on a vertical rail, timed to jump phases detected by an IMU; studies on five jump effects and use in VR and games.
works.method_zh: 无线背包内有沿竖直导轨移动、由电机驱动的配重，其时序与惯性测量单元检测到的跳跃阶段同步；研究测试了五种跳跃效果及其在 VR 与游戏中的使用。

paper.title: JumpMod: Haptic Backpack that Modifies Users' Perceived Jump

works.title: Making Energy Matter
works.description: A first-person soma design engagement with household energy moved from restrictive 'sustainability' designs to enacting material relations with energy, such as feeling residual heat and running water with the hands.
works.description_zh: 一项关于家庭能源的第一人称身体设计实践，从限制性的“可持续”设计转向与能源建立物质关系，例如用手去感受余热和流水。
works.idea_en: Sustainability framed rationally breeds fatalism; somatic relations with energy open a more ethical, felt way of being with it.
works.idea_zh: 被理性框定的“可持续”会滋生宿命感；与能源建立身体关系，则打开一种更合乎伦理、可被感受的相处方式。
works.method: Autobiographical design over months, with body maps, sketches and co-performed kitchen experiments.
works.method_zh: 持续数月的自传式设计，配合身体地图、草图，以及与他人共同进行的厨房实验。

paper.title: Making Energy Matter: Soma Design for Ethical Relations in Energy Systems

works.title: Self-Tracking to Do Less
works.description: An autoethnography of living with long COVID, in which the author used self-tracking to pace activity and rest, turning tracking from a tool for doing more into one for doing less.
works.description_zh: 一份与长新冠共处的自我民族志：作者用自我追踪来调控活动与休息的节奏，把追踪从“做更多”的工具变成“做更少”的工具。
works.idea_en: With a chronically ill body, the goal is to feel limits early; tracking can support listening to the body instead of pushing past it.
works.idea_zh: 对一个慢性病的身体来说，目标是更早感到极限；追踪可以支持倾听身体，而不是逼身体越界。
works.method: Longitudinal first-person account of self-tracking heart rate and activity for pacing, analysed to derive design implications for pacing technologies.
works.method_zh: 长期的第一人称记录：以心率与活动追踪进行节奏调控，并据此提出节奏调控技术的设计启示。

paper.title: Self-Tracking to Do Less: An Autoethnography of Long COVID That Informs the Design of Pacing Technologies

works.title_zh: 为了做更少而自我追踪

works.title: Soma Express Kit
works.description: A toolkit of wearable physiological sensors with haptic and sound modules that lets people with visual impairment express their somaesthetic experience of a place to sighted partners in real time.
works.description_zh: 一套由可穿戴生理传感器与触觉、声音模块组成的工具包，让视障人士把自己对场所的身体美学经验实时传达给明眼的同伴。
works.idea_en: Blind and low-vision people's heightened somatic sensitivity is expertise: designing from it produces non-visual, shared experiences for everyone.
works.idea_zh: 盲人与低视力人士更敏锐的身体感受力是一种专长：从这种专长出发设计，可以为所有人创造非视觉的共享体验。
works.method: Wearable physiological sensing combined with multi-sensory haptic and audio output modules, used in collaborative sessions (with Kai Kunze, Keio KMD).
works.method_zh: 可穿戴生理传感结合多感官的触觉与声音输出模块，用于协作体验环节（与庆应 KMD 的 Kai Kunze 合作）。

paper.title: Soma Express Kit: Understanding the Somaesthetic Experience of People with Visual Impairment

works.title: Tactful Feminist Sensing
works.description: Design explorations, four concepts and one working prototype sense the conductivity of cervical mucus, adding touch-based bodily knowledge to fertility tracking.
works.description_zh: 设计探索、四个概念和一个可用原型感测宫颈黏液的导电性，为生育力追踪加入以触摸为基础的身体知识。
works.idea_en: Sensing intimate fluids can stay close to the fleshy, tactile body instead of abstracting it into numbers.
works.idea_zh: 对私密体液的感测可以贴近有血有肉、可触摸的身体，而不是把它抽象成数字。
works.method: A conductivity sensor prototype for vaginal fluids, presented as a pictorial with material explorations of proximity, visibility and temporality.
works.method_zh: 一个测量阴道分泌物导电性的传感器原型，以图文论文形式呈现，并对接近程度、可见性与时间性进行材料探索。

paper.title: Tactful Feminist Sensing: Designing for Touching Vaginal Fluids

works.title: Toward Understanding the Design of Intertwined Human–Computer Integrations
works.description: The paper studies systems in which user and machine control the user's body at the same moment, so that it is no longer clear who did what, and offers design tactics for this 'intertwined' integration.
works.description_zh: 论文研究用户与机器在同一时刻控制用户身体的系统：到底是谁做了什么已不再清楚；论文为这种“交织式”融合提供了设计策略。
works.idea_en: When agency over one's body is shared, the question 'who moved?' becomes part of the experience, and designers can tune how aware the person is of the machine and how aligned it is with them.
works.idea_zh: 当对身体的能动性被共享时，“是谁在动？”本身就成为体验的一部分；设计者可以调节人对机器的觉察程度，以及机器与人的一致程度。
works.method: Three case studies (an EMS game, an eBike and a brain-computer system) analysed along two dimensions, awareness of the machine's agency and alignment of the machine's agency.
works.method_zh: 用三个案例（一款肌肉电刺激游戏、一辆电动自行车和一个脑机系统），沿“对机器能动性的觉察”与“机器能动性的一致性”两个维度进行分析。

paper.title: Toward Understanding the Design of Intertwined Human–Computer Integrations

works.title_zh: 理解交织式人机融合的设计

works.title: A Calming Hug
works.description: A soft cushion held against the chest that slowly expands and contracts like breathing; people hugging it before a stressful test tended to slow their own breath to match.
works.description_zh: 一个抱在胸前的柔软靠垫，像呼吸一样缓慢地膨胀与收缩；人们在压力测验前抱着它，往往会把自己的呼吸放慢去跟随。
works.idea_en: The body entrains to a rhythm it can feel against it; calm can be passed on through touch without any screen or voice.
works.idea_zh: 身体会跟上贴着它的、可以被感受的节律；平静无需屏幕或声音，也能经由触碰传递。
works.method: A shape-changing soft robotic cushion with an internal mechanism simulating breathing, validated in a lab study with an anxiety-inducing maths test.
works.method_zh: 内部机构模拟呼吸的形变软体机器人靠垫，在一个诱发焦虑的数学测验实验中得到验证。

paper.title: A calming hug: Design and validation of a tactile aid to ease anxiety

works.title: An Annotated Soma Design Process of the Pelvic Chair
works.description: An annotated portfolio of the whole soma design process behind the Pelvic Chair, a chair that helps people feel their pelvic floor, making each design move and its felt reason visible.
works.description_zh: 对 Pelvic Chair（一把帮助人感受盆底的椅子）整个身体设计过程所做的注释性作品集，让每一步设计选择及其身体感受上的理由都清楚可见。
works.idea_en: Soma design knowledge lives in the process; annotating that process shows how felt judgments steer the design.
works.idea_zh: 身体设计的知识存在于过程之中；为过程作注释，能展示被感受的判断如何引导设计。
works.method: Annotated portfolio method applied to a first-person soma design process (with Marianela Ciolfi Felice and Irene Kaklopoulou).
works.method_zh: 把注释性作品集方法应用于第一人称的身体设计过程（与 Marianela Ciolfi Felice、Irene Kaklopoulou 合著）。

paper.title: An Annotated Soma Design Process of the Pelvic Chair

works.title_zh: Pelvic Chair 身体设计过程注释

works.title: Body Maps: A Generative Tool for Soma-based Design
works.description: Body maps — outlines of a body that people draw and colour to locate sensations and feelings — used as a generative tool for soma design rather than only as a record.
works.description_zh: 身体地图——人们在身体轮廓上绘画、涂色以标出感觉与情绪的位置——被用作身体设计的生成工具，而不只是记录。
works.idea_en: Drawing where and how something is felt helps people notice and share sensations they could not put into words.
works.idea_zh: 画出“在哪里、以怎样的方式”感受到，能帮助人注意并分享说不出口的感觉。
works.method: Workshops with body-map templates, drawing materials and somatic exercises, analysed across several soma design studies.
works.method_zh: 工作坊使用身体地图模板、绘画材料与身体练习，并在多项身体设计研究中比较分析。

paper.title: Body Maps: A Generative Tool for Soma-based Design

works.title_zh: 身体地图：身体设计的生成工具

works.title: Diffraction-in-action: Lived Data
works.description: Five biodata case studies, in which design researchers lived with their own data in slow, open-ended ways, show how the data became entangled with their everyday lives rather than standing apart as objective measurement.
works.description_zh: 五个生物数据案例中，设计研究者以缓慢而开放的方式与自己的数据共处，展示了这些数据如何与日常生活缠绕在一起，而不是作为客观测量站在生活之外。
works.idea_en: Data about a body is lived: it changes what it measures, and designers learn most by staying with its messiness over time.
works.idea_zh: 关于身体的数据是“活的”：它会改变它所测量的东西；设计者长期与它的杂乱共处，才学得最多。
works.method: Five first-person biodata case studies analysed through Karen Barad's agential realism and diffraction.
works.method_zh: 五个第一人称生物数据案例，借助凯伦·巴拉德的能动实在论与“衍射”概念进行分析。

paper.title: Diffraction-in-action: Designerly Explorations of Agential Realism Through Lived Data

works.title_zh: 行动中的衍射：活的数据

works.title: Expressive Bodies
works.description: A design critique method drawn from disability dance and embodied disability cultures, in which disabled participants use movement to respond to and critique technology designs.
works.description_zh: 一种源自残障舞蹈与具身残障文化的设计评论方法：残障参与者用动作回应并评论技术设计。
works.idea_en: Disabled bodies carry expert knowledge of how technology feels; letting critique happen through movement values that knowledge.
works.idea_zh: 残障的身体拥有关于技术感受的专家知识；让评论通过动作发生，就是重视这种知识。
works.method: Workshops pairing embodied practices from disability arts with collaborative design critique.
works.method_zh: 把残障艺术中的具身实践与协作式设计评论相结合的工作坊。

paper.title: Expressive Bodies Engaging with Embodied Disability Cultures for Collaborative Design Critiques

works.title: Fabulating Biodata Futures
works.description: The paper synthesises design research on biodata and offers three fabulations, Weaving Alongside, Diffracting Selves and Collective Affect, that imagine biodata shared among diverse human and non-human bodies.
works.description_zh: 论文综述生物数据相关的设计研究，并给出三则“虚构”——Weaving Alongside、Diffracting Selves、Collective Affect——想象在多样的人类与非人身体之间共享生物数据。
works.idea_en: Biodata need not be individual and diagnostic; it can be a medium for living and knowing together with other bodies.
works.idea_zh: 生物数据不必是个人的、诊断性的，它可以成为与其他身体共同生活、共同认识的媒介。
works.method: Thematic synthesis of design exemplars followed by speculative fabulation written by an international group of biodata design researchers.
works.method_zh: 先对设计案例做主题综合，再由一个国际生物数据设计研究者小组撰写思辨性的虚构故事。

paper.title: Fabulating Biodata Futures for Living and Knowing Together

works.title: Focusing for Interaction Design: An Introspective Somatic Method
works.description: Adapts Eugene Gendlin's Focusing into steps designers can use to attend to a vague bodily 'felt sense' and let it unfold into words, images and design ideas.
works.description_zh: 把 Eugene Gendlin 的 Focusing（体会聚焦）改造为设计师可用的步骤，去关注模糊的身体“体会”，并让它展开为词语、意象与设计想法。
works.idea_en: Meaning often begins as an unclear bodily feeling; staying with it patiently lets understanding and emotion emerge together.
works.idea_zh: 意义常常始于一种模糊的身体感受；耐心地与它待在一起，理解与情绪会一同浮现。
works.method: Method developed through first-person studies and workshops (following the authors' 2018 Design Journal technique paper).
works.method_zh: 通过第一人称研究与工作坊发展而来（延续作者 2018 年发表于《Design Journal》的技巧论文）。

paper.title: Focusing for Interaction Design: An Introspective Somatic Method

works.title_zh: 用于交互设计的 Focusing：一种内省式身体方法

works.title: Integrated Exertion
works.description: Three eBikes that act on the rider, for example adding motor power to catch green lights or responding to the rider's brain state, are used to build a framework for exertion experiences where the machine is a partner acting on the body.
works.description_zh: 三辆会作用于骑行者的电动自行车（例如为赶上绿灯而增减助力，或响应骑行者的大脑状态）被用来建立一个框架：在运动体验中，机器是作用于身体的伙伴。
works.idea_en: When a machine shares the effort, riders describe feeling 'super-powered' or as one with the bike; the framework asks designers to shape that shared exertion rather than simply display data.
works.idea_zh: 当机器分担用力时，骑行者会说自己像“有了超能力”或与车融为一体；这个框架要求设计者去塑造这种共享的用力，而不只是显示数据。
works.method: Three eBike systems, including Ari (traffic-light-aware assistance) and likely an EEG-driven system that reads the rider's peripheral awareness, studied in the field; findings synthesised into a framework with design tactics.
works.method_zh: 对三套电动自行车系统进行田野研究，其中包括 Ari（根据红绿灯时序助力），很可能还有一套读取骑行者脑电“周边觉察”状态的系统；归纳出带有设计策略的框架。

paper.title: Integrated Exertion—Understanding the Design of Human–Computer Integration in an Exertion Context

works.title: JIZAI Body
works.description: A concept paper proposing the 'JIZAI Body': a person who can freely control, or hand over control of, their natural body and its physical and virtual extensions, so as to live as they wish in society.
works.description_zh: 一篇概念论文，提出“自在身体”：一个人可以自由地控制（或交出控制）自己的自然身体及其物理与虚拟延伸，从而在社会中按自己的意愿生活。
works.idea_en: The goal of augmentation is framed as jizai, the ease and freedom of the whole person, not maximum performance; control that is sometimes delegated can still feel like one's own body.
works.idea_zh: 增强的目标被理解为“自在”：整个人的从容与自由，而不是性能最大化；即使控制有时被委托出去，身体仍可被感受为自己的。
works.method: Literature review across augmentation, cybernetics, robotics, VR, neuroscience and the humanities, five key aspects illustrated with existing works, and speculative scenarios of a JIZAI society.
works.method_zh: 综述人类增强、控制论、机器人学、虚拟现实、神经科学与人文学科的文献，用已有作品阐述五个关键面向，并描绘“自在社会”的设想情景。

paper.title: Cyborgs, Human Augmentation, Cybernetics, and JIZAI Body

works.title: Making New Worlds: Transformative Becomings with Soma Design
works.description: Argues that soma design changes designers and users, not only products, and reads soma design projects as ways of becoming — and of imagining other worlds for bodies.
works.description_zh: 主张身体设计改变的不只是产品，还有设计师与使用者；把身体设计项目理解为“生成”的方式，以及为身体想象另一种世界的方式。
works.idea_en: Working through the body transforms who we are; soma design is also a practice of changing how bodies are allowed to live.
works.idea_zh: 透过身体工作会改变我们是谁；身体设计也是一种改变身体被允许如何生活的实践。
works.method: Theoretical reading of soma design cases through feminist new materialism and transformation (with Rob Comber).
works.method_zh: 借女性主义新物质主义与“转化”理论解读身体设计案例（与 Rob Comber 合著）。

paper.title: Making New Worlds – Transformative Becomings with Soma Design

works.title_zh: 创造新世界：身体设计中的转化性生成

works.title: Menstrual Garden
works.description: A multisensory installation with scent bottles holding the smells of fresh menstrual blood, stagnant menstrual blood and menstrual pain, beside 3D-printed sculptures of proteins found only in menstrual blood, identified from the artist's own samples.
works.description_zh: 一件多感官装置：香水瓶中分别装着新鲜经血、陈旧经血和经痛的气味，旁边是只存在于经血中的蛋白质的 3D 打印雕塑，这些蛋白质来自艺术家本人的样本。
works.idea_en: Giving menstrual pain a smell makes an inner, often hidden sensation shareable and discussable.
works.idea_zh: 为经痛赋予气味，让一种内在的、常被隐藏的感受变得可以分享、可以讨论。
works.method: Mass spectrometry of the artist's menstrual effluent over many cycles to build a menstrual blood proteome, translated into perfumes and 3D-printed protein models.
works.method_zh: 对艺术家多个周期的经血进行质谱分析，建立经血蛋白质组，再转化为香水与 3D 打印的蛋白质模型。

works.title: Parallel Adaptation
works.description: People switch back and forth between two virtual bodies, each with the opposite visual distortion of their reach; with the right perspective cues they learn both at once instead of one erasing the other.
works.description_zh: 参与者在两个虚拟身体之间来回切换，每个身体的伸手动作带有相反的视觉偏移；在合适的视角提示下，他们能同时学会两者，而不是一个抹去另一个。
works.idea_en: One body-mind can hold two motor selves if the switch between them is clearly marked, a first step toward living in several bodies.
works.idea_zh: 只要两者之间的切换被清晰标示，一个身心就可以容纳两个运动自我；这是走向同时栖居多个身体的第一步。
works.method: VR reaching task (N=21) with opposite gradual visuomotor rotations for body A and body B, crossing first- versus third-person perspective and head rotation cues.
works.method_zh: VR 伸手任务（21 人），身体 A 与身体 B 施加相反的渐进视觉运动旋转，交叉操纵第一/第三人称视角与头部转动提示。

paper.title: Parallel Adaptation: Switching between Two Virtual Bodies with Different Perspectives Enables Dual Motor Adaptation

works.title_zh: 平行适应：在两个虚拟身体间切换

works.title: Pelvic Chair
works.description: The Pelvic Chair uses soft latex air pockets in the seat to touch the outer pelvic floor in gentle rhythms, drawing attention to its anatomy, muscles and connections.
works.description_zh: Pelvic Chair 在座面中用柔软的乳胶气囊，以轻柔的节奏触碰外侧盆底，把注意力引向它的解剖结构、肌肉与联系。
works.idea_en: Rhythmic, technology-initiated touch can build somatic literacy of a hidden muscle group: feeling tension and release where words fail.
works.idea_zh: 有节奏的、由技术发起的触摸，可以建立对一组隐秘肌群的身体素养：在言语无法到达之处感受紧张与放松。
works.method: Inflatable latex pockets with tuned layers, volume and timing, developed through an annotated soma design process (Ståhl et al., DIS 2022) and studied with 14 participants (Yadav et al., CHI 2025).
works.method_zh: 层次、体积与时序经过调校的充气乳胶气囊，通过注释式身体设计开发（DIS 2022），并以 14 位参与者进行研究（Yadav 等，CHI 2025）。

paper.title: A Route to Somatic Literacy of the Pelvic Floor through Technology-Initiated Touch

works.title: Rethinking Menstrual Trackers Towards Period-Positive Ecologies
works.description: A critique of menstrual tracking apps and a proposal for period-positive design that supports how people feel and live with their cycles, not only how they log them.
works.description_zh: 批判月经追踪应用，提出“经期正向”的设计：支持人们如何感受并与自己的周期共处，而不只是记录它。
works.idea_en: A cycle is lived, not just predicted; period-positive design treats the menstruating body as something to be felt and talked about without shame.
works.idea_zh: 周期是被活出来的，不只是被预测的；“经期正向”的设计把经期身体当作可以被感受、被坦然谈论的东西。
works.method: Review of menstrual tracking apps and design research with users in India, leading to a period-positive ecology framework.
works.method_zh: 梳理月经追踪应用，并与印度用户开展设计研究，提出“经期正向生态”框架。

paper.title: Rethinking Menstrual Trackers Towards Period-Positive Ecologies

works.title_zh: 重新思考月经追踪：走向经期正向的生态

works.title: Shared User Interfaces of Physiological Data
works.description: A systematic review of 64 studies of social biofeedback, systems in which two or more people see, hear or feel each other's heart rate, breath or arousal.
works.description_zh: 一篇系统综述，梳理 64 项社会生物反馈研究，即两人或多人彼此看到、听到或感受到对方心率、呼吸或唤醒水平的系统。
works.idea_en: Shared body signals change relationships at three levels, within oneself, between people and around a shared task, and their meaning depends on timing and social context.
works.idea_zh: 共享的身体信号在三个层面改变关系：自身之内、人与人之间、围绕共同任务；其意义取决于时机与社会情境。
works.method: PRISMA-style systematic review of HCI literature, synthesised into the Social Biofeedback Interactions framework.
works.method_zh: 按 PRISMA 方式对人机交互文献做系统综述，并归纳为“社会生物反馈交互”框架。

paper.title: Shared User Interfaces of Physiological Data: Systematic Review of Social Biofeedback Systems and Contexts in HCI

works.title_zh: 生理数据的共享用户界面

works.title: Sketching Soma Bits
works.description: Describes the Soma Bits toolkit — small, soft modules that give heat, vibration and shape-change on the body, plus sensors — and how designers use it to sketch felt experiences directly on their skin.
works.description_zh: 介绍 Soma Bits 工具包——在身体上给出热、振动与形变的柔软小模块，外加传感器——以及设计师如何用它直接在皮肤上勾画被感受的体验。
works.idea_en: Designers need materials they can feel on their own body within minutes; that immediacy is what lets the soma lead the design.
works.idea_zh: 设计师需要几分钟内就能在自己身上感受到的材料；正是这种即时性让身体得以主导设计。
works.method: Modular hardware toolkit with actuators and sensors in fabric shapes, used and refined in workshops and courses (with Jarmo Laaksolahti).
works.method_zh: 模块化硬件工具包，把执行器与传感器装进织物外形中，在工作坊与课程中使用和改进（与 Jarmo Laaksolahti 合著）。

paper.title: Sketching Soma Bits

works.title_zh: 用 Soma Bits 画草图

works.title: Soma Corset
works.description: The Soma Corset senses breathing around the torso and answers with inflating pads, so the garment can feel like a harmonious partner, an organic 'other' with its own will, or a twisted mirror of one's own breath.
works.description_zh: Soma Corset 感测躯干的呼吸并以充气垫回应，于是这件衣服可能像一个和谐的伙伴，像一个有自己意志的有机“他者”，也可能像自己呼吸的扭曲镜像。
works.idea_en: When a garment mirrors your breath in tight loops, the line between wearer and technology blurs, and not always comfortably.
works.idea_zh: 当一件衣服在紧密的回路中映照你的呼吸时，穿着者与技术的边界会变得模糊，而且未必总是舒服的。
works.method: Breathing sensors and inflatable actuators placed over the diaphragm, intercostal muscles and lower back, run in closed sensing-actuation loops and explored by the design team over a long soma design process.
works.method_zh: 呼吸传感器与充气执行器分布在膈肌、肋间肌和下背部，以闭环的感测—执行方式运行，由设计团队在长时间的身体设计过程中探索。

paper.title: Touching Our Breathing through Shape-Change: Monster, Organic Other, or Twisted Mirror

works.title: Vulnerability as an Ethical Stance in Soma Design Processes
works.description: Examines moments in soma design where designers expose their bodies and feelings, and argues that holding vulnerability with care is itself an ethical stance.
works.description_zh: 考察身体设计中设计师暴露自己的身体与感受的时刻，并主张以关怀承接脆弱性本身就是一种伦理立场。
works.idea_en: Designing from the body means being exposed; vulnerability handled with care produces both better knowledge and fairer processes.
works.idea_zh: 从身体出发做设计就意味着会暴露自己；被细心对待的脆弱性，既带来更好的知识，也带来更公平的过程。
works.method: Reflective analysis of first-person soma design processes and workshops (with Airi Lampinen).
works.method_zh: 对第一人称身体设计过程与工作坊的反思性分析（与 Airi Lampinen 合著）。

paper.title: Vulnerability as an ethical stance in soma design processes

works.title_zh: 脆弱性作为身体设计过程中的伦理立场

works.title: Whose Touch is This?
works.description: EMS moves a participant's finger to touch a target, sometimes against what they intended and sometimes helping them do what they could not; the study charts when the touch still feels like theirs.
works.description_zh: 肌肉电刺激移动参与者的手指去触碰目标，有时违背其意图，有时帮助他们完成做不到的事；研究描绘了这种触碰何时仍被感受为自己的。
works.idea_en: Agency is a trade-off, not a switch: a computer can help the body and keep the feeling of authorship if assistance stays close to what the person was about to do.
works.idea_zh: 能动感是一种权衡而不是开关：只要辅助贴近人本来要做的动作，计算机就能在帮助身体的同时保留“由我发起”的感受。
works.method: Controlled experiments crossing user intention with EMS-driven outcomes (aligned, forced, assisted), with agency ratings, leading to a design framework for digital touch.
works.method_zh: 受控实验把用户意图与电刺激驱动的结果（一致、强制、辅助）交叉组合，测量能动感评分，并据此提出数字触觉的设计框架。

paper.title: Whose Touch is This?: Understanding the Agency Trade-Off Between User-Driven Touch vs. Computer-Driven Touch

works.title: Articulating Soma Experiences using Trajectories
works.description: Soma trajectories: a way of drawing and describing how a felt experience unfolds over time — moments of attention, sensation and transition — for design and analysis.
works.description_zh: 身体轨迹：一种描绘并叙述被感受的经验如何随时间展开的方式——注意、感觉与转换的时刻——用于设计与分析。
works.idea_en: A soma experience has a shape in time; mapping that shape helps designers orchestrate transitions rather than single effects.
works.idea_zh: 身体经验在时间中有形状；描绘这种形状，帮助设计师编排过渡，而不只是单个效果。
works.method: Extends Benford's trajectories framework with first-person accounts from several soma design projects.
works.method_zh: 以多个身体设计项目的第一人称叙述，扩展 Benford 的“轨迹”框架。

paper.title: Articulating Soma Experiences using Trajectories

works.title: Breathing Garment
works.description: A garment with inflatable cushions presses firmly on the torso in relation to the wearer's breathing, sometimes following it, sometimes leading it.
works.description_zh: 一件带充气垫的衣服，根据穿着者的呼吸对躯干施加稳定的压力，时而跟随呼吸，时而引导呼吸。
works.idea_en: Deep pressure can direct attention to the muscles and bones of breathing; the most evocative rhythm sits between following and leading the breath.
works.idea_zh: 深压可以把注意力引向参与呼吸的肌肉与骨骼；最动人的节奏介于跟随与引导呼吸之间。
works.method: A breathing sensor drives pneumatic actuators placed symmetrically and asymmetrically on the torso, inspired by Deep Pressure Therapy; first-person explorations led to 'breathing correspondence' interactions.
works.method_zh: 呼吸传感器驱动在躯干上对称或不对称分布的气动执行器，灵感来自深压疗法；第一人称探索得出了“呼吸呼应”的交互方式。

paper.title: Exploring Awareness of Breathing through Deep Touch Pressure

works.title: Breathing Shell
works.description: Designed with a classical singer, the Breathing Shell is a wearable breathing sensor that also presses back on the body, so the singer feels 'the sensor feeling you'.
works.description_zh: Breathing Shell 与一位古典歌手共同设计，是一种可穿戴呼吸传感器，同时也会反压身体，让歌手感到“传感器在感受我”。
works.idea_en: Being sensed is itself a bodily experience; a sensor that is felt makes the relation between body and data reciprocal.
works.idea_zh: 被感测本身就是一种身体经验；一个能被感觉到的传感器，让身体与数据之间的关系成为双向的。
works.method: A new sensing mechanism built from shape-change (inflatable) technology around the singer's torso, developed through soma design sessions on non-habitual breathing.
works.method_zh: 在歌手躯干周围用形变（充气）技术构成一种新的感测机制，经由关于“非习惯性呼吸”的身体设计练习发展而来。

paper.title: “Feeling the Sensor Feeling you”: A Soma Design Exploration on Sensing Non-habitual Breathing

works.title: Can You Hear My Heartbeat?
works.description: In a lab study, 27 people recognised others' emotions while sometimes hearing that person's heartbeat; hearing it shifted their emotional perspective and raised their sense of 'feeling what the other was feeling'.
works.description_zh: 在一项实验室研究中，27 名参与者辨认他人的情绪，其间有时能听见对方的心跳；听见心跳改变了他们的情绪视角，也增强了“感受对方所感”的体验。
works.idea_en: A heartbeat heard, not seen, reaches the listener's body directly and can open an embodied path to empathy.
works.idea_zh: 被听见而非被看见的心跳，直接抵达聆听者的身体，可以打开一条具身的共情之路。
works.method: Within-subjects emotion recognition task with auditory heartbeat conditions and empathy measures (CHI 2021; with Bruce Walker and Grace Leslie).
works.method_zh: 被试内设计的情绪识别任务，设置不同的心跳声条件并测量共情（CHI 2021；合作者 Bruce Walker、Grace Leslie）。

paper.title: Can You Hear My Heartbeat?: Hearing an Expressive Biosignal Elicits Empathy

works.title: Chemical Haptics
works.description: A wearable pumps small amounts of skin-safe chemicals onto the skin to produce tingling (sanshool), numbness (lidocaine), stinging (cinnamaldehyde), warmth (capsaicin) and cooling (menthol) in VR scenes.
works.description_zh: 一个可穿戴装置把少量对皮肤安全的化学物质泵到皮肤上，在 VR 场景中产生刺麻（山椒素）、麻木（利多卡因）、刺痛（肉桂醛）、温热（辣椒素）和清凉（薄荷醇）的感觉。
works.idea_en: The skin's own chemistry can be the display: sensations arise inside the body's receptors rather than being pushed onto it by a motor.
works.idea_zh: 皮肤自身的化学反应就可以成为显示：感觉在身体的感受器内部产生，而不是由马达从外部施加。
works.method: A wearable with small reservoirs and pumps delivers liquid stimulants onto the skin; user studies on how each sensation feels, its onset and duration, and its use in VR scenes.
works.method_zh: 带小型储液器与泵的可穿戴装置把液体刺激物输送到皮肤上；用户研究测试每种感觉的质感、起效与持续时间，以及在 VR 场景中的使用。

paper.title: Chemical Haptics: Rendering Haptic Sensations via Topical Stimulants

works.title: HuggieBot
works.description: A human-sized robot with a soft, warm, inflated chest and padded arms that sees a person approach, fits its embrace to their body and lets go when they want.
works.description_zh: 一台真人大小的机器人，拥有柔软、温暖的充气胸膛和带衬垫的手臂；它看到有人走近，按对方身体调整拥抱，并在对方想结束时松开。
works.idea_en: A good robot hug is defined by how it feels: soft, warm, the right size, responsive, and above all willing to release.
works.idea_zh: 好的机器人拥抱由感觉来定义：柔软、温暖、尺寸合适、有回应，尤其是愿意松开。
works.method: HuggieBot 2.0 uses an inflated, heated torso with pressure sensing, a camera to see the user and arm control adapted to user size; evaluated in a user study that proposed six 'hug commandments'.
works.method_zh: HuggieBot 2.0 采用可感压的充气加热躯干、用于看见使用者的摄像头，以及按使用者身材调节的手臂控制；在提出六条“拥抱诫命”的用户研究中评估。
keywords: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems

paper.title: The Six Hug Commandments: Design and Evaluation of a Human-Sized Hugging Robot with Visual and Haptic Perception

works.title: Limited Control Over the Body as Intriguing Play Design Resource
works.description: Using three of their own bodily play systems, the authors argue that losing some control over one's body, through external triggers or other bodily activity, can make play more interesting rather than less.
works.description_zh: 作者用自己的三个身体游戏系统论证：通过外部触发或其他身体活动而失去对身体的部分控制，可以让游戏更有趣，而不是更糟。
works.idea_en: Not being fully in charge of one's body can be a source of curiosity and reflection; designers can offer it through four strategies: exploration, reflection, learning and embracement.
works.idea_zh: 不完全掌控自己的身体，可以成为好奇与反思的来源；设计者可以通过探索、反思、学习与接纳四种策略来提供这种体验。
works.method: Design analysis of three bodily play systems varying the player's degree of indirect control, leading to four strategies.
works.method_zh: 对三个身体游戏系统进行设计分析，改变玩家间接控制的程度，并归纳出四种策略。

paper.title: Limited Control Over the Body as Intriguing Play Design Resource

works.title_zh: 以对身体的有限控制作为游戏设计资源

works.title: Menstrual Technologies Designed with Adolescents
works.description: Seven adolescents aged 16 to 18 used Menarche Bits in two workshops to design technologies that respond to menstrual cramps and to anxious feelings before a period, so they can keep playing sport.
works.description_zh: 七位 16 至 18 岁的青少年在两场工作坊中使用 Menarche Bits，设计能回应经期痉挛和经前焦虑的技术，让这些年轻人能继续参加体育运动。
works.idea_en: Participatory soma design lets young people listen to and care for newly menstruating bodies instead of hiding them.
works.idea_zh: 参与式身体设计让年轻人倾听并照顾刚开始来月经的身体，而不是把它藏起来。
works.method: Two participatory soma design workshops with the Menarche Bits toolkit, run with sports clubs and a high school as part of menstrual advocacy.
works.method_zh: 使用 Menarche Bits 工具包的两场参与式身体设计工作坊，与运动俱乐部和一所高中合作，作为月经倡导的一部分。

paper.title: Designing Menstrual Technologies with Adolescents

works.title_zh: 与青少年共同设计的月经技术

works.title: OmniFiber
works.description: OmniFiber is a thin fluidic fibre that contracts and senses its own strain, so it can be woven or knitted into garments that move, squeeze and guide the body.
works.description_zh: OmniFiber 是一种细的流体纤维，能收缩并感测自身的拉伸，可以织入或编入服装，让衣服移动、挤压并引导身体。
works.idea_en: A textile that behaves like muscle lets movement be taught and shared through the fabric we already wear.
works.idea_zh: 像肌肉一样工作的织物，让动作可以通过我们本来就穿着的衣物被教授和分享。
works.method: Fluidic artificial muscle fibres (under 1.8 mm) with integrated soft sensors, woven into on-body haptic devices for embodied learning (with the MIT Media Lab Tangible Media Group).
works.method_zh: 直径小于 1.8 毫米、集成柔性传感器的流体人工肌肉纤维，织入身体上的触觉装置用于具身学习（与 MIT 媒体实验室可触媒体组合作）。

paper.title: OmniFiber: Integrated Fluidic Fiber Actuators for Weaving Movement based Interactions into the 'Fabric of Everyday Life'

works.title: Physical Warm-up Games
works.description: Studies warm-up games in physical education and circus training, and adds open-ended wearables to them, to show how warm-ups prepare people physically, socially and mentally.
works.description_zh: 研究体育课与马戏训练中的热身游戏，并为其加入开放式可穿戴设备，说明热身如何让人在身体、社交与心理上做好准备。
works.idea_en: Warm-ups tune body and mind together; light, open-ended technology can support that tuning without taking over.
works.idea_zh: 热身同时调谐身体与心智；轻量、开放的技术可以支持这种调谐而不喧宾夺主。
works.method: Collection of warm-up games from teachers online plus design interventions with wearable light/sound artefacts in a circus training course.
works.method_zh: 收集教师在线分享的热身游戏，并在马戏训练课中用可穿戴的光/声装置进行设计干预。

paper.title: Physical Warm-up Games: Exploring the Potential of Play and Technology Design

works.title: Preserving Agency During Electrical Muscle Stimulation Training
works.description: EMS made participants react to a target faster than they could alone; when the stimulation was timed so they still felt they had moved themselves, they stayed faster even after the EMS was removed.
works.description_zh: 肌肉电刺激让参与者对目标的反应比自己更快；当刺激的时机让他们仍觉得是自己在动时，即使撤掉电刺激，他们的反应仍然更快。
works.idea_en: Keeping the felt sense of 'I did it' is not a luxury: learning through an assisted body works better when the movement is still experienced as one's own.
works.idea_zh: 保留“是我做的”这种感受并不是奢侈：当动作仍被体验为自己的，借由被辅助的身体进行学习效果更好。
works.method: Reaction-time task with EMS on the forearm at different onsets relative to each person's natural reaction; sense of agency rated after each trial, and performance measured after EMS was removed.
works.method_zh: 反应时任务，前臂肌肉电刺激相对于每个人自然反应的起始时间设置不同；每次试验后评定能动感，并在撤除电刺激后测量表现。

paper.title: Preserving Agency During Electrical Muscle Stimulation Training Speeds up Reaction Time Directly After Removing EMS

works.title_zh: 在肌肉电刺激训练中保留能动感

works.title: Reclaiming the Body through Design: Menopause
works.description: Interviews with twelve women and a design workshop produced concepts that bring design close to the body during menopause, resisting its framing as a medical problem.
works.description_zh: 对十二位女性的访谈和一场设计工作坊产生了若干概念，让设计在更年期中贴近身体，抵抗把更年期仅视为医学问题的框架。
works.idea_en: Menopause is an entanglement of physical and psychosocial change; design can recognise and transform it rather than only treat symptoms.
works.idea_zh: 更年期是身体变化与心理社会变化的交织；设计可以承认并转化它，而不只是治疗症状。
works.method: Interviews with 12 women and a participatory design workshop with three, analysed from a holistic, body-first perspective.
works.method_zh: 访谈 12 位女性，并与其中三位进行参与式设计工作坊，从整体、以身体为先的视角分析。

paper.title: Resisting the Medicalisation of Menopause: Reclaiming the Body through Design

works.title_zh: 以设计找回身体：更年期

works.title: Robotic Hand Augmentation Drives Changes in Neural Body Representation
works.description: Able-bodied volunteers wore the Third Thumb for five days, in the lab and in daily life; they learned to use it even without looking, reported it feeling more like part of their body, and brain decoding showed the representation of their own biological hand had partly collapsed.
works.description_zh: 健全的志愿者连续五天在实验室和日常生活中佩戴 Third Thumb；他们即使不看也学会了使用它，报告它越来越像身体的一部分，而脑解码显示他们原本那只手的脑内表征出现了部分“塌缩”。
works.idea_en: Adding a limb is not free: as the extra thumb is taken into the body, the felt and neural hand it attaches to changes as well.
works.idea_zh: 增加一个肢体并非没有代价：当额外的拇指被纳入身体时，它所连接的那只手在感受上和神经表征上也随之改变。
works.method: Five-day training study with motor and dexterity tasks, embodiment questionnaires, hand kinematics and fMRI decoding of finger representations before and after training.
works.method_zh: 为期五天的训练研究，结合运动与灵巧性任务、具身感问卷、手部运动学，以及训练前后手指表征的功能磁共振成像解码。

paper.title: Robotic hand augmentation drives changes in neural body representation

works.title_zh: 机器人手部增强改变大脑的身体表征

works.title: Significant Otter
works.description: A watch and phone app for romantic partners: the app reads the sender's heart rate and suggests matching animated otters (calm, excited, angry…) to send, and the partner can respond with otter gestures such as a hug.
works.description_zh: 为恋人设计的手表与手机应用：它读取发送者的心率，推荐相应的水獭动画（平静、兴奋、生气……）供其发送，对方可以用拥抱等水獭动作回应。
works.idea_en: Sensing made communication feel easier and more authentic, but also raised worries about who authors a feeling; biosignals work best as suggestions the person can accept or refuse.
works.idea_zh: 传感让交流更轻松、更真实，却也引发“一种感受由谁执笔”的担忧；生物信号最好作为可接受也可拒绝的建议。
works.method: Apple Watch heart rate informs a small set of suggested otter animations; a one-month study with 20 couples compared sensing off and on (CHI 2021).
works.method_zh: Apple Watch 心率决定推荐的几种水獭动画；与 20 对伴侣进行了为期一个月、比较传感开与关的研究（CHI 2021）。

paper.title: Significant Otter: Understanding the Role of Biosignals in Communication

works.title: Stereo-Smell via Electrical Trigeminal Stimulation
works.description: A small device on the nasal septum electrically stimulates the trigeminal nerve so wearers feel a smell-like sensation coming from the left or right, and can follow a virtual odour source by turning their head.
works.description_zh: 放在鼻中隔上的小装置以电刺激三叉神经，让佩戴者感到类似气味的感觉来自左边或右边，并能转头追踪一个虚拟气味源。
works.idea_en: Smell is partly a bodily, tactile sense inside the nose; addressing that nerve directly gives smell a direction, as hearing has.
works.idea_zh: 嗅觉部分是鼻腔内的身体性、触觉性感觉；直接作用于这条神经，就能像听觉那样赋予嗅觉方向。
works.method: Electrodes on the septum deliver lateralised electrical pulses to trigeminal nerve endings; user studies on perceived direction and navigation to a virtual smell in VR.
works.method_zh: 鼻中隔上的电极向三叉神经末梢施加左右不同的电脉冲；用户研究测试感知方向以及在 VR 中循虚拟气味导航。

paper.title: Stereo-Smell via Electrical Trigeminal Stimulation

works.title_zh: 经三叉神经电刺激的立体嗅觉

works.title: SymbioSinging (ADA)
works.description: SymbioSinging is a soft robotic garment, ADA, that re-enacts the felt movements of singing on the body of someone who is not singing.
works.description_zh: SymbioSinging 是一件名为 ADA 的软体机器人服装，它在不唱歌的人身上重现歌唱时的身体感受。
works.idea_en: Somatic knowledge can be partly transposed from one body to another through touch.
works.idea_zh: 身体知识可以借由触觉，部分地从一个身体转移到另一个身体。
works.method: A pneumatically controlled, fibre-based air-driven actuator garment developed through a soma design process with a singer.
works.method_zh: 一件以气动控制、基于纤维的空气驱动执行器服装，通过与歌手的身体设计过程开发而成。

paper.title: SymbioSinging: Robotically transposing singing experience across singing and non-singing bodies

works.title: The Bodies of TEI
works.description: A review of papers at the TEI conference that asks which bodies embodied interaction design assumes, and finds a default body that is able, binary-gendered and normatively sized.
works.description_zh: 对 TEI 会议论文的综述，追问具身交互设计默认了哪些身体，结论是默认的身体往往健全、性别二元、体型标准。
works.idea_en: Designing 'for the body' always means designing for some bodies; soma design has to ask whose felt experience it takes as the norm.
works.idea_zh: “为身体设计”总意味着为某些身体设计；身体设计必须追问，它把谁的亲身感受当作常态。
works.method: Systematic analysis of TEI papers for how bodies are described, sensed and addressed, from a critical, queer and disability-studies stance.
works.method_zh: 从批判、酷儿与残障研究的立场，系统分析 TEI 论文如何描述、感知与对待身体。

paper.title: The Bodies of TEI – Investigating Norms and Assumptions in the Design of Embodied Interaction

works.title: The Breathing Wings
works.description: The Breathing Wings is a wearable over the shoulder blades whose soft shape-changing parts swell and embrace the back, inviting the wearer to feel a neglected part of the body.
works.description_zh: Breathing Wings 覆盖在肩胛骨上，柔软的形变部件鼓起、环抱后背，邀请穿着者去感受一处常被忽略的身体部位。
works.idea_en: A material that touches you slowly can blur the boundary between garment and body and make the shoulder blades felt again.
works.idea_zh: 缓慢触碰你的材料，会模糊衣物与身体的边界，让肩胛骨重新被感受到。
works.method: Autobiographical soma design with soft inflatable and shape-change materials, documented as a pictorial.
works.method_zh: 以柔软的充气与形变材料进行自传式身体设计，以图文论文（pictorial）形式记录。

paper.title: The Breathing Wings: An Autobiographical Soma Design Exploration of Touch Qualities through Shape-Change Materials

works.title: Towards Understanding the Design of Bodily Integration
works.description: A design framework for systems where body and computer act on each other, laid out along two axes, bodily agency and bodily ownership, giving four experiences: Super-Body, Tele-Body, Chauffeured-Body and Possessed-Body.
works.description_zh: 一个针对身体与计算机相互作用之系统的设计框架，沿“身体能动感”与“身体归属感”两条轴展开，得到四种体验：超级身体、远程身体、被驾驶的身体与被附身的身体。
works.idea_en: Whether a device feels like 'me' and whether I feel I am acting are separate questions; designers can move deliberately between them, instead of assuming more control is always better.
works.idea_zh: 设备是否像“我”，与我是否感到自己在行动，是两个不同的问题；设计者可以有意在两者之间移动，而不是默认控制越多越好。
works.method: Analysis of the authors' own EMS, eBike, ingestible and GVS systems and others' work to derive a four-quadrant design space.
works.method_zh: 分析作者自己的肌肉电刺激、电动自行车、可吞咽传感器与前庭电刺激系统以及他人作品，归纳出四象限设计空间。

paper.title: Towards understanding the design of bodily integration

works.title: Towards a Contemplative Research Framework for Training Self-Observation in HCI
works.description: Uses the researcher's own practice of Tonglen compassion meditation to propose a framework for training self-observation, so first-person HCI research can rest on cultivated attention.
works.description_zh: 以研究者自己修习“施受法”（Tonglen）慈悲冥想为例，提出训练自我观察的框架，让第一人称人机交互研究建立在被培养的注意力之上。
works.idea_en: Observing one's own body-mind is a skill; contemplative traditions offer tested ways to train it.
works.idea_zh: 观察自己的身心是一门技能；冥想传统提供了经过检验的训练方法。
works.method: Autoethnographic study of compassion cultivation combined with micro-phenomenological description, synthesised into a contemplative research framework.
works.method_zh: 对慈悲修习的自我民族志研究，结合微观现象学描述，提炼为冥想式研究框架。

paper.title: Towards a Contemplative Research Framework for Training Self-Observation in HCI: A Study of Compassion Cultivation

works.title_zh: 迈向训练人机交互中自我观察的冥想式研究框架

works.title: Tracing Conceptions of the Body in HCI: From User to More-Than-Human
works.description: Homewood, Hedemyr, Fagerberg Ranten and Kozel trace how HCI has conceived the body, from the user's body as an input device, through the lived, somatic body, to the more-than-human body entangled with other beings.
works.description_zh: Homewood、Hedemyr、Fagerberg Ranten 与 Kozel 梳理了人机交互如何理解身体：从作为输入设备的用户身体，到活的、身体性的身体，再到与其他存在交织的超越人类的身体。
works.idea_en: Which body we assume shapes what we design; the soma is one step toward bodies that are relational and more-than-human.
works.idea_zh: 我们预设怎样的身体，就会设计出怎样的东西；soma 是走向关系性、超越人类的身体的一步。
works.method: Critical literature review of CHI and related publications, organised by conceptions of the body.
works.method_zh: 对 CHI 及相关出版物的批判性文献综述，按身体观加以组织。

paper.title: Tracing Conceptions of the Body in HCI: From User to More-Than-Human

works.title_zh: 追溯人机交互中的身体观：从用户到超越人类

works.title: Unpacking Non-Dualistic Design: The Soma Design Case
works.description: A TOCHI article that uses a series of soma design projects to show what design looks like when it refuses the split between mind and body, self and other, subject and object.
works.description_zh: TOCHI 论文，以一系列身体设计项目展示：当设计拒绝心与身、自我与他者、主体与客体的二分时，会是什么样子。
works.idea_en: Feeling, thinking and moving are one process; methods that treat the designer's soma as data make that non-dualism practical.
works.idea_zh: 感受、思考与动作是同一个过程；把设计师的身体当作数据的方法，让这种非二元立场变得可操作。
works.method: Theoretical paper built from case projects by KTH and Nottingham teams, analysed as design strategies for non-dualistic design.
works.method_zh: 理论论文，基于 KTH 与诺丁汉团队的案例项目，把它们分析为非二元设计的策略。

paper.title: Unpacking Non-Dualistic Design: The Soma Design Case

works.title_zh: 拆解非二元设计：以身体设计为例

works.title: Validity and Rigour in Soma Design: Sketching with the Soma
works.description: Describes 'sketching with the soma' — the iterative, felt trying-out of materials and movements on one's own body — and argues for what makes such first-person design rigorous and valid.
works.description_zh: 描述“用身体画草图”——在自己身上反复、亲身地试验材料与动作——并论证这类第一人称设计何以严谨、有效。
works.idea_en: The designer's felt sense can be trained, tested against others and made accountable; that is where the rigour of soma design lies.
works.idea_zh: 设计师的身体感受可以被训练、与他人对照、被问责；身体设计的严谨就在于此。
works.method: Analysis of several soma design processes, identifying practices of sensitisation, iteration and shared articulation.
works.method_zh: 分析多个身体设计过程，识别出敏化、迭代与共同表述等实践。

paper.title: Validity and Rigour in Soma Design-Sketching with the Soma

works.title_zh: 身体设计的有效性与严谨性：用身体画草图

works.title: What Can HCI Learn from Sexual Consent?
works.description: A feminist model of sexual consent (voluntary, ongoing, informed, specific and revocable) carried into interaction design, especially for technologies that act on or read the body.
works.description_zh: 把女性主义的性同意模式（自愿、持续、知情、具体、可撤回）带入交互设计，特别是作用于或读取身体的技术。
works.idea_en: Consent is felt and negotiated moment to moment between bodies; technologies that touch or sense the body should be designed to ask, listen and stop.
works.idea_zh: 同意是在身体之间一刻一刻被感受与协商的；会触碰或感知身体的技术，应被设计成会询问、会倾听、会停下。
works.method: Conceptual transfer of feminist and sexual consent literature into design principles, with examples from bodily and intimate technologies.
works.method_zh: 把女性主义与性同意文献中的概念转译为设计原则，并以身体与亲密技术为例。

paper.title: What Can HCI Learn from Sexual Consent? A Feminist Process of Embodied Consent for Interactions with Emerging Technologies

works.title_zh: 人机交互能从性同意中学到什么？

works.title: aSpire
works.description: A small pneumatic device clipped to a strap or belt inflates air pouches against the body at a slow, personalised rhythm, and breathing tends to follow; tested with car passengers during real commutes.
works.description_zh: 一个夹在背带或腰带上的小型气动装置，以缓慢、个性化的节律让气囊贴着身体充气，呼吸会随之放慢；在真实通勤中与乘车者一起测试。
works.idea_en: Breath can be guided by touch rather than by instruction: a soft rhythm on the body invites slower breathing without adding mental load.
works.idea_zh: 呼吸可以由触摸而不是指令来引导：身体上柔和的节律邀请呼吸放慢，而不会增加心理负担。
works.method: Array of individually inflating air pouches driven by a mobile pump and valves, with adjustable pattern, intensity and frequency (MIT Media Lab).
works.method_zh: 由移动气泵与阀门驱动的可独立充放气的气囊阵列，模式、强度与频率可调（MIT 媒体实验室）。

paper.title: aSpire: Clippable, Mobile Pneumatic-Haptic Device for Breathing Rate Regulation via Personalizable Tactile Feedback

works.title: Articulating Experience: Reflections from Experts Applying Micro-Phenomenology to Design Research in HCI
works.description: Interviews expert practitioners on how they use micro-phenomenology in HCI design research, and draws out its strengths, pitfalls and training needs.
works.description_zh: 访谈在人机交互设计研究中使用微观现象学的专家，梳理其优势、陷阱与训练需求。
works.idea_en: Getting people to describe how an experience unfolds — not what they think about it — takes practice from both interviewer and interviewee.
works.idea_zh: 让人描述一段经验如何展开——而不是他们对它怎么想——需要访谈者与受访者双方的练习。
works.method: Qualitative study with experienced micro-phenomenology practitioners in design and HCI (with Philippe Pasquier).
works.method_zh: 对设计与人机交互领域有经验的微观现象学实践者的质性研究（与 Philippe Pasquier 合著）。

paper.title: Articulating Experience: Reflections from Experts Applying Micro-Phenomenology to Design Research in HCI

works.title_zh: 说出经验：专家在人机交互设计研究中运用微观现象学的反思

works.title: Body RemiXer
works.description: A mixed-reality installation where participants' bodies appear as abstract, light-like avatars that stretch toward and mix with each other, inviting touch and synchronised movement between strangers.
works.description_zh: 一件混合现实装置：参与者的身体化为抽象、如光般的化身，彼此伸展、交融，邀请陌生人之间的触碰与同步动作。
works.idea_en: Blurring where one body ends and another begins can lower social boundaries, but it also unsettles one's sense of owning a body.
works.idea_zh: 模糊一个身体在哪里结束、另一个身体从哪里开始，可以降低社交边界，但也会动摇对自身身体的拥有感。
works.method: Asymmetric XR with body tracking, projection and a headset; body-mixing avatars; studied with phenomenological interviews.
works.method_zh: 非对称扩展现实系统，结合身体追踪、投影与头显；化身可相互交融；以现象学访谈研究。

paper.title: Diffusing Social Boundaries through Virtual Bodies: How Mixed Reality Embodied Experiences Can Foster Social Connection

works.title: Curious Cycles
works.description: Curious Cycles is a set of objects that invite people to look at and touch their menstrual blood, saliva and cervical mucus over a full cycle.
works.description_zh: Curious Cycles 是一组物件，邀请人们在一个完整的月经周期中观看并触摸自己的经血、唾液和宫颈黏液。
works.idea_en: Touching and looking at one's own fluids builds self-knowledge and a nurturing appreciation of the changing body, against the stigma that teaches disgust.
works.idea_zh: 触摸和观看自己的体液，能建立对自身的认识，并对变化中的身体生出滋养性的欣赏，以对抗教人厌恶的污名。
works.method: Research through Design: a kit of objects and interactions deployed with five participants over a menstrual cycle, with diaries and interviews.
works.method_zh: 以设计为研究：一套物件与互动方式，由五位参与者在一个月经周期中使用，配合日记与访谈。

paper.title: Touching and Being in Touch with the Menstruating Body

works.title: Designing Drone Chi
works.description: A pictorial that retraces how the sensory experience of tai chi was carried, step by step, into the form, flight and feel of the Drone Chi drone.
works.description_zh: 一篇图文论文，回溯太极的感官经验如何一步步被带进 Drone Chi 无人机的外形、飞行与手感之中。
works.idea_en: Designing a robot for the soma is slow work that moves between the designer's own practice, product design and engineering.
works.idea_zh: 为身体而设计机器人是一项缓慢的工作，需要在设计者自己的修习、产品设计与工程之间来回。
works.method: Quasi-chronological design account with sketches, prototypes and first-person tai chi practice, reflecting on somaesthetic, product design and engineering perspectives.
works.method_zh: 以准时间顺序的设计记录，结合草图、原型与第一人称的太极修习，从身体美学、产品设计与工程三种视角反思。

paper.title: Designing Drone Chi: Unpacking the Thinking and Making of Somaesthetic Human-Drone Interaction

works.title: Designing Trans Technology
works.description: Participatory design sessions with 21 trans people that produced ideas for technologies for changing bodies, changing appearance, safety and finding resources.
works.description_zh: 与 21 位跨性别者进行参与式设计，提出面向改变身体、改变外表、安全与寻找资源的技术构想。
works.idea_en: Trans communities name body change as a design space of their own; design that centres them treats transition as care for a felt self.
works.idea_zh: 跨性别社群把身体的改变命名为属于他们自己的设计空间；以他们为中心的设计，把性别转变看作对被感受之自我的照护。
works.method: Participatory design workshops with trans participants, analysed into four categories of envisioned technologies and challenges.
works.method_zh: 与跨性别参与者开展参与式设计工作坊，把构想的技术与挑战归纳为四类。

paper.title: Designing Trans Technology: Defining Challenges and Envisioning Community-Centered Solutions

works.title: Drone Chi
works.description: A person moves slowly in a tai chi-like practice with a small drone hovering close to their hands; the drone follows and leads their movement, and its downdraft is felt on the skin.
works.description_zh: 一个人以类似太极的方式缓慢运动，一架小型无人机在手边近距离悬停；无人机跟随又引领其动作，旋翼下洗的气流落在皮肤上被感受到。
works.idea_en: A drone can be a partner in a meditative movement practice rather than a remote-controlled tool: slowness, closeness and airflow let it be felt, not piloted.
works.idea_zh: 无人机可以是冥想式动作修习中的伙伴，而不是遥控工具：缓慢、贴近与气流让它被感受，而不是被驾驶。
works.method: A micro-quadcopter in a custom protective shell, likely tracked by motion capture, responds to the practitioner's hand movements; designed with soma design and Somaesthetic Appreciation principles and studied with practitioners.
works.method_zh: 一架装在定制保护外壳中的微型四旋翼（很可能由动作捕捉追踪）回应修习者的手部动作；按身体设计与“身体美学鉴赏”原则设计，并与修习者一起研究。

paper.title: Drone Chi: Somaesthetic Human-Drone Interaction

works.title: Ethics in Movement
works.description: A video analysis of a choreographer, an opera singer and a choir of five drones performing together shows how the human-drone assemblage limits or frees movement against the norms of operatic performance.
works.description_zh: 对一位编舞者、一位歌剧演唱者与五架无人机“合唱团”同台演出的视频分析，展示了人与无人机的组合如何在歌剧表演规范面前限制或解放动作。
works.idea_en: Ethics is not only rules 'out there': how a technology informs or dictates movement shapes what we can feel and freely choose, and somatic awareness widens that freedom.
works.idea_zh: 伦理不只是“外在”的规则：技术如何塑造或规定动作，决定了我们能感受什么、能自由选择什么；身体觉察则拓宽了这份自由。
works.method: Detailed video analysis of rehearsals and performances of a drone opera, read through Shusterman's somaesthetic perspective on ethics (with Shusterman as co-author).
works.method_zh: 对一部无人机歌剧的排练与演出做细致的视频分析，并从舒斯特曼的身体美学伦理视角解读（舒斯特曼为合著者）。

paper.title: Ethics in Movement: Shaping and Being Shaped in Human-Drone Interaction

works.title: From Biodata to Somadata
works.description: Proposes 'somadata': biosignals such as muscle tension or breathing explored as design material through felt feedback on the body, instead of charts on a screen.
works.description_zh: 提出“身体数据（somadata）”：把肌电、呼吸等生物信号当作设计材料，通过身体上的感受反馈来探索，而不是屏幕上的图表。
works.idea_en: Data about the body becomes meaningful when it is felt by the body; turning biodata into somadata keeps experience and measurement together.
works.idea_zh: 关于身体的数据，只有被身体感受到才有意义；把生物数据变成身体数据，让经验与测量不再分离。
works.method: Design workshops where designers wore EMG and breathing sensors mapped to sound, vibration and heat, analysed as material exploration.
works.method_zh: 设计工作坊：设计师佩戴肌电与呼吸传感器，信号映射为声音、振动与热，并作为材料探索加以分析。

paper.title: From Biodata to Somadata

works.title_zh: 从生物数据到身体数据

works.title: HandMorph
works.description: A passive exoskeleton glove that maps the wearer's hand onto a smaller set of mechanical fingers, so an adult grasps objects with a child's hand size and feels how a child's hand fits the world.
works.description_zh: 一种被动外骨骼手套，把佩戴者的手映射到一组更小的机械手指上，让成年人以儿童的手掌尺寸抓握物体，体会儿童的手如何与世界相处。
works.idea_en: Changing the size of the grasping body changes what things afford, so empathy with another body can be felt in one's own hand.
works.idea_zh: 改变抓握身体的尺寸，就改变了物体所提供的可能性；对另一个身体的共情因此可以在自己的手中被感受到。
works.method: Linkage-based exoskeleton without motors; each finger of the wearer drives a shorter mechanical finger; used by designers to evaluate products for children.
works.method_zh: 无电机的连杆式外骨骼，佩戴者的每根手指驱动一根更短的机械手指；设计者用它来评估面向儿童的产品。

paper.title: HandMorph: a Passive Exoskeleton that Miniaturizes Grasp

works.title: Interdisciplinary Insights for Digital Touch Communication
works.description: An open-access book from the IN-TOUCH project that brings together design, social science and computing to ask how digital touch changes intimacy, care and social norms.
works.description_zh: IN-TOUCH 项目的开放获取著作，汇集设计、社会科学与计算研究，追问数字触碰如何改变亲密、照护与社会规范。
works.idea_en: Touch is social and cultural before it is technical: designing digital touch means designing who may touch whom, how and when.
works.idea_zh: 触碰先是社会的、文化的，然后才是技术的：设计数字触碰就是设计谁能触碰谁、如何触碰、何时触碰。
works.method: Speculative design workshops, interviews and case studies with artists, engineers and the public, analysed through multimodal social semiotics.
works.method_zh: 与艺术家、工程师和公众一起开展思辨设计工作坊、访谈和案例研究，并以多模态社会符号学分析。

paper.title: Interdisciplinary Insights for Digital Touch Communication

works.title_zh: 数字触碰沟通的跨学科洞见

works.title: Menarche Bits
works.description: Menarche Bits is an open-ended kit of heat pads and soft shape-changing actuators, worn on the skin or in pockets of a stretchy garment, for young people to create body-worn technologies around their first periods.
works.description_zh: Menarche Bits 是一套开放式套件，包含加热片和柔软的形变执行器，可贴在皮肤上或放进弹性衣物的口袋里，供年轻人围绕自己的初潮创作贴身技术。
works.idea_en: Warmth and pressure on the body can open conversations about menstruation and help young people trust their menstruating bodies.
works.idea_zh: 身体上的温暖与压力可以打开关于月经的对话，帮助年轻人信任自己正在来月经的身体。
works.method: Soft robotic inflatables and heat elements that stimulate, press, heat and massage the skin and muscles; later used in participatory workshops with adolescents in sports clubs.
works.method_zh: 软体充气件与加热元件，可刺激、按压、加热和按摩皮肤与肌肉；后来用于与运动俱乐部青少年进行的参与式工作坊。

paper.title: Designing with Intimate Materials and Movements: Making “Menarche Bits”

works.title: Menstrual (Im)Mobilities and Safe Spaces
works.description: A study of how menstruating people in urban India plan where they can go, change and rest, and how the lack of safe toilets and spaces restricts their movement during periods.
works.description_zh: 研究印度城市中来月经的人如何规划能去哪里、在哪里更换与休息，以及缺乏安全厕所与空间如何限制经期时的出行。
works.idea_en: The menstruating body is felt in public space: a missing toilet or a hostile room becomes pain, worry and a smaller world.
works.idea_zh: 经期的身体在公共空间中被感受：缺一间厕所、一个不友好的房间，就会变成疼痛、担忧与更小的生活范围。
works.method: Interviews and design activities with menstruators in India, analysed through mobility and safe-space lenses.
works.method_zh: 对印度月经者进行访谈与设计活动，以“流动性”与“安全空间”的视角分析。

paper.title: Menstrual (Im)Mobilities and Safe Spaces

works.title_zh: 月经的（不）流动性与安全空间

works.title: Mettāmatics
works.description: A meditation artwork in which a guided loving-kindness practice, a real-time visualisation and a soundscape respond to changes in the participant's heart rate variability.
works.description_zh: 一件冥想艺术作品：引导式的慈心（mettā）练习、实时可视化与声景，随参与者心率变异性的变化而回应。
works.idea_en: Feelings of compassion and gratitude have a bodily signature; a slow interface lets people sense that shift in themselves, a 'being as a way of doing'.
works.idea_zh: 慈悲与感恩的感受有其身体印记；一个缓慢的界面让人感知自身的这种转变——“以存在作为行动”。
works.method: A fingertip or earlobe pulse sensor feeds heart rate variability into visuals and sound, paired with guided mettā meditation (with Callum Howard; TEI 2020).
works.method_zh: 指尖或耳垂脉搏传感器把心率变异性送入影像与声音，配合引导式慈心冥想（与 Callum Howard 合作；TEI 2020）。

paper.title: Mettāmatics

works.title: Neo-Noumena
works.description: Two people wear EEG headsets and mixed-reality headsets for three days; the system reads each person's emotional state and shows it to the other as animated graphics in mixed reality around them.
works.description_zh: 两人连续三天佩戴脑电头带与混合现实头显；系统读取每个人的情绪状态，并在其周围以混合现实中的动态图像显示给对方看。
works.idea_en: Emotion read from the brain becomes something partners see and respond to together; participants got better at regulating each other's feelings, showing that neural data can support felt, shared attunement rather than only measurement.
works.idea_zh: 从大脑读出的情绪变成伴侣共同看见并回应的东西；参与者调节彼此情绪的能力提高了，说明神经数据可以支持被感受的、共享的调谐，而不只是测量。
works.method: Consumer EEG with a machine-learning emotion classifier drives procedurally generated visuals in two head-mounted displays; field study with five pairs, emotional-competence measures and interviews.
works.method_zh: 消费级脑电设备配合机器学习情绪分类器，驱动两台头戴显示器中程序生成的图像；对五对参与者进行田野研究，结合情绪能力量表与访谈。

paper.title: Neo-Noumena: Augmenting Emotion Communication

works.title: Next Steps for Human-Computer Integration
works.description: An agenda written by 29 researchers after a five-day workshop on systems that merge with the body, from muscle stimulation to implants, and the ethical questions they raise.
works.description_zh: 29 位研究者在为期五天的工作坊后写成的议程，讨论从肌肉电刺激到植入物等与身体融合的系统及其伦理问题。
works.idea_en: When computers act inside the body, design must ask how agency, ownership and the felt self are shared between person and machine.
works.idea_zh: 当计算机在身体内部行动时，设计必须追问：能动性、拥有感与被感受的自我如何在人与机器之间分配。
works.method: Structured workshop of experts in body-integrated systems, synthesised into a set of research challenges.
works.method_zh: 由身体融合系统领域专家参加的结构化工作坊，归纳出一组研究挑战。

paper.title: Next Steps for Human-Computer Integration

works.title: Reimagining (Women's) Health: HCI, Gender and Essentialised Embodiment
works.description: A critique of 'women's health' research in HCI that ties health needs to assumed female anatomy, and a call to design for trans, intersex and non-binary people whose bodies do not fit that model.
works.description_zh: 批判人机交互中把健康需求绑定于预设女性解剖结构的“女性健康”研究，呼吁为身体不符合这一模型的跨性别、间性与非二元者设计。
works.idea_en: Tying care to a presumed body leaves out the people whose felt bodies differ; health design should start from lived embodiment, not from categories.
works.idea_zh: 把照护绑定在一个预设的身体上，就会遗漏那些被感受的身体与之不同的人；健康设计应从亲历的具身经验出发，而不是从分类出发。
works.method: Critical review of women's health literature in HCI, informed by trans and queer theory.
works.method_zh: 以跨性别与酷儿理论为依据，批判性回顾人机交互中的女性健康文献。

paper.title: Reimagining (Women's) Health: HCI, Gender and Essentialised Embodiment

works.title_zh: 重新想象（女性）健康：人机交互、性别与本质化的具身

works.title: Removal as a Method
works.description: A first-person design method: the researcher stops using fertility and menstrual self-tracking tools and records how the felt sense of one's own cycle and body changes once the data is gone.
works.description_zh: 一种第一人称设计方法：研究者停用自己的生育与月经追踪工具，记录数据消失后，自己对周期与身体的感受如何变化。
works.idea_en: Taking a tracker away shows what it was doing to the felt body; removal lets designers notice how data had replaced bodily attention.
