works.idea_zh: 把追踪器拿走，才看得出它原本对被感受的身体做了什么；“移除”让设计者注意到数据如何取代了对身体的关注。
works.method: Autoethnographic study in which the designer removes self-tracking technologies from daily life and documents the experience over time, proposed as a fourth-wave HCI method.
works.method_zh: 自我民族志研究：设计者从日常生活中移除自我追踪技术，并长期记录这一经验，作为“第四波人机交互”的方法提出。

paper.title: Removal as a Method: A Fourth Wave HCI Approach to Understanding the Experience of Self-Tracking

works.title: Soma Design and Sensory Misalignment
works.description: A workshop report that brings together soma designers and researchers of sensory misalignment in VR and rides, arguing that each practice can extend the other.
works.description_zh: 一份工作坊报告，把身体设计者与研究 VR、游乐设施中感官错位的研究者聚在一起，论证两种实践可以相互扩展。
works.idea_en: Deliberately misaligning the senses is a technological form of estrangement: it disrupts the habitual body so that it can be felt anew.
works.idea_zh: 有意让感官错位是一种技术化的陌生化：它打乱惯常的身体，使之能被重新感受。
works.method: Joint workshop of the Nottingham Mixed Reality Lab and KTH soma design researchers, with hands-on sessions on misalignment prototypes, synthesised into design themes.
works.method_zh: 诺丁汉混合现实实验室与 KTH 身体设计研究者共同举办的工作坊，动手体验错位原型，并归纳为设计主题。

paper.title: Soma Design and Sensory Misalignment

works.title: The Body Electric
works.description: The Body Electric is a singing corset that captures the breathing movements of the singer's torso and uses them to shape the soundscape, so the instrument steers the singer's voice as much as the singer steers the instrument.
works.description_zh: The Body Electric 是一件歌唱束衣，它捕捉歌手躯干的呼吸起伏并用来塑造声景；于是歌手的声音被乐器牵引的程度，不亚于歌手驾驭乐器的程度。
works.idea_en: An instrument designed from the singer's felt breathing can unsettle control and open new ways of relating to one's own voice.
works.idea_zh: 从歌手亲身感受的呼吸出发设计的乐器，会动摇“控制”，打开与自己嗓音相处的新方式。
works.method: Breathing sensors on a corset stream biofeedback to a live electronic composition; performed in Hamburg in July 2020 and documented as a NIME paper.
works.method_zh: 束衣上的呼吸传感器把生物反馈传入现场电子作曲；2020 年 7 月在汉堡演出，并写成 NIME 论文。

paper.title: The Body Electric: A NIME designed through and with the somatic experience of singing

works.title: The Designer's Body as Resource in Design
works.description: Maps how designers use their own bodies in design by combining point of view (first, second, third person) with tense (past, present, future), and shows each combination in practice.
works.description_zh: 把视角（第一、第二、第三人称）与时态（过去、现在、将来）组合起来，梳理设计师如何在设计中使用自己的身体，并逐一举例。
works.idea_en: Imagining, remembering and enacting a felt experience are different bodily resources; a designer can switch among them on purpose.
works.idea_zh: 想象、回忆与演出一段身体经验，是不同的身体资源；设计师可以有意识地在它们之间切换。
works.method: Conceptual framework grounded in Merleau-Ponty and illustrated with student design projects and the authors' practice.
works.method_zh: 以 Merleau-Ponty 为基础的概念框架，并用学生设计项目与作者的实践加以说明。

paper.title: The Designer's Body as Resource in Design: Exploring Combinations of Point-of-view and Tense

works.title_zh: 设计师的身体作为设计资源

works.title: ThermoPixels
works.description: ThermoPixels is a crafting toolkit of thermochromic materials, heating elements and skin conductance sensors with which people make their own colour-changing displays of physiological arousal.
works.description_zh: ThermoPixels 是一套手工工具包，包含热致变色材料、加热元件和皮肤电传感器，人们用它自己动手制作随生理唤醒而变色的显示物。
works.idea_en: Making your own representation of arousal, with your hands, turns biodata into something personal you can regulate emotion with.
works.idea_zh: 亲手为自己的唤醒制作表征，会让生物数据成为属于自己的、可以用来调节情绪的东西。
works.method: GSR sensing drives heating elements under thermochromic paint and fabric; 20 participants created personalised shapes and colours in 10 workshops.
works.method_zh: 皮肤电信号驱动热致变色颜料与织物下的加热元件；20 位参与者在 10 场工作坊中制作了个性化的形状与色彩。

paper.title: ThermoPixels: Toolkit for Personalizing Arousal-based Interfaces through Hybrid Crafting

works.title: ambienBeat
works.description: A wristband that taps a gentle pulse on the skin at a rhythm slightly slower than the wearer's heart rate, helping the heart settle without the wearer having to watch a screen or follow instructions.
works.description_zh: 一款腕带，以略慢于佩戴者心率的节律在皮肤上轻轻敲击，帮助心跳平缓下来，佩戴者无需看屏幕或遵循指令。
works.idea_en: The body entrains to rhythms it feels: a calm beat on the skin can guide the heart below the level of deliberate effort.
works.idea_zh: 身体会与它感受到的节律同步：皮肤上平静的拍子可以在刻意努力之外引导心跳。
works.method: Wrist-worn tactile actuator paired with heart rate sensing, delivering a personalised 'calming heartbeat' pattern (MIT Media Lab, Tangible Media Group).
works.method_zh: 腕戴触觉振动器结合心率感测，提供个性化的“安定心跳”节律（MIT 媒体实验室 Tangible Media Group）。

paper.title: ambienBeat: Wrist-worn Mobile Tactile Biofeedback for Heart Rate Rhythmic Regulation

works.title: A Sample of One: First-Person Research Methods in HCI
works.description: A DIS workshop that gathered autoethnography, autobiographical design, soma design and other first-person methods to discuss their rigour, ethics and value in HCI.
works.description_zh: DIS 工作坊，汇集自我民族志、自传式设计、身体设计等第一人称方法，讨论它们在人机交互中的严谨性、伦理与价值。
works.idea_en: When the researcher is also the participant, the body that lives with the design becomes the instrument of knowing.
works.idea_zh: 当研究者同时是参与者，与设计共同生活的身体就成了认识的工具。
works.method: Workshop with position papers and hands-on sessions; it led to a TOCHI special issue on first-person methods (2021).
works.method_zh: 工作坊包括立场论文与实践环节，后来促成 TOCHI 第一人称方法特刊（2021）。

paper.title: A Sample of One: First-Person Research Methods in HCI

works.title_zh: 一人样本：人机交互中的第一人称研究方法

works.title: Animo
works.description: A smartwatch app that turns the wearer's heart rate into a small animated shape, an 'animo', that close friends or partners can send to each other as a lightweight way of saying how they are.
works.description_zh: 一款智能手表应用，把佩戴者的心率变成一个会动的小图形（animo），亲密的朋友或伴侣可以互相发送，以轻量的方式告诉对方自己的状态。
works.idea_en: A biosignal shared as an expressive, abstract form lets people feel close without words, while leaving the meaning of the body's state open to both.
works.idea_zh: 以可表达的抽象形态分享的生物信号，让人无需言语就感到亲近，同时让身体状态的意义对双方保持开放。
works.method: Smartwatch heart rate drives the colour and motion of an animated shape, likely with features for dyadic sending and viewing; a two-week field study with 34 participants (IMWUT 2019).
works.method_zh: 智能手表采集的心率驱动动画图形的颜色与运动，并支持两人之间的发送与查看；与 34 位参与者进行了为期两周的实地研究（IMWUT 2019）。

paper.title: Animo: Sharing Biosignals on a Smartwatch for Lightweight Social Connection

works.title: Ari, the eBike
works.description: An electric bike that knows the traffic-light timing ahead and adds or holds back motor power so rider and bike reach the green light together.
works.description_zh: 一辆电动自行车知道前方红绿灯的时间，通过增加或保留电机助力，让骑手与车一起赶上绿灯。
works.idea_en: When a machine acts on your effort, the felt question is how to share control of your own body's work.
works.idea_zh: 当机器直接作用于你的用力时，感受上的问题是：如何分享对自己身体劳动的控制。
works.method: An eBike augmented with traffic-light data and motor control, plus light cues, studied with riders on city routes.
works.method_zh: 一辆接入红绿灯数据并可控制电机的电动自行车，配合灯光提示，在城市路线上与骑手一起研究。

paper.title: "Co-riding With My eBike to Get Green Lights"

works.title: Arque
works.description: A wearable artificial tail that swings to the opposite side when the wearer leans, helping them keep balance as a monkey's or cheetah's tail does.
works.description_zh: 一条可穿戴人工尾巴：佩戴者身体倾斜时，它会甩向相反方向，像猴子或猎豹的尾巴那样帮助保持平衡。
works.idea_en: A tail makes balance, usually unnoticed, into something felt at the back of the body, and lets a human borrow an animal's way of being upright.
works.idea_zh: 尾巴让通常不被察觉的平衡成为身体后方能感受到的东西，也让人借用动物的站立方式。
works.method: Vertebra-like modules strung on four artificial pneumatic muscles; body tilt is tracked and the tail is driven to counter-balance, with the tail's length and weight adjustable to the wearer.
works.method_zh: 由类似脊椎的模块串联在四根人工气动肌肉上；追踪身体倾斜并驱动尾巴反向平衡，长度与重量可按佩戴者调整。

paper.title: Arque: Artificial Biomimicry-Inspired Tail for Extending Innate Body Functions

works.title: As Light as You Aspire to Be
works.description: Sound-altering footwear (the 'Magic Shoes' line of work) tested during exertion such as gym stepping and stair climbing: lighter footstep sounds made people feel lighter even while working hard, depending on the body they aspired to.
works.description_zh: 改变声音的鞋（“魔法鞋”系列研究）在健身踏步、爬楼梯等发力情境中测试：更轻的脚步声让人即使在用力时也感到身体变轻，效果因人所向往的身体而异。
works.idea_en: Altering the felt body can support physical activity without numbers or targets, but the effect depends on each person's weight and body ideals and fades when the sound stops, which design must take seriously.
works.idea_zh: 改变被感受的身体可以在没有数字与目标的情况下支持身体活动，但效果取决于每个人的体重与身体理想，并在声音停止后消退，设计必须认真对待。
works.method: A wearable senses footsteps and alters their sound in real time; two studies in exertion contexts measured body perception, emotion and after-effects (CHI 2019).
works.method_zh: 可穿戴设备感测脚步并实时改变其声音；在两项发力情境研究中测量身体知觉、情绪与后效（CHI 2019）。

paper.title: As Light as You Aspire to Be: Changing Body Perception with Sound to Support Physical Activity

works.title: Compression Cradle
works.description: A person lies in a machine that slowly squeezes the whole body with a sequence of inflating volumes, like being held.
works.description_zh: 一个人躺进一台机器，机器以一系列充气体积缓缓挤压全身，就像被拥抱。
works.idea_en: Deep, even pressure calms the body; McRae asks whether machine touch could stand in for human touch in a touch-starved future, and what is lost if it does.
works.idea_zh: 深而均匀的压力让身体平静；McRae 追问在一个缺乏触摸的未来，机器的触摸能否替代人的触摸，若能，又会失去什么。
works.method: Inflatable chambers in a padded cradle inflate in a timed choreography around the lying body; exhibited at Triennale Milano.
works.method_zh: 软垫摇篮中的充气腔围绕躺着的身体按时序依次充气；曾在米兰三年展展出。

works.title: Dancing With Drones
works.description: For a commissioned opera with custom drones on stage, the choreographer used their own moving body to feel the drones' 'otherness', showed the engineer how the drones' behaviour should change, and re-choreographed as the drones improved.
works.description_zh: 为一部由无人机登台的委约歌剧，编舞者用自己的身体去感受无人机的“他者性”，向工程师示范其行为该如何改变，并随着无人机的改进不断重编舞蹈。
works.idea_en: Expressive machine movement is shaped through the designer's own moving body: an intercorporeal understanding between human and drone.
works.idea_zh: 富有表现力的机器动作，是通过设计者自己运动着的身体塑造出来的：一种人与无人机之间的身体间理解。
works.method: Analysis of months of artistic development of drone behaviours for an opera, based on observation, video and interviews with choreographer Åsa Unander-Scharin and the team.
works.method_zh: 基于观察、录像以及对编舞者 Åsa Unander-Scharin 和团队的访谈，分析为歌剧开发无人机行为的数月艺术过程。

paper.title: Dancing With Drones: Crafting Novel Artistic Expressions Through Intercorporeality

works.title: Egocentric Smaller-Person Experience
works.description: A wearable visual translator lowers the wearer's eye level to waist height, so adults see and move through a nursing school or museum from a child's viewpoint.
works.description_zh: 一种可穿戴的视觉转换装置，把穿戴者的视线高度降到腰部，让成年人以儿童的视角观看和穿行于护理学校或博物馆中。
works.idea_en: Changing only the height of the eyes changes the felt size of the body, and with it how people act toward objects and others.
works.idea_zh: 只改变眼睛的高度，就会改变身体被感受到的大小，也随之改变人对物与他人的行动方式。
works.method: Head-mounted display fed by a waist-mounted stereo camera that follows head movements, tested in field studies with nursing students and museum visitors.
works.method_zh: 头戴显示器接收腰部立体摄像头的画面，摄像头随头部转动；在护理学生与博物馆观众中进行实地研究。

paper.title: Egocentric Smaller-person Experience through a Change in Visual Perspective

works.title_zh: 以自我为中心的“小个子”体验

works.title: Evoking Physiological Synchrony and Empathy Using Social VR with Biofeedback
works.description: Pairs do a compassion meditation together in social VR while seeing each other's breathing rate and an EEG-based empathy signal; the more their signals synchronised, the more empathy they reported.
works.description_zh: 两人一组在社交 VR 中一起做慈悲冥想，同时看到彼此的呼吸频率与基于脑电的共情信号；两人信号越同步，报告的共情越多。
works.idea_en: Seeing another body's rhythm alongside one's own can pull two people into sync and toward empathy.
works.idea_zh: 在看到自己节律的同时看到另一个身体的节律，可以把两个人拉入同步，并引向共情。
works.method: Lab study (N = 72) in the DYNECOM VR meditation environment with respiration and EEG frontal-asymmetry biofeedback, shown solo or shared; a companion paper (Järvelä et al. 2021) reports respiratory synchrony and social presence.
works.method_zh: 在 DYNECOM VR 冥想环境中进行的实验室研究（N = 72），以呼吸与脑电额叶不对称作为生物反馈，分为单人或共享呈现；姊妹论文（Järvelä 等 2021）报告了呼吸同步与社会临场感。

paper.title: Evoking Physiological Synchrony and Empathy Using Social VR With Biofeedback

works.title_zh: 以生物反馈社交 VR 唤起生理同步与共情

works.title: HCI and Affective Health
works.description: A review of 139 CHI-family papers on depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder finds most innovation in automated diagnosis and self-tracking, and calls for interventions and ethical involvement of people living with these conditions.
works.description_zh: 对 139 篇 CHI 系列会议中关于抑郁、焦虑和双相障碍的论文的综述发现，大多数创新集中在自动诊断和自我追踪，并呼吁更多干预性设计，以及以合乎伦理的方式让患者参与。
works.idea_en: Producing more body data is not care; mental health technology should help people live with and act on what they feel.
works.idea_zh: 产出更多身体数据并不等于照护；心理健康技术应当帮助人与自己的感受共处，并据此行动。
works.method: Systematic literature review of ten years of SIGCHI proceedings, coded for condition, approach, technology and evaluation.
works.method_zh: 对十年 SIGCHI 会议论文的系统文献综述，按病症、方法、技术与评估方式编码。

paper.title: HCI and Affective Health: Taking stock of a decade of studies and charting future research directions

works.title: Heart Sounds Bench
works.description: A red public bench that amplifies the heart sounds of the people sitting on it into the surrounding space, and also plays back recorded heartbeats of earlier sitters.
works.description_zh: 一张红色公共长椅，把坐在上面的人的心音放大到周围空间，也回放此前坐过的人被录下的心跳。
works.idea_en: Biosensing can affirm being alive rather than diagnose or score; heart sounds felt as intimate yet anonymous invite rest and a sense of shared life, while respecting each person's right to stay opaque to data.
works.idea_zh: 生物传感可以是对“活着”的肯定，而不是诊断或打分；亲密却匿名的心音邀请人休息、感到共享的生命，同时尊重每个人不被数据看透的权利。
works.method: Heart sounds, likely picked up with stethoscope-style microphones, are amplified through speakers without labels or scores, and past sitters' recordings are replayed; a study with 19 participants in public space (CHI 2019).
works.method_zh: 心音（很可能由听诊器式麦克风拾取）经扬声器放大，不做标注或打分，并回放此前坐者的录音；在公共空间中与 19 位参与者进行研究（CHI 2019）。

paper.title: Life-Affirming Biosensing in Public: Sounding Heartbeats on a Red Bench

exhibited: Extension of Self, Georgia Tech Art Gallery (2022)

works.title: JeL
works.description: Two people in VR breathe to grow a coral reef of jellyfish-like forms; the reef grows most when their breathing falls into sync.
works.description_zh: 两个人在 VR 中用呼吸让一片由水母般形态组成的珊瑚礁生长；当他们的呼吸同步时，珊瑚礁长得最快。
works.idea_en: Synchronised breath can link people to each other and to a living world at once.
works.idea_zh: 同步的呼吸可以同时把人与人、人与一个活的世界连在一起。
works.method: Two VR headsets with breathing sensors; a shared virtual reef responds to each breath and to their synchrony; evaluated through interviews.
works.method_zh: 两台 VR 头显配呼吸传感器；共享的虚拟珊瑚礁回应每一次呼吸及二人的同步程度；以访谈评估。

paper.title: JeL: Breathing Together to Connect with Others and Nature

works.title: Parting the Red Sea: Lived Experiences of Menopause
works.description: A study of a menopause forum on Reddit, where women make sense of hot flushes, bleeding and mood together, showing that the experience of menopause is social as much as bodily.
works.description_zh: 研究 Reddit 上一个更年期论坛：女性在这里一起理解潮热、出血与情绪，表明更年期经验既是身体的，也是社会的。
works.idea_en: A body in transition is not a list of symptoms; its changes become meaningful through shared stories, so design should support that sense-making rather than only track signs.
works.idea_zh: 转变中的身体不是一张症状清单；它的变化要在共享的故事里获得意义，设计应支持这种意义建构，而不只是追踪体征。
works.method: Qualitative analysis of posts in a menopause subreddit, informed by feminist social science methods that centre women's lived experience.
works.method_zh: 以重视女性亲历经验的女性主义社会科学方法，对一个更年期子论坛的帖子做质性分析。

paper.title: Parting the Red Sea: Sociotechnical Systems and Lived Experiences of Menopause

works.title_zh: 分开红海：更年期的亲历经验

works.title: Patching Gender: Non-binary Utopias in HCI
works.description: A short speculative piece imagining technologies that treat gender as open and changeable rather than as a fixed binary field in a system.
works.description_zh: 一篇简短的思辨文章，想象把性别当作开放、可变之物而非系统中固定二元字段的技术。
works.idea_en: Systems that fix gender also fix how bodies may be felt and read; non-binary utopias let design imagine bodies otherwise.
works.idea_zh: 把性别固定下来的系统，也固定了身体可以被如何感受与解读；非二元的乌托邦让设计能够想象另一种身体。
works.method: Speculative, utopian writing grounded in non-binary experience, proposing ways to 'patch' gender in computing.
works.method_zh: 以非二元经验为基础的思辨与乌托邦写作，提出在计算中“修补”性别的方式。

paper.title: Patching Gender: Non-binary Utopias in HCI

works.title_zh: 修补性别：人机交互中的非二元乌托邦

works.title: Philosophical Posthumanism
works.description: Ferrando maps posthumanism, transhumanism, antihumanism, new materialism and related movements, and develops a philosophical posthumanism of relation and embodiment.
works.description_zh: Ferrando 梳理后人类主义、超人类主义、反人文主义、新唯物主义等思潮，并发展出一种关于关系与具身的哲学后人类主义。
works.idea_en: Useful for designers who need to tell the enhancement agenda apart from posthumanisms that keep the body and other species at the centre.
works.idea_zh: 适合需要区分“增强议程”与“以身体和其他物种为中心的后人类主义”的设计者。
works.method: Philosophy textbook-monograph in the Theory in the New Humanities series, with a glossary of posthuman terms.
works.method_zh: 收入 Theory in the New Humanities 丛书的哲学专著兼教材，附后人类术语表。

paper.title: Philosophical Posthumanism

works.title: Preemptive Action
works.description: Electrical muscle stimulation makes the user's hand react faster than it would alone, and by timing the stimulation just before the person's own reaction, users still feel that they moved.
works.description_zh: 肌肉电刺激让使用者的手比自身反应更快地动作；通过把刺激时机安排在本人即将反应之前，使用者仍会觉得是自己在动。
works.idea_en: The sense of 'I did it' depends on timing: assistance that arrives in step with one's intention is felt as one's own movement.
works.idea_zh: “是我做的”这种感觉取决于时机：与意图同步到来的辅助，会被感受为自己的动作。
works.method: Reaction-time studies varying EMS onset relative to natural reaction, with sense-of-agency ratings (with Pedro Lopes, University of Chicago).
works.method_zh: 反应时实验，改变电刺激相对于自然反应的起始时间，并测量能动感评分（与芝加哥大学 Pedro Lopes 合作）。

paper.title: Preemptive Action: Accelerating Human Reaction using Electrical Muscle Stimulation Without Compromising Agency

works.title: Purrble
works.description: A plush creature whose heartbeat races when a child picks it up; stroking it slows the heartbeat until it purrs, so the child calms the toy and, in doing so, calms down.
works.description_zh: 一只毛绒生物，孩子一抱起它，它的心跳就很快；抚摸它会让心跳慢下来直到发出咕噜声，于是孩子在安抚玩具的同时也安抚了自己。
works.idea_en: Soothing another body in one's lap is a way of soothing one's own; emotion regulation is practised through the hands, in the moment it is needed.
works.idea_zh: 安抚怀里的另一个身体，也是安抚自己的方式；情绪调节在需要它的当下，通过双手来练习。
works.method: Soft toy with touch sensors and a vibration motor that simulates heartbeat and purring; deployed at home with children in a feasibility study, later commercialised.
works.method_zh: 内置触摸传感器与振动马达的软体玩具，模拟心跳与咕噜声；在儿童家中开展可行性研究，后来商品化。

paper.title: A Smart Toy Intervention to Promote Emotion Regulation in Middle Childhood: Feasibility Study

works.title: Soma Design and Politics of the Body
works.description: A short paper arguing that design tends to repeat dichotomies such as body-mind, male-female and emotion-thinking, and that closer somatic engagement with digital materials can help designers bypass them and counter privilege.
works.description_zh: 一篇短论文，指出设计常常重复身/心、男/女、情绪/思考等二分，而更深入地以身体投入数字材料，能帮助设计师绕开这些现成概念、对抗特权。
works.idea_en: Feeling your own body more finely also makes visible the social norms written into it; soma design has to engage those politics.
works.idea_zh: 更细致地感受自己的身体，也会让刻写在身体上的社会规范显现出来；身体设计必须面对这些政治。
works.method: Position paper reflecting on the KTH group's soma design projects through non-dualism and feminist qualities such as pluralism and participation (with Ciolfi Felice, Campo Woytuk, Kilic Afsar, Tsaknaki and Ståhl).
works.method_zh: 立场论文，从非二元立场与多元、参与等女性主义品质出发，反思 KTH 团队的身体设计项目（与 Ciolfi Felice、Campo Woytuk、Kilic Afsar、Tsaknaki、Ståhl 合著）。

paper.title: Soma Design and Politics of the Body

works.title: Teaching Soma Design
works.description: Reports soma design courses in which students did Feldenkrais-style body scans and movement exercises, then explored heat, vibration and shape-change on their own bodies before designing.
works.description_zh: 记录身体设计课程：学生先做类似 Feldenkrais 的身体扫描与动作练习，再在自己身上探索热、振动与形变，然后才开始设计。
works.idea_en: Somaesthetic sensitivity can be taught; slowing down with the body first changes what students go on to design.
works.idea_zh: 身体美学的感受力是可以教的；先与身体一起慢下来，会改变学生后来设计出的东西。
works.method: Analysis of several soma design courses and workshops with somatic exercises, material explorations and design briefs.
works.method_zh: 分析若干身体设计课程与工作坊，包括身体练习、材料探索与设计任务。

paper.title: Teaching Soma Design

works.title: Understanding the Role of Interactive Machine Learning in Movement Interaction Design
works.description: An essay arguing that movement interaction should be designed by moving: the designer performs examples and machine learning captures the embodied knowledge that cannot be written as rules.
works.description_zh: 一篇论文主张动作交互应当通过运动来设计：设计者亲自示范，机器学习捕捉那些无法写成规则的具身知识。
works.idea_en: Movement knowledge is tacit and felt, so the best specification of a movement interaction is a body performing it.
works.idea_zh: 动作知识是默会的、被感受的，因此一个动作交互最好的规格说明就是一个正在做它的身体。
works.method: Synthesis of theories of embodied and tacit knowledge with case studies of interactive machine learning tools for movement.
works.method_zh: 把具身与默会知识的理论与面向动作的交互式机器学习工具案例综合起来。

paper.title: Understanding the Role of Interactive Machine Learning in Movement Interaction Design

works.title_zh: 理解交互式机器学习在动作交互设计中的角色

works.title: Vivewell
works.description: A speculative workplace wellness product that tracks employees' menstrual cycles, presented through a fictional brochure and artefacts to show how current data practices could turn intimate body data into a tool of control.
works.description_zh: 一款思辨性的职场健康产品，追踪员工的月经周期；通过虚构的宣传册与物件，展示现有数据实践如何把私密身体数据变成控制工具。
works.idea_en: Body data about menstruation is never neutral; imagining who else reads it makes the politics of tracking a felt, not abstract, concern.
works.idea_zh: 关于月经的身体数据从来不是中立的；想象还有谁在读它，让追踪的政治成为可感的而非抽象的担忧。
works.method: Speculative design: a fictional company's product materials built from existing menstrual-tracking and workplace-wellness data practices, used to provoke discussion.
works.method_zh: 思辨设计：以现有月经追踪与职场健康的数据实践为素材，制作虚构公司的产品材料，用以引发讨论。

paper.title: Vivewell: Speculating Near-Future Menstrual Tracking through Current Data Practices

works.title: AISOMA / Living Archive
works.description: A machine-learning tool trained on 25 years of McGregor's filmed choreography that proposes new movement phrases in response to a dancer's pose.
works.description_zh: 一个机器学习工具，以 McGregor 25 年的舞蹈影像为训练数据，根据舞者的姿态提出新的动作短句。
works.idea_en: An archive of a choreographer's bodily style can become a partner that dancers answer with their own bodies.
works.idea_zh: 一位编舞家的身体风格档案，可以成为舞者用自己身体回应的伙伴。
works.method: Pose estimation over archival video trains a sequence model that generates continuations; developed with Google Arts & Culture Lab.
works.method_zh: 对档案视频进行姿态估计，训练生成后续动作的序列模型；与 Google Arts & Culture Lab 合作开发。

works.title: Agonist-Antagonist Myoneural Interface (AMI)
works.description: An amputation surgery that reconnects muscle pairs in the residual limb, so that when a bionic ankle moves, the person feels its position and movement as if it were their own joint.
works.description_zh: 一种截肢手术：在残肢中重新连接成对的肌肉，使仿生踝关节运动时，人能像感受自己关节一样感受到它的位置与运动。
works.idea_en: A prosthesis is taken into the body when it can be felt from within: restoring proprioception, not only control, is what lets people say the limb is 'mine'.
works.idea_zh: 假体被纳入身体，是在它能被从内部感受到的时候：恢复本体感，而不只是控制，才让人说这条腿“是我的”。
works.method: Surgically linked agonist-antagonist muscles send natural stretch signals; electrodes read their activity to drive a powered ankle-foot prosthesis, whose motion is fed back as muscle stretch.
works.method_zh: 通过手术相连的主动肌与拮抗肌产生自然的牵张信号；电极读取其活动来驱动动力踝足假体，假体的运动再以肌肉牵张的形式反馈回来。

paper.title: Proprioception from a neurally controlled lower-extremity prosthesis

works.title_zh: 主动肌-拮抗肌肌神经接口（AMI）

works.title: Attending to Breath
works.description: An immersive virtual environment for focused-attention meditation in which sound and visuals follow the user's breathing, helping them keep attention on the breath.
works.description_zh: 一个用于专注式冥想的沉浸式虚拟环境，声音与画面跟随使用者的呼吸，帮助其把注意力保持在呼吸上。
works.idea_en: Mapping breath directly into sound and image can hold attention on the body from within, and micro-phenomenology can show how that awareness unfolds.
works.idea_zh: 把呼吸直接映射为声音与影像，可以从内部把注意力留在身体上；微观现象学则能揭示这种觉察如何展开。
works.method: A breathing sensor drives a generative soundtrack and visuals in VR; experience studied with micro-phenomenological interviews.
works.method_zh: 呼吸传感器驱动 VR 中的生成式声音与画面；以微观现象学访谈研究体验。

paper.title: Attending to Breath: Exploring How the Cues in a Virtual Environment Guide the Attention to Breath and Shape the Quality of Experience to Support Mindfulness

works.title: Breeze
works.description: A pendant worn around the neck that senses the wearer's breathing and relays it to a partner's pendant as light, vibration or sound; people often breathed along with the feedback to sense what the other felt.
works.description_zh: 一枚挂在颈间的吊坠，感测佩戴者的呼吸，并以光、振动或声音传给伴侣的吊坠；人们常常跟着反馈一起呼吸，以体会对方的感受。
works.idea_en: Sharing breath invites bodily attunement: matching another's breathing is itself a way of understanding their emotion, from the inside.
works.idea_zh: 分享呼吸会引发身体上的调谐：去跟随他人的呼吸，本身就是一种从内部理解对方情绪的方式。
works.method: A wearable pendant measures breathing and renders digital breathing patterns through visual, audio and haptic output; patterns were evaluated for emotional interpretation in a lab study (CHI 2018).
works.method_zh: 可穿戴吊坠测量呼吸，并以视觉、听觉与触觉输出呈现数字化呼吸模式；在实验室研究中评估人们对这些模式的情绪诠释（CHI 2018）。

paper.title: Breeze: Sharing Biofeedback through Wearable Technologies

works.title: Designing with the Body: Somaesthetic Interaction Design
works.description: Höök's book that defines soma design: it tells how she learned Feldenkrais and horseback riding, walks through the Soma Mat, Breathing Light and other cases, and sets out a soma design manifesto, theory and methods.
works.description_zh: Höök 奠定身体设计的专著：讲述她如何学习 Feldenkrais 与骑马，逐一剖析 Soma Mat、Breathing Light 等案例，并提出身体设计宣言、理论与方法。
works.idea_en: Design starts from a body-mind trained to feel more finely; the designer's own soma is the first instrument of design, not an afterthought.
works.idea_zh: 设计始于一个被训练得更敏锐的身心；设计师自己的身体是第一件设计工具，而不是事后才考虑的东西。
works.method: Book (MIT Press, Design Thinking, Design Theory series) combining Shusterman's somaesthetics, first-person design accounts and a catalogue of methods such as estrangement, somatic training and soma-based material exploration.
works.method_zh: 专著（MIT 出版社“设计思维·设计理论”丛书），结合 Shusterman 的身体美学、第一人称设计叙述，以及陌生化、身体训练、以身体探索材料等方法。

paper.title: Designing with the Body: Somaesthetic Interaction Design

works.title_zh: 《用身体设计：身体美学交互设计》

works.title: Ecology of the Brain: The Phenomenology and Biology of the Embodied Mind
works.description: Fuchs argues against 'brain-centrism': the brain is an organ that mediates the relations of a living body with its environment and with others, not the seat of the mind.
works.description_zh: Fuchs 反对“大脑中心主义”：大脑是调节活的身体与环境、与他人之间关系的器官，而不是心智的居所。
works.idea_en: The person, not the brain, feels and thinks; mind is a living body in relation.
works.idea_zh: 感受与思考的是人，而不是大脑；心智是处在关系中的活的身体。
works.method: Phenomenological and biological argument using circular causality, homeostasis, body memory and psychiatric cases.
works.method_zh: 以循环因果、稳态、身体记忆与精神病学案例展开的现象学与生物学论证。

paper.title: Ecology of the Brain: The Phenomenology and Biology of the Embodied Mind

works.title_zh: 大脑的生态学：具身心智的现象学与生物学

works.title: Eingeweide
works.description: Two performers become entangled on stage with an AI-driven facial prosthesis, pulsing out-of-body organs grown from microbial cultures, and animal remains.
works.description_zh: 两位表演者在舞台上与一个由 AI 驱动的面部义体、由微生物培养出的搏动的体外器官以及动物遗骸纠缠在一起。
works.idea_en: The prosthesis learns in real time how to move on the face, so the body must negotiate with it rather than command it; intimacy with a machine is felt as strain and care.
works.idea_zh: 义体在脸上实时学习如何运动，身体只能与它协商而非命令它；与机器的亲密被感受为紧张与照料。
works.method: Adaptive neural networks drive the facial prosthesis while biosensors pick up the performers' muscle sounds, which AI transforms into the score; Pevere's biomaterials leak and crawl on stage.
works.method_zh: 自适应神经网络驱动面部义体，生物传感器采集表演者的肌肉声音，再由 AI 转化为配乐；Pevere 的生物材料在舞台上渗漏、爬行。

works.title: Embracing First-Person Perspectives in Soma-Based Design
works.description: A 22-author paper in which soma designers each describe a first-person design case and together argue that the designer's own felt experience is a legitimate source of design knowledge.
works.description_zh: 22 位身体设计研究者各自讲述一个第一人称设计案例，共同论证设计师自己的身体感受是正当的设计知识来源。
works.idea_en: To design for felt experience, designers must first examine their own; first-person inquiry is disciplined practice, not self-indulgence.
works.idea_zh: 要为被感受的经验而设计，设计师得先审视自己的经验；第一人称探究是有纪律的实践，而非自我沉溺。
works.method: Collective paper that grew out of the CHI 2017 Soma-Based Design Theory workshop, gathering cases from breathing, dance, heat, sound and play.
works.method_zh: 源自 CHI 2017“Soma-Based Design Theory”工作坊的集体论文，汇集呼吸、舞蹈、热、声音与游戏等案例。

paper.title: Embracing First-Person Perspectives in Soma-Based Design

works.title_zh: 在身体设计中拥抱第一人称视角

works.title: Emotional Biosensing: Exploring Critical Alternatives
works.description: A critical study of emotion-sensing products and research that reads their promises against their assumptions, and sketches alternatives in which biosensing supports people's own emotional meaning-making.
works.description_zh: 一篇批判性研究：把情绪传感产品与研究的承诺和其背后的假设对照阅读，并勾勒另一些可能，让生物传感支持人们自己为情绪赋义。
works.idea_en: Emotion is not a hidden state that sensors reveal; designs that return interpretation to the feeling person resist the reduction of the body-mind to a category.
works.idea_zh: 情绪不是等待传感器揭示的隐藏状态；把诠释交还给正在感受的人的设计，才能抵抗把身心化约为一个类别。
works.method: Critical analysis of emotional biosensing technologies, drawing on design research and critical theory (CSCW / PACM HCI 2018).
works.method_zh: 结合设计研究与批判理论，对情绪生物传感技术进行批判性分析（CSCW / PACM HCI 2018）。

paper.title: Emotional Biosensing: Exploring Critical Alternatives

works.title_zh: 情绪生物传感：探索批判性的替代方案

works.title: Experiencing the Body as Play
works.description: Argues that games are moving from using the body as a controller to letting players experience their own body as the play itself, and offers design tactics for it.
works.description_zh: 论证游戏正从“把身体当控制器”走向“让玩家把自己的身体体验为游戏本身”，并给出相应的设计策略。
works.idea_en: Designing for the Leib (the lived body) as well as the Körper (the object body) turns play into a way of feeling oneself.
works.idea_zh: 既为 Leib（活的身体）也为 Körper（作为物体的身体）而设计，游戏就成了感受自己的一种方式。
works.method: Two phenomenological perspectives (Körper and Leib) applied to the lab's and others' bodily games to derive a suite of design tactics.
works.method_zh: 把 Körper 与 Leib 两种现象学视角应用于本实验室及他人的身体游戏，归纳出一套设计策略。

paper.title: Experiencing the Body as Play

works.title: Fusion
works.description: A backpack with a robot head and two robot arms lets a remote operator see from the wearer's shoulders and act with extra arms, or take hold of the wearer's own arms to guide them; two people share one body.
works.description_zh: 一个装有机器人头部和两只机械臂的背包，让远方的操作者从佩戴者肩上观看、用额外的手臂行动，或抓住佩戴者自己的手臂加以引导：两个人共享一个身体。
works.idea_en: When two people inhabit one body, the boundary of 'my' body and 'my' action becomes negotiable, and guidance can be felt directly in the limbs.
works.idea_zh: 当两个人栖居在同一个身体中，“我的”身体与“我的”行动的边界变得可以协商，引导也能直接在肢体上被感受到。
works.method: Wearable robotic head with stereo cameras and two anthropomorphic arms, teleoperated by a remote user in a VR headset with motion tracking.
works.method_zh: 可穿戴机器人头部带立体摄像头与两只拟人机械臂，由佩戴 VR 头显、动作被追踪的远程用户操控。

paper.title: Fusion: Full Body Surrogacy for Collaborative Communication

works.title: HUG
works.description: A soft, cuddly companion with long arms, a beating heart and a speaker that plays the person's favourite music, made for people living with advanced dementia.
works.description_zh: 一个柔软、可以抱着的伙伴，有长长的手臂、会跳动的心脏和能播放主人最爱音乐的扬声器，为晚期失智者而做。
works.idea_en: When words fail, care continues through touch, rhythm and sound; a held heartbeat can calm a body that is anxious.
works.idea_zh: 当语言失效，照护仍可通过触摸、节律与声音继续；被抱着的心跳能让焦虑的身体平静下来。
works.method: Weighted soft body with an embedded vibration heartbeat and music player activated by hugging; co-designed with people with dementia and carers and studied in care settings.
works.method_zh: 带配重的柔软身体，内置振动心跳与音乐播放器，拥抱时启动；与失智者及照护者共同设计，并在照护机构研究。

paper.title: HUG: A Compassionate Approach to Designing for Wellbeing in Dementia Care

works.title: Learning from and with Menstrupedia
works.description: A study of Menstrupedia, an Indian comic and website that teaches girls about periods, and of how young people, parents and teachers use it to talk about a taboo body.
works.description_zh: 研究 Menstrupedia（一套向女孩讲解月经的印度漫画与网站），以及年轻人、家长与教师如何借它谈论一个被视为禁忌的身体。
works.idea_en: Where the menstruating body is hidden, education that is friendly, visual and local is the first technology of care.
works.idea_zh: 在经期身体被隐藏的地方，友好、图像化、在地的教育，是第一种照护技术。
works.method: Qualitative study of Menstrupedia's content and of interviews with its users and creators in India.
works.method_zh: 对 Menstrupedia 的内容以及印度使用者与创作者的访谈进行质性研究。

paper.title: Learning from and with Menstrupedia: Towards Menstrual Health Education in India

works.title_zh: 向 Menstrupedia 学习、与之共学

works.title: Magic Room
works.description: A smart multisensory room where lights, projections, sounds, bubbles and smart objects respond to children's movement and touch, used in therapy for neurodevelopmental conditions.
works.description_zh: 一间智能多感官房间：灯光、投影、声音、泡泡与智能物件回应孩子的动作与触摸，用于神经发育障碍的治疗。
works.idea_en: A responsive room lets each child explore the senses at their own pace; the environment adapts to the body instead of the other way round.
works.idea_zh: 一间会回应的房间让每个孩子按自己的节奏探索感官；是环境去适应身体，而不是反过来。
works.method: Room-scale installation with projections, smart lights, sensors and connected toys, configurable by therapists; deployed in therapy centres and schools.
works.method_zh: 由投影、智能灯、传感器与联网玩具组成的房间尺度装置，可由治疗师配置；部署在治疗中心与学校。

paper.title: Magic Room: A Smart Space for Children with Neurodevelopmental Disorder

works.title: Motion-Sound Mapping through Interaction
works.description: People demonstrate a movement together with a sound they imagine for it; the system learns the relation so they can then play and feel their movement as sound.
works.description_zh: 人们示范一个动作，并配上他们为之想象的声音；系统学习二者的关系，之后人们就能把自己的动作当作声音来演奏和感受。
works.idea_en: Mapping by demonstration lets people design body-sound feedback from their own movement sense instead of programming it.
works.idea_zh: 示范式映射让人们从自己的动作感出发设计身体—声音反馈，而不必编写程序。
works.method: Interactive machine learning (Gaussian mixture and hidden Markov regression) trained on a few demonstrations of paired motion and sound.
works.method_zh: 交互式机器学习（高斯混合与隐马尔可夫回归），用少量动作与声音配对的示范来训练。

paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems
paper.title: Motion-Sound Mapping through Interaction: An Approach to User-Centered Design of Auditory Feedback Using Machine Learning

works.title_zh: 通过交互建立动作—声音映射

works.title: Project Spectra
works.description: A free, open-source voice training app built with an online community of trans people, with exercises, warm-ups, pitch tracking and goals each user sets for their own voice.
works.description_zh: 一款免费开源的嗓音训练应用，与线上跨性别社群一起开发，包括练习、热身、音高追踪，以及由每位使用者为自己的嗓音设定的目标。
works.idea_en: The voice is a felt part of gendered embodiment; training it is somatic practice, and the trainee, not the software, decides what sounds right.
works.idea_zh: 嗓音是被感受的性别化身体的一部分；训练嗓音是一种身体修习，决定什么声音“对”的，是练习者而不是软件。
works.method: Mobile app with real-time pitch tracking and guided exercises, developed through community-based participatory design on Discord and GitHub.
works.method_zh: 带实时音高追踪与引导练习的手机应用，通过 Discord 与 GitHub 上以社群为本的参与式设计开发。

paper.title: Online Community-based Design of Free and Open Source Software for Transgender Voice Training

works.title: Revealing Tensions in Autobiographical Design in HCI
works.description: Reflects on the tensions of autobiographical design — between researcher and participant, private life and publication, genuine need and research agenda — using the authors' own long-term projects.
works.description_zh: 借作者自己的长期项目，反思自传式设计中的张力：研究者与参与者、私人生活与发表、真实需要与研究议程之间。
works.idea_en: Using your own life as data demands care about what you expose and how honestly you report your own body and home.
works.idea_zh: 把自己的生活当作数据，就需要谨慎处理暴露什么，以及如何诚实地报告自己的身体与家。
works.method: Reflective analysis of the authors' autobiographical design projects (with Aubree Ball), structured as five tensions.
works.method_zh: 对作者（与 Aubree Ball）的自传式设计项目进行反思性分析，整理为五种张力。

paper.title: Revealing Tensions in Autobiographical Design in HCI

works.title_zh: 揭示人机交互自传式设计中的张力

works.title: Ripple
works.description: Everyday shirts with thermochromic pinstripes embroidered on the sleeve that shift colour at moments of heightened skin conductance; friends, housemates and couples wore them in daily life.
works.description_zh: 日常穿着的衬衫，袖子上用热致变色线绣出的细条纹会在皮肤电升高时变色；朋友、室友和伴侣把它穿进了日常生活。
works.idea_en: Emotional biosensing raises the question of who has interpretive authority over a feeling, the person or the data; a subtle garment display keeps that authority with the wearer's own felt sense.
works.idea_zh: 情绪生物传感引出一个问题：谁对一种感受拥有诠释权，是人还是数据？一件含蓄显示的衣服把这份诠释权留给了穿着者自己的体感。
works.method: A Bitalino skin conductance sensor feeds an Arduino that heats embroidered conductive thread coated with thermochromic pigment when a spike is detected; a field study with pairs of wearers (CHI 2018).
works.method_zh: Bitalino 皮肤电传感器把数据送入 Arduino，检测到峰值时加热涂有热致变色颜料的刺绣导电线；以成对穿着者进行实地研究（CHI 2018）。

paper.title: Tensions of Data-Driven Reflection: A Case Study of Real-Time Emotional Biosensing

works.title: Sensory Bodystorming for Collocated Physical Training Design
works.description: A bodystorming variant in which trainers and trainees try out sensory props — lights, sounds, vibrations — during real training sessions to imagine technology that supports learning movement together.
works.description_zh: 身体风暴的一种变体：教练与学员在真实训练课中试用光、声、振动等感官道具，想象支持共同学习动作的技术。
works.idea_en: Sensory feedback is best designed inside the shared activity, where trainer and trainee feel each other's movement.
works.idea_zh: 感官反馈最好在共同活动之中设计，在那里教练与学员能感受彼此的动作。
works.method: Workshops in circus and fitness training settings using simple sensory props, analysed for design qualities (with Annika Waern).
works.method_zh: 在马戏与健身训练场景中用简单感官道具开展工作坊，并分析设计品质（与 Annika Waern 合著）。

paper.title: Sensory bodystorming for collocated physical training design

works.title_zh: 面向共处身体训练设计的感官身体风暴

works.title: Synchrony and Social Connection in Immersive Virtual Reality
works.description: Participants in VR move in time with two virtual co-participants whose timing is secretly set to be in or out of sync with them; those in sync feel closer to their virtual partners.
works.description_zh: 参与者在 VR 中与两名虚拟同伴一起按节拍运动，同伴的时间被暗中设定为与其同步或不同步；同步组对虚拟同伴感到更亲近。
works.idea_en: Moving in time with others is itself a source of felt closeness, even when the others are virtual and no shared intention is involved.
works.idea_zh: 与他人同步运动本身就会带来被感受到的亲近，即便对方是虚拟的，也无需共同意图。
works.method: Immersive VR with full-body avatars in a joint movement task; timing of virtual co-participants covertly manipulated; social closeness measured by questionnaire.
works.method_zh: 沉浸式 VR 中以全身化身完成共同动作任务；暗中操控虚拟同伴的时间；以问卷测量社会亲近感。

paper.title: Synchrony and social connection in immersive Virtual Reality

works.title_zh: 沉浸式虚拟现实中的同步与社会联结

works.title: Tai Chi in the Clouds
works.description: Micro drones act as the 'clouds' of the tai chi image 'wave hands like clouds': they lead or follow the practitioner's hands and glow to show how smooth the movement is.
works.description_zh: 微型无人机化身太极意象“云手”中的“云”：它们引领或跟随修习者的双手，并以灯光显示动作是否顺滑。
works.idea_en: Tai chi teaches through metaphor; technology can help a practitioner live the metaphor instead of measuring posture.
works.idea_zh: 太极借由意象来教学；技术可以帮助修习者活出这个意象，而不是去测量姿势。
works.method: Micro UAVs with LEDs, likely tracked in a motion-capture space, lead or follow hand movements and give live light feedback on smoothness.
works.method_zh: 带 LED 的微型无人机（很可能在动作捕捉空间中被追踪）引领或跟随手部动作，并以灯光实时反馈动作的顺滑程度。

paper.title: Tai Chi In The Clouds: Using Micro UAV's To Support Tai Chi Practice

works.title: The Guts Game
works.description: Two players each swallow a temperature-sensing capsule and compete over a day or more to raise or lower their core body temperature on command; the game ends when the capsule leaves one player's body.
works.description_zh: 两名玩家各吞下一粒测温胶囊，在一天或更长时间里按指令升高或降低自己的核心体温来比赛；当胶囊离开某位玩家的身体时，游戏结束。
works.idea_en: The inside of the body can be played with: making core temperature a game goal turns hidden physiology into felt, shared awareness.
works.idea_zh: 身体内部也可以成为游戏对象：把核心体温设为游戏目标，让隐藏的生理过程变成被感受、被分享的觉察。
works.method: Ingestible core-temperature sensor pill transmitting to a phone app with tasks; interview study with 14 players yielding themes of bodily awareness, integration, agency and discomfort (Exertion Games Lab).
works.method_zh: 可吞咽的核心体温传感胶囊把数据传到手机应用，应用发布任务；对 14 名玩家的访谈得出身体觉察、人机融合、能动性与不适感等主题（Exertion Games Lab）。

paper.title: The Guts Game: Towards Designing Ingestible Games

works.title: The Somatic Turn in Human-Computer Interaction
works.description: An interactions article that names HCI's 'somatic turn': designers drawing on somatic practices to treat felt, first-person experience as central to design.
works.description_zh: 《interactions》文章，命名人机交互的“身体转向”：设计师借鉴身体修习，把被感受的第一人称经验放到设计的中心。
works.idea_en: Somatic practices give designers disciplined ways to attend to the body-mind as a whole, which is what makes soma design possible.
works.idea_zh: 身体修习为设计师提供了有纪律的方式，把身心作为整体来关注，这正是身体设计得以成立的前提。
works.method: Short overview essay linking Feldenkrais, Laban, Body-Mind Centering and other somatics to HCI methods.
works.method_zh: 简短的综述文章，把 Feldenkrais、Laban、身心平衡技法（BMC）等身心学与人机交互方法联系起来。

paper.title: The somatic turn in human-computer interaction

works.title: We Live in an Ocean of Air
works.description: A multi-person VR installation around a giant sequoia in which visitors see their own breath leave the body as particles and pass into the tree, and the tree's exhalation return to them.
works.description_zh: 一件围绕巨型红杉的多人 VR 装置：观众看到自己的呼吸化作粒子离开身体、进入树中，树的呼出又回到他们身上。
works.idea_en: Breath is an exchange between bodies and species; making it visible turns breathing into a felt relation with plants.
works.idea_zh: 呼吸是身体之间、物种之间的交换；让它可见，就把呼吸变成与植物之间可被感受的关系。
works.method: Untethered VR with breath and heart-rate sensors; each visitor's breath and pulse are rendered as particles in a shared scene.
works.method_zh: 无线 VR 配合呼吸与心率传感器；每位观众的呼吸与脉搏都在共享场景中被渲染成粒子。
works.title_zh: 我们生活在空气的海洋中

works.title: Wire Costume (Reinterpreting Schlemmer's Triadic Ballet)
works.description: Inspired by Oskar Schlemmer's Bauhaus Triadic Ballet, the Wire Costume restricts the dancer's lower body and turns arm movements into LED 'sparks' and 'waves' on a tutu-like wire skirt.
works.description_zh: 受包豪斯艺术家奥斯卡·施莱默《三元芭蕾》启发，这件金属丝服装限制舞者下半身的动作，把手臂动作变成裙撑般的金属丝裙上的 LED“火花”与“波浪”。
works.idea_en: Restricting and altering the senses creates a new soma to train into; the costume's character is only revealed once it is worn and danced.
works.idea_zh: 限制与改变感官，会造出一个需要重新训练的“新身体”；服装的性格只有在被穿上、被舞动时才显现。
works.method: Motion sensing on the arms drives LED light sequences in a wire costume; designed with cultural research, expert interviews and a dancer's rehearsals (Bauhaus-Universität Weimar with KTH).
works.method_zh: 手臂上的动作感测驱动金属丝服装中的 LED 灯光序列；结合文化史研究、专家访谈与舞者排练设计（魏玛包豪斯大学与 KTH 合作）。

paper.title: Reinterpreting Schlemmer's Triadic Ballet: Interactive Costume for Unthinkable Movements

works.title_zh: 金属丝服装：重新诠释施莱默的《三元芭蕾》

works.title: CuddleBits
works.description: Small, simple robots held in the hands that 'breathe' by expanding and contracting; designers sketch their bodies and their breathing behaviours together to express emotions.
works.description_zh: 握在手中的小而简单的机器人，靠膨胀与收缩来“呼吸”；设计者把它们的身体与呼吸行为放在一起草拟，用来表达情绪。
works.idea_en: A robot's felt emotion comes from the coupling of body and behaviour, so both have to be prototyped at the same time and by feel.
works.idea_zh: 机器人被感受到的情绪来自身体与行为的耦合，因此两者必须同时、凭感觉一起做原型。
works.method: Paper, foam and fur bodies driven by a single servo or voice-coil actuator; behaviours sketched with a custom tool and rated by participants.
works.method_zh: 纸、泡沫和毛皮做成的身体由单个舵机或音圈执行器驱动；用定制工具草拟行为，并由参与者评分。

paper.title: Sketching CuddleBits: Coupled Prototyping of Body and Behaviour for an Affective Robot Pet

works.title: Cultivating Kinaesthetic Awareness through Interaction
works.description: Draws on somatic practices and embodied cognition to propose how interactive systems — here movement sonification — can help people cultivate kinaesthetic awareness.
works.description_zh: 借鉴身体修习与具身认知，提出交互系统——此处为动作声音化——如何帮助人培养动觉觉察。
works.idea_en: Awareness of movement grows through attention practices; interaction can support that growth rather than replace it.
works.idea_zh: 对动作的觉察通过注意力练习而增长；交互可以支持这种增长，而不是取而代之。
works.method: Theoretical synthesis of Feldenkrais-style somatic education and enactive cognition, grounded in a movement-sound design study.
works.method_zh: 综合 Feldenkrais 式身体教育与生成认知理论，以一项动作—声音设计研究为基础。

paper.title: Cultivating kinaesthetic awareness through interaction: Perspectives from somatic practices and embodied cognition

works.title_zh: 通过交互培养动觉觉察

works.title: Data Rituals in Intimate Infrastructures: Crip Time and the Disabled Cyborg Body as an Epistemic Site of Feminist Science
works.description: Forlano writes in the first person about living with an insulin pump and continuous glucose monitor: the alarms, rituals and sleepless nights of a body joined to an automated system.
works.description_zh: Forlano 以第一人称书写与胰岛素泵和连续血糖监测仪共同生活：一个与自动化系统相连的身体所经历的警报、仪式与不眠之夜。
works.idea_en: The actual cyborg body is disabled, tired and caring for its machines; felt experience of living with devices is itself a source of knowledge.
works.idea_zh: 真实的赛博格身体是残障的、疲惫的、需要照料它的机器的；与设备共同生活的切身感受本身就是知识的来源。
works.method: Autoethnographic essay drawing on feminist technoscience and crip theory, based on years of her own device data and routines.
works.method_zh: 借鉴女性主义技术科学与残障（crip）理论的自我民族志文章，基于她自己多年的设备数据与日常。

paper.title: Data Rituals in Intimate Infrastructures: Crip Time and the Disabled Cyborg Body as an Epistemic Site of Feminist Science

works.title_zh: 私密基础设施中的数据仪式：残障时间与作为女性主义科学认知场所的残障赛博格身体

works.title: Designing for Bodily Interplay in Social Exertion Games
works.description: A design dimension for how players' bodies act on one another in exertion games, from parallel play side by side to interdependent pushing, blocking and cooperating.
works.description_zh: 一个设计维度，描述运动游戏中玩家身体如何相互作用：从并排的平行游戏到相互依赖的推挤、阻挡与合作。
works.idea_en: Social exertion is felt between bodies; designers can tune how much bodies meet in physical and virtual space.
works.idea_zh: 社交性的用力发生在身体之间；设计者可以调节身体在物理与虚拟空间中相遇的程度。
works.method: Conceptual framework (parallel vs. interdependent play, across physical and virtual space) derived from the lab's exertion game designs and studies.
works.method_zh: 概念框架（平行与相互依赖的游戏，跨越物理与虚拟空间），源自实验室的运动游戏设计与研究。

paper.title: Designing for Bodily Interplay in Social Exertion Games

works.title_zh: 为社交运动游戏中的身体互动而设计

works.title: Designing for Kinesthetic Awareness
works.description: Studies an interactive movement-sonification system and uses second-person interviews, inspired by micro-phenomenology, to reveal how people's kinesthetic awareness shifts.
works.description_zh: 研究一个动作声音化的交互系统，借鉴微观现象学，用第二人称访谈揭示人们的动觉觉察如何变化。
works.idea_en: Subtle changes in bodily awareness are invisible to logs and surveys; guided second-person inquiry can bring them into words.
works.idea_zh: 身体觉察的细微变化在日志与问卷中看不到；有引导的第二人称询问能把它们带入语言。
works.method: User study with a sonification system and second-person interview protocol, analysed for dimensions of kinesthetic experience.
works.method_zh: 以声音化系统开展用户研究，采用第二人称访谈流程，并分析动觉体验的维度。

paper.title: Designing for Kinesthetic Awareness: Revealing User Experiences through Second-Person Inquiry

works.title: Embodied Design Ideation Methods: Analysing the Power of Estrangement
works.description: Compares embodied ideation methods from three design practices and shows how estrangement — odd props, unusual constraints, unfamiliar ways of moving — opens up new design ideas.
works.description_zh: 比较三种设计实践中的具身构思方法，说明陌生化——古怪的道具、不寻常的限制、陌生的动作方式——如何打开新的设计想法。
works.idea_en: Disturbing how the body usually moves and senses is a reliable way to make designers notice possibilities they would otherwise overlook.
works.idea_zh: 打乱身体惯常的运动与感知方式，是让设计师注意到原本会忽略的可能性的可靠途径。
works.method: Comparative analysis of workshop methods by Wilde, Vallgårda and Tomico, identifying strategies of estrangement.
works.method_zh: 对 Wilde、Vallgårda 与 Tomico 的工作坊方法作比较分析，归纳陌生化策略。

paper.title: Embodied Design Ideation Methods: Analysing the Power of Estrangement

works.title_zh: 具身设计构思方法：剖析陌生化的力量

works.title: HeartChat
works.description: A mobile chat app that attaches the sender's heart rate, sensed by a wearable, to messages, so friends and partners can glimpse each other's bodily state while texting.
works.description_zh: 一款手机聊天应用，把可穿戴设备感测到的发送者心率附在消息上，让朋友和伴侣在聊天时瞥见彼此的身体状态。
works.idea_en: Adding a live body signal to text restores some of the felt presence that written messages lose, supporting empathy as well as raising questions about privacy.
works.idea_zh: 在文字中加入实时的身体信号，能找回书面消息丢失的一部分可感在场，既支持共情，也带来隐私问题。
works.method: Heart rate from a wearable sensor is displayed in the chat interface in several forms; evaluated in a field study with pairs of users (CHI 2017).
works.method_zh: 可穿戴传感器的心率以多种形式显示在聊天界面中；与成对用户进行实地研究评估（CHI 2017）。

paper.title: HeartChat: Heart Rate Augmented Mobile Chat to Support Empathy and Awareness

works.title: How Emotions Are Made
works.description: A book presenting the theory of constructed emotion: emotions are not fixed circuits or universal expressions but are built by the brain from interoceptive sensations, concepts and context.
works.description_zh: 一本阐述情绪建构理论的书：情绪不是固定的神经回路或普遍的面部表情，而是大脑依据内感受、概念与情境建构出来的。
works.idea_en: Every feeling starts from the body's own budget of energy and sensation; emotion is body-mind activity, which undercuts designs that 'detect' emotions as fixed categories.
works.idea_zh: 每一种感受都始于身体自身的能量与感觉预算；情绪是身心的活动，这动摇了把情绪当固定类别去“检测”的设计。
works.method: Synthesis of neuroscience, psychology and anthropology on predictive processing, interoception ('body budgeting') and emotion concepts (Houghton Mifflin Harcourt).
works.method_zh: 综合神经科学、心理学与人类学关于预测加工、内感受（“身体预算”）与情绪概念的研究（Houghton Mifflin Harcourt 出版）。

paper.title: How Emotions Are Made: The Secret Life of the Brain

works.title: Hybrid Body Craft
works.description: A design approach that builds on-skin electronics out of body-decoration traditions, such as gold-leaf metallic tattoos (DuoSkin), colour-changing makeup and machine-embroidered lace worn on the skin.
works.description_zh: 一种设计方法：以身体装饰传统来制作贴肤电子，例如金箔金属纹身（DuoSkin）、变色化妆品以及贴在皮肤上的机绣蕾丝。
works.idea_en: Skin is not a neutral surface for sensors; it carries identity and culture, so technology that joins the body should be designed as adornment people choose to wear.
works.idea_zh: 皮肤不是放置传感器的中性表面，它承载着身份与文化；与身体融合的技术应被设计为人们愿意佩戴的装饰。
works.method: Fabrication with skin-safe materials (gold leaf, temporary tattoo paper, thermochromic pigments, embroidery), co-design with wearers and body-craft practitioners.
works.method_zh: 使用对皮肤安全的材料（金箔、临时纹身纸、热致变色颜料、刺绣）进行制作，并与佩戴者和身体装饰从业者共同设计。

paper.title: Hybrid Body Craft: Toward Culturally and Socially Inclusive Design for On-Skin Interfaces

works.title: Inner Garden
works.description: A sandbox landscape shaped by hand and brought to life with projected water and weather that respond to the person's breathing and heart rhythm, used as a space for mindfulness practice.
works.description_zh: 一个可以用手塑形的沙盘景观，投影出的水与天气会回应人的呼吸与心律，成为练习正念的空间。
works.idea_en: Tending a small world with one's hands and breath turns inner states into something to care for rather than to control.
works.idea_zh: 用手与呼吸照料一个小世界，把内在状态变成需要照顾的东西，而不是需要控制的东西。
works.method: Spatial augmented reality projects onto a physical sandbox tracked by a depth camera; breathing and heart-rate sensors drive the simulated weather and sea; optional VR view for meditation.
works.method_zh: 深度相机追踪实体沙盘，空间增强现实在其上投影；呼吸与心率传感器驱动模拟的天气与海洋；冥想时可切换 VR 视角。

paper.title: Inner Garden: Connecting Inner States to a Mixed Reality Sandbox for Mindfulness

works.title: Life Tree
works.description: A virtual reality game in which slow, deep breaths make a tree grow and bloom; a study examined what makes breathing exercise engaging enough to return to.
works.description_zh: 一款虚拟现实游戏：缓慢而深长的呼吸让一棵树生长、开花；研究探讨什么能让呼吸练习有趣到让人愿意回来。
works.idea_en: Breath practice sticks when it feels like play; slowing the breath becomes a pleasure rather than a prescription.
works.idea_zh: 当呼吸练习感觉像游戏时，它才会被坚持；放慢呼吸成为一种乐趣，而不是一张处方。
works.method: Breath sensed through a chest-worn sensor drives the growth of a tree in a VR scene; field study with players to derive design strategies for breathing games.
works.method_zh: 胸部传感器感知呼吸，驱动 VR 场景中树的生长；与玩家进行实地研究，提炼呼吸游戏的设计策略。

paper.title: Life Tree: Understanding the Design of Breathing Exercise Games

works.title: Malleable Embodiment
works.description: Participants see a virtual body that shows their movement slightly in the past or slightly in the future, predicted by the system, and their sense of the body and their actual movement both change.
works.description_zh: 参与者看到一个虚拟身体，显示的是自己稍早的动作，或由系统预测的稍后的动作；他们对身体的感受和实际动作都随之改变。
works.idea_en: The sense of 'this is my body' can hold a body that is a little ahead of itself, so time as well as space is malleable in embodiment.
works.idea_zh: “这是我的身体”的感受可以容纳一个略微超前于自己的身体：在具身中，时间和空间一样可以被塑形。
works.method: Full-body motion capture with a model that estimates past and future poses, rendered as a deformed avatar; embodiment questionnaires and movement analysis.
works.method_zh: 全身动作捕捉结合估计过去与未来姿态的模型，渲染为变形的化身；使用具身感问卷与动作分析。

paper.title: Malleable Embodiment: Changing Sense of Embodiment by Spatial-Temporal Deformation of Virtual Human Body

works.title: MetaLimbs
works.description: Two robotic arms mounted on the wearer's back are controlled by the wearer's own legs and feet, so that after practice the person uses four arms to hold, reach and solder at once.
works.description_zh: 两条装在穿戴者背后的机械臂由穿戴者自己的腿和脚来控制，经过练习后，人可以用四条手臂同时拿、够、焊接。
works.idea_en: The body schema is plastic: with direct, continuous control, new limbs start to feel like part of one's own body rather than a tool.
works.idea_zh: 身体图式是可塑的：在直接、连续的控制下，新的肢体开始被感受为自己身体的一部分，而不是工具。
works.method: Backpack-mounted robot arms mapped to foot and knee positions tracked by motion sensors, with toe-controlled grippers and haptic feedback at the feet (Keio KMD with Masahiko Inami's lab).
works.method_zh: 背负式机械臂，映射到由运动传感器追踪的脚与膝的位置，脚趾控制夹爪，脚部有触觉反馈（庆应 KMD 与稻见昌彦实验室合作）。

paper.title: MetaLimbs: multiple arms interaction metamorphism

works.title: My Tai-Chi Coaches
works.description: A head-mounted augmented reality tool in which several virtual tai chi coaches surround the learner, so that whichever way the learner turns during the form, a coach is in view to follow.
works.description_zh: 一个头戴式增强现实工具：多个虚拟太极教练围绕在学习者周围，无论学习者在拳架中转向哪个方向，眼前都有一位教练可以跟随。
works.idea_en: Learning a form is learning from many viewpoints; placing the teacher's body around the learner keeps attention on one's own movement instead of on turning to look.
works.idea_zh: 学拳架需要从多个视角学习；把教练的身体安排在学习者四周，能让注意力留在自己的动作上，而不是用在转头观看上。
works.method: Virtual coach avatars rendered in a head-mounted display around the learner's tracked position, likely evaluated with novice tai chi learners at National Taiwan University (Yi-Ping Hung's group).
works.method_zh: 在头戴显示器中，把虚拟教练化身呈现在被追踪的学习者四周，很可能在台湾大学（洪一平团队）与太极初学者一起做了评估。

paper.title: My Tai-Chi coaches: an augmented-learning tool for practicing Tai-Chi Chuan

works.title: Neurocognitive Barriers to the Embodiment of Technology
works.description: A perspective article asking what it would take for a prosthesis or augmentation device to be experienced as part of the body, and what stands in the way in the brain.
works.description_zh: 一篇观点文章，追问要让假体或增强设备被体验为身体的一部分需要什么，以及大脑中存在哪些阻碍。
works.idea_en: Embodiment is not a yes-or-no property of a device; it depends on how the body's sensing, control and self-model take it in, and designers should aim for that felt integration rather than raw function.
works.idea_zh: 具身不是设备“有或没有”的属性，而取决于身体的感知、控制与自我模型如何接纳它；设计者应追求这种被感受到的融合，而不只是功能。
works.method: Review of body-ownership illusions, amputee and prosthesis studies and motor-control research, by Tamar Makin, Frédérique de Vignemont and A. Aldo Faisal.
works.method_zh: 综述身体归属错觉、截肢者与假体研究以及运动控制研究，作者为 Tamar Makin、Frédérique de Vignemont 与 A. Aldo Faisal。

paper.title: Neurocognitive barriers to the embodiment of technology

works.title_zh: 技术具身化的神经认知障碍

works.title: North Sense
works.description: A small silicone device attached to the chest with titanium piercings that gives a short vibration whenever the wearer faces magnetic north.
works.description_zh: 一个用钛制穿刺固定在胸前的小型硅胶装置，每当佩戴者面向磁北时就轻轻振动一下。
works.idea_en: Worn on the skin day and night, a sense of direction becomes part of the felt self rather than an app one checks.
works.idea_zh: 日夜贴在皮肤上，方向感成为被感受的自我的一部分，而不是一个需要查看的应用。
works.method: Compass sensor and vibration motor in a sealed unit, mounted with two surface bars through the skin; the founders published year-long first-person video accounts of living with it.
works.method_zh: 封装的罗盘传感器与振动马达，通过两根穿过皮肤的表面钉固定；创始人发布了佩戴一年后的第一人称影像自述。

works.title: Radical Choreographic Object [RCO]
works.description: A participatory dance performance by Jean-Marc Matos and Sarah Fdili Alaoui in which audience members join dancers in scored, interactive movement.
works.description_zh: Jean-Marc Matos 与 Sarah Fdili Alaoui 的参与式舞蹈表演：观众与舞者一起进入有谱的互动动作。
works.idea_en: A choreographic object can be shared: the audience learns by moving, not by watching.
works.idea_zh: 编舞对象可以被分享：观众通过移动来理解，而不是通过观看。
works.method: Performance with movement scores and interactive media, staged in community venues in the Toulouse area (2017–2018).
works.method_zh: 结合动作谱与互动媒体的表演，在图卢兹地区的社区场所上演（2017–2018）。

paper.title: Radical Choreographic Object [RCO]

works.title: Seeing, Sensing and Recognizing Laban Movement Qualities
works.description: Certified Laban Movement Analysts helped choose sensors and features so that a computer could recognise Effort qualities such as lightness, strength and sustainment.
works.description_zh: 认证的 Laban 动作分析师参与挑选传感器与特征，让计算机能识别轻、强、持续等力效质感。
works.idea_en: Movement experts' embodied knowledge should shape what the machine measures; adding physiological signals captures qualities that position alone misses.
works.idea_zh: 动作专家的具身知识应当决定机器测量什么；加入生理信号能捕捉仅凭位置无法捕捉的质感。
works.method: Multimodal capture (motion capture, accelerometers, EMG) with features designed with LMA experts, evaluated against expert annotations of Laban Efforts.
works.method_zh: 多模态采集（动作捕捉、加速度计、肌电），特征与 LMA 专家共同设计，并以专家对 Laban 力效的标注评估。

paper.title: Seeing, Sensing and Recognizing Laban Movement Qualities

works.title_zh: 看见、感受与识别 Laban 动作质感

works.title: Social Touch Technology: A Survey of Haptic Technology for Social Touch
works.description: A survey of devices that mediate social touch, from hugging shirts to robot pets, read against the psychology and neuroscience of affective touch.
works.description_zh: 一篇综述，梳理从拥抱衬衫到机器宠物等中介社会触碰的装置，并对照情感触碰的心理学与神经科学加以解读。
works.idea_en: Designs for touch at a distance work when they respect what skin evolved to feel: slow, warm, gentle stroking reads as care.
works.idea_zh: 远距离触碰的设计要尊重皮肤演化出来的感受方式：缓慢、温暖、轻柔的抚触才会被读作关怀。
works.method: Literature review organised by touch type, device and study outcome, drawing on C-tactile afferent research.
works.method_zh: 按触碰类型、装置与研究结果组织的文献综述，并借鉴 C 触觉传入纤维研究。

paper.title: Social Touch Technology: A Survey of Haptic Technology for Social Touch

works.title_zh: 社会触碰技术：面向社会触碰的触觉技术综述

works.title: Soma-Based Design Theory
works.description: A CHI 2017 workshop where soma designers moved, touched and discussed together to work out a shared theory of soma-based design; its cases became the 2018 first-person paper.
works.description_zh: CHI 2017 工作坊：身体设计研究者一起动身体、触摸、讨论，尝试形成共同的身体设计理论；其中的案例后来成为 2018 年第一人称论文。
works.idea_en: Theory of soma design is built by doing it together with bodies in the room, not only by reading.
works.idea_zh: 身体设计的理论要靠大家带着身体在场一起做出来，不只靠阅读。
works.method: One-day workshop combining somatic exercises, sharing of first-person design cases and collective writing.
works.method_zh: 一天的工作坊，结合身体练习、第一人称设计案例分享与集体写作。

paper.title: Soma-Based Design Theory

works.title: Supporting Everyday Function in Chronic Pain Using Wearable Technology
works.description: A home study in which people with chronic pain used a movement-sonification wearable during everyday tasks such as cooking and cleaning, not only during exercise.
works.description_zh: 一项居家研究：慢性疼痛者不只在锻炼时，也在做饭、打扫等日常活动中使用动作声音化可穿戴设备。
works.idea_en: Rehabilitation lives in ordinary movement; sensing the body during daily chores helps people pace and trust it where pain actually happens.
works.idea_zh: 康复发生在日常动作里；在做家务时感知身体，帮助人在疼痛真实出现的地方调整节奏、信任身体。
works.method: Wearable sonification device deployed at home with people with chronic pain, studied through interviews and diaries.
works.method_zh: 将声音化可穿戴设备部署到慢性疼痛者家中，通过访谈与日记进行研究。

paper.title: Supporting Everyday Function in Chronic Pain Using Wearable Technology

works.title_zh: 用可穿戴技术支持慢性疼痛者的日常活动

works.title: Tacit Narratives: Surfacing Aesthetic Meaning by Using Wearable Props and Focusing
works.description: Participants wear simple props and follow Focusing steps to bring tacit, bodily meanings of an experience into narrative.
works.description_zh: 参与者穿戴简单的道具，并按照 Focusing 步骤，把一段经验中默会的、身体性的意义讲成叙述。
works.idea_en: Objects on the body can act as handles for felt meanings that are otherwise hard to reach.
works.idea_zh: 身体上的物件可以成为把手，帮助我们触及原本难以触及的被感受的意义。
works.method: Workshop study combining wearable props, guided Focusing and narrative analysis.
works.method_zh: 结合可穿戴道具、引导式 Focusing 与叙事分析的工作坊研究。

paper.title: Tacit Narratives: Surfacing Aesthetic Meaning by Using Wearable Props and Focusing

works.title_zh: 默会叙事：借可穿戴道具与 Focusing 浮现审美意义

works.title: The Third Thumb
works.description: A 3D-printed robotic thumb worn on the side of the hand opposite the natural thumb, moved by pressure sensors under the big toes, so the wearer can hold and manipulate objects with one hand in new ways.
works.description_zh: 一只 3D 打印的机器人拇指，戴在与原生拇指相对的手掌一侧，由大脚趾下的压力传感器控制，让佩戴者用一只手以新的方式握持和操作物体。
works.idea_en: Made as a reframing of prosthetics as extension rather than replacement, the thumb shows how quickly a foot movement can come to feel like a finger movement once the body learns it.
works.idea_zh: 它把假体重新理解为延伸而非替代；一旦身体学会，脚的动作能很快被感受为手指的动作。
works.method: Two wireless force sensors under the toes drive motors that pull cables in the thumb; created as a Royal College of Art graduate project and later used in the Makin lab's neuroscience studies.
works.method_zh: 两个置于脚趾下的无线压力传感器驱动电机拉动拇指内的线缆；最初是皇家艺术学院的毕业作品，后来用于 Makin 实验室的神经科学研究。

works.title: Tree
works.description: In VR you grow from a seed into a rainforest tree, your arms become branches, and you feel wind, heat and vibration until the forest burns.
works.description_zh: 在 VR 中，你从种子长成一棵雨林中的树，手臂成为枝干，感受风、热与振动，直到森林起火。
works.idea_en: Taking on a tree's body and slow life through touch, heat and rumble makes deforestation felt as something happening to a body.
works.idea_zh: 借由触感、热和震动承担一棵树的身体与缓慢的一生，会让森林砍伐被感受为发生在一个身体上的事。
works.method: Room-scale VR with haptic vibration, wind and heat (and likely scent), synchronised to the tree's life stages.
works.method_zh: 房间尺度的 VR，配合触觉振动、风与热（很可能还有气味），与树的生命阶段同步。

works.title: VR Playground
works.description: Riders on a real playground swing wear VR headsets and travel through four virtual worlds, each of which amplifies, reverses or distorts the felt motion of swinging.
works.description_zh: 乘客坐在真实的游乐场秋千上戴着 VR 头显，穿越四个虚拟世界，每个世界都会放大、颠倒或扭曲荡秋千时身体感到的运动。
works.idea_en: Deliberately mismatching what the eyes see and what the inner ear feels can be a source of delight, and a way to make one's own motion strange.
works.idea_zh: 有意让眼睛所见与内耳所感错位，可以带来乐趣，也能让自己的运动变得陌生。
works.method: A sensor on the swing measures its motion and drives four 'abstract machines' that map physical swing to virtual movement; toured to over 5,000 riders.
works.method_zh: 秋千上的传感器测量其运动，驱动四种把实体摆动映射为虚拟运动的“抽象机器”；巡展吸引了五千多名乘客。

paper.title: Abstract Machines: Overlaying Virtual Worlds on Physical Rides

works.title: bioSync
works.description: A pair of wearables that read muscle activity from one person and play it into another person's muscles through electrical stimulation, so that, for example, a therapist can feel a patient's tremor or stiffness in their own arm.
works.description_zh: 一对可穿戴设备：读取一个人的肌肉活动，并通过电刺激传到另一个人的肌肉中；例如治疗师可以在自己的手臂上感受到患者的震颤或僵硬。
works.idea_en: Empathy can be kinesthetic: feeling another's movement in your own muscles gives an understanding that watching cannot.
works.idea_zh: 共情可以是动觉的：在自己的肌肉中感受他人的动作，能获得旁观无法带来的理解。
works.method: Wearable electrodes that switch between EMG sensing and EMS actuation, linking two people bidirectionally in real time.
works.method_zh: 可在肌电感测与肌肉电刺激之间切换的可穿戴电极，实时双向连接两个人。

paper.title: bioSync: A Paired Wearable Device for Blending Kinesthetic Experience

works.title: A Quantified Past
works.description: A study of how self-trackers look back on their old personal data, arguing that tracking is also a way of remembering one's life, not only of monitoring performance.
works.description_zh: 一项研究：考察自我追踪者如何回看旧的个人数据，并主张追踪也是一种回忆自己生活的方式，而不只是监测表现。
works.idea_en: Body data gains meaning when it is tied back to lived experience and memory; design should support reminiscence and ambiguity, not only goals.
works.idea_zh: 身体数据只有与亲历经验和记忆重新联结时才有意义；设计应支持回忆与模糊性，而不只是目标。
works.method: Qualitative interviews with Quantified Self practitioners about revisiting their data, leading to design considerations for remembering (Human-Computer Interaction journal; with David Kirk and Abigail Durrant).
works.method_zh: 对 Quantified Self 实践者回看自身数据进行质性访谈，并提出面向回忆的设计考量（Human-Computer Interaction 期刊；合著者 David Kirk、Abigail Durrant）。

paper.title: A Quantified Past: Toward Design for Remembering With Personal Informatics

works.title: Balance Ninja
works.description: Two players balance on a line while electrodes behind their ears disturb their sense of balance; each player's movements control the vertigo felt by the opponent.
works.description_zh: 两名玩家在一条线上保持平衡，耳后的电极扰乱他们的平衡感；一方的动作控制着对方感受到的眩晕。
works.idea_en: Vertigo makes the usually invisible vestibular sense felt, and can be shaped as a playful, shared experience.
works.idea_zh: 眩晕让通常无形的前庭感被感受到，并且可以被塑造成有趣的共享体验。
works.method: Galvanic vestibular stimulation whose strength is likely driven by the other player's tracked movement; studied with 20 players to derive vertigo-game design strategies.
works.method_zh: 前庭电刺激的强度很可能由另一名玩家被追踪的动作驱动；通过 20 名玩家的研究总结眩晕游戏的设计策略。

paper.title: Balance Ninja: Towards the Design of Digital Vertigo Games via Galvanic Vestibular Stimulation

works.title: Bodystorming for Movement-Based Interaction Design
works.description: Adapts bodystorming to movement-based interaction: participants explore movement, props and early technology together in the actual activity setting.
works.description_zh: 把身体风暴改造用于基于动作的交互设计：参与者在真实活动场景中一起探索动作、道具与早期技术。
works.idea_en: For movement design, the ideas worth keeping are the ones that feel right in the body during the activity itself.
works.idea_zh: 对动作设计来说，值得保留的想法，是在活动本身中身体觉得对的那些。
works.method: Analysis of bodystorming sessions in movement-based design projects (with Asreen Rostami).
works.method_zh: 分析基于动作的设计项目中的身体风暴环节（与 Asreen Rostami 合著）。

paper.title: Bodystorming for movement-based interaction design

works.title_zh: 面向动作交互设计的身体风暴

works.title: Breathing Light
works.description: Breathing Light is a lamp with a curtain of fabric and strings that encloses a person lying beneath it; the light slowly dims in and out with their breathing.
works.description_zh: Breathing Light 是一盏垂着布帘和细绳的灯，把躺在下面的人围成一个“房中之房”；灯光随着这个人的呼吸缓缓明暗。
works.idea_en: Seeing your breath softly reflected in ambient light lets you notice breathing without trying to control it.
works.idea_zh: 看到自己的呼吸被柔和地映在环境光里，人便能察觉呼吸，而不急着去控制它。
works.method: A sensor on the chest measures breathing movement and drives a dimmable lamp inside a fabric and string enclosure; evaluated together with the Soma Mat, and later in a three-month home study.
works.method_zh: 胸前的传感器测量呼吸起伏，驱动布帘与细绳围合内的可调光灯；与 Soma Mat 一起评估，之后又在家庭中进行了三个月的研究。

paper.title: The Soma Mat and Breathing Light

works.title: Choreographic Inscriptions
works.description: A framework for noticing how devices and social norms 'choreograph' everyday movement, described in Laban Effort and Shape terms.
works.description_zh: 一个框架，用来察觉设备与社会规范如何“编排”日常动作，并以 Laban 的力效与形状来描述。
works.idea_en: Technology quietly scripts how we move; naming those scripts in movement-quality terms lets designers choose them.
works.idea_zh: 技术在悄悄编写我们的动作；用动作质感的语言说出这些脚本，设计者才能有意识地选择它们。
works.method: Combines actor-network inscriptions with Laban Movement Analysis, demonstrated on a case study of an affective gesture-based mobile device.
works.method_zh: 把行动者网络理论中的“铭写”与 Laban 动作分析结合，并以一款情感手势移动设备为案例演示。

paper.title: Choreographic Inscriptions: A Framework for Exploring Sociomaterial Influences on Qualities of Movement for HCI

works.title: Corpus Nil
works.description: A performer moves slowly in near darkness while an autonomous system listens to his muscles' electrical and acoustic signals and answers with sound and light.
works.description_zh: 表演者在近乎黑暗中缓慢移动，一个自主系统聆听他肌肉的电信号与声学信号，并以声音和光回应。
works.idea_en: Human and machine form a hybrid body; bodily norms are unsettled when a machine co-shapes how a body moves and sounds.
works.idea_zh: 人与机器构成一个混合的身体；当机器共同塑造身体如何移动和发声时，身体规范被动摇。
works.method: Biophysical sensors (Xth Sense bioacoustic and bioelectric) on the limbs feed machine-learning algorithms that autonomously drive sound and light (premiered at ZKM, 2016).
works.method_zh: 四肢上的生物物理传感器（Xth Sense 生物声学与生物电）输入机器学习算法，由其自主驱动声音与灯光（2016 年于 ZKM 首演）。
exhibited: Prix Ars Electronica 2017, Award of Distinction (Sound Art)

works.title: DANCE: Sonifying Movement Qualities
works.description: Qualities such as lightness, heaviness and fragility in a dancer's movement are analysed live and turned into sound, with the aim that blind and sighted people can 'see' dance through listening.
works.description_zh: 舞者动作中的轻盈、沉重、脆弱等质感被实时分析并转为声音，目标是让盲人与明眼人都能通过聆听“看见”舞蹈。
works.idea_en: Movement qualities can travel between senses: a felt quality in one body can be heard by another.
works.idea_zh: 动作质感可以在感官之间传递：一个身体感受到的质感，可以被另一个人听见。
works.method: EyesWeb-based real-time analysis of motion-capture and inertial data into a multi-layered model of qualities, sonified with designed sound (EU H2020 DANCE project, with choreographer Virgilio Sieni).
works.method_zh: 基于 EyesWeb，把动作捕捉与惯性数据实时分析为多层次的质感模型，再以设计好的声音呈现（欧盟 H2020 DANCE 项目，与编舞 Virgilio Sieni 合作）。

paper.title: The Dancer in the Eye: Towards a Multi-Layered Computational Framework of Qualities in Movement

works.title: DEEP
works.description: A meditative VR world under the sea that you move through only by breathing: slow, deep belly breaths carry you along and change the glowing landscape.
works.description_zh: 一个只能用呼吸移动的海底冥想 VR 世界：缓慢深长的腹式呼吸带着你前行，并改变发光的景观。
works.idea_en: When breath is the only control, the practice of slowing down becomes the game itself, and calm is felt rather than instructed.
works.idea_zh: 当呼吸是唯一的控制方式时，放慢这件修习本身就成了游戏；平静是被感受到的，而不是被指示的。
works.method: A custom stretch-sensor belt around the diaphragm drives movement and visuals in a VR headset; later tested as biofeedback for anxious children.
works.method_zh: 绕在腹部的定制拉伸传感带驱动 VR 头显中的移动与视觉；后来作为焦虑儿童的生物反馈加以检验。

paper.title: DEEP: A Biofeedback Virtual Reality Game for Children At-risk for Anxiety

works.title: Embodied Companion Technologies for Autistic Children
works.description: Smart objects co-designed with autistic children, each built around what that child enjoys and how they move and sense, rather than around deficits to be corrected.
works.description_zh: 与自闭症儿童共同设计的智能物件，每一件都围绕这个孩子喜欢什么、如何移动与感受来打造，而不是围绕需要被矫正的缺陷。
works.idea_en: Designing with autistic children's own sensory pleasures respects their embodied experience instead of normalising it.
works.idea_zh: 与自闭症儿童自己的感官乐趣一起设计，是尊重他们的具身经验，而不是把它“正常化”。
works.method: Participatory design over several months with individual autistic children, producing bespoke sensor-actuator objects; evaluated through the children's own experience.
works.method_zh: 与单个自闭症儿童进行数月的参与式设计，制作定制的传感与执行物件，并以孩子自己的经验来评估。

paper.title: Embodied Companion Technologies for Autistic Children

works.title_zh: 为自闭症儿童设计的具身陪伴技术

works.title: Embodied Sketching
works.description: A family of ideation methods in which designers and users sketch with their moving bodies, props and play in real settings, before any technology exists.
works.description_zh: 一组构思方法：在任何技术出现之前，设计师与用户在真实情境中用运动的身体、道具与游戏来画草图。
works.idea_en: Bodies at play are sketching tools; the felt, social qualities of an activity can be explored before they are engineered.
works.idea_zh: 游戏中的身体就是草图工具；一种活动被感受到的、社会性的品质，可以在工程实现之前就被探索。
works.method: Synthesis of several design projects (games, physiotherapy, dance) using bodystorming, embodied play tests and minimal props.
works.method_zh: 综合多个设计项目（游戏、物理治疗、舞蹈），使用身体风暴、具身游戏测试与极简道具。

paper.title: Embodied Sketching

works.title: Emma Watch
works.description: A wrist-worn device with vibrating motors that reduced the hand tremor of Emma Lawton, a graphic designer with early-onset Parkinson's, enough for her to write and draw straight lines again.
works.description_zh: 一款装有振动马达的腕戴设备，减轻了早发性帕金森病患者、平面设计师 Emma Lawton 的手部震颤，让她重新能够写字和画直线。
works.idea_en: A rhythm felt on the skin can change how a body moves: designing with one person's lived experience produced care that feels like getting one's hand back.
works.idea_zh: 皮肤上感受到的节律可以改变身体的运动：与一个人的亲身经验一同设计，产生的照护就像把自己的手找回来。
works.method: Wrist wearable with an array of vibration motors running a pattern (likely distracting the brain's feedback loop), designed with Emma Lawton for the BBC's Big Life Fix at Microsoft Research.
works.method_zh: 带振动马达阵列的腕戴设备，以某种节律振动（很可能是在干扰大脑的反馈回路），在微软研究院与 Emma Lawton 共同设计，参与 BBC《Big Life Fix》节目。

works.title: EmotionCheck
works.description: A wrist device that lets anxious users feel, through vibration, a heart rate slower than their real one; believing their heart was calm, people reported less anxiety.
works.description_zh: 一款腕上设备，通过振动让焦虑的使用者感到比真实心率更慢的心跳；以为自己的心很平静，人们报告的焦虑就减少了。
works.idea_en: Emotion is partly built from how we read our body: feeling a slower heartbeat can calm us, a reminder that interoceptive feedback is itself persuasive.
works.idea_zh: 情绪部分地由我们如何解读身体建构而成：感到心跳变慢就能让人平静，这也提醒我们，内感受反馈本身就有说服力。
works.method: A wearable renders vibrotactile heartbeats at a false, slower rate; tested in an anxiety-inducing task with physiological and self-report measures (UbiComp 2016).
works.method_zh: 可穿戴设备以虚假的、较慢的速率呈现振动心跳；在诱发焦虑的任务中结合生理与自我报告测量进行测试（UbiComp 2016）。

paper.title: EmotionCheck: Leveraging Bodily Signals and False Feedback to Regulate Our Emotions

works.title: GoatMan
works.description: A designer builds prosthetic legs and an artificial rumen and lives for days with a herd of goats in the Alps, walking on four limbs.
works.description_zh: 一位设计师制作义肢腿和人工瘤胃，在阿尔卑斯山与一群山羊一起生活数日，用四肢行走。
works.idea_en: Trying to live in another species' body shows how deeply thought, mood and worry are tied to one's own posture and gait.
works.idea_zh: 尝试活在另一物种的身体里，会显示出思考、情绪与忧虑与自己的姿态和步态绑得有多紧。
works.method: Prosthetic limbs designed with prosthetists and animal experts, a helmet and an external digestion device; tested in a first-person expedition.
works.method_zh: 与假肢师和动物专家一起设计的义肢、头盔与体外消化装置，在第一人称的远行中检验。

works.title: HCI and Intimate Care as an Agenda for Change in Women's Health
works.description: A study of urinary incontinence from the side of women and of pelvic floor therapists, which argues that HCI has ignored the intimate, leaking, ageing female body and sets out an agenda for designing intimate care.
works.description_zh: 一项从女性与盆底治疗师两方视角出发的尿失禁研究，指出人机交互长期忽视会漏尿、会衰老的女性身体，并提出为私密照护而设计的议程。
works.idea_en: Feeling better starts from knowing and feeling the pelvic floor: designing for women's health means designing against the silence that keeps this part of the body unfelt.
works.idea_zh: 感觉更好，始于认识并感觉到盆底：为女性健康设计，就是对抗让这部分身体无法被感受的沉默。
works.method: Interviews with women and physiotherapists about pelvic floor training, read through feminist HCI to derive knowledge, esteem and agency as design goals.
works.method_zh: 访谈女性与物理治疗师关于盆底训练的经验，以女性主义人机交互解读，提炼出知识、自尊与能动性三项设计目标。

paper.title: HCI and Intimate Care as an Agenda for Change in Women's Health

works.title_zh: 以私密照护推动女性健康变革的人机交互议程

works.title: Hint
works.description: A T-shirt whose screen-printed thermochromic pattern slowly changes colour when the wearer's skin conductance rises; pairs of friends wore it while talking and tried to read what the change meant.
works.description_zh: 一件 T 恤，丝网印刷的热致变色图案会在穿着者皮肤电升高时慢慢变色；两位朋友穿着它交谈，试着读出这些变化意味着什么。
works.idea_en: A body signal worn in public becomes a social cue whose meaning is made together; keeping it ambiguous lets people treat arousal as joy, embarrassment or nothing, instead of a verdict on what they feel.
works.idea_zh: 穿在身上、公开可见的身体信号会变成一种由双方共同赋义的社交线索；保持它的模糊，人们才能把唤醒读成喜悦、尴尬或什么都不是，而不是一纸对感受的裁决。
works.method: A skin conductance sensor and microcontroller detect sudden rises and heat conductive thread under thermochromic ink; studied with pairs of friends in conversation (DIS 2016).
works.method_zh: 皮肤电传感器与微控制器检测突然的升高，并加热热致变色油墨下的导电线；研究以朋友两两对话的方式进行（DIS 2016）。

paper.title: Biosignals as Social Cues: Ambiguity and Emotional Interpretation in Social Displays of Skin Conductance

works.title: Lands of Fog
works.description: A floor-projected world covered in fog that two children, an autistic child and a neurotypical peer, clear by moving together, discovering creatures that invite shared play.
works.description_zh: 一个投影在地面、被雾覆盖的世界，两个孩子（一位自闭症儿童和一位非自闭症同伴）一起走动来驱散雾气，发现邀请他们一起玩的生物。
works.idea_en: Social connection can grow from moving in the same space; the body opens the encounter before words do.
works.idea_zh: 社交联结可以从在同一空间中一起移动生长出来；身体先于语言打开了相遇。
works.method: Full-body interaction on a floor projection tracked by overhead sensors, with a butterfly-net tangible; studied with pairs of children with and without autism.
works.method_zh: 头顶传感器追踪地面投影上的全身交互，配合一个捕蝶网道具；与自闭症与非自闭症儿童组成的搭档一起研究。

paper.title: Lands of Fog: Helping Children with Autism in Social Interaction through a Full-Body Interactive Experience

works.title: Make the Breast Pump Not Suck: A Feminist HCI Approach to Postpartum Technologies
works.description: An account of the Make the Breast Pump Not Suck hackathon at the MIT Media Lab, where parents, designers and clinicians redesigned the breast pump and the postpartum experience around it.
