works.description_zh: 记录 MIT 媒体实验室“让吸奶器不再糟糕”黑客松：父母、设计师与临床人员一起重新设计吸奶器及其周边的产后经验。
works.idea_en: A device clamped to the breast for hours a day is a somatic experience; asking lactating people what it feels like reveals design that had ignored their bodies.
works.idea_zh: 每天在乳房上夹好几个小时的设备，是一种身体经验；去问哺乳者感觉如何，就能看出设计曾怎样忽视哺乳者的身体。
works.method: Hackathon and participatory design with parents and experts, analysed through feminist HCI to reflect on process, inclusion and outcomes.
works.method_zh: 以黑客松与参与式设计联合父母和专家，用女性主义人机交互反思过程、包容性与成果。

paper.title: A Feminist HCI Approach to Designing Postpartum Technologies: "When I first saw a breast pump I was wondering if it was a joke"

works.title_zh: 让吸奶器不再糟糕：以女性主义人机交互设计产后技术

works.title: MotionComposer
works.description: A camera device that turns any movement, from a wave of the arm to a blink, into music, designed so that people with very different abilities can dance and compose together.
works.description_zh: 一台摄像设备，能把从挥臂到眨眼的任何动作变成音乐，专为让能力差异很大的人一起跳舞和作曲而设计。
works.idea_en: When any movement can make music, people with limited mobility can feel their own movement as expressive.
works.idea_zh: 当任何动作都能发出音乐时，行动受限的人也能感到自己的动作是有表现力的。
works.method: Stereo/depth and video tracking with sound environments tuned for small and large movements, developed with therapists and disabled users.
works.method_zh: 立体/深度与视频追踪，配合为细微与大幅动作调校的声音环境，与治疗师和残障使用者共同开发。

works.title: Move to be Moved
works.description: A CHI 2016 workshop where participants learned soma design by moving: somatic exercises, sharing of movement-based design cases and hands-on exploration.
works.description_zh: CHI 2016 工作坊：参与者通过动起来学习身体设计——身体练习、分享基于动作的设计案例、动手探索。
works.idea_en: You cannot learn to design for movement by talking about it; the designer's own body has to be moved.
works.idea_zh: 为动作而设计，靠谈论是学不会的；设计师自己的身体得先被触动。
works.method: Workshop organised by a large group of movement and soma design researchers, alternating movement practice with discussion.
works.method_zh: 由众多动作与身体设计研究者共同组织的工作坊，动作练习与讨论交替进行。

paper.title: Move to be Moved

works.title: Muscle-plotter
works.description: While the user sketches a shape with a pen, electrical muscle stimulation pulls their wrist to draw the output of a simulation, such as the airflow around a car they have just drawn, on the same sheet of paper.
works.description_zh: 用户用笔画出一个形状时，肌肉电刺激拉动他们的手腕，在同一张纸上画出模拟结果，例如刚画好的汽车周围的气流。
works.idea_en: The user's own arm becomes the computer's output device, so results are felt as movements one makes rather than read off a screen.
works.idea_zh: 用户自己的手臂成为计算机的输出设备，结果被感受为自己做出的动作，而不是从屏幕上读到的信息。
works.method: Pen tracked on paper, a simulation computed on a laptop, and EMS electrodes on the forearm driving wrist flexion and extension to plot lines.
works.method_zh: 追踪纸上的笔迹，在笔记本电脑上计算模拟，前臂上的肌肉电刺激电极驱动手腕屈伸来绘制线条。

paper.title: Muscle-plotter: An Interactive System based on Electrical Muscle Stimulation that Produces Spatial Output

works.title: Musically Informed Sonification for Chronic Pain Rehabilitation
works.description: A sonification that plays a musical phrase as a person with chronic pain stretches, resolving at the target point so the listener feels when to stop and when progress was made.
works.description_zh: 一种声音化设计：慢性疼痛者伸展时播放一个乐句，在目标位置落定，让聆听者感到何时该停、何时有了进步。
works.idea_en: Musical expectation is felt in the body; a phrase that wants to resolve can guide movement without the anxiety of numbers.
works.idea_zh: 音乐期待是在身体里被感受的；一个想要落定的乐句，可以在不带来数字焦虑的情况下引导动作。
works.method: Movement sensors drive harmonic musical phrases whose cadence resolves at a set range of motion; tested with people with chronic pain.
works.method_zh: 动作传感器驱动和声乐句，在设定的活动范围处进入终止式；与慢性疼痛者一起测试。

paper.title: Musically Informed Sonification for Chronic Pain Rehabilitation: Facilitating Progress & Avoiding Over-Doing

works.title_zh: 面向慢性疼痛康复的音乐化声音呈现

works.title: Open-Source 3D Clitoris Model
works.description: A free, life-size, 3D-printable model of the whole clitoris, including its internal bulbs and crura, released for schools and sex education.
works.description_zh: 一个免费、等大、可 3D 打印的完整阴蒂模型，包括其内部的球体与脚部，供学校与性教育使用。
works.idea_en: An organ of pleasure that textbooks drew as a dot becomes knowable when it can be held; tactile knowledge corrects a political omission.
works.idea_zh: 一个在教科书中只被画成一个点的愉悦器官，一旦能被握在手里，就变得可知；触觉上的认识纠正了一种政治性的遗漏。
works.method: Anatomically based 3D model released under an open licence for anyone to print; used in French classrooms and exhibitions.
works.method_zh: 依据解剖学制作的 3D 模型，以开放许可发布，任何人都可打印；被用于法国课堂与展览。

works.title: SKIN
works.description: An interactive dance piece in which sensors map the dancers' inner movement and bodily sensations to sound and video on stage; its making was studied through interviews with the team and audience.
works.description_zh: 一部互动舞蹈作品：传感器把舞者的内在动作与身体感受映射为舞台上的声音与影像；创作过程通过对团队和观众的访谈加以研究。
works.idea_en: Integrating technology into dance creates tensions; experience interviews show what 'inner movement' made audible means to dancers and audience.
works.idea_zh: 把技术融入舞蹈会产生张力；经验访谈揭示了让“内在动作”被听见对舞者与观众意味着什么。
works.method: Research-through-practice: iterative cycles of choreography and interaction design with wearable sensing, then micro-phenomenological (explicitation) interviews.
works.method_zh: 以实践为研究：编舞与交互设计反复迭代，配合可穿戴传感，之后进行微观现象学（经验阐明）访谈。

paper.title: Making an Interactive Dance Piece: Tensions in Integrating Technology in Art

works.title: Sarka
works.description: Sarka is a mat that sonifies how a person lying on it distributes their weight and how intensely each part of the body moves, to support inward listening during body-awareness exercises.
works.description_zh: Sarka 是一张会发声的垫子：它把躺在上面的人如何分配体重、各部位动得多强烈转化为声音，帮助人在身体觉察练习中向内聆听。
works.idea_en: Sound feedback can support attention to the body only if it stays quiet enough not to become the thing you listen to.
works.idea_zh: 声音反馈要能支持对身体的注意，前提是它足够安静，不至于喧宾夺主、成为被聆听的对象本身。
works.method: Sensing of weight distribution and movement across zones of the mat (likely pressure sensors) drives an interactive sonification designed through Somaesthetic Appreciation Design.
works.method_zh: 垫子各区域对体重分布和动作的感测（可能是压力传感器）驱动一套交互式声音化系统，按“身体美学鉴赏设计”的方法设计。

paper.title: Sarka: Sonification and Somaesthetic Appreciation Design

works.title: Soma Mat
works.description: The Soma Mat is a padded mat with heating elements beneath its surface; lying on it during a guided body scan, the listener feels warmth appear under the body part the recorded voice names.
works.description_zh: Soma Mat 是一张表面下装有加热元件的软垫；人躺在上面听引导式身体扫描录音，录音念到哪个部位，那个部位下方就慢慢变暖。
works.idea_en: Slow, subtle heat does not signal anything; it quietly draws attention to parts of the body we rarely feel.
works.idea_zh: 缓慢而细微的热并不传递讯息，它只是静静地把注意力引向平时很少感觉到的身体部位。
works.method: Heat pads under a sculpted felt surface are switched in sequence with a Feldenkrais-inspired body-scan recording; the user study examined heat as an aesthetic material (inertia, subtleness, heat transfer).
works.method_zh: 塑形毛毡表面下的加热片随一段受费登奎斯启发的身体扫描录音依次开启；用户研究把热当作审美材料来考察（惯性、细微、热传导）。

paper.title: The Aesthetics of Heat: Guiding Awareness with Thermal Stimuli

works.title: Somaesthetic Appreciation Design
works.description: The CHI paper behind the Soma Mat and Breathing Light that names design qualities for systems of somaesthetic appreciation: subtle guidance, making space and intimate correspondence.
works.description_zh: Soma Mat 与 Breathing Light 背后的 CHI 论文，提出“身体美学鉴赏”系统的设计品质：细微的引导、留出空间与亲密的对应。
works.idea_en: Systems for bodily awareness work when they guide lightly and leave room for the person's own felt sense to lead.
works.idea_zh: 帮助身体觉察的系统，要轻轻引导，并为人自身的身体感受留出主导的空间。
works.method: Research-through-design with Feldenkrais-trained designers, heat and light prototypes, and first-person and user studies.
works.method_zh: 以设计为研究：由受过 Feldenkrais 训练的设计师制作热与光的原型，并结合第一人称与用户研究。

paper.title: Somaesthetic Appreciation Design

works.title: Treehugger: Wawona
works.description: Visitors put their heads into a sculpted tree trunk and see and hear the inside of a giant sequoia, following water as it rises through the tree.
works.description_zh: 观众把头伸进一截雕塑般的树干，看到并听到一棵巨型红杉的内部，跟随水分沿树干上升。
works.idea_en: Hugging a tree, physically and in VR, invites a slower, bodily sense of a life on another timescale.
works.idea_zh: 在实体与 VR 中拥抱一棵树，邀请人以更慢的、身体性的方式感受另一时间尺度上的生命。
works.method: A physical tree-trunk sculpture with embedded VR headset and haptics, using scan data of a giant sequoia turned into a particle visualisation.
works.method_zh: 内嵌 VR 头显与触觉装置的实体树干雕塑，把一棵巨型红杉的扫描数据转为粒子可视化。

works.title: Affordance++
works.description: When a user reaches for an object, muscle stimulation moves their hand to show how to use it: to shake a spray can, or to let go of a hot teapot.
works.description_zh: 当使用者伸手去拿物品时，肌肉电刺激会移动其手部，示范该如何使用：摇一摇喷漆罐，或松开一只滚烫的茶壶。
works.idea_en: An object's use can be communicated through the user's own movement, which raises the question of who is acting when the body moves.
works.idea_zh: 物品的用法可以通过使用者自己的动作来传达；这也提出一个问题：当身体动起来时，是谁在行动。
works.method: Optical tracking detects which object is being reached for and EMS electrodes on the arm trigger the matching hand and wrist movement.
works.method_zh: 光学追踪识别使用者伸手拿的物品，手臂上的肌肉电刺激电极触发相应的手部与手腕动作。

paper.title: Affordance++: Allowing Objects to Communicate Dynamic Use

works.title: As Light as Your Footsteps
works.description: Shoes with microphones pick up the wearer's footsteps and play them back through headphones with the high frequencies raised or lowered; walkers feel lighter or heavier, walk differently and report a changed mood.
works.description_zh: 装有麦克风的鞋拾取穿着者的脚步声，经耳机回放时提高或降低其高频；行走者会感到身体变轻或变重，步态随之改变，情绪也不同了。
works.idea_en: The felt size and weight of the body is not fixed: changing one sound of one's own movement shifts body image, emotion and gait together, showing them as one process.
works.idea_zh: 身体被感受到的大小与重量并非固定：改变自身动作的一种声音，身体意象、情绪与步态会一起变化，说明它们是同一个过程。
works.method: Real-time frequency shifting of footstep sounds captured by shoe-mounted microphones; body-weight estimates, emotion ratings, galvanic skin response and gait were measured (CHI 2015).
works.method_zh: 对鞋上麦克风捕捉的脚步声做实时频移；测量了体重估计、情绪评分、皮肤电与步态（CHI 2015）。

paper.title: As Light as your Footsteps: Altering Walking Sounds to Change Perceived Body Weight, Emotional State and Gait

works.title: CueS
works.description: A wrist-worn device that senses how much a stroke survivor uses the affected arm and gives vibration cues to use it more during everyday life.
works.description_zh: 一款腕戴设备，感知中风幸存者使用受影响手臂的程度，并在日常生活中以振动提示多使用它。
works.idea_en: A gentle touch on the wrist can bring a neglected limb back into awareness; rehabilitation happens between sessions, in the body's daily habits.
works.idea_zh: 手腕上一次轻轻的触碰，能把被忽略的肢体带回觉察；康复发生在治疗之间，发生在身体的日常习惯里。
works.method: Wrist-worn accelerometers measure arm activity and trigger vibrotactile prompts; studied with stroke survivors at home.
works.method_zh: 腕戴加速度计测量手臂活动并触发振动提示；在中风幸存者家中开展研究。

paper.title: CueS: cueing for upper limb rehabilitation in stroke

works.title: Emotions Mediated Through Mid-Air Haptics
works.description: One group of people designed mid-air ultrasound touch patterns on the palm to express emotions such as happy, sad, excited and afraid; two further groups recognised and validated them.
works.description_zh: 一组参与者在掌心设计半空超声触觉图样，用来表达快乐、悲伤、兴奋、害怕等情绪；另两组参与者对其进行识别与验证。
works.idea_en: How a touch feels, where, how fast and how strong, carries emotion in non-arbitrary ways, so felt qualities of touch are a vocabulary for affective design.
works.idea_zh: 触碰的感觉，包括位置、速度与强度，以非任意的方式承载情绪；因此触觉的质感可以成为情感设计的词汇。
works.method: An ultrasonic mid-air haptic array; participants composed haptic descriptions for emotions, which were reviewed and validated by two other groups (CHI 2015).
works.method_zh: 使用超声波半空触觉阵列；参与者为情绪创作触觉描述，再由另两组参与者审阅与验证（CHI 2015）。

paper.title: Emotions Mediated Through Mid-Air Haptics

works.title_zh: 经由半空触觉传递的情绪

works.title: Go-with-the-Flow
works.description: A wearable that turns movement and breathing into sound while people with chronic pain exercise, so they can hear how far they have stretched and when they hold their breath.
works.description_zh: 一款可穿戴设备，在慢性疼痛者锻炼时把动作与呼吸转成声音，让人听见自己伸展了多远、何时屏住了呼吸。
works.idea_en: Sound gives a fearful body a new way to feel itself; hearing movement and breath rebuilds confidence to move, so feeling better starts from feeling more.
works.idea_zh: 声音让一个害怕的身体以新的方式感受自己；听见动作与呼吸能重建活动的信心：感觉更好，始于感觉更多。
works.method: Smartphone-based wearable and Kinect versions track trunk movement and breathing and sonify them within user-defined exercise spaces; studied with people with chronic pain and physiotherapists.
works.method_zh: 基于智能手机的可穿戴版与 Kinect 版追踪躯干动作与呼吸，并在使用者自定的练习范围内声音化；与慢性疼痛者和物理治疗师一起研究。

paper.title: Go-with-the-Flow: Tracking, Analysis and Sonification of Movement and Breathing to Build Confidence in Activity Despite Chronic Pain

works.title: Homuncular Flexibility in Virtual Reality
works.description: In virtual reality people learned to control avatars whose arms and legs were swapped, or who had a third arm moved by wrist rotation, and did so within minutes.
works.description_zh: 在虚拟现实中，参与者学习操控手脚互换、或拥有一只由手腕旋转控制的第三只手臂的化身，并在几分钟内就掌握了。
works.idea_en: Jaron Lanier's idea of 'homuncular flexibility' holds up: the body schema can quickly reorganise around a body plan it never had.
works.idea_zh: Jaron Lanier 提出的“小人灵活性”得到验证：身体图式能很快围绕一个从未拥有过的身体结构重新组织。
works.method: Two VR experiments with motion tracking remapping limbs to avatar parts; performance on a target-hitting task measured over time, by Won, Bailenson, Lee and Lanier.
works.method_zh: 两项使用动作追踪、把肢体重新映射到化身部位的 VR 实验，测量击打目标任务的表现随时间的变化；作者为 Won、Bailenson、Lee 与 Lanier。

paper.title: Homuncular Flexibility in Virtual Reality

works.title_zh: 虚拟现实中的小人灵活性

works.title: Huang Yi & KUKA
works.description: Huang Yi dances a duet with an industrial KUKA robot arm that he programmed himself, mirroring and answering its movements; a light on the arm's tip draws lines across his body.
works.description_zh: 黄翊与一台由他亲自编程的 KUKA 工业机械臂共舞，模仿并回应它的动作；机械臂末端的灯光在他身上划出线条。
works.idea_en: Partnering a machine depends on timing and attention more than on sensing: the dancer's own attunement makes the robot feel like a partner.
works.idea_zh: 与机器搭档更依赖时机与专注，而不是传感：舞者自身的调谐让机器人感觉像一位舞伴。
works.method: Choreography keyframed by hand, pose by pose, into the robot's controller over many hours, then performed live with dancers.
works.method_zh: 编舞者花费大量时间逐个姿势手动为机器人控制器设定关键帧，再与舞者现场演出。

works.title: Impacto
works.description: A small armband makes a virtual punch or ball hit feel real: a solenoid taps the skin while muscle stimulation jerks the arm backwards, splitting the impact into touch and force.
works.description_zh: 一个小臂带让虚拟的拳击或球击感觉真实：电磁铁敲击皮肤，同时肌肉电刺激让手臂向后一震，把冲击拆分为触感与力感。
works.idea_en: Felt impact is two sensations the body puts together; supplying each through the body's own channels is enough to make it believable without heavy machines.
works.idea_zh: 被感受到的冲击是身体组合起来的两种感觉；分别通过身体自身的通道提供它们，就足以令人信服，无需笨重的机器。
works.method: A solenoid tapper for the tactile part and EMS on the biceps or triceps for the kinesthetic part, tested in VR boxing and baseball.
works.method_zh: 电磁敲击器提供触觉部分，二头肌或三头肌上的肌肉电刺激提供动觉部分，在 VR 拳击与棒球中测试。

paper.title: Impacto: Simulating Physical Impact by Combining Tactile Stimulation with Electrical Muscle Stimulation

works.title: In the Eyes of the Animal
works.description: Visitors in a forest wear headsets and a vibrating backpack and see the same forest through the senses of a mosquito, a dragonfly, a frog and an owl.
works.description_zh: 观众在森林里戴上头显和会振动的背包，透过蚊子、蜻蜓、青蛙和猫头鹰的感官看同一片森林。
works.idea_en: Borrowing another species' senses unsettles the human body as the default measure of perception.
works.idea_zh: 借用另一物种的感官，会动摇“人类身体是感知默认尺度”的想法。
works.method: LiDAR and CT scans of the forest rendered as particle worlds in VR, with a binaural soundtrack and a subwoofer backpack delivering vibration to the body.
works.method_zh: 把森林的激光雷达与 CT 扫描数据渲染成 VR 中的粒子世界，配合双耳声轨与把振动传到身体的低音背包。

works.title: JackIn Head
works.description: A person wears an omnidirectional camera on their head, and remote viewers 'jack in' to their surroundings in VR, looking around freely while riding along with the wearer's body.
works.description_zh: 一个人头戴全景摄像头，远方的观看者在 VR 中“接入”其周围环境，随着佩戴者的身体移动，同时自由环顾。
works.idea_en: Sharing a body's viewpoint without sharing its gaze creates a strange in-between presence, half inside another person and half free.
works.idea_zh: 共享一个身体的视点却不共享其目光，会产生一种奇特的中间状态：一半在他人之中，一半自由。
works.method: Head-worn omnidirectional cameras with image stabilisation that decouples the viewer's view from the wearer's head motion, reducing motion sickness; streamed to remote HMD users.
works.method_zh: 头戴全景摄像头配合图像稳定算法，使观看者的视角与佩戴者的头部运动解耦以减少晕动，并实时传输给远程头显用户。

paper.title: JackIn Head: Immersive Visual Telepresence System with Omnidirectional Wearable Camera

works.title: Knowing Your Own Heart
works.description: A study showing that how accurately people detect their heartbeat, how well they believe they sense their body, and how well their confidence tracks their accuracy are three separate abilities.
works.description_zh: 一项研究表明：人们感知心跳的准确度、自认为感知身体的能力，以及信心与准确度是否相符，是三种彼此独立的能力。
works.idea_en: Feeling the body well is not one thing: a design that trains or displays interoception should say whether it addresses accuracy, belief or the awareness between them.
works.idea_zh: “感受身体”并非一件事：训练或呈现内感受的设计，应说明它针对的是准确度、自我信念，还是二者之间的觉知。
works.method: Heartbeat tracking and discrimination tasks, confidence ratings and questionnaires with 80 participants (Biological Psychology, 2015; with Anil Seth, Hugo Critchley and others).
works.method_zh: 在 80 名参与者中进行心跳追踪与辨别任务、信心评分与问卷（Biological Psychology，2015；合作者包括 Anil Seth、Hugo Critchley 等）。

paper.title: Knowing your own heart: Distinguishing interoceptive accuracy from interoceptive awareness

works.title: Labella
works.description: A pair of marked underwear and a smartphone app: the woman points the phone at her own body and sees an augmented view of the vulva, then learns anatomy and pelvic floor exercises through it.
works.description_zh: 一条印有标记的内裤加一款手机应用：女性把手机对准自己的身体，看到外阴的增强影像，再借此学习解剖结构与盆底练习。
works.idea_en: Looking at one's own genitals through a playful interface turns a taboo into first-person bodily knowledge, from the 'very basics' to how the pelvic muscles feel when they work.
works.idea_zh: 透过一个好玩的界面看自己的生殖器，把禁忌变成第一人称的身体知识，从“最基本的认识”到感受盆底肌如何发力。
works.method: Fiducial markers printed on underwear let a phone camera overlay 3D anatomy models on the body; the app guides identification of body parts and pelvic floor exercises; evaluated with women at home.
works.method_zh: 内裤上的标记让手机摄像头在身体上叠加 3D 解剖模型；应用引导辨认身体部位并做盆底练习；在女性家中进行评估。

paper.title: On Looking at the Vagina through Labella

works.title: Nebula
works.description: Nebula is a heavy studded cloak that turns both intentional gestures and the incidental swing of its folds into sound, so the wearer hears how they move.
works.description_zh: Nebula 是一件缀满铆钉的厚重斗篷，它把有意的手势和褶皱无意的摆动都转化为声音，让穿着者听见自己的动作。
works.idea_en: A garment's drape can itself be the interface: implicit movement, not commands, carries the expression.
works.idea_zh: 衣物的垂坠本身就可以是界面：承载表达的是不经意的动作，而不是指令。
works.method: Metal studs act as a sensing material and visual feature in a draped heavy fabric; a sound design exploits the garment's material qualities (with sound researcher Ludvig Elblaus at KTH).
works.method_zh: 金属铆钉在厚重垂坠的布料中既是感测材料，也是视觉元素；声音设计利用了衣物的材料特性（与 KTH 的声音研究者 Ludvig Elblaus 合作）。

paper.title: A Wearable Nebula: Material Investigations of Implicit Interaction

works.title: Proprioceptive Interaction
works.description: Electrical muscle stimulation tilts the user's wrist in response to a device's state, so information is felt through one's own posture and muscles rather than seen on a screen.
works.description_zh: 肌肉电刺激按设备的状态让使用者的手腕倾斜，信息通过自身的姿态与肌肉被感受，而不是在屏幕上被看到。
works.idea_en: Proprioception can be an output channel: a computer can speak to you by gently moving your own body.
works.idea_zh: 本体感可以成为输出通道：计算机可以通过轻轻移动你自己的身体来“说话”。
works.method: EMS electrodes on the forearm actuate wrist muscles against the user's own movement; users read values by feeling the resulting force and position.
works.method_zh: 前臂上的肌肉电刺激电极驱动手腕肌肉与使用者自身的动作相抗，使用者通过感受由此产生的力与位置读出数值。

paper.title: Proprioceptive Interaction

works.title: Seven Principles to Design for Embodied Sensemaking
works.description: Seven principles for designing systems that support sensemaking through the body, grounded in enactive cognition rather than information processing.
works.description_zh: 七条设计原则，用于支持“通过身体理解意义”的系统，立足于生成认知而非信息加工。
works.idea_en: People make sense of the world by moving in it; design should support that bodily sensemaking, not bypass it.
works.idea_zh: 人通过在世界中运动来理解世界；设计应支持这种身体性的意义建构，而不是绕过它。
works.method: Principles derived from enactivism and phenomenology and illustrated with TU/e design projects (with Jelle van Dijk).
works.method_zh: 从生成主义与现象学中提炼原则，并以埃因霍温理工大学的设计项目为例（与 Jelle van Dijk 合著）。

paper.title: Seven Principles to Design for Embodied Sensemaking

works.title_zh: 为具身意义建构而设计的七条原则

works.title: Somaesthetic Design
works.description: An interactions cover story that introduced somaesthetic design to a broad HCI audience, using the Soma Mat, heat and breath-driven light as examples of technology that turns attention inward.
works.description_zh: 《interactions》杂志封面文章，向广大人机交互读者介绍身体美学设计，以 Soma Mat、热感与呼吸驱动的灯光为例，说明技术如何把注意力引向身体内部。
works.idea_en: Technology can be designed to slow us down and help us feel our own body-mind more richly, instead of pulling attention outward.
works.idea_zh: 技术可以被设计成让我们慢下来、更丰富地感受自己的身心，而不是把注意力拉向外部。
works.method: Magazine essay drawing on Feldenkrais-inspired design workshops and prototypes built in Höök's group.
works.method_zh: 杂志文章，取材于 Höök 团队受 Feldenkrais 启发的设计工作坊与原型。

paper.title: Somaesthetic design

works.title: Superhuman Sports
works.description: A movement, and a Japanese society founded in 2015, that designs new sports around human augmentation, such as bouncing in bubble suits on spring stilts, so that people of different ages and abilities can play together.
works.description_zh: 一场运动，以及 2015 年在日本成立的协会：围绕人类增强设计新的体育项目，例如穿着气泡服踩弹簧高跷弹跳，让不同年龄与能力的人能一起玩。
works.idea_en: If augmentation can level differences between bodies, sport becomes a way to explore what an extended body feels like in play rather than to rank bodies.
works.idea_zh: 如果增强能拉平身体之间的差异，体育就可以成为在游戏中探索延展身体感受的方式，而不是给身体排名。
works.method: Sports designed in hackathons and competitions with wearable devices, AR and robotics; the 2017 IEEE Pervasive Computing article sets out the research agenda.
works.method_zh: 通过黑客松与比赛，结合可穿戴设备、增强现实与机器人设计体育项目；2017 年发表于 IEEE Pervasive Computing 的文章阐述了研究议程。

paper.title: Superhuman Sports: Applying Human Augmentation to Physical Exercise

works.title: Tovertafel
works.description: A ceiling-mounted projector that throws interactive light games onto a care-home table: residents with dementia sweep leaves, catch fish or bat a ball of light with their hands.
works.description_zh: 一台装在天花板上的投影仪，把互动光影游戏投在养老院的桌面上：失智居民用手扫落叶、抓鱼、拍打光球。
works.idea_en: Play invites apathetic bodies to reach and touch again; activation comes through the hands and shared laughter, not instructions.
works.idea_zh: 游戏邀请陷入淡漠的身体重新伸手与触碰；激活来自双手与共同的笑声，而不是指令。
works.method: Projector with infrared sensors above a table detects hand and arm movements and updates the projected games; developed from a TU Delft PhD with people with dementia.
works.method_zh: 桌子上方的投影仪配红外传感器，检测手与手臂的动作并更新投影游戏；源自代尔夫特理工大学一项与失智者合作的博士研究。

works.title: Understanding Gesture Expressivity through Muscle Sensing
works.description: Performers repeat gestures with different expressive intentions while EMG and motion are recorded; the muscle signal captures variation in effort that motion data misses.
works.description_zh: 表演者以不同的表达意图重复手势，同时记录肌电与运动数据；肌肉信号捕捉到运动数据遗漏的发力变化。
works.idea_en: Expressivity is felt from inside as effort and tension; sensing the muscles gets closer to what the mover feels than tracking the limb.
works.idea_zh: 表现力是从内部被感受到的发力与张力；感知肌肉比追踪肢体更接近运动者自己的感受。
works.method: Combined EMG and accelerometer recordings of repeated gestures, analysed with machine learning for expressive variation; collaboration with Marco Donnarumma and Atau Tanaka.
works.method_zh: 对重复手势同时记录肌电与加速度数据，并用机器学习分析表达上的变化；与 Marco Donnarumma、Atau Tanaka 合作。

paper.title: Understanding Gesture Expressivity through Muscle Sensing

works.title_zh: 以肌肉传感理解手势表现力

works.title: VEST and Neosensory Buzz
works.description: A vest, and later a wristband, that turns sound into patterns of vibration on the skin, so deaf people can learn to feel speech and environmental sounds.
works.description_zh: 一件背心（后来是一只腕带），把声音转换为皮肤上的振动图案，让聋人学会“感受”语音和环境声音。
works.idea_en: The skin can carry a new stream of meaning if the body lives with it long enough; the brain does not care which door the signal comes through.
works.idea_zh: 只要身体与之共处得足够久，皮肤就能承载一条新的意义之流；大脑并不在意信号从哪扇门进来。
works.method: Microphone audio split into frequency bands mapped to 32 vibration motors on the torso (VEST) or four on the wrist (Buzz), worn daily for weeks of training.
works.method_zh: 麦克风音频被分成频带，映射到躯干上的 32 个振动马达（VEST）或手腕上的 4 个（Buzz），需每日佩戴数周进行训练。

paper.title: Using space and time to encode vibrotactile information: toward an estimate of the skin's achievable throughput

works.title: doppel
works.description: A wristband that taps a heartbeat-like rhythm on the inside of the wrist; a slow rhythm is meant to calm and a faster one to energise, without displaying any data.
works.description_zh: 一只在手腕内侧敲出类似心跳节律的腕带；慢节律用于平静，快节律用于提神，不显示任何数据。
works.idea_en: Rather than measuring the body and telling us about it, technology can speak to the body in its own rhythms and let it respond.
works.idea_zh: 技术不必测量身体再向我们报告，它可以用身体自己的节律对身体说话，让身体自己回应。
works.method: A vibrotactile actuator produces heartbeat-like pulses at a chosen tempo; a controlled study found lower skin conductance and anxiety before public speaking (Scientific Reports, 2017).
works.method_zh: 振动触觉执行器以设定的速度产生类似心跳的脉动；对照研究发现，演讲前佩戴者的皮肤电反应与焦虑更低（Scientific Reports，2017）。

paper.title: The calming effect of a new wearable device during the anticipation of public speech

works.title: Being the Machine
works.description: A portable system projects a 3D printer's toolpath as a laser point, and the person follows it by hand with found materials, becoming the printer.
works.description_zh: 一个便携系统把 3D 打印机的路径投射成激光点，人用手拿着随手找到的材料跟着它走，自己成了打印机。
works.idea_en: Performing a machine's motions with one's own hands makes both the machine and one's bodily skill strange, and puts control back in negotiation.
works.idea_zh: 用自己的手去执行机器的动作，会让机器和自己的身体技能都变得陌生，也让“谁在控制”重新变成协商。
works.method: A laser guide driven by G-code shows the next point to 'print'; participants chose when to follow or deviate, studied in field sessions.
works.method_zh: 由 G 代码驱动的激光引导显示下一个要“打印”的点；参与者自行决定何时跟随、何时偏离，并在实地环节中研究。

paper.title: Being the Machine: Reconfiguring Agency and Control in Hybrid Fabrication

works.title: Birdly
works.description: You lie face down on a machine, spread your arms as wings and fly as a bird over a city; flapping, tilting and a fan-driven headwind make the flight felt through the whole body.
works.description_zh: 你俯卧在一台机器上，张开手臂作翅膀，化身为鸟飞过城市；拍动、倾斜和风扇吹来的迎面风让飞行被全身感受到。
works.idea_en: Becoming another creature starts with posture: lying prone with arms as wings is what makes the flight felt.
works.idea_zh: 成为另一种生物，要从姿态开始：俯卧、以臂为翼，才让飞翔被身体感受到。
works.method: A motorised platform responds to arm flapping and body tilt, with a VR headset, a fan for headwind and spatial sound.
works.method_zh: 电动平台回应手臂的拍动与身体的倾斜，配合 VR 头显、提供迎面风的风扇与空间声音。

paper.title: Birdly an attempt to fly

works.title: Bounden
works.description: A two-player game on one phone: both players hold an end of the phone and follow a path on a sphere, which turns them into a couple dancing around each other.
works.description_zh: 一款两人共用一部手机的游戏：两人各握手机一端，沿着球面上的路径转动，于是彼此围绕着跳起舞来。
works.idea_en: A shared object held by two hands can choreograph bodies into closeness, so the game designs the dance rather than the screen.
works.idea_zh: 两只手共同握着的物件可以把身体编排成亲近的姿态；这款游戏设计的是舞蹈，而不是屏幕。
works.method: The phone's gyroscope tracks rotation along choreographies developed with the Dutch National Ballet.
works.method_zh: 手机陀螺仪追踪沿编舞路径的旋转，编舞与荷兰国家芭蕾舞团合作完成。

works.title: Crafting the Body-Tool
works.description: A body-centred perspective on wearables in which the body and the worn object are crafted together as one 'body-tool' through felt exploration.
works.description_zh: 一种以身体为中心的可穿戴视角：身体与穿戴物在亲身探索中被一起“打造”为一个“身体—工具”。
works.idea_en: A wearable is not added to the body; it becomes part of how the body feels itself.
works.idea_zh: 可穿戴物不是加在身体上的东西；它成为身体感受自己的一部分。
works.method: Design study with wearable props and somatic exploration, drawing on phenomenology and somaesthetics.
works.method_zh: 借助可穿戴道具与身体探索开展的设计研究，理论上取自现象学与身体美学。

paper.title: Crafting the body-tool: a body-centred perspective on wearable technology

works.title: Frebble
works.description: A palm-sized device you hold like a hand: squeezing it makes the partner's Frebble press against the back of their hand, so two people can hold hands during a call or a film.
works.description_zh: 一个手掌大小、像手一样握着的装置：捏一下，对方的 Frebble 就压向其手背，让两个人在通话或看电影时“牵着手”。
works.idea_en: Holding hands is a small, continuous touch; a mediated version can change how shared moments feel even at a distance.
works.idea_zh: 牵手是一种细微而持续的触碰；即便隔着距离，它的中介版本也能改变共度时刻的感受。
works.method: Pressure sensors and vibration actuators in a hand-shaped shell, linked over the internet; TNO tested it during a remotely shared sad film.
works.method_zh: 手形外壳中装有压力传感器与振动执行器，经互联网相连；TNO 在双方远程共看悲伤影片的实验中对其进行了检验。

paper.title: Effects of mediated social touch on affective experiences and trust

works.title: Intimate Care: eTextiles for Pelvic Fitness
works.description: Soft e-textile prototypes worn close to the body that help women locate and feel the pelvic floor muscles and learn to contract them correctly.
works.description_zh: 贴身穿戴的柔性电子织物原型，帮助女性找到、感受盆底肌，并学会正确收缩。
works.idea_en: A muscle most people cannot see or name becomes trainable once a soft material gives it a felt, readable response.
works.idea_zh: 一块大多数人看不见、叫不出名字的肌肉，一旦有柔软材料给出可感、可读的回应，就能被训练。
works.method: Textile sensors and conductive fabric worn against the perineum pick up pelvic floor contraction and give feedback during training (early design exploration).
works.method_zh: 贴近会阴的织物传感器与导电面料检测盆底收缩，在训练时提供反馈（早期设计探索）。

paper.title: Intimate care: exploring eTextiles for teaching female pelvic fitness

works.title_zh: 私密照护：用于盆底锻炼的电子织物

works.title: Motivating People with Chronic Pain to Do Physical Activity
works.description: Interviews with people living with chronic pain and with physiotherapists about why moving is hard, which found that fear, anxiety and lost trust in the body, not lack of information, hold people back.
works.description_zh: 访谈慢性疼痛者与物理治疗师，了解为什么活动变得困难；结论是：阻碍人的不是信息不足，而是恐惧、焦虑与对身体失去信任。
works.idea_en: Pain is a felt state of body and mind together; technology for rehabilitation should rebuild trust in the moving body rather than count steps.
works.idea_zh: 疼痛是身与心一起被感受的状态；康复技术应该重建对运动中身体的信任，而不是去数步数。
works.method: Qualitative interviews and focus groups with people with chronic pain and clinicians, leading to design opportunities for affect-aware activity support.
works.method_zh: 对慢性疼痛者与临床人员进行质性访谈与焦点小组，提出关注情感的活动支持设计机会。

paper.title: Motivating people with chronic pain to do physical activity: opportunities for technology design

works.title_zh: 激励慢性疼痛者进行身体活动

works.title: Movement-Based Game Guidelines
works.description: Ten design guidelines for movement games, drawn from expert designers, such as 'celebrate movement articulation' and 'embrace ambiguity' in sensing.
works.description_zh: 从专家设计师经验中总结的十条动作游戏设计准则，例如“赞美动作的表达”“拥抱传感中的模糊性”。
works.idea_en: Good movement games are designed for how movement feels and looks to others, not for sensing accuracy.
works.idea_zh: 好的动作游戏是为动作的感受以及它在他人眼中的样子而设计的，而不是为传感精度而设计。
works.method: Guidelines derived from interviews and workshops with movement-game designers and prior work, organised by movement requirements, feedback and social aspects.
works.method_zh: 准则来自对动作游戏设计师的访谈、工作坊与既有研究，按动作要求、反馈与社交方面组织。

paper.title: Movement-based game guidelines

works.title: Practicing Somaesthetics
works.description: Design students did somaesthetic awareness exercises before ideating interactive products, and the study compared their ideas with those produced without the practice.
works.description_zh: 设计学生在构思交互产品之前先做身体美学觉察练习，研究比较了有无这些练习时产生的想法。
works.idea_en: Training the designer's own body awareness before ideation shifts ideas toward bodily experience: somatic practice is a design tool.
works.idea_zh: 在构思前训练设计者自身的身体觉察，会让想法更关注身体经验：身体修习本身就是设计工具。
works.method: Workshop study (likely comparing practice and control conditions) with somaesthetic exercises drawn from Shusterman's pragmatic somaesthetics, followed by ideation and analysis of the resulting concepts.
works.method_zh: 工作坊研究（很可能比较有练习与无练习两种条件），练习取自 Shusterman 的实用身体美学，随后进行构思并分析所得概念。

paper.title: Practicing somaesthetics: exploring its impact on interactive product design ideation

works.title: Prototype
works.description: A music film in which Viktoria Modesta performs with a series of designed prosthetic legs, including a spike, presenting the amputee body as powerful and stylish.
works.description_zh: 一部音乐影片，Viktoria Modesta 穿戴一系列设计过的义肢（包括一根尖锥形义肢）表演，把截肢的身体呈现为有力而时尚的。
works.idea_en: A prosthesis can be felt and shown as part of one's expressive body, not as a hidden replacement for a missing part.
works.idea_zh: 义肢可以被感受、被展示为自我表达身体的一部分，而不是对缺失部位的隐藏替代。
works.method: Music video directed by Saam Farahmand for Channel 4, with prosthetic legs designed with Sophie de Oliveira Barata (The Alternative Limb Project).
works.method_zh: 由 Saam Farahmand 为英国第四频道执导的音乐影片，义肢与 Sophie de Oliveira Barata（The Alternative Limb Project）合作设计。

works.title: SensoryPaint
works.description: A large projected canvas where children with neurodevelopmental conditions paint by moving textured balls and their own bodies, turning sensory therapy into play.
works.description_zh: 一面巨大的投影画布，神经发育障碍儿童通过移动不同触感的球和自己的身体来作画，把感统治疗变成游戏。
works.idea_en: Sensory integration works best when it feels like play; the whole body becomes the brush.
works.idea_zh: 感觉统合在感觉像游戏时效果最好；整个身体都成了画笔。
works.method: Depth camera tracks balls of different textures and body movement in front of a projection; colour and sound respond; studied in a sensory therapy setting.
works.method_zh: 深度相机追踪不同质地的球与身体动作，投影中的颜色与声音随之回应；在感统治疗环境中研究。

paper.title: SensoryPaint: a multimodal sensory intervention for children with neurodevelopmental disorders

works.title: Teegi
works.description: A small tangible character on whose head a person's own EEG activity is projected in real time; by handling and turning it, novices explore what their brain is doing as they move, close their eyes or relax.
works.description_zh: 一个小巧的实体人偶，头上实时投射出使用者自己的脑电活动；新手通过拿起、转动它，探索自己在动作、闭眼或放松时大脑在做什么。
works.idea_en: Turning an abstract brain signal into a figure one can hold makes one's own inner activity approachable and felt, rather than a chart to be decoded.
works.idea_zh: 把抽象的脑信号变成可以握在手中的形象，让自身的内在活动变得亲近、可感，而不是一张有待解码的图表。
works.method: EEG headset signals are processed in real time and projected onto a tracked figurine with spatial augmented reality; an exploratory study with novice users (UIST 2014).
works.method_zh: 脑电头戴设备的信号经实时处理，通过空间增强现实投射到被追踪的人偶上；与新手用户进行探索性研究（UIST 2014）。

paper.title: Teegi: Tangible EEG Interface

works.title: The Body Keeps the Score
works.description: Van der Kolk describes how trauma changes brain and body, including interoception and heart rate variability, and reviews treatments from EMDR and neurofeedback to yoga and theatre.
works.description_zh: 范德考克描述创伤如何改变大脑与身体，包括内感受与心率变异性，并综述了从 EMDR、神经反馈到瑜伽与戏剧的疗法。
works.idea_en: The book brought the idea that recovery must go through the body to a mass audience; some of its neuroscience claims are contested, so designers should read it as a framing rather than as evidence.
works.idea_zh: 此书把“康复必须经由身体”的观点带给大众；其中部分神经科学主张存在争议，设计者应把它当作一种框架而非证据来读。
works.method: Clinical narrative and research review on trauma, interoception and body-based therapies; Viking, 2014.
works.method_zh: 关于创伤、内感受与身体疗法的临床叙事与研究综述；Viking，2014 年。

paper.title: The Body Keeps the Score: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma

works.title: The Feeling Body: Affective Science Meets the Enactive Mind
works.description: Colombetti argues that the whole living body is affective, that emotion is not a separate module but a dynamical pattern of the organism, and that bodily feelings can be background, not only objects of attention.
works.description_zh: Colombetti 主张整个活的身体都是情感性的：情绪不是独立的模块，而是机体的动态模式；身体感受可以作为背景存在，而不只是注意的对象。
works.idea_en: Feeling is not added to cognition; the body is the feeling organ of a single, affective sense-making process.
works.idea_zh: 感受不是附加在认知之上的；身体是同一个情感性意义生成过程的感受器官。
works.method: Philosophical synthesis of enactivism, phenomenology and affective science, including psychophysiology and dynamical systems.
works.method_zh: 综合生成论、现象学与情感科学（包括心理生理学与动力系统）的哲学论述。

paper.title: The Feeling Body: Affective Science Meets the Enactive Mind

works.title_zh: 感受的身体：情感科学遇见生成的心智

works.title: The Robotic Sixth Finger
works.description: A modular robotic finger strapped to the wrist that works with the hand's own fingers to grasp; later soft versions, driven by a muscle signal, help people with stroke hold objects again with their weakened hand.
works.description_zh: 一根绑在手腕上的模块化机器人手指，与手的原有手指配合抓握；后来的柔性版本由肌电信号控制，帮助中风患者用无力的手重新握住物体。
works.idea_en: An extra finger can complete a hand that has lost function, so the body is repaired by adding to it rather than restoring it.
works.idea_zh: 一根额外的手指可以补全失去功能的手：身体是通过增添而不是复原得到修补的。
works.method: Servo-driven finger modules on a wrist band; the soft version is controlled by EMG from a forehead or arm muscle and closes to oppose the paretic hand.
works.method_zh: 腕带上由舵机驱动的手指模块；柔性版本由额头或手臂肌肉的肌电信号控制，闭合时与患手相对抓握。

paper.title: The Sixth-Finger: A modular extra-finger to enhance human hand capabilities

works.title: Vocalizing Dance Movement
works.description: Dancers vocalize while moving; the system learns the link between their voice and Laban Effort qualities and then sonifies new movement so dancers can hear their own quality.
works.description_zh: 舞者边动边发声；系统学习嗓音与 Laban 力效质感之间的关系，再把新的动作声音化，让舞者听见自己的动作质感。
works.idea_en: The voice is a bodily bridge: sounds made by movement experts let others hear and learn a movement quality from inside.
works.idea_zh: 嗓音是身体的桥梁：动作专家发出的声音让他人能从内部听见并学习一种动作质感。
works.method: Vocalizations of movement experts recorded with motion data train a probabilistic motion-sound mapping; explored in a dance pedagogy workshop.
works.method_zh: 录制动作专家的发声与动作数据，训练概率式的动作—声音映射；在舞蹈教学工作坊中探索。

paper.title: Vocalizing dance movement for interactive sonification of laban effort factors

works.title: Embodied Cognition and the Magical Future of Interaction Design
works.description: Kirsh reviews embodied cognition and reports his studies of dancers 'marking' a phrase, showing that people think by using their bodies and things as external representations.
works.description_zh: Kirsh 回顾具身认知，并报告他对舞者“标记”舞句的研究，表明人把身体与物当作外部表征来思考。
works.idea_en: The body is a thinking medium: moving a partial version of an action helps us reason about the whole.
works.idea_zh: 身体是思考的媒介：做出一个动作的局部版本，能帮助我们推理整个动作。
works.method: Review of embodied cognition plus empirical study with professional dancers at Random Dance (Wayne McGregor).
works.method_zh: 具身认知综述，加上与 Wayne McGregor 的 Random Dance 舞团专业舞者合作的实证研究。

paper.title: Embodied cognition and the magical future of interaction design

works.title_zh: 具身认知与交互设计的神奇未来

works.title: Fidget Widgets
works.description: A set of small tangible objects to click, squeeze, spin and roll at the desk, designed from a study of how people fidget to manage stress, focus and boredom during digital work.
works.description_zh: 一组放在桌边可以按、捏、转、滚的小物件，源于一项关于人们在数字工作中如何用小动作应对压力、专注与无聊的研究。
works.idea_en: Fidgeting is the body regulating the mind; small objects for the hands can support emotional self-regulation without a screen.
works.idea_zh: 摆弄小动作是身体在调节心；给手的小物件，可以在没有屏幕的情况下支持情绪的自我调节。
works.method: Survey of fidgeting habits and a range of physical prototypes with distinct tactile qualities; later NordiCHI study of their use.
works.method_zh: 对摆弄习惯做问卷调查，并制作一系列触感各异的实体原型；后续在 NordiCHI 研究其使用。

paper.title: Understanding Fidget Widgets: Exploring the Design Space of Embodied Self-Regulation

works.title: Human Tails
works.description: In VR, participants have an avatar with a tail they swing by moving their hips; after using it to block falling objects, many react as if the tail were part of their body.
works.description_zh: 在 VR 中，参与者拥有一个带尾巴的化身，通过扭动臀部来摆动尾巴；用它拦截落下的物体之后，许多人的反应就像尾巴是自己身体的一部分。
works.idea_en: The body schema is plastic: with the right sensorimotor loop, a mover can come to feel a limb that humans have never had.
works.idea_zh: 身体图式是可塑的：只要感觉运动回路合适，运动者就能感到一个人类从未有过的肢体。
works.method: Full-body tracked avatar in immersive VR with a tail driven by hip movement (synchronous or random) and a task of blocking objects with body and tail; questionnaires and behaviour measured.
works.method_zh: 在沉浸式 VR 中使用全身追踪化身，尾巴由臀部动作驱动（同步或随机），并完成用身体与尾巴拦截物体的任务；以问卷与行为测量。

paper.title: Human Tails: Ownership and Control of Extended Humanoid Avatars

works.title: Illusory Ownership of a Virtual Child Body
works.description: Adults embodied in the virtual body of a four-year-old child overestimated the size of objects and associated themselves more with child-like traits.
works.description_zh: 被赋予四岁儿童虚拟身体的成年人会高估物体的尺寸，并更多地把自己与孩童特质联系在一起。
works.idea_en: The felt body shapes perception and self-concept at once: change the body, and both the world and the self look different.
works.idea_zh: 被感受的身体同时塑造知觉与自我概念：改变身体，世界与自我看起来都会不同。
works.method: Immersive VR with full-body motion capture and synchronous visuomotor feedback in a child or scaled adult body; size estimation and implicit association tests.
works.method_zh: 沉浸式 VR 配合全身动作捕捉，在儿童身体或等比缩小的成人身体中给予同步视动反馈；进行尺寸估计与内隐联想测验。

paper.title: Illusory ownership of a virtual child body causes overestimation of object sizes and implicit attitude changes

works.title_zh: 对虚拟儿童身体的错觉拥有感

works.title: Incendiary Reflection
works.description: A mirror-like display subtly deforms the viewer's face in real time into a slight smile or frown; people who see themselves smiling report feeling more positive and rate things more favourably.
works.description_zh: 一面类似镜子的显示屏实时轻微改变观看者的面孔，使之略带微笑或愁容；看到自己在微笑的人会报告情绪更积极，对事物的评价也更正面。
works.idea_en: Emotion flows from the felt and seen face inward: changing the body's expression changes the feeling, not only the other way round.
works.idea_zh: 情绪会从被感受、被看见的面孔向内流动：改变身体的表情就会改变感受，而不只是反过来。
works.method: Camera and real-time facial image warping shown on a display framed as a mirror, with studies on emotion and preference (University of Tokyo, Hirose-Narumi lab).
works.method_zh: 摄像头加实时面部图像变形，呈现在镜框式显示屏上，并进行情绪与偏好实验（东京大学广濑-鸣海实验室）。

paper.title: Manipulation of an emotional experience by real-time deformed facial feedback

works.title: Interaction Design for and with the Lived Body: Some Implications of Merleau-Ponty's Phenomenology
works.description: Svanæs reads Merleau-Ponty for interaction designers: the lived body, body schema and motor intentionality, and proposes that designers use their own bodies as instruments in the design process.
works.description_zh: Svanæs 为交互设计师解读 Merleau-Ponty：活的身体、身体图式与运动意向性，并提出设计师应在设计过程中把自己的身体当作工具。
works.idea_en: Design for the lived body by designing with it: the designer's own felt, moving body is a source of design knowledge.
works.idea_zh: 为活的身体设计，就要用活的身体来设计：设计师自身被感受的、运动的身体是设计知识的来源。
works.method: Philosophical analysis with design examples, including role-play and bodily enactment in a health-technology project.
works.method_zh: 结合设计实例的哲学分析，包括一个健康技术项目中的角色扮演与身体演绎。

paper.title: Interaction design for and with the lived body: Some implications of Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology

works.title_zh: 为活的身体、与活的身体一起做交互设计：Merleau-Ponty 现象学的若干启示

works.title: Metaphone
works.description: Metaphone is a large machine on two wheels that rolls across a sheet of watercolour paper, dripping paint and making sound according to the visitor's skin conductance and heart rate.
works.description_zh: Metaphone 是一台装在两个大轮子上的机器，它在一张水彩纸上滚动，依据参与者的皮肤电和心率滴下颜料、发出声音。
works.idea_en: A slow, machine-like response to one's pulse can feel strangely relaxing: machine aesthetics can make the living body stand out by contrast.
works.idea_zh: 对脉搏作出缓慢、机械般回应的机器，会让人感到出奇地放松：机器美学能通过对比，让活生生的身体凸显出来。
works.method: GSR and heart-rate sensors drive a rotating shaft that drips paint onto paper on the floor, with a soundscape following the biosignals; six invited commentators interacted with it.
works.method_zh: 皮肤电和心率传感器驱动一根旋转的轴，把颜料滴到地上的纸上，声景随生物信号变化；邀请了六位评论者与之互动。

paper.title: Metaphone: machine aesthetics meets interaction design

works.title: Moving and Making Strange: An Embodied Approach to Movement-Based Interaction Design
works.description: A design methodology with tools for making habitual movement strange, so that designers can notice, describe and design from how movement feels, looks and is sensed by machines.
works.description_zh: 一套设计方法及工具，把惯常的动作陌生化，让设计师注意、描述，并从动作的感受、样貌以及机器如何感知它出发来设计。
works.idea_en: Only when a familiar movement becomes strange do we feel it again; that renewed feeling is the starting point for design.
works.idea_zh: 只有当熟悉的动作变得陌生，我们才会重新感受到它；这种重新的感受正是设计的起点。
works.method: Methodology with three perspectives (mover, observer, machine), using movement scores, somatic exercises and notation, built from dance-based design projects.
works.method_zh: 包含三种视角（动者、观察者、机器）的方法论，使用动作谱、身体练习与记谱，源自以舞蹈为基础的设计项目。

paper.title: Moving and making strange: An embodied approach to movement-based interaction design

works.title_zh: 动起来并陌生化：基于动作的交互设计的具身方法

works.title: Musical Embrace
works.description: Two strangers play a music game by hugging a large pillow-like controller between them and moving together to steer it.
works.description_zh: 两个陌生人把一个大枕头状控制器抱在中间，一起移动来操控它，玩一个音乐游戏。
works.idea_en: Social awkwardness and close bodily contact can be a resource for play, not something to avoid.
works.idea_zh: 社交尴尬与亲密的身体接触可以成为游戏资源，而不是需要回避的东西。
works.method: A soft controller with embedded motion sensing, observed at public events to derive strategies for 'facilitating social awkwardness'.
works.method_zh: 内嵌动作传感的柔软控制器，在公开活动中观察，总结出“促成社交尴尬”的设计策略。

paper.title: Musical embrace: facilitating engaging play experiences through social awkwardness

works.title: Putting Yourself in the Skin of a Black Avatar
works.description: Light-skinned participants embodied in a dark-skinned virtual body, seen in a virtual mirror, showed reduced implicit racial bias afterwards.
works.description_zh: 浅肤色参与者被赋予一个深肤色的虚拟身体，并在虚拟镜子中看到它，之后他们的内隐种族偏见有所下降。
works.idea_en: Owning a different body for a while can loosen the boundary between self and other that bias depends on, though such effects raise their own ethical questions.
works.idea_zh: 暂时拥有一个不同的身体，可以松动偏见所依赖的自我与他者之间的边界，不过这类效果本身也带来伦理问题。
works.method: Immersive VR with full-body tracking and a virtual mirror, comparing light-skinned, dark-skinned, alien and no-body conditions with pre/post implicit association tests.
works.method_zh: 沉浸式 VR 配合全身追踪与虚拟镜子，比较浅肤色、深肤色、外星人与无身体几种条件，并做前后测内隐联想测验。

paper.title: Putting yourself in the skin of a black avatar reduces implicit racial bias

works.title: Seismic Sense / Waiting for Earthquakes
works.description: Sensors implanted in Moon Ribas's feet vibrated whenever an earthquake happened anywhere on Earth; in Waiting for Earthquakes she stands still and dances each tremor as it arrives.
works.description_zh: 植入 Moon Ribas 双脚的传感器会在地球任何地方发生地震时振动；在《Waiting for Earthquakes》中她静静站立，随每次震动到来而起舞。
works.idea_en: The sense ties her body to the planet's movement: a steady, low background feeling that she learns to attend to, like breath.
works.idea_zh: 这种感官把她的身体与地球的运动相连：一种持续而低沉的背景感受，她学会去留意它，如同留意呼吸。
works.method: Online seismograph data drove vibration implants (first in the elbow, later the feet), with intensity scaled to magnitude; the performance lasts as long as the quakes do.
works.method_zh: 在线地震仪数据驱动振动植入物（先在手肘，后在双脚），强度随震级变化；表演时长取决于地震本身。

works.title: Somatic Techniques for Experience Design (CHI courses)
works.description: Hands-on CHI courses — 'Body, Whys & Videotape' (2013) and 'Designing for Sensory Appreciation' (2020) — that teach HCI practitioners somatic exercises for designing and evaluating experience.
works.description_zh: CHI 实践课程——“Body, Whys & Videotape”（2013）与“Designing for Sensory Appreciation”（2020）——教人机交互从业者用身体练习来设计与评估体验。
works.idea_en: Designers can learn, in a few hours, to use breath, attention and movement as instruments for sensing experience.
works.idea_zh: 设计师可以在几小时内学会把呼吸、注意力与动作当作感知体验的工具。
works.method: Course with case studies, video and in-class somatic exercises drawn from Laban, Feldenkrais and other practices.
works.method_zh: 课程包括案例、视频与课堂身体练习，取材于 Laban、Feldenkrais 等实践。

paper.title: Designing for Sensory Appreciation: Cultivating Somatic Approaches to Experience Design

works.title_zh: 用于体验设计的身体技巧（CHI 课程）

works.title: TaSST: Tactile Sleeve for Social Touch
works.description: A pair of forearm sleeves: stroking or squeezing the pressure-sensitive layer of one sleeve is played back as a pattern of vibration on the other person's arm.
works.description_zh: 一对前臂袖套：抚摸或捏压一只袖套的压力感应层，另一人手臂上就会重现为一串振动图案。
works.idea_en: Social touch is carried by its pattern in time and space, a stroke versus a tap, more than by force alone.
works.idea_zh: 社会触碰的含义更多在于时间与空间中的样式（抚过还是轻拍），而不只是力度。
works.method: A grid of conductive-foam pressure sensors on one sleeve maps onto a matching grid of vibration motors on the other.
works.method_zh: 一只袖套上的导电泡沫压力传感器阵列一一对应到另一只袖套上的振动电机阵列。

paper.title: The TaSSt: Tactile sleeve for social touch

works.title_zh: TaSST 社会触碰触觉袖套

works.title: The Design Space of Body Games
works.description: Defines body games as games whose main pleasure is bodily engagement, and shows how the physical and social setting can matter as much as the technology.
works.description_zh: 把“身体游戏”定义为主要乐趣来自身体投入的游戏，并说明物理与社会情境可以与技术同样重要。
works.idea_en: When sensing is limited, the room, the rules and the other players carry the felt experience.
works.idea_zh: 当传感能力有限时，空间、规则与其他玩家承载了身体感受。
works.method: Literature study plus design experiments with children playing multiplayer games on the BodyBug wearable.
works.method_zh: 文献研究，加上儿童使用 BodyBug 可穿戴设备玩多人游戏的设计实验。

paper.title: The design space of body games: technological, physical, and social design

works.title: The Posthuman
works.description: Braidotti sets out a critical posthumanism that moves beyond the ideal of 'Man' toward subjects that are embodied, embedded and bound up with animals, machines and the earth.
works.description_zh: Braidotti 提出一种批判的后人类主义，超越“人”的理想，走向具身的、嵌入的、与动物、机器和地球相互缠绕的主体。
works.idea_en: She rejects transhumanist escape from the body and grounds the posthuman in vital, relational matter; the body is where the subject happens, not a vehicle.
works.idea_zh: 她拒绝超人类主义对身体的逃离，把后人类扎根于有生命力的、关系性的物质；身体是主体发生之处，而非载具。
works.method: Philosophical book drawing on Spinoza, Deleuze and feminist theory, with chapters on life beyond the self, beyond species and beyond death.
works.method_zh: 借鉴斯宾诺莎、德勒兹与女性主义理论的哲学著作，分章讨论超越自我、超越物种与超越死亡的生命。

paper.title: The Posthuman

works.title: The Transhumanist Reader: Classical and Contemporary Essays on the Science, Technology, and Philosophy of the Human Future
works.description: An anthology of transhumanist writing, from Max More's principles of extropy to essays on morphological freedom, life extension and mind uploading.
works.description_zh: 一部超人类主义文集，从 Max More 的“外熵原则”到关于形态自由、寿命延长与心灵上传的文章。
works.idea_en: Read as a map of positions: some essays treat the body as a platform for a mind that could move substrates (dualist); others, like morphological freedom, keep the body central.
works.idea_zh: 可当作立场地图来读：一些文章把身体当作可更换“基质”的心灵平台（二元论）；另一些，如形态自由，则仍以身体为中心。
works.method: Edited volume of about 40 essays, including reprints of classic texts and new contributions.
works.method_zh: 约 40 篇文章的编著，包括经典文本重刊与新稿。

paper.title: The Transhumanist Reader

works.title: The Vocal Chorder
works.description: A large instrument of steel wires that an opera singer pushes, leans on and bends while singing, to control their own accompaniment.
works.description_zh: 一件由钢丝构成的大型乐器，歌剧演唱者在演唱时推、倚、弯折钢丝，来控制自己的伴奏。
works.idea_en: Designed from the singer's own bodily experience on stage, it lets the whole singing body, not only the voice, shape the music.
works.idea_zh: 它从歌手自己在舞台上的身体经验出发设计，让整个歌唱的身体，而不只是嗓音，塑造音乐。
works.method: Sensors measure the bending of tensioned steel wires and map it to tempo and accompaniment; developed through autobiographical design and stage material explorations, with Kristina Höök.
works.method_zh: 传感器测量张紧钢丝的弯曲，并映射为速度与伴奏；通过自传式设计与舞台材料探索开发，合作者包括 Kristina Höök。

paper.title: The vocal chorder: empowering opera singers with a large interactive instrument

works.title: Turning Body and Self Inside Out
works.description: Participants saw a projected image of their own body outlined by a silhouette that flashed with their heartbeat; when the flashing was in sync, they identified more with the virtual body and felt touch displaced toward it.
works.description_zh: 参与者看到自己身体的投影影像，轮廓光圈随其心跳闪烁；当闪烁与心跳同步时，他们更认同这具虚拟身体，触觉也向它偏移。
works.idea_en: The inner heartbeat helps locate the self in space: making interoception visible outside the body can move where 'I' feel I am.
works.idea_zh: 内部的心跳参与在空间中定位自我：把内感受在体外变得可见，就能挪动“我”所感到的所在之处。
works.method: A cardio-visual full-body illusion: real-time video of the participant's body with a heartbeat-synchronous or asynchronous illuminated silhouette, measuring self-identification, self-location and tactile perception (Psychological Science, 2013; with Olaf Blanke and others).
works.method_zh: 心-视全身错觉：参与者身体的实时影像配以与心跳同步或不同步的发光轮廓，测量自我认同、自我定位与触觉知觉（Psychological Science，2013；合作者包括 Olaf Blanke）。

paper.title: Turning Body and Self Inside Out: Visualized Heartbeats Alter Bodily Self-Consciousness and Tactile Perception

works.title_zh: 把身体与自我翻转过来

works.title: A Light Touch (Movement Qualities as Interaction Modality)
works.description: An installation where a spot of light moves with the quality of a visitor's hand movement, how it moves, not where it goes.
works.description_zh: 一件装置：一个光点随观众手部动作的质感而运动，回应的是“怎么动”，而不是“动到哪里”。
works.idea_en: Using movement quality, rather than trajectory, as input invites exploratory and expressive movement.
works.idea_zh: 以动作质感而非轨迹作为输入，会引导人更具探索性和表现力地移动。
works.method: Hand motion is tracked and classified into dance-derived movement qualities that drive the behaviour of a projected light spot; evaluated in a user experiment.
works.method_zh: 追踪手部运动并将其归类为源自舞蹈的动作质感，用以驱动投影光点的行为；通过用户实验评估。

paper.title: Movement qualities as interaction modality

works.title_zh: 轻触（以动作质感作为交互模态）

works.title: Autobiographical Design in HCI Research
works.description: Defines autobiographical design — building and living with a system you made for yourself — and shows through interviews with practitioners that it yields knowledge ordinary studies miss.
works.description_zh: 定义“自传式设计”——为自己做一个系统并与之长期共处——并通过访谈实践者表明，它能得到一般研究得不到的知识。
works.idea_en: Long, genuine use by the designer's own life and body surfaces the small frictions and pleasures that short studies never reach.
works.idea_zh: 设计师以自己的生活与身体长期、真实地使用，能发现短期研究触及不到的细小摩擦与乐趣。
works.method: Interview study with researchers who had designed for themselves, synthesised into features of the method.
works.method_zh: 对“为自己做设计”的研究者进行访谈，归纳出这一方法的特征。

paper.title: Autobiographical design in HCI research: designing and learning through use-it-yourself

works.title_zh: 人机交互研究中的自传式设计

works.title: Distillery: Waveforming
works.description: A gallery version of Khut's heart-rate-controlled tablet work: visitors hold a sensor and watch forms bloom as their heart rate changes, beside video portraits of earlier participants recalling what they thought and felt.
works.description_zh: Khut 心率控制平板作品的美术馆版本：观众握住传感器，看着图形随心率变化而绽放；旁边是早先参与者回忆当时所思所感的视频肖像。
works.idea_en: Directing attention quietly inward to the heartbeat reveals how mind and body answer each other moment by moment.
works.idea_zh: 把注意力安静地转向心跳，就能看见心与身如何时时刻刻地相互回应。
works.method: Heart-rate sensing on iPads drives generative visuals and sound; shown with three vertical video portraits of participants' first-person accounts.
works.method_zh: iPad 上的心率感测驱动生成式图像与声音；与三幅竖屏视频肖像一同展出，记录参与者的第一人称讲述。
exhibited: 2012 National New Media Art Award (winner), Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art

works.title: Hanging off a Bar
works.description: Players hang from an exercise bar above a projected river for as long as they can, like an action hero; the game is almost all effort and almost no movement.
works.description_zh: 玩家像动作片英雄一样，悬挂在投影出的河流上方的单杠上，坚持得越久越好；游戏几乎全是用力，几乎没有动作。
works.idea_en: Exertion can be felt without movement: sustained effort and muscle burn are the play.
works.idea_zh: 用力可以在没有动作时被感受到：持续的用力与肌肉酸痛就是游戏。
works.method: An exercise bar with sensing of whether the player is still hanging, with projected graphics and sound; observed at three public events.
works.method_zh: 单杠配备检测玩家是否仍在悬挂的传感，配合投影画面与声音；在三次公开活动中观察。

paper.title: Hanging off a bar

works.title: Sonic Cradle
works.description: A person lies suspended in a hammock-like chair in a dark chamber; a respiration belt turns each breath into layers of ambient music, and people without meditation experience drift into calm attention.
works.description_zh: 人悬躺在暗室里一张吊床式的椅子上；呼吸带把每一次呼吸转成层层叠叠的氛围音乐，没有冥想经验的人也会渐渐进入平静的专注。
works.idea_en: Hearing one's own breath as music makes attention settle in the body without instruction; calm arrives through feeling, not effort.
works.idea_zh: 把自己的呼吸听成音乐，注意力无需指令便落回身体；平静经由感受而来，而不是靠用力。
works.method: Chest respiration sensor maps breathing patterns to generative ambient sound in a light-free, suspended setup; studied with first-time users through interviews.
works.method_zh: 胸部呼吸传感器把呼吸模式映射为生成式氛围声音，置于无光、悬吊的环境中；通过访谈与初次体验者一起研究。

paper.title: Sonic Cradle: designing for an immersive experience of meditation by connecting respiration to music

works.title: Strong Concepts: Intermediate-Level Knowledge in Interaction Design Research
works.description: Defines strong concepts: design ideas that sit between a single artefact and a general theory, can be reused across designs, and are grounded in examples. Soma design uses them to share what it learns.
works.description_zh: 定义“强概念”：介于单个作品与普遍理论之间、可在不同设计中复用、以实例为依据的设计想法。身体设计借此分享它的发现。
works.idea_en: Felt design knowledge can be shared without flattening it into rules: name the interaction pattern and show the cases.
works.idea_zh: 被感受的设计知识可以分享而不必压成规则：命名交互模式，并给出案例。
works.method: Conceptual paper illustrated with strong concepts such as social navigation and seamfulness, later used for soma design concepts.
works.method_zh: 概念性论文，以社会导航、接缝可见等强概念为例；这一框架后来被用于提炼身体设计的概念。

paper.title: Strong concepts: Intermediate-level knowledge in interaction design research

works.title_zh: 强概念：交互设计研究中的中间层知识

works.title: Swarming Emotional Pianos
works.description: Six robotic chime instruments surround a projection of an actress moving through extreme emotions; her recorded heartbeat, sweat and breathing drive the robots' musical outbursts.
works.description_zh: 六台机器人鸣钟乐器环绕着一位女演员的投影，她正经历一段段极端情绪；录下的心跳、出汗与呼吸数据驱动机器人奏出一阵阵音乐。
works.idea_en: Visitors meet two windows onto one emotional body, the face and the physiology, and feel how much, and how little, of feeling survives the translation into data.
works.idea_zh: 观众面对同一个情绪身体的两扇窗：面孔与生理；并感受到感受在转译为数据时，能留存多少、又丢失多少。
works.method: Custom biosensors recorded heart rate, skin conductance and respiration during timed emotional performances; the data drives servo-mallets on aluminium-tube robots.
works.method_zh: 自制生物传感器在限时情绪表演中记录心率、皮肤电与呼吸；这些数据驱动铝管机器人上的舵机琴槌。

works.title: TECHTILE Toolkit
works.description: A kit of a microphone, an amplifier and vibration actuators that lets anyone record the feel of an action, such as pouring marbles into a cup, and play it back into another object or hand; used in workshops where people sketch with touch.
works.description_zh: 一套由麦克风、放大器与振动器组成的工具包，任何人都能录下某个动作的触感（如把弹珠倒进杯子），再回放到另一个物体或手上；常用于用触觉来构思的工作坊。
works.idea_en: Touch becomes a design material once it can be recorded and replayed: designers learn by feeling and remixing textures with their own hands.
works.idea_zh: 触觉一旦可以被录制和回放，就成为设计材料：设计者通过亲手感受并重新组合质感来学习。
works.method: Audio-based haptic recording: contact microphones capture vibration, which is amplified and sent to voice-coil actuators attached to cups, paper or skin.
works.method_zh: 基于音频的触觉录制：接触式麦克风捕捉振动，经放大后传给贴在杯子、纸或皮肤上的音圈振动器。

paper.title: TECHTILE toolkit: a prototyping tool for designing haptic media

works.title: TELESAR V
works.description: An operator wearing a head-mounted display and haptic gloves moves a humanoid robot and sees, hears and feels through it, down to the texture of cloth under the robot's fingertips, so the robot body is experienced as one's own.
works.description_zh: 操作者戴着头显与触觉手套控制一台人形机器人，并通过它去看、去听、去触摸，甚至能感到机器人指尖下布料的纹理，从而把机器人身体体验为自己的身体。
works.idea_en: Telexistence shows that presence depends on closing the loop of seeing, moving and touching; with it, the self can be felt in a distant body.
works.idea_zh: 远程存在表明，临场感取决于看、动、触之间的闭环；闭合之后，自我可以在远方的身体中被感受到。
works.method: Master-slave humanoid robot with stereo vision, binaural audio and fingertip haptic sensors whose signals are reproduced on the operator's fingers.
works.method_zh: 主从式人形机器人，配有立体视觉、双耳音频与指尖触觉传感器，其信号在操作者手指上重现。

paper.title: TELESAR V: TELExistence Surrogate Anthropomorphic Robot

works.title: The Machine to Be Another
works.description: Two people wear headsets showing each other's first-person view; they move in agreed synchrony and touch the same objects, so each feels, for a while, in the other's body.
works.description_zh: 两个人戴上头显，看到彼此的第一人称视角；他们按约定同步移动、触摸相同的物件，于是各自在一段时间里感到身处对方的身体中。
works.idea_en: Embodiment is choreographed between people: the illusion of being another depends on two bodies attending to each other and moving together.
works.idea_zh: 具身是在人与人之间被编排出来的：成为他人的错觉，取决于两个身体彼此专注、一起移动。
works.method: Head-mounted cameras stream each participant's view to the other's HMD; performers mirror movements and apply matching touch; shown as an installation and used in workshops.
works.method_zh: 头戴摄像机把每位参与者的视野传到对方的头显中；表演者镜像动作并施以对应的触碰；以装置形式展出，也用于工作坊。

works.title: The Sense of Embodiment in Virtual Reality
works.description: A theory paper that splits the sense of embodiment in a virtual body into three parts, self-location, agency and body ownership, and reviews how each can be induced.
works.description_zh: 一篇理论论文，把对虚拟身体的具身感分为自我定位、能动感与身体拥有感三部分，并回顾如何分别诱发它们。
works.idea_en: Feeling embodied is several felt senses working together; designers can tune each one rather than treating 'presence' as a single switch.
works.idea_zh: 感到具身是几种感受共同作用的结果；设计者可以分别调节它们，而不是把“临场感”当作一个开关。
works.method: Conceptual review of body-ownership, agency and self-location research in neuroscience and VR.
works.method_zh: 对神经科学与 VR 中身体拥有感、能动感与自我定位研究的概念性综述。

paper.title: The Sense of Embodiment in Virtual Reality

works.title: Thinking through the Body: Essays in Somaesthetics
works.description: A collection of essays that extends somaesthetics to education, the art of living, East Asian self-cultivation, eroticism and urban experience.
works.description_zh: 身体美学文集，把身体美学延伸到教育、生活艺术、东亚修身传统、情爱与城市经验。
works.idea_en: We think with and through the body; educating somatic sensibility is part of educating the mind.
works.idea_zh: 我们用身体、也透过身体思考；培养身体的感受力，就是培养心智的一部分。
works.method: Essays combining philosophy, somatic practice and cross-cultural readings, including Confucian and Zen body cultivation.
works.method_zh: 结合哲学、身体修习与跨文化解读的文章，包括儒家与禅宗的身体修养。

paper.title: Thinking through the Body: Essays in Somaesthetics

works.title_zh: 通过身体来思考：身体美学文集

works.title: Understanding Heart Rate Sharing
works.description: A qualitative study of people sharing their heart rate with others in everyday situations, which found that a shared heartbeat can feel intimate and create connection, and that its meaning depends on the relationship.
works.description_zh: 一项质性研究：考察人们在日常情境中与他人分享心率，发现共享的心跳会让人感到亲密、产生联结，而其意义取决于彼此的关系。
works.idea_en: A heartbeat shared between people is not neutral data but a 'physiosocial' cue: it carries intimacy and responsibility and must be designed for as a relationship.
works.idea_zh: 人与人之间共享的心跳不是中性的数据，而是一种“生理-社会”线索：它承载亲密与责任，必须当作一段关系来设计。
works.method: Qualitative field study of heart rate sharing across social settings, analysed to map the dimensions of a 'physiosocial space' (CHI 2012; with Geraldine Fitzpatrick).
works.method_zh: 对不同社交情境中的心率分享进行质性实地研究，并据此勾画“生理-社会空间”的维度（CHI 2012；合作者 Geraldine Fitzpatrick）。

paper.title: Understanding heart rate sharing: towards unpacking physiosocial space

works.title: Yamove!
works.description: A dance-battle game for pairs: each dancer holds a phone, and the game scores how energetic, varied and above all synchronised the partners move.
works.description_zh: 一款双人斗舞游戏：每位舞者手持一部手机，游戏根据两人动作的力度、变化，尤其是同步程度来计分。
works.idea_en: Rewarding synchrony rather than individual skill choreographs social connection: partners must watch and feel each other to win.
works.idea_zh: 奖励同步而非个人技巧，就是在编排社会联结：搭档必须看着彼此、感受彼此才能赢。
works.method: Phone accelerometers track both dancers; an emcee and audience frame the play; studies observed how pairs coordinate.
works.method_zh: 手机加速度计追踪两位舞者；主持人与观众构成游戏的框架；研究观察搭档如何协调动作。

paper.title: Yamove! A Movement Synchrony Game That Choreographs Social Interaction

works.description: Two dancers in grey, hair loose, keep moving continuously for the whole piece, their bodies circling, folding and releasing without a pause or a narrative.
works.description_zh: 两名身着灰衣、长发散开的舞者在整部作品中持续不停地运动，身体环绕、折叠、释放，没有停顿，也没有叙事。
works.idea_en: Continuous circular movement makes the whole body a single flowing line; stamina turns into a meditative, felt state.
works.idea_zh: 连续的圆运动让整个身体成为一条流动的线；体力的消耗转化为一种冥想式的、被感受的状态。
works.method: Part of TAO Dance Theater's numbered series, built on Tao Ye's 'circular movement system' of releasing weight through the spine; premiered at the M.A.D.E festival in Umeå in 2011.
works.method_zh: 陶身体剧场“数字系列”之一，基于陶冶以脊柱释放重量的“圆运动体系”；2011 年在瑞典于默奥 M.A.D.E 艺术节首演。

works.title: Augmented Gustation Using Electricity
works.description: Weak electric current passed through a straw or fork changes the taste of food and drink in the mouth; the line of work later became the Kirin Electric Salt Spoon, which makes low-salt food taste saltier.
works.description_zh: 通过吸管或叉子传入的微弱电流会改变口中食物与饮料的味道；这一研究后来发展为麒麟电盐勺，让低盐食物尝起来更咸。
works.idea_en: Taste, felt as a private and given sense, turns out to be adjustable from outside, which makes eating a place to notice how perception is made.
works.idea_zh: 味觉看似私密而既定，实际上可以从外部调节；饮食因此成为察觉知觉如何生成的地方。
works.method: Electrodes in eating utensils close a circuit through the tongue; the polarity and waveform of the current can add an 'electric' taste or strengthen or weaken salty taste.
works.method_zh: 餐具中的电极经由舌头形成回路；电流的极性与波形可以增添一种“电味”，或增强、减弱咸味。

paper.title: Augmented gustation using electricity

works.title: BrightHearts
works.description: An iPad app in which glowing, overlapping circles change colour and size as a child's heart rate slows, used to help children relax during painful and recurring hospital procedures.
works.description_zh: 一款 iPad 应用：随着孩子心率放缓，发光的重叠圆环改变颜色与大小；用于帮助孩子在痛苦且反复的住院治疗中放松。
works.idea_en: Relaxation can be learned as a felt skill: a gentle, playful mirror of the heart gives a child a way to act on fear from inside the body.
works.idea_zh: 放松可以作为一种体感技能被学会：一面温和、好玩的“心之镜”让孩子得以从身体内部应对恐惧。
works.method: A pulse sensor streams heart rate to the app, which maps slowing heart rate to visual and sound changes; developed with Dr Angela Morrow at The Children's Hospital at Westmead and evaluated in clinical pilot studies.
works.method_zh: 脉搏传感器把心率传给应用，心率放缓对应视觉与声音的变化；与威斯敏德儿童医院的 Angela Morrow 医生合作开发，并在临床试点研究中评估。

paper.title: Developing BrightHearts: A Pediatric Biofeedback-Mediated Relaxation App to Manage Procedural Pain and Anxiety

works.title: Broncomatic
works.description: A mechanical bucking bronco that riders steer with their breath, while the ride itself throws the body and makes controlled breathing hard.
works.description_zh: 一台用呼吸操控的机械牛，而机械牛本身把身体甩来甩去，使得控制呼吸变得困难。
works.idea_en: Breath is both voluntary and involuntary, so using it as a control under physical stress makes the rider feel the struggle between will and body.
works.idea_zh: 呼吸既可控又不可控；在身体受压时用它来控制，会让骑手感到意志与身体之间的角力。
works.method: A breathing sensor on the rider's chest likely drives the rotation of a rodeo machine; studied with riders at public events.
works.method_zh: 骑手胸前的呼吸传感器很可能驱动机械牛的旋转；在公共活动中与骑手一起研究。

paper.title: Breath control of amusement rides

works.title: How HCI Talks about Sexuality
works.description: A discourse analysis of HCI papers that mention sex and sexuality, showing how the field frames sexuality as risk, identity or health data while avoiding the sexual body itself.
works.description_zh: 对提到性与性取向的人机交互论文做话语分析，揭示该领域把性框定为风险、身份或健康数据，却回避性的身体本身。
works.idea_en: What a field will not say about bodies shapes what it can design for; naming the blind spot is the first step toward designing with desire and pleasure.
works.idea_zh: 一个领域不愿谈论身体的哪些部分，就决定了它能为什么设计；指出盲点，是走向与欲望和愉悦一起设计的第一步。
works.method: Critical reading of the HCI literature on sexuality, identifying discursive strategies, blind spots and research opportunities.
works.method_zh: 批判性阅读人机交互中关于性的文献，归纳其话语策略、盲点与研究机会。

paper.title: How HCI talks about sexuality: discursive strategies, blind spots, and opportunities for future research

works.title: Johann Sebastian Joust
works.description: A screenless game for motion controllers: players must keep their controller still while trying to jostle others'; when Bach's music slows, the controllers become more sensitive.
works.description_zh: 一款无屏幕的体感手柄游戏：玩家要保持自己的手柄不动，同时设法晃动别人的；当巴赫音乐放慢时，手柄变得更敏感。
works.idea_en: Removing the screen turns attention back to bodies, balance and each other.
works.idea_zh: 去掉屏幕，注意力就回到了身体、平衡与彼此身上。
works.method: PlayStation Move controllers measure acceleration against a threshold that changes with the tempo of the Brandenburg Concertos.
works.method_zh: PlayStation Move 手柄测量加速度，阈值随《勃兰登堡协奏曲》的速度变化。

works.title: Just a Heartbeat Away from One's Body
works.description: People counted their own heartbeats and then took part in the rubber hand illusion; those who sensed their heartbeat less accurately more readily felt a rubber hand as their own.
works.description_zh: 参与者先数自己的心跳，再体验橡胶手错觉；心跳感知越不准确的人，越容易把橡胶手感到是自己的。
works.idea_en: Interoception anchors the sense of owning one's body: the better we feel from inside, the less our body-image is pulled around by what we see.
works.idea_zh: 内感受为身体拥有感提供了锚点：从内部感受得越清楚，身体意象就越不容易被所见之物牵着走。
works.method: Heartbeat perception task to measure interoceptive sensitivity, followed by the rubber hand illusion with proprioceptive drift and questionnaires (Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 2011).
works.method_zh: 用心跳感知任务测量内感受敏感性，随后进行橡胶手错觉实验，测量本体感偏移并填写问卷（《英国皇家学会学报 B》，2011）。

paper.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 2011
paper.title: Just a heartbeat away from one's body: interoceptive sensitivity predicts malleability of body-representations

works.title: MO – Modular Musical Objects
works.description: Small wireless motion-sensing modules that can be attached to balls, hands or everyday objects, turning shaking, tapping and throwing into music.
works.description_zh: 小型无线动作传感模块，可以装在球、手或日常物件上，把摇晃、敲击和抛掷变成音乐。
works.idea_en: Instruments can be 'finished' by the player: the meaning of a gesture comes from how the body uses the object.
works.idea_zh: 乐器可以由演奏者来“完成”：手势的意义来自身体如何使用这个物件。
works.method: Wireless inertial sensor modules with accessories, mapped to sound through gesture following and recognition software from IRCAM's Interlude project.
works.method_zh: 带配件的无线惯性传感模块，通过 IRCAM Interlude 项目的手势跟随与识别软件映射为声音。

paper.title: Modular musical objects towards embodied control of digital music

works.title: May the Horse Live in Me
works.description: After months of immunising herself, artist Marion Laval-Jeantet is injected with horse blood plasma and then walks with a horse on stilts shaped like hooves.
works.description_zh: 艺术家 Marion Laval-Jeantet 经过数月免疫准备后，被注射马的血浆，随后踩着马蹄形状的高跷与一匹马同行。
works.idea_en: Letting another species' blood act inside one's body is an extreme first-person test of where one's own body ends.
works.idea_zh: 让另一物种的血液在自己体内起作用，是对“自己的身体止于何处”的一次极端的第一人称检验。
works.method: Progressive immunisation to horse immunoglobulins, followed by a live injection and a walk with a horse on hoof-stilts; documented as performance.
works.method_zh: 逐步对马免疫球蛋白进行免疫，随后现场注射，并踩马蹄高跷与马同行；以表演形式记录。
exhibited: Prix Ars Electronica 2011, Golden Nica, Hybrid Art

works.title: Motivating Mobility: Lived Motivation in Stroke Rehabilitation
works.description: A study of how stroke survivors actually find motivation to rehabilitate at home, and the design of home rehabilitation technologies around their lived, changing motivations.
works.description_zh: 研究中风幸存者在家康复时实际如何找到动力，并围绕他们亲历、变化的动力设计居家康复技术。
works.idea_en: Rehabilitation is lived in a whole life, not in exercise counts; motivation comes from what movement means to the person.
works.idea_zh: 康复活在整个生活里，而不在练习次数里；动力来自动作对这个人意味着什么。
works.method: Participatory design and home deployment of rehabilitation prototypes with stroke survivors, analysed for lived motivation.
works.method_zh: 与中风幸存者开展参与式设计，并在家中部署康复原型，分析其亲历的动力。

paper.title: Motivating mobility: designing for lived motivation in stroke rehabilitation

works.title_zh: 激发活动：中风康复中的亲历动力

works.title: Pleasure is Your Birthright: Digitally Enabled Designer Sex Toys
works.description: A study of how designers of high-end digital sex toys work, arguing that these vibrators are sophisticated interactive artefacts for embodied pleasure that HCI had refused to study.
works.description_zh: 研究高端数字情趣用品的设计师如何工作，指出这些振动器是为身体愉悦而精心设计的交互物件，而人机交互一直拒绝研究它们。
works.idea_en: Designing for pleasure is designing for the whole felt body; leaving sexuality out of HCI is itself a norm about which bodies and experiences count.
works.idea_zh: 为愉悦设计，就是为整个被感受的身体设计；把性排除在人机交互之外，本身就是一种关于哪些身体与经验才算数的规范。
works.method: Interviews with sex toy designers and analysis of their process (critical immersion, conversations with users and sexual health experts, iterated 3D prototypes), framed as third-wave HCI.
works.method_zh: 访谈情趣用品设计师并分析其流程（沉浸式批判、与用户及性健康专家对话、反复迭代 3D 原型），放在“第三波人机交互”框架下讨论。

paper.title: Pleasure is your birthright: digitally enabled designer sex toys as a case of third-wave HCI

works.title_zh: 愉悦是你与生俱来的权利：数字化的设计师情趣用品

works.title: PossessedHand
works.description: A forearm band with electrode pads moves individual finger joints by electrical muscle stimulation, used for example to guide a beginner's fingers on the koto, a Japanese string instrument.
works.description_zh: 一个带电极片的前臂带用肌肉电刺激驱动单个手指关节，例如引导初学者在日本弦乐器“筝”上的指法。
works.idea_en: Having one's fingers moved from outside is strange at first, and that strangeness shows how much of skill lives in the hand rather than in instructions.
works.idea_zh: 手指被外力驱动起初很陌生，而这种陌生恰恰显示了技能有多少存在于手中，而不在指令里。
works.method: Twenty-eight electrode pads on the forearm stimulate the muscles behind 16 finger joints; tested for posture accuracy and in instrument-learning scenarios.
works.method_zh: 前臂上的 28 个电极片刺激控制 16 个手指关节的肌肉；测试了姿势准确度以及在乐器学习中的应用。

paper.title: PossessedHand: Techniques for Controlling Human Hands Using Electrical Muscles Stimuli

works.title: Self-Evidence: Applying Somatic Connoisseurship to Experience Design
works.description: Introduces somatic connoisseurship: using the trained felt sense of somatic practitioners as evidence in designing and evaluating experience.
works.description_zh: 提出“身体鉴赏力”：把身体修习者训练过的身体感受当作设计与评估体验的证据。
works.idea_en: The felt sense, when trained, is evidence; designers can learn to trust and articulate it.
works.idea_zh: 经过训练的身体感受就是证据；设计师可以学会信任并说出它。
works.method: Essay drawing on somatics (Laban, Feldenkrais, Body-Mind Centering) and the author's wearable and installation works.
works.method_zh: 论文取材于身心学（Laban、Feldenkrais、身心平衡技法 BMC）以及作者的可穿戴与装置作品。

paper.title: Self-evidence: applying somatic connoisseurship to experience design

works.title_zh: 自证：把身体鉴赏力用于体验设计

works.title: Sex Toys and Designing for Sexual Wellness
works.description: A user study of how people choose, use and talk about sex toys, turned into design principles for sexual wellness technology.
works.description_zh: 一项关于人们如何挑选、使用和谈论情趣用品的用户研究，并据此提出性健康技术的设计原则。
works.idea_en: Sexual pleasure belongs to health: a toy that helps someone know what their body enjoys is a wellness device, not a joke.
works.idea_zh: 性愉悦属于健康：一件帮助人了解自己身体喜欢什么的玩具，是健康用品，不是笑话。
works.method: Survey and interviews with sex toy users, analysed for experiences, barriers and preferences, leading to design principles.
works.method_zh: 对情趣用品使用者进行问卷与访谈，分析其经验、障碍与偏好，得出设计原则。

paper.title: Sex toys and designing for sexual wellness

works.title_zh: 情趣用品与为性健康而设计

works.title: Surging Verticality
works.description: A body-focused interactive artwork in which an artist guides a visitor through touch and slow movement to sense how their skeleton holds them upright.
works.description_zh: 一件以身体为中心的互动艺术作品：艺术家通过触摸与缓慢动作引导观众，感受自己的骨骼如何把身体撑直。
works.idea_en: Feldenkrais-style guidance shows that artist care and the visitor's receptivity are part of the interface.
works.idea_zh: 费登奎斯式的引导表明，艺术家的照料与观众的接受状态本身就是界面的一部分。
works.method: Prototype built by applying the Feldenkrais Method to proprioception and touch, tested with audiences and reflected on by the artist-researchers.
works.method_zh: 把费登奎斯方法应用于本体感与触摸而构建的原型，经观众测试，并由艺术家研究者反思。

paper.title: Surging verticality: an experience of balance

works.title_zh: 涌动的垂直：一种平衡体验

works.title: Swallowable Parfum
works.description: A speculative cosmetic pill that would make the skin sweat fragrance, shown through images, a film and a gallery 'live lab'.
works.description_zh: 一种思辨性的美容药丸，设想让皮肤随汗液散发香味，以图像、影片和画廊中的“现场实验室”呈现。
works.idea_en: Augmentation from the inside out: the body itself becomes the atomiser, so scent follows exertion, heat and emotion rather than being applied.
works.idea_zh: 由内而外的增强：身体本身成为喷香器，香气随用力、体温与情绪而生，而不是被涂抹上去。
works.method: Developed with synthetic biologist Sharef Mansy as a design fiction; the pill is a proposal presented through photography, film and guided gallery sessions.
works.method_zh: 与合成生物学家 Sharef Mansy 合作的设计虚构；药丸是一个提案，通过摄影、影片和画廊导览体验呈现。

works.title: The Haptic Creature
works.description: A furry, lap-sized robot animal without face or eyes that breathes, purrs and stiffens its ears under a person's hand, communicating only through touch.
works.description_zh: 一只没有脸和眼睛、放在腿上的毛绒机器动物，在人的手下呼吸、发出咕噜声、竖起耳朵，只通过触碰来交流。
works.idea_en: Emotion between human and robot can live entirely in touch: how a person strokes, and how the creature breathes back.
works.idea_zh: 人与机器人之间的情绪可以完全存在于触碰之中：人如何抚摸，生物又如何以呼吸回应。
works.method: Touch sensors under fur detect gestures; actuators control breathing, purring vibration and ear stiffness; a study mapped touch gestures to intended emotions.
works.method_zh: 毛皮下的触觉传感器识别手势，执行器控制呼吸、咕噜振动与耳朵的软硬；研究把触碰手势与意图表达的情绪相对应。

paper.title: The Role of Affective Touch in Human-Robot Interaction: Human Intent and Expectations in Touching the Haptic Creature

works.title: The Illusion of Owning a Third Arm
works.description: Participants look down at a rubber arm placed beside their real right arm while both are stroked at the same time, and many come to feel they have two right arms.
works.description_zh: 参与者低头看着放在真实右臂旁的一只橡胶手臂，同时两者被同步抚触，许多人会感到自己有两只右臂。
