works.idea_en: The felt body is not fixed to the number of limbs one has: it can hold a supernumerary arm, which is the ground on which extra-limb design stands.
works.idea_zh: 被感受的身体并不受限于实际肢体数量，它可以容纳一只多出来的手臂；这正是额外肢体设计的基础。
works.method: Variant of the rubber hand illusion with the real arm left visible; ownership measured by questionnaires and skin conductance responses to a threatened rubber arm or real arm.
works.method_zh: 橡胶手错觉的变体，真实手臂保持可见；通过问卷和对橡胶手或真实手受威胁时的皮肤电反应测量归属感。

paper.title: The Illusion of Owning a Third Arm

works.title_zh: 拥有第三只手臂的错觉

works.title: The Virtual Meditative Walk
works.description: An immersive VR walk through a forest with guided mindfulness for people living with chronic pain; the fog lifts as the person's physiological arousal drops.
works.description_zh: 一段沉浸式 VR 森林漫步，为慢性疼痛者提供正念引导；当人的生理唤醒下降时，雾气随之散去。
works.idea_en: Instead of distracting from pain, the VR teaches a different relationship to it, so pain is attended to calmly rather than escaped.
works.idea_zh: 这个 VR 不是让人从疼痛上分心，而是教人与疼痛建立另一种关系：平静地注意它，而不是逃离它。
works.method: Head-mounted display VR environment with mindfulness-based stress reduction audio and biofeedback from skin conductance controlling fog density; studied with chronic pain patients.
works.method_zh: 头戴式 VR 环境配合正念减压引导音频，以皮肤电生物反馈控制雾的浓度；与慢性疼痛患者一起研究。

paper.title: The Virtual Meditative Walk: Virtual Reality Therapy for Chronic Pain Management

works.title: Xth Sense
works.description: A wearable instrument that amplifies the sound of the performer's own muscle contractions and blood flow and shapes it into live music.
works.description_zh: 一件可穿戴乐器，把表演者自己肌肉收缩与血流的声音放大，并塑造成现场音乐。
works.idea_en: Music can come from inside the body: the felt effort of muscles, not visible gesture, drives the sound.
works.idea_zh: 音乐可以来自身体内部：驱动声音的是肌肉被感受到的用力，而不是可见的手势。
works.method: Microphone sensors on the arms capture mechanomyographic (MMG) vibrations, which software analyses and processes into sound; free and open hardware (created 2010).
works.method_zh: 手臂上的麦克风传感器采集肌音（MMG）振动，由软件分析并处理成声音；开源免费硬件（2010 年创建）。

works.title: 3rdi
works.description: For about a year Wafaa Bilal had a small camera attached to the back of his head that took a photo every minute and posted it online, recording what he left behind.
works.description_zh: 大约一年里，Wafaa Bilal 的后脑装着一台小相机，每分钟拍一张照片并上传网络，记录他身后留下的景象。
works.idea_en: An eye that sees what the body cannot feel becomes a burden: his body rejected the implant, and pain ended up governing the concept.
works.idea_zh: 一只看见身体无法感受之物的眼睛成了负担：他的身体排斥了植入物，疼痛最终主导了这个构想。
works.method: A camera was mounted on a titanium plate surgically placed under the scalp; after infection and rejection it was removed and worn on a strap.
works.method_zh: 相机固定在手术植入头皮下的钛板上；因感染和排斥被取出，改用绑带佩戴。

works.title: Affective Health
works.description: Affective Health is a mobile stress-management service that mirrors short-term stress reactions measured by wearable sensors back to users as a moving spiral of colour, so they can reflect on their own patterns.
works.description_zh: Affective Health 是一款手机压力管理服务：它把可穿戴传感器测到的短时应激反应，以彩色旋转的螺旋反映给用户，让他们反思自己的模式。
works.idea_en: Stress cannot be read off the body as a diagnosis; it is better to mirror bodily reactions and let people interpret them in the context of their lives.
works.idea_zh: 压力无法从身体上直接读出诊断；更好的做法是把身体反应反映出来，让人在自己的生活情境中去解读。
works.method: Skin conductance, heart rate and movement sensors stream to a phone that renders arousal and activity as layered and spiral visualisations over time; designed through a multidisciplinary process at SICS.
works.method_zh: 皮肤电、心率与运动传感器把数据传到手机，手机把唤醒与活动随时间绘成分层与螺旋的可视化；在 SICS 经由跨学科过程设计。

paper.title: Mind the body! Designing a mobile stress management application encouraging personal reflection

works.title: Bodystorming as Embodied Designing
works.description: An interactions article that presents bodystorming as embodied thinking: physically acting out a situation to generate and test design ideas.
works.description_zh: 《interactions》文章，把身体风暴阐述为具身的思考：通过亲身演出情境来产生并检验设计想法。
works.idea_en: Acting a scenario out with the whole body produces knowledge that talking and sketching on paper do not.
works.idea_zh: 用整个身体把情境演出来，能产生口头讨论与纸上草图得不到的知识。
works.method: Practitioner account with guidance for running bodystorming sessions (with Peter Jones and Oksana Kachur).
works.method_zh: 实践者经验总结，附有组织身体风暴的指引（与 Peter Jones、Oksana Kachur 合著）。

paper.title: Bodystorming as embodied designing

works.title_zh: 身体风暴：一种具身的设计

works.title: ExoBuilding
works.description: A tent-like room that breathes with the person inside: its fabric rises and falls with their abdominal breathing, their heartbeat plays as sound and light, and skin conductance is projected on the walls.
works.description_zh: 一个帐篷般的房间与其中的人一同呼吸：织物随其腹式呼吸起伏，心跳化作声音与光，皮肤电被投影在墙面上。
works.idea_en: When architecture takes on the rhythm of the body, a person can feel their own physiology from the outside, as the space around them.
works.idea_zh: 当建筑承接了身体的节律，人就能从外部、以周围空间的形式感受自己的生理状态。
works.method: A breathing belt, ECG and EDA sensors drive actuators that change the tent's shape, plus sound, lights and projection; iterated from scale model to full size.
works.method_zh: 呼吸带、心电与皮肤电传感器驱动改变帐篷形状的执行器，以及声音、灯光与投影；从比例模型迭代到实际尺寸。

paper.title: ExoBuilding: breathing life into architecture

works.title: Feminist HCI: Taking Stock and Outlining an Agenda for Design
works.description: The paper that named feminist HCI: it proposes qualities such as pluralism, participation, advocacy, ecology, embodiment and self-disclosure to guide interaction design.
works.description_zh: 命名“女性主义人机交互”的论文：提出多元、参与、倡导、生态、具身与自我披露等品质，作为交互设计的指引。
works.idea_en: Design always assumes a user's body and life; feminist HCI makes that assumption visible and asks designers to answer for it.
works.idea_zh: 设计总会预设使用者的身体与生活；女性主义人机交互让这种预设显形，并要求设计者为之负责。
works.method: Theoretical synthesis of feminist theory for interaction design, yielding a set of design qualities with examples.
works.method_zh: 把女性主义理论综合转译到交互设计，提出一组附带示例的设计品质。

paper.title: Feminist HCI: taking stock and outlining an agenda for design

works.title_zh: 女性主义人机交互：盘点与设计议程

works.title: First Person Experience of Body Transfer in Virtual Reality
works.description: Adult men in VR saw, from a first-person view, the body of a young girl in place of their own, and felt it as theirs, with bodily reactions when the girl was threatened.
works.description_zh: 成年男性在 VR 中以第一人称视角看到一个小女孩的身体取代了自己的身体，并把它感受为自己的；当女孩受到威胁时，他们出现身体反应。
works.idea_en: A first-person perspective alone can transfer ownership to a very different body, which opens VR as a tool for living in another's body.
works.idea_zh: 仅凭第一人称视角就能把拥有感转移到一个非常不同的身体上，这让 VR 成为“活在他人身体里”的工具。
works.method: Immersive VR with a virtual female body seen from first-person or third-person perspective, with visuotactile stroking; heart-rate deceleration to a threat measured.
works.method_zh: 沉浸式 VR，以第一或第三人称视角看到虚拟女性身体，配合视触同步抚触；测量面对威胁时的心率减速。

paper.title: First Person Experience of Body Transfer in Virtual Reality

works.title_zh: 虚拟现实中身体转移的第一人称体验

works.title: Gesture Follower
works.description: A system that learns a gesture from one example and then follows it in real time, so a sound can be stretched or compressed to the pace at which the gesture is performed.
works.description_zh: 一个系统从单个示例中学会一个手势，然后实时跟随它，使声音随手势的快慢被拉伸或压缩。
works.idea_en: Following the continuous time of a gesture, rather than only recognising it at the end, keeps the performer's timing and feel in the sound.
works.idea_zh: 持续跟随手势的时间进程，而不是只在结束时识别，才能让表演者的节奏与感受留在声音里。
works.method: Hidden-Markov-model-based real-time alignment of multidimensional sensor data to recorded templates, used with dancers and musicians at IRCAM.
works.method_zh: 基于隐马尔可夫模型，把多维传感数据与录制模板实时对齐；在 IRCAM 与舞者和音乐家一起使用。

paper.venue: Gesture in Embodied Communication and Human-Computer Interaction (LNCS)
paper.title: Continuous Realtime Gesture Following and Recognition

works.title: Intimate Heartbeats
works.description: A set of studies, including one in an immersive virtual environment, showing that people perceive another's heartbeat as an intimate signal and that hearing it changes how close they feel to that person.
works.description_zh: 一组研究（其中一项在沉浸式虚拟环境中进行）表明，人们把他人的心跳感知为一种亲密信号，而听见它会改变人们感到与对方的亲近程度。
works.idea_en: The heartbeat is felt as one of the most intimate body signals; hearing it gives technology a way to mediate closeness through the body, with the care that intimacy requires.
works.idea_zh: 心跳被体验为最亲密的身体信号之一；听见它，让技术有了一种经由身体传递亲近的途径，也要求相应的审慎。
works.method: Survey and experimental studies on the perceived intimacy of heartbeats, including an immersive virtual environment study of interpersonal distance (IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing, 2010; with Jeremy Bailenson and others).
works.method_zh: 关于心跳亲密感的问卷与实验研究，包括一项在沉浸式虚拟环境中测量人际距离的研究（IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing，2010；合作者包括 Jeremy Bailenson）。

paper.title: Intimate Heartbeats: Opportunities for Affective Communication Technology

works.title: Menstruation Machine – Takashi's Take
works.description: A metal device resembling a chastity belt, with a blood-dispensing system and electrodes that stimulate the lower abdomen, reproduces the pain and bleeding of a five-day period; in the music video a boy, Takashi, wears it to feel what menstruation is like.
works.description_zh: 一个形似贞操带的金属装置，配有出血装置与刺激下腹部的电极，重现五天经期的疼痛与出血；在音乐录像中，少年 Takashi 戴上它，去感受来月经是什么样子。
works.idea_en: Feeling another body's cycle in your own body turns a gendered experience into shared, felt knowledge and questions who gets to have it.
works.idea_zh: 在自己身上感受另一种身体的周期，把一种性别化的经验变成共享的、被感受的知识，也追问谁有资格拥有这种经验。
works.method: Wearable device with electrical abdominal stimulation and a blood reservoir, presented with a pop music video; made at the Royal College of Art.
works.method_zh: 带腹部电刺激与血液储存装置的可穿戴设备，配合一支流行音乐录像展出；创作于英国皇家艺术学院。

works.title: Robocygne
works.description: A small robot performs the dying swan from Swan Lake, its movements recorded from the choreographer's own body.
works.description_zh: 一台小型机器人表演《天鹅湖》中的天鹅之死，其动作录自编舞家自己的身体。
works.idea_en: Moving a dancer's felt movement into a machine body makes both the robot and the ballet strange, and asks what expression survives the transfer.
works.idea_zh: 把舞者被感受的动作移入机器身体，让机器人与芭蕾都变得陌生，也追问经过转移后还剩下什么表达。
works.method: Humanoid robot programmed from motion recordings of Åsa Unander-Scharin, built with Mälardalen University, to Tchaikovsky's music arranged by Carl Unander-Scharin.
works.method_zh: 人形机器人依据 Åsa Unander-Scharin 的动作录制编程，由梅拉达伦大学参与制造，配以 Carl Unander-Scharin 改编的柴可夫斯基音乐。

works.title: Transferring Qualities from Horseback Riding to Design
works.description: Höök's autoethnography of learning to ride a horse: how rider and horse come to communicate through subtle shifts of weight and muscle, and which of those qualities design could borrow.
works.description_zh: Höök 学骑马的自我民族志：骑手与马如何借由重心与肌肉的细微变化相互沟通，以及设计可以借用哪些品质。
works.idea_en: Years of bodily learning with another living body reveal interaction qualities — subtlety, rhythm, mutual attunement — that screens rarely offer.
works.idea_zh: 与另一个活的身体共同学习多年，揭示了屏幕少有的交互品质：细腻、节奏与相互调谐。
works.method: First-person autoethnographic account drawn from the author's years of riding lessons, analysed for design qualities.
works.method_zh: 第一人称自我民族志，取材于作者多年的骑马课程，并从中分析设计品质。

paper.title: Transferring qualities from horseback riding to design

works.title_zh: 把骑马的品质迁移到设计中

works.title: Affective Loop Experiences
works.description: Höök's essay defines the affective loop: a system that is influenced by and influences the user corporeally, drawing on eMoto, the Affective Diary and other SICS systems.
works.description_zh: Höök 的这篇论文界定了“情感回路”：系统在身体层面既受用户影响、也影响用户；论证以 eMoto、Affective Diary 等 SICS 系统为例。
works.idea_en: Emotions are processes constructed in interaction, starting from bodily, cognitive and social experience; the user, not the system, holds the responsibility for interpreting them.
works.idea_zh: 情绪是在互动中构建的过程，起于身体、认知与社会经验；解读情绪的责任在用户，而不在系统。
works.method: Conceptual analysis of a series of built systems (eMoto, FriendSense, Affective Diary) and their user studies, published in a theme issue on computation of emotions.
works.method_zh: 对一系列已建成系统（eMoto、FriendSense、Affective Diary）及其用户研究的概念分析，发表于一期关于情绪计算的主题专刊。

paper.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 2009
paper.title: Affective loop experiences: designing for interactional embodiment

works.title: Design Representations of Moving Bodies for Interactive, Motion-Sensing Spaces
works.description: Compares ways of representing movement for design — Labanotation, video, scores, personas of movement — and what each lets designers see about the moving body.
works.description_zh: 比较为设计表示动作的各种方式——Laban 记谱法、视频、动作谱、动作人物画像——以及每种方式让设计师看见运动身体的哪些方面。
works.idea_en: How a designer notates movement shapes what they can feel and design; choose representations that keep the mover's experience.
works.idea_zh: 设计师如何记录动作，决定了他们能感受到并设计什么；应选择能保留动者经验的表示方式。
works.method: Design case of an interactive motion-sensing space, with representations drawn from dance notation and interaction design.
works.method_zh: 以一个交互式动作感应空间为设计案例，采用来自舞蹈记谱与交互设计的表示方法。

paper.title: Design representations of moving bodies for interactive, motion-sensing spaces

works.title_zh: 交互式动作感应空间中运动身体的设计表示

works.title: Enactive Intersubjectivity: Participatory Sense-Making and Mutual Incorporation
works.description: Fuchs and De Jaegher describe social understanding as bodies in interaction: through coordinated movement and rhythm, each partner's body extends into the other's, creating meaning neither makes alone.
works.description_zh: Fuchs 与 De Jaegher 把社会理解描述为互动中的身体：通过协调的动作与节律，每个人的身体都延伸进对方的身体，创造出单方无法独自产生的意义。
works.idea_en: Understanding others is not mind-reading but mutual incorporation: two bodies forming one felt system.
works.idea_zh: 理解他人不是“读心”，而是相互吸纳：两个身体构成一个被共同感受的系统。
works.method: Theoretical paper combining Merleau-Ponty's intercorporeality with dynamical systems and developmental studies of interaction.
works.method_zh: 把 Merleau-Ponty 的身体间性与动力系统和互动发展研究相结合的理论论文。

paper.title: Enactive intersubjectivity: Participatory sense-making and mutual incorporation

works.title_zh: 生成的主体间性：参与式意义生成与相互吸纳

works.title: My 12 Pairs of Legs
works.description: In a short TED talk Aimee Mullins shows her prosthetic legs, from carbon-fibre sprinting legs to carved wooden legs, and explains how each changes her height, gait and self.
works.description_zh: 在一场简短的 TED 演讲中，Aimee Mullins 展示她的义肢——从碳纤维短跑腿到雕花木腿——并讲述每一双如何改变她的身高、步态和自我。
works.idea_en: With exchangeable legs, the body is chosen daily from inside: prosthetics can widen, not only restore, how a person can feel and appear.
works.idea_zh: 有了可更换的腿，身体每天都从内部被选择：义体不只是修复，还能拓宽一个人的感受与呈现方式。
works.method: Talk and demonstration with legs including Cheetah running blades and hand-carved wooden legs she wore on Alexander McQueen's 1999 runway.
works.method_zh: 演讲与展示，所示义肢包括猎豹跑步刀片和她在 1999 年 Alexander McQueen 秀场上穿的手工雕刻木腿。

works.title: On Being Supple: In Search of Rigor without Rigidity
works.description: Proposes 'supple' interaction — social, emotional, bodily — and asks how to evaluate it with rigour but without the rigid metrics of task performance.
works.description_zh: 提出“柔韧的”（supple）交互——社会的、情感的、身体的——并探讨如何以严谨而不僵硬的方式评估它，不再依赖任务绩效指标。
works.idea_en: Evaluating felt, bodily experience needs methods as flexible as the experience itself.
works.idea_zh: 评估被感受的身体经验，需要与经验本身一样灵活的方法。
works.method: Position paper drawing on the authors' affective and movement-based systems (eMoto, SenToy, games).
works.method_zh: 立场论文，取材于作者的情感与动作系统（eMoto、SenToy、游戏）。

paper.title: On being supple: in search of rigor without rigidity in meeting new design and evaluation challenges for HCI practitioners

works.title_zh: 论柔韧：寻求不僵化的严谨

works.title: Synchronous Objects for One Flat Thing, reproduced
works.description: An online set of visualisations that reveal the hidden counterpoint in Forsythe's dance for 17 dancers and 20 tables: cues, alignments and timing between bodies.
works.description_zh: 一组在线可视化，揭示 Forsythe 为 17 名舞者与 20 张桌子创作的舞蹈中隐藏的对位：身体之间的提示、呼应与时间关系。
works.idea_en: Choreography is a system of attention between dancers; data can show how bodies cue and align with each other.
works.idea_zh: 编舞是舞者之间的注意力系统；数据可以显示身体如何互相提示与对齐。
works.method: Annotation of multi-camera video of the dance, turned into animations and interactive objects by The Forsythe Company and Ohio State University (Palazzi, Zuniga Shaw).
works.method_zh: 对多机位舞蹈视频进行标注，再由 The Forsythe Company 与俄亥俄州立大学（Palazzi、Zuniga Shaw）制成动画与互动对象。

paper.title: Synchronous Objects for One Flat Thing, reproduced

works.title: Wekinator
works.description: Free software for interactive machine learning: a person demonstrates gestures with a sensor or camera, pairs them with sounds or visuals, and trains a model on the spot.
works.description_zh: 一款用于交互式机器学习的免费软件：人用传感器或摄像头示范手势，把它们与声音或影像配对，当场训练模型。
works.idea_en: Teaching a model by moving lets designers keep the knowledge in their body, tuning a mapping by feel rather than by code.
works.idea_zh: 通过运动来训练模型，让设计者把知识留在身体里，凭感觉而不是凭代码去调整映射。
works.method: Real-time supervised learning (classification, regression) from OSC inputs to outputs; the user records examples, trains, plays and re-trains in a loop.
works.method_zh: 对 OSC 输入到输出做实时监督学习（分类、回归）；使用者循环进行录制示例、训练、演奏与再训练。

paper.title: Machine Learning as Meta-Instrument: Human-Machine Partnerships Shaping Expressive Instrumental Creation

works.title: Animal Superpowers
works.description: Wearable devices give children animal senses: an 'ant' device magnifies what their hands touch 50 times, a 'bird' device lets them feel magnetic fields, a 'giraffe' device raises their eyes.
works.description_zh: 可穿戴装置赋予孩子动物的感官：“蚂蚁”装置把手触到的东西放大 50 倍，“鸟”装置让他们感到磁场，“长颈鹿”装置抬高他们的视线。
works.idea_en: Changing the scale and senses of a child's body is a playful way to feel that other creatures live in different worlds.
works.idea_zh: 改变孩子身体的尺度与感官，是一种感受“其他生物生活在不同世界里”的游戏方式。
works.method: Hand-worn cameras with helmet displays, a vibrating GPS/compass device and periscope-like goggles, made as playful critical-design objects.
works.method_zh: 手戴摄像头配头盔显示器、振动的 GPS 与指南针装置、潜望镜式护目镜，作为游戏性的批判设计物件。

works.title: Body Consciousness: A Philosophy of Mindfulness and Somaesthetics
works.description: Shusterman reads Merleau-Ponty, Foucault, Beauvoir, Wittgenstein, James and Dewey to argue that explicit, reflective body awareness is worth cultivating, against the view that it disturbs spontaneous action.
works.description_zh: Shusterman 通过解读 Merleau-Ponty、Foucault、Beauvoir、Wittgenstein、James 与 Dewey，论证明确的、反思性的身体觉察值得培养，反驳它会干扰自发行动的观点。
works.idea_en: Habits live in the body-mind; to change them you must first notice, through trained attention, how you actually move and feel.
works.idea_zh: 习惯存在于身心之中；要改变它们，必须先通过训练过的注意力，觉察自己实际上如何运动与感受。
works.method: Philosophical critique combined with Shusterman's own Feldenkrais practice, using examples such as neck tension, breathing and posture.
works.method_zh: 哲学批判结合 Shusterman 自身的 Feldenkrais 实践，以颈部紧张、呼吸与姿态等为例展开。

paper.title: Body Consciousness: A Philosophy of Mindfulness and Somaesthetics

works.title: Choreographic Language Agent
works.description: Software that generates abstract, moving visual prompts for dancers to translate into movement; its interactive form 'Becoming' was used to create the piece Atomos (2013).
works.description_zh: 一个软件，生成抽象、流动的视觉提示，由舞者把它转化为动作；其互动形态“Becoming”被用于创作作品《Atomos》（2013）。
works.idea_en: Choreography is thinking with the body; an agent can provoke that thinking without replacing it.
works.idea_zh: 编舞是用身体思考；智能体可以激发这种思考，而不取代它。
works.method: Rule-based and generative graphics developed with cognitive scientists and digital artists, projected in the studio as a creative partner during rehearsal.
works.method_zh: 与认知科学家和数字艺术家共同开发的基于规则的生成图形，在排练时投影于排练厅，作为创作伙伴。
exhibited: Thinking with the Body, Wellcome Collection 2013–14

works.title: Electric Stimulus to Face
works.description: Electrodes on the faces of Manabe and his friends deliver electrical muscle stimulation driven by music, so their faces twitch and grimace in rhythm while they sit still.
works.description_zh: 贴在真锅大度及其朋友脸上的电极，按照音乐施加肌肉电刺激，他们静坐不动，脸却随节奏抽动、做出怪相。
works.idea_en: When an outside signal moves your face, the link between expression and feeling becomes strange and visible.
works.idea_zh: 当外部信号驱动你的脸时，表情与感受之间的联系变得陌生而可见。
works.method: Custom EMS device controlled from music software, with myoelectric sensors in later tests to pass facial movement between people.
works.method_zh: 由音乐软件控制的定制肌肉电刺激装置，后续测试中加入肌电传感器，在人与人之间传递面部动作。

works.title: If I Were You: Perceptual Illusion of Body Swapping
works.description: Seeing through cameras on another person's head while shaking hands with them, participants felt the other person's body as their own and their own as someone else's.
works.description_zh: 通过戴在另一人头上的摄像机观看，同时与对方握手，参与者把对方的身体感受为自己的，而把自己的身体感受为别人的。
works.idea_en: The boundary between my body and yours is held by synchrony of sight and touch; change it, and bodies can be swapped.
works.idea_zh: 我的身体与你的身体之间的边界靠视觉与触觉的同步维持；改变它，身体就可以互换。
works.method: Head-mounted cameras on a mannequin or experimenter stream to the participant's HMD; synchronous squeezing and handshakes, with threat-evoked skin conductance.
works.method_zh: 装在人体模型或实验者头部的摄像机把画面传到参与者的头显；同步的捏压与握手，并测量威胁诱发的皮肤电反应。

paper.title: If I Were You: Perceptual Illusion of Body Swapping

works.title_zh: 如果我是你：身体互换的知觉错觉

works.title: Kinesthetic Interaction: Revealing the Bodily Potential in Interaction Design
works.description: Fogtmann, Fritsch and Kortbek define kinesthetic interaction as a concept for designing with the body's kinaesthetic sense, with design parameters such as engagement, sociality and movability.
works.description_zh: Fogtmann、Fritsch 与 Kortbek 把“动觉交互”定义为借助身体动觉进行设计的概念，并提出投入度、社会性与可动性等设计参数。
works.idea_en: The kinaesthetic sense, how we feel our own movement, is a material designers can work with directly.
works.idea_zh: 动觉——我们对自身运动的感受——是设计师可以直接使用的材料。
works.method: Theoretical framework drawing on physiology and phenomenology, applied to interactive installations for movement.
works.method_zh: 借鉴生理学与现象学的理论框架，应用于鼓励运动的交互装置。

paper.title: Kinesthetic interaction: revealing the bodily potential in interaction design

works.title_zh: 动觉交互：揭示交互设计中的身体潜能

works.title: Les Archives du Cœur
works.description: An archive of recorded human heartbeats, collected from people around the world since 2008 and housed on Teshima island, Japan, where visitors listen to strangers' hearts, record their own, and stand in a dark room where a bulb pulses with a heartbeat.
works.description_zh: 一座人类心跳录音档案，自 2008 年起在世界各地收集，收藏于日本丰岛；来访者可以聆听陌生人的心跳、录下自己的心跳，并走进一间灯泡随心跳明灭的暗室。
works.idea_en: The sound of a heartbeat is at once anonymous and unmistakably a living person; hearing it in the dark makes one's own life felt as fragile and shared.
works.idea_zh: 心跳声既是匿名的，又无疑属于一个活着的人；在黑暗中聆听它，会让人感到自己的生命既脆弱又与他人相连。
works.method: Heartbeats are recorded in a recording room (likely with a stethoscope-style microphone), stored in a small permanent museum for listening, and visitors take their own recording home on CD; a heart room links a bulb to amplified heartbeat sound.
works.method_zh: 在录音室中录下心跳（很可能使用听诊器式麦克风），存入一座可供聆听的小型永久美术馆，来访者可把自己的录音制成 CD 带回家；“心之房间”让一只灯泡与放大的心跳声联动。

works.title: United-pulse
works.description: A pair of rings for lovers apart: each ring measures its wearer's pulse and taps it softly onto the partner's finger.
works.description_zh: 为分隔两地的恋人设计的一对戒指：每只戒指测量佩戴者的脉搏，再轻轻敲打到伴侣的手指上。
works.idea_en: A pulse felt on the skin is a quiet way of being with someone, closer to presence than to messaging.
works.idea_zh: 在皮肤上感受到的脉搏是一种安静的陪伴方式，更接近在场，而不是发讯息。
works.method: A pulse sensor and a small actuator in each ring, likely linked wirelessly through the wearers' phones.
works.method_zh: 每只戒指内有脉搏传感器与小型执行器，很可能经由佩戴者的手机无线相连。

paper.title: United-pulse: feeling your partner's pulse

works.title: BodyBug
works.description: A small creature-like device that slides along a strap worn on the body and reacts to the wearer's movement, inviting full-body, dance-like play.
works.description_zh: 一个像小生物的设备，沿着穿戴在身上的绑带滑动，并对穿戴者的动作作出反应，邀请全身的、舞蹈般的玩耍。
works.idea_en: Movement interaction should start from people's own movement experience, drawing on modern dance, rather than from sensor capabilities.
works.idea_zh: 动作交互应当从人们自身的动作经验出发（借鉴现代舞），而不是从传感器能力出发。
works.method: Accelerometer-equipped device that climbs a wire strapped to the body, designed from movement workshops; later sold as Oriboo.
works.method_zh: 装有加速度计的设备沿绑在身上的线攀爬，从动作工作坊中设计而来；后来以 Oriboo 为名上市。

paper.title: From hand-held to body-worn: embodied experiences of the design and use of a wearable movement-based interaction concept

works.title: Closer: Performance, Technologies, Phenomenology
works.description: Kozel's book that researches telematic dance, motion capture and wearables from inside her own performing body, developing phenomenology as a hands-on research method.
works.description_zh: Kozel 的专著：从她自己表演着的身体内部，研究远程舞蹈、动作捕捉与可穿戴物，把现象学发展为一种亲身实践的研究方法。
works.idea_en: The researcher's dancing body can be a precise instrument for understanding technology, if its experience is described with care.
works.idea_zh: 只要细致地描述经验，研究者跳舞的身体就能成为理解技术的精确工具。
works.method: Book (MIT Press, Leonardo series) combining Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology with first-person accounts of the author's performances.
works.method_zh: 专著（MIT 出版社 Leonardo 丛书），把 Merleau-Ponty 的现象学与作者表演的第一人称叙述结合起来。

paper.title: Closer: Performance, Technologies, Phenomenology

works.title: Embodied Imagination: A Hybrid Method of Designing for Intimacy
works.description: A method that combines dance improvisation with design scenarios so that participants imagine future intimate technologies through their own bodies.
works.description_zh: 把舞蹈即兴与设计情境结合的方法，让参与者借自己的身体去想象未来的亲密技术。
works.idea_en: Imagination is embodied: moving with another person makes possible technologies for intimacy felt before they are built.
works.idea_zh: 想象是具身的：与另一个人一起动起来，能让尚未造出的亲密技术先被感受到。
works.method: Workshops mixing improvisation scores, props and discussion, developed around wearable and intimate technologies.
works.method_zh: 工作坊融合即兴谱、道具与讨论，围绕可穿戴与亲密技术展开。

paper.title: Embodied imagination: a hybrid method of designing for intimacy

works.title_zh: 具身想象：为亲密而设计的混合方法

works.title: How Emotion Is Made and Measured
works.description: A critique of affective computing's 'informational' view of emotion as an internal state to be sensed and transmitted, proposing instead an 'interactional' view in which emotion is made in social and cultural interaction.
works.description_zh: 对情感计算“信息观”的批判：该观点把情绪看作可被感测和传输的内部状态；作者提出“互动观”，认为情绪是在社会与文化互动中被造就的。
works.idea_en: Design should help people experience, interpret and reflect on their own emotions rather than have a system decide what they feel, which is the ground of affective loops.
works.idea_zh: 设计应帮助人们体验、诠释并反思自己的情绪，而不是由系统判定他们感受到什么，这正是情感回路的基础。
works.method: A theoretical argument drawing on social and cultural accounts of emotion, with design examples of interactional systems (International Journal of Human-Computer Studies, 2007; with Rogério DePaula and Paul Dourish).
works.method_zh: 借助关于情绪的社会与文化理论进行论证，并给出互动式系统的设计示例（《国际人机研究期刊》，2007；合著者 Rogério DePaula、Paul Dourish）。

paper.title: How emotion is made and measured

works.title_zh: 情绪如何被造就与测量

works.title: Jogging over a Distance
works.description: Two runners in different places talk through headsets while jogging; if one runs harder than usual relative to their heart rate, their voice seems to come from ahead, otherwise from behind.
works.description_zh: 身处两地的跑者边跑边通过耳机交谈；若一方相对自身心率跑得更努力，其声音就像从前方传来，否则从后方传来。
works.idea_en: Mapping effort, not speed, lets people of different fitness run 'together' and feel each other's exertion.
works.idea_zh: 映射的是用力程度而不是速度，让体能不同的人也能“一起”跑，并感受彼此的用力。
works.method: Heart-rate monitors and mobile phones compare each jogger's heart rate to a personal target and place the partner's voice in spatial audio accordingly.
works.method_zh: 心率监测与手机把每位跑者的心率和个人目标比较，并据此把同伴的声音放在空间音频中的相应位置。

paper.title: Jogging over a distance between Europe and Australia

works.title: Mind in Life: Biology, Phenomenology, and the Sciences of Mind
works.description: Thompson argues for a deep continuity of life and mind: the self-organising processes of living organisms already carry the basic structure of sense-making that experience develops.
works.description_zh: Thompson 主张生命与心智的深度连续性：生命体自我组织的过程本身就具有意义生成的基本结构，经验在此之上展开。
works.idea_en: Where there is life there is mind; the felt body is the living organism experiencing itself, not a container for a mind.
works.idea_zh: 有生命之处就有心智；被感受的身体是生命体对自身的经验，而不是装着心智的容器。
works.method: Combines autopoiesis and dynamical systems theory with Husserlian phenomenology of time, emotion and empathy.
works.method_zh: 把自创生、动力系统理论与 Husserl 关于时间、情绪和移情的现象学相结合。

paper.title: Mind in Life: Biology, Phenomenology, and the Sciences of Mind
paper.venue: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press

works.title_zh: 生命中的心智：生物学、现象学和心智科学

works.title: Move to Get Moved: A Search for Methods, Tools and Knowledge to Design for Expressive and Rich Movement-Based Interaction
works.description: Hummels, Overbeeke and Klooster argue that movement-based interaction should aim at expressive, rich movement that engages people's perceptual-motor, emotional and social skills, and propose design methods to get there.
works.description_zh: Hummels、Overbeeke 与 Klooster 主张基于动作的交互应追求富有表现力的、丰富的动作，调动人的知觉运动、情感与社会技能，并提出实现这一目标的设计方法。
works.idea_en: Designers must move to be moved: bodily skill and emotion are one, and designing movement requires moving yourself.
works.idea_zh: 设计师要“动起来才能被打动”：身体技能与情感是一体的，设计动作就要亲身去动。
works.method: Reflection on design cases and education at TU/e, drawing on phenomenology and Gibson's ecological psychology.
works.method_zh: 基于埃因霍温理工大学的设计案例与教学反思，借鉴现象学与 Gibson 的生态心理学。

paper.title: Move to get moved: a search for methods, tools and knowledge to design for expressive and rich movement-based interaction

works.title_zh: 动起来才能被打动：为富有表现力的动作交互寻找方法、工具与知识

works.title: The Case against Perfection: Ethics in the Age of Genetic Engineering
works.description: Sandel argues against enhancement in sport, parenting and genetics, saying the drive to master our nature erodes humility, responsibility and solidarity.
works.description_zh: Sandel 反对体育、育儿与遗传学中的增强，认为驾驭自身本性的冲动会侵蚀谦逊、责任与团结。
works.idea_en: His idea of the 'giftedness' of life fits soma design's attitude of appreciating the body one has before trying to fix it.
works.idea_zh: 他所说生命的“被赐予性”契合身体设计的态度：先欣赏自己拥有的身体，再考虑修正它。
works.method: Short philosophical book grown out of his work on the President's Council on Bioethics and a 2004 Atlantic essay.
works.method_zh: 一部简短的哲学著作，源于他在美国总统生命伦理委员会的工作和 2004 年发表于《大西洋月刊》的文章。

paper.title: The Case against Perfection: Ethics in the Age of Genetic Engineering

works.title_zh: 反对完美：科技与人性的正义之战

works.title: The Experimental Induction of Out-of-Body Experiences
works.description: Participants see themselves from behind through goggles fed by cameras while their chest is touched, and report feeling located outside their own body, where the cameras are.
works.description_zh: 参与者通过接在摄像机上的眼镜从背后看见自己，同时胸口被触碰，他们报告感到自己位于身体之外、摄像机所在之处。
works.idea_en: Where 'I' am is felt, not known: with the right sensory match the self can step out of its own body.
works.idea_zh: “我”在哪里是被感受到的，而不是被知道的；只要感官匹配得当，自我可以走出自己的身体。
works.method: Stereo cameras behind the participant feed an HMD; a rod touches the real chest while moving toward the illusory body; skin conductance to a threat measured.
works.method_zh: 放在参与者身后的立体摄像机把画面送入头显；一根棍子触碰真实的胸口，同时朝错觉中的身体移动；测量面对威胁时的皮肤电反应。

paper.title: The Experimental Induction of Out-of-Body Experiences

works.title: The Feel Dimension of Technology Interaction: Exploring Tangibles through Movement and Touch
works.description: Larssen, Robertson and Edwards argue that interaction with technology should be understood from how it feels to the moving body, using kinaesthetic and tactile experience rather than visual appearance as the design lens.
works.description_zh: Larssen、Robertson 与 Edwards 主张从运动中的身体“感觉如何”来理解技术交互，以动觉与触觉经验而非视觉外观作为设计视角。
works.idea_en: How an interaction feels in the mover's body is a design dimension in its own right.
works.idea_zh: 交互在动作者身体中的感受，本身就是一个设计维度。
works.method: Conceptual paper grounded in Merleau-Ponty and illustrated with analysis of movement-based and tangible interactions.
works.method_zh: 以 Merleau-Ponty 为理论基础，并以对动作与有形交互的分析加以说明的概念性论文。

paper.title: The feel dimension of technology interaction: exploring tangibles through movement and touch

works.title_zh: 技术交互的感觉维度：通过动作与触碰探索有形交互

works.title: The Meaning of the Body: Aesthetics of Human Understanding
works.description: Johnson argues that meaning begins below words, in felt qualities, emotions and movement, and that aesthetics, the study of how things feel, is therefore the ground of all understanding.
works.description_zh: Johnson 主张意义始于语言之下，在被感受的品质、情绪与动作之中；因此研究“事物如何被感受”的美学，是一切理解的基础。
works.idea_en: Meaning is felt before it is thought; the qualities of bodily experience are where sense begins.
works.idea_zh: 意义先被感受，后被思考；身体经验的品质是意义开始的地方。
works.method: Pragmatist philosophy drawing on Dewey, James, Gendlin and cognitive neuroscience, with examples from music, painting and infant development.
works.method_zh: 以 Dewey、James、Gendlin 与认知神经科学为资源的实用主义哲学，以音乐、绘画与婴儿发展为例。

paper.title: The Meaning of the Body: Aesthetics of Human Understanding

works.title_zh: 身体的意义：人类理解的美学

works.title: Understanding Movement for Interaction Design
works.description: Compares several frameworks for describing movement, from HCI models to Labanotation, by applying them to players of a camera-based body game.
works.description_zh: 把从人机交互模型到 Laban 舞谱的几种动作描述框架，应用到一款摄像头体感游戏的玩家身上加以比较。
works.idea_en: Each framework makes a different aspect of the moving body visible; designers need dance-derived vocabularies to see movement quality.
works.idea_zh: 每个框架让运动身体的不同面向变得可见；设计者需要来自舞蹈的词汇才能看见动作质感。
works.method: Analytic comparison of frameworks on video of EyeToy game play, with Laban-based notation of players' movements.
works.method_zh: 以 EyeToy 游戏过程的视频为材料比较各框架，并用 Laban 记谱记录玩家的动作。

paper.title: Understanding movement for interaction design: frameworks and approaches

works.title: Video Ergo Sum
works.description: Wearing a head-mounted display, participants see a video of their own back being stroked two metres in front of them while their real back is stroked, and begin to feel that body as theirs.
works.description_zh: 参与者戴着头戴显示器，看到自己背部在前方两米处被抚摸的影像，同时真实的背部也被抚摸，于是开始把那个身体感受为自己的。
works.idea_en: The felt 'I am here, in this body' can be shifted with a camera and a brush: self-location is part of the living, adjustable soma.
works.idea_zh: “我在这里、在这个身体里”的感受可以用一台摄像机和一支画笔挪动：自我定位是活的、可调节的身体的一部分。
works.method: Full-body illusion with a camera filming the participant from behind into an HMD, synchronous or asynchronous back-stroking, then drift in self-location measured.
works.method_zh: 全身错觉：摄像机从背后拍摄参与者并送入头显，进行同步或不同步的背部抚触，再测量自我定位的漂移。

paper.title: Video Ergo Sum: Manipulating Bodily Self-Consciousness

works.title: hipDisk
works.description: Two stiff disks worn around the hips and chest sound a note when the wearer bends their torso to bring the disks' edges together, so the body becomes a playable instrument.
works.description_zh: 两片硬质圆盘分别戴在髋部与胸部，穿戴者弯曲躯干使圆盘边缘相碰时会发出音符，身体成了可以演奏的乐器。
works.idea_en: An awkward, funny wearable can extend how people move and make the torso's range of motion newly felt.
works.idea_zh: 一件别扭又好笑的可穿戴设备，可以拓展人的动作方式，让躯干的活动范围被重新感受到。
works.method: Contact points around the edges of the two disks trigger tones, so each torso tilt plays a pitch; explored in performance and workshops.
works.method_zh: 两片圆盘边缘的接触点触发音高，每次躯干倾斜都会奏出一个音；在表演与工作坊中探索。

paper.venue: International Journal of Performance Arts and Digital Media
paper.title: hipDisk: Using sound to encourage physical extension, exploring humour in interface design

works.title: soft(n)
works.description: A group of soft, pillow-like networked objects responds when people hold, stroke or hug them, passing touch on to each other as vibration, light and sound.
works.description_zh: 一组柔软、枕头般的联网物件在被抱住、抚摸或拥抱时作出回应，并以振动、光与声音把触摸传给彼此。
works.idea_en: The paper that introduced Shusterman's somaesthetics to HCI: design for how touch feels, not only for what it triggers.
works.idea_zh: 这是把 Shusterman 的身体美学引入人机交互的论文：为触摸的感受而设计，而不只是为它触发什么而设计。
works.method: Soft tangible objects with embedded touch sensing and vibration/light/sound actuators, networked so that touching one affects others; designed with V2_Lab.
works.method_zh: 柔软的可触物件内置触摸传感与振动、光、声音执行器，彼此联网，触碰一个会影响其他；与 V2_Lab 合作设计。

paper.title: soft(n): toward a somaesthetics of touch

works.title: A Leg to Stand On: Prosthetics, Metaphor, and Materiality
works.description: Sobchack, who lives with an above-knee prosthesis, writes about how the leg actually feels and behaves, and criticises theorists who use 'prosthesis' as a loose metaphor.
works.description_zh: 膝上截肢、使用义肢生活的 Sobchack 写下这条腿实际的感受与表现，并批评把“义体”当作随意隐喻的理论家。
works.idea_en: The prosthetic body is lived through balance, fatigue, sound and skin; any theory of augmentation should start from that first-person material experience.
works.idea_zh: 义体身体是通过平衡、疲劳、声音与皮肤被活出来的；任何关于增强的理论都应从这种第一人称的物质经验出发。
works.method: Phenomenological essay grounded in her own experience of amputation and rehabilitation, published in the edited volume The Prosthetic Impulse.
works.method_zh: 基于她自身截肢与康复经验的现象学文章，收录于论文集《The Prosthetic Impulse》。

paper.venue: In M. Smith & J. Morra (eds.), The Prosthetic Impulse, MIT Press, 2006
paper.title: A Leg to Stand On: Prosthetics, Metaphor, and Materiality

works.title_zh: 一条立足之腿：义肢、隐喻与物质性

works.title: Affective Diary
works.description: The Affective Diary pairs a biosensor armband with a tablet diary: in the evening, the day's arousal and movement appear as ambiguous, colourful body figures next to the user's text messages and photos, and the user can scribble on them.
works.description_zh: Affective Diary 把生物传感臂环与平板日记结合：晚上，当天的唤醒与活动数据以模糊、彩色的人形出现在用户的短信和照片旁，用户可以在上面随手涂写。
works.idea_en: Body data works best as an open mirror: vague shapes invite people to remember how the day felt instead of telling them what they felt.
works.idea_zh: 身体数据最好是一面开放的镜子：模糊的形状邀请人回忆那一天的感受，而不是告诉他们“你感觉到了什么”。
works.method: A SenseWear armband logs galvanic skin response and step counts; a Tablet PC renders them as abstract, posture-like figures on a timeline with mobile phone data; studied with users over several weeks (with Microsoft Research Cambridge).
works.method_zh: SenseWear 臂环记录皮肤电和步数；平板电脑把它们与手机数据一起，在时间轴上呈现为抽象的、姿态般的人形；与剑桥微软研究院合作，由用户使用数周进行研究。

paper.title: Experiencing the Affective Diary

works.title: Ear on Arm
works.description: After years of planning, surgeons grew an ear-shaped scaffold under the skin of Stelarc's left forearm; it is meant eventually to carry a microphone streaming what it hears online.
works.description_zh: 经过多年筹划，外科医生在 Stelarc 左前臂的皮下培育出一个耳朵形状的支架；最终设想是在其中放入麦克风，把它“听到”的声音在线传播。
works.idea_en: An extra organ can be grown into the body, but living with it is slow and fragile: infection, healing and skin decide the work as much as the idea.
works.idea_zh: 一个额外的器官可以长进身体，但与它共存缓慢而脆弱：感染、愈合与皮肤和想法本身一样决定着这件作品。
works.method: A porous biopolymer scaffold was implanted under the skin in staged surgeries so tissue and blood vessels could grow into it; a microphone was tested and removed after infection.
works.method_zh: 分阶段手术把多孔生物聚合物支架植入皮下，让组织和血管长入其中；曾测试植入麦克风，因感染而取出。

works.title: Fairground: Thrill Laboratory
works.description: Riders on real fairground rides wear sensors and cameras; their heart rate, face and screams are shown live to the crowd, who watch the ride from the inside of another body.
works.description_zh: 真实游乐设施上的乘客佩戴传感器与摄像头；他们的心率、面部与尖叫被实时展示给人群，观众得以从另一个身体内部观看这趟旅程。
works.idea_en: Thrill is social: making a rider's bodily state visible turns spectators into participants in someone else's fear and joy.
works.idea_zh: 刺激感是社会性的：让乘客的身体状态可见，就把旁观者变成了他人恐惧与欢乐的参与者。
works.method: Telemetry of heart rate, acceleration, audio and video from riders streamed to a spectator display; studied as a performance frame.
works.method_zh: 把乘客的心率、加速度、音频与视频遥测数据传到观众屏幕上，并作为表演框架加以研究。

paper.title: Performing thrill: designing telemetry systems and spectator interfaces for amusement rides

works.title: Getting a Grip on Tangible Interaction: A Framework on Physical Space and Social Interaction
works.description: Hornecker and Buur propose a framework for tangible interaction with four themes, tangible manipulation, spatial interaction, embodied facilitation and expressive representation, that treats bodily movement in space as interaction.
works.description_zh: Hornecker 与 Buur 提出有形交互的框架，包含四个主题：有形操作、空间交互、具身促成与表现性表征，把身体在空间中的运动视为交互。
works.idea_en: Bodies in space are always interacting, with things and with each other; design should shape that whole-body, social situation.
works.idea_zh: 空间中的身体始终在与物、与彼此互动；设计要塑造的是这一全身的、社会性的情境。
works.method: Conceptual framework derived from literature and case studies of tangible and interactive installations.
works.method_zh: 从文献与有形/交互装置案例研究中推导出的概念框架。

paper.title: Getting a grip on tangible interaction: a framework on physical space and social interaction

works.title_zh: 把握有形交互：关于物理空间与社会互动的框架

works.title: Glow
works.description: A 27-minute duet between a dancer on the floor and projected light that tracks, outlines and extends her body as it moves.
works.description_zh: 一段 27 分钟的双人舞：舞者在地面上舞动，投影光追踪、勾勒并延伸她的身体。
works.idea_en: Projection that answers the body in real time can make the dancer's own kinesphere visible and strange.
works.idea_zh: 实时回应身体的投影，可以让舞者自身的动作空间变得可见而陌生。
works.method: Infrared camera tracking from above drives real-time generative graphics projected onto the floor (software by Frieder Weiss).
works.method_zh: 从上方的红外摄像追踪驱动实时生成图形并投影到地面（软件由 Frieder Weiss 开发）。

works.title: Haptic Radar / Extended Skin
works.description: A headband of modules that each sense the distance to nearby objects and vibrate when something approaches, letting blindfolded wearers dodge objects approaching from behind, like insect antennae or whiskers.
works.description_zh: 一个由多个模块组成的头带，每个模块感知与附近物体的距离，有东西靠近时便振动，让蒙眼的佩戴者像昆虫触角或胡须那样躲开从背后接近的物体。
works.idea_en: Skin can be extended into the surrounding space, so that the edge of the felt body moves out beyond the physical one.
works.idea_zh: 皮肤可以延伸到周围的空间，让被感受到的身体边界超出物理身体。
works.method: Infrared rangefinders paired with vibration motors, each module acting as an 'optical antenna'; tested with participants avoiding unseen approaching objects.
works.method_zh: 红外测距器与振动马达成对组成模块，每个模块如同一根“光学触角”；测试参与者能否避开看不见的靠近物体。

paper.title: Augmenting spatial awareness with Haptic Radar

works.title_zh: 触觉雷达 / 延展皮肤

works.title: Heart Chamber Orchestra
works.description: Twelve classical musicians wear heart sensors; their heartbeats generate the musical score in real time, which they read from screens and play, so the music feeds back into the hearts that write it.
works.description_zh: 十二位古典乐手佩戴心脏传感器；他们的心跳实时生成乐谱，乐手看着屏幕演奏，于是音乐又反过来作用于书写它的心脏。
works.idea_en: A performance is a loop between bodies and sound: the players' excitement shapes the score, and the score shapes their excitement.
works.idea_zh: 表演是一个身体与声音之间的回路：乐手的激动塑造乐谱，乐谱又塑造他们的激动。
works.method: ECG sensors stream the musicians' heartbeats to software that generates notation and visuals live on stage.
works.method_zh: 心电传感器把乐手的心跳传给软件，在台上实时生成乐谱与影像。

works.title: How Bodies Matter: Five Themes for Interaction Design
works.description: Klemmer, Hartmann and Takayama distil five themes from embodied cognition for interaction design: thinking through doing, performance, visibility, risk, and thickness of practice.
works.description_zh: Klemmer、Hartmann 与 Takayama 从具身认知中提炼出五个交互设计主题：通过做来思考、表演、可见性、风险与实践的厚度。
works.idea_en: People think with their hands and bodies, so interfaces that strip away bodily engagement also strip away thinking.
works.idea_zh: 人用手和身体思考；剥夺身体参与的界面，也剥夺了思考。
works.method: Synthesis of research from psychology, education, sociology and philosophy into design themes, with examples from tangible interfaces.
works.method_zh: 把心理学、教育、社会学与哲学的研究综合为设计主题，并以有形界面为例。

paper.title: How bodies matter: five themes for interaction design

works.title_zh: 身体何以重要：交互设计的五个主题

works.title: Pulse Room
works.description: A visitor grips a sensor and a bare light bulb above starts to flash with their heartbeat; the pulse then moves along a field of hundreds of bulbs, each blinking with the heartbeat of an earlier visitor.
works.description_zh: 观众握住传感器，头顶一只裸灯泡开始随其心跳闪烁；随后这段脉搏沿着数百只灯泡的阵列移动，每只灯泡都在以某位先前观众的心跳闪烁。
works.idea_en: One's own heartbeat, seen as light among hundreds of others, is felt both as intimately personal and as part of a collective pulse.
works.idea_zh: 自己的心跳化作数百盏灯中的一盏光，既被感到是极其私人的，也被感到是集体脉搏的一部分。
works.method: A heart-rate sensor on a handle drives up to 300 incandescent bulbs through dimmers, keeping the most recent recordings; the combined pulses are also heard.
works.method_zh: 手柄上的心率传感器通过调光器驱动多达 300 只白炽灯泡，保存最近的录入；众多脉搏的叠加也可以被听见。

works.title: Staying Open to Interpretation
works.description: An argument that interactive systems, and their evaluations, should support many valid interpretations by users rather than one meaning fixed by the designer.
works.description_zh: 一篇论述：交互系统及其评估，应支持使用者作出多种合理诠释，而不是由设计者固定唯一的意义。
works.idea_en: Leaving body data ambiguous is a design resource: it invites people to bring their own felt sense and context to what a signal means.
works.idea_zh: 让身体数据保持模糊是一种设计资源：它邀请人们把自己的体感与处境带入对信号意义的理解。
works.method: Conceptual analysis with examples from the authors' own design projects and evaluation practices (DIS 2006; with Bill Gaver).
works.method_zh: 以作者自己的设计项目与评估实践为例进行概念分析（DIS 2006；合著者 Bill Gaver）。

paper.title: Staying open to interpretation: engaging multiple meanings in design and evaluation

works.title: The Micro-Phenomenological Interview
works.description: An interview technique that guides a person back into one specific past moment and helps them describe, in fine detail, what they felt and did — gestures, sensations, shifts of attention.
works.description_zh: 一种访谈技巧：引导人回到过去某个具体时刻，帮助他们细致描述当时的感受与动作——手势、感觉、注意力的转移。
works.idea_en: Much of felt experience is pre-reflective; careful questioning can bring it into awareness without imposing interpretations.
works.idea_zh: 许多被感受的经验是前反思的；细致的提问可以把它带入觉察，而不强加解释。
works.method: Second-person interview protocol (evocation of a singular experience, open 'how' questions, redirection from content to process).
works.method_zh: 第二人称访谈流程（唤起一次具体经验、开放的“如何”提问、从内容转向过程）。

paper.title: Describing one's subjective experience in the second person: An interview method for the science of consciousness

works.title: The Sensual Evaluation Instrument
works.description: A set of eight smooth, abstract sculpted objects that people hold and arrange to show how they feel while using a system, as a nonverbal alternative to questionnaires.
works.description_zh: 一组八个光滑、抽象的雕塑物件，人们在使用系统时握着、摆放它们来表达感受，作为问卷之外的非语言选择。
works.idea_en: Feelings are bodily; letting people answer with their hands captures affect that words and rating scales flatten.
works.idea_zh: 情绪是身体性的；让人用手来回答，能捕捉到被语言和评分量表压平的情感。
works.method: Hand-sized sculpted objects made by an artist co-author, tested in user and cross-cultural studies (with Jarmo Laaksolahti).
works.method_zh: 由一位艺术家合作者雕刻的手掌大小物件，并在用户研究与跨文化研究中检验（与 Jarmo Laaksolahti 合著）。

paper.title: The sensual evaluation instrument: developing an affective evaluation tool

works.title: How the Body Shapes the Mind
works.description: Gallagher separates the body schema, the pre-reflective system that runs posture and movement, from the body image, what we perceive and believe about our body, and shows how both shape cognition.
works.description_zh: Gallagher 区分了身体图式（前反思地调控姿态与动作的系统）与身体意象（我们对自身身体的知觉与信念），并说明二者如何塑造认知。
works.idea_en: Much of the mind works through a body schema we never notice; design can act on it without passing through conscious image.
works.idea_zh: 心智的大部分运作依赖我们从未察觉的身体图式；设计可以直接作用于它，而不必经过有意识的身体意象。
works.method: Integrates phenomenology with neuroscience and clinical cases such as deafferentation (Ian Waterman), neonate imitation and schizophrenia.
works.method_zh: 把现象学与神经科学和临床案例相结合，如传入神经阻断（Ian Waterman）、新生儿模仿与精神分裂症。

paper.title: How the Body Shapes the Mind

works.title: Hug over a Distance
works.description: An air-inflatable vest lets couples in long-distance relationships send a hug: when one partner squeezes a koala-shaped soft toy, the other's vest inflates around the torso.
works.description_zh: 一件充气背心让异地伴侣“寄出”拥抱：一方捏一下考拉形状的毛绒玩具，另一方的背心就在躯干周围鼓起。
works.idea_en: An embrace is felt as pressure closing around the torso; the vest designs that closure rather than a signal of affection.
works.idea_zh: 拥抱被感受为环绕躯干收拢的压力；这件背心设计的是那种收拢，而不是一个“表示爱意”的信号。
works.method: A PDA-linked koala with a pressure sensor triggers a pump that inflates air pockets in the partner's vest; tested with couples in a field study.
works.method_zh: 带压力传感器的考拉玩具连着掌上电脑，触发气泵给伴侣背心的气囊充气；以伴侣实地研究检验。

paper.title: Hug over a distance

works.title: In Defense of Posthuman Dignity
works.description: Bostrom replies to bioconservative critics that enhanced 'posthumans' could have dignity too, and that people should be free to use technology to extend their capacities.
works.description_zh: Bostrom 回应生物保守主义批评者：被增强的“后人类”同样可以拥有尊严，人们应当有自由用技术扩展自己的能力。
works.idea_en: The enhancement view in its clearest form; it treats the body mainly as a set of capacities to raise, and says little about how an enhanced body would feel from inside.
works.idea_zh: 增强立场最清晰的表述；它主要把身体看作一组待提升的能力，却很少谈被增强的身体从内部会有怎样的感受。
works.method: Philosophical essay responding to Fukuyama, Kass and the President's Council on Bioethics.
works.method_zh: 回应 Fukuyama、Kass 与美国总统生命伦理委员会的哲学论文。

paper.title: In Defense of Posthuman Dignity

works.title: Making by Making Strange: Defamiliarization and the Design of Domestic Technologies
works.description: Uses ethnographic and historical material to make the ordinary home look strange, so designers can question assumptions built into domestic technology.
works.description_zh: 借民族志与历史材料，让平常的家显得陌生，让设计师能够质疑家用技术中内置的假设。
works.idea_en: What is most familiar — including our own bodily habits — is hardest to design for until it is made strange.
works.idea_zh: 最熟悉的东西——包括我们自己的身体习惯——在被陌生化之前最难为之设计。
works.method: Defamiliarization strategies from literary theory and anthropology (cross-cultural comparison, historical reading, cultural critique).
works.method_zh: 借自文学理论与人类学的陌生化策略（跨文化比较、历史阅读、文化批判）。

paper.title: Making by making strange: Defamiliarization and the design of domestic technologies

works.title_zh: 以陌生化来创造：陌生化与家用技术设计

works.title: Pichet Klunchun and Myself
works.description: Sitting face to face, French choreographer Jérôme Bel and Thai khon dancer Pichet Klunchun ask each other questions and demonstrate movements, explaining what their bodies know and why.
works.description_zh: 法国编舞家 Jérôme Bel 与泰国孔剧舞者 Pichet Klunchun 面对面坐着，互相提问并示范动作，解释各自的身体懂得什么、为什么。
works.idea_en: A dance body is a body of knowledge: putting it into words, in dialogue with a foreign body, reveals assumptions that neither could see alone.
works.idea_zh: 舞蹈的身体是一种知识体系：在与异文化身体的对话中把它说出来，能揭示双方各自看不见的预设。
works.method: Staged conversation and demonstration created in 2005 and toured internationally.
works.method_zh: 舞台上的对话与示范，创作于 2005 年，随后国际巡演。

works.title: Shaking the World / Save YourSelf!!!
works.description: A headset passes weak currents behind the ears (galvanic vestibular stimulation) so the wearer feels pulled left or right; the related art piece Save YourSelf!!! lets visitors feel their balance being shifted from outside.
works.description_zh: 头戴装置在耳后施加微弱电流（电前庭刺激），让穿戴者感到被向左或向右拉；相关艺术作品《Save YourSelf!!!》让观众感受到自己的平衡被外力改变。
works.idea_en: Balance is felt, not given: when technology writes directly to the vestibular sense, the ground itself seems to move and the body's certainty becomes strange.
works.idea_zh: 平衡是被感受出来的，而不是既定的：当技术直接写入前庭觉时，地面仿佛在动，身体的确定感变得陌生。
works.method: Bilateral GVS electrodes on the mastoids driven by a small current controller; the art version likely drives the current from sensor input.
works.method_zh: 在乳突处放置双侧电前庭刺激电极，由小型电流控制器驱动；艺术版本很可能以传感器输入来驱动电流。

paper.title: Shaking the world: galvanic vestibular stimulation as a novel sensation interface

works.title: exhale: breath between bodies
works.description: A group of networked skirts that respond to their wearers' breath: small fans and vibrations let each wearer feel the breath of others in the room.
works.description_zh: 一组联网的裙子会回应穿着者的呼吸：小风扇与振动让每位穿着者感受到房间里其他人的呼吸。
works.idea_en: Breath can be a shared, felt medium between bodies; the garment makes the space between people breathable.
works.idea_zh: 呼吸可以是身体之间共享的、被感受到的介质；衣物让人与人之间的空间变得可以“呼吸”。
works.method: Breath sensors on each wearer drive fans and vibrotactile actuators embedded in the skirts of the other wearers over a wireless network.
works.method_zh: 每位穿着者身上的呼吸传感器通过无线网络驱动其他人裙子里的风扇与振动执行器。

paper.title: exhale: breath between bodies

works.title: feelSpace Belt
works.description: A belt of vibration motors in which the motor pointing north always buzzes; after weeks of wearing it, people reported that space itself felt different, and that they felt secure and 'never lost'.
works.description_zh: 一条装有振动马达的腰带，始终是朝北的那个马达在振动；连续佩戴数周后，人们报告空间本身的感觉变了，并感到安心、“不会迷路”。
works.idea_en: A new sense does not add data on top of experience; it changes how the surrounding space is felt through the body, and the change fades when the belt is removed.
works.idea_zh: 新感官并不是在经验之上叠加数据，而是改变了身体对周围空间的感受；摘下腰带后，这种变化也会消退。
works.method: A ring of vibrotactile motors around the waist driven by an electronic compass; long-term wearing studies with navigation tasks, interviews and questionnaires (Nagel et al. 2005; Kaspar, König et al. 2014).
works.method_zh: 绕腰一圈的振动马达由电子罗盘驱动；包括导航任务、访谈与问卷的长期佩戴研究（Nagel 等 2005；Kaspar、König 等 2014）。

paper.title: Beyond sensory substitution—learning the sixth sense

works.title: Action in Perception
works.description: Noë argues that perception is not something that happens in us but something we do: to perceive is to have practical, bodily knowledge of how sensation changes as we move.
works.description_zh: Noë 主张知觉不是发生在我们身上的事，而是我们去做的事：知觉就是对“运动时感觉如何变化”的实践性、身体性知识。
works.idea_en: Perceiving is a skilful activity of the whole moving body, so changing how we move changes what we feel and see.
works.idea_zh: 知觉是整个运动身体的技能活动，因此改变我们的动作方式就会改变我们的感受与所见。
works.method: Philosophical argument using sensory substitution, change blindness, inverting goggles and touch as test cases for the sensorimotor theory.
works.method_zh: 以感官替代、变化盲视、倒视镜与触觉为检验案例，论证感觉运动理论。

paper.title: Action in Perception

works.title: Bio Mapping
works.description: Participants walk their neighbourhood wearing a skin conductance sensor linked to GPS; afterwards they annotate the peaks of arousal on a map together, producing community 'emotion maps' of places such as Greenwich and San Francisco.
works.description_zh: 参与者佩戴与 GPS 相连的皮肤电传感器在社区里行走，之后一起在地图上为唤醒峰值加注释，形成格林尼治、旧金山等地的社区“情绪地图”。
works.idea_en: A skin conductance peak says little on its own; its meaning comes from the walker's memory and from collective discussion, making body data a starting point for shared stories.
works.idea_zh: 单独一个皮肤电峰值说明不了什么；它的意义来自行走者的记忆与集体讨论，让身体数据成为共同讲述的起点。
works.method: A galvanic skin response logger and a GPS unit record arousal and position; mapping software visualises tracks, and group workshops add annotations (published as Emotional Cartography, 2009).
works.method_zh: 皮肤电记录器与 GPS 记录唤醒与位置；地图软件把轨迹可视化，工作坊中集体添加注释（汇编为 Emotional Cartography，2009）。

works.title: Cardiomorphologies
works.description: A seated participant watches a floor-to-ceiling, mandala-like projection of concentric circles and hears a soundscape that expand and contract with their own breath and heart rate over a 20–30 minute session.
works.description_zh: 参与者坐着，面对一幅落地的曼陀罗式同心圆投影，并聆听一段声景；在 20–30 分钟里，它们随参与者自己的呼吸与心率扩张、收缩。
works.idea_en: Seeing and hearing one's heart and breath in slow, simple forms turns attention inward; participants learn by doing how thought, feeling and physiology change together.
works.idea_zh: 以缓慢、简单的形式看见和听见自己的心跳与呼吸，会把注意力转向内部；参与者在实践中体会到念头、感受与生理是一起变化的。
works.method: Heart rate and chest or abdominal breathing sensors drive real-time video and sound (with Lizzie Muller, Greg Turner and John Tonkin); experience was studied through post-session interviews.
works.method_zh: 心率传感器与胸腹部呼吸传感器实时驱动影像与声音（与 Lizzie Muller、Greg Turner、John Tonkin 合作）；通过体验后的访谈研究参与者的经验。

paper.title: Cardiomorphologies: An Inner Journey through Art

works.title: Célula Nave
works.description: A large soft architecture of stretched fabric held down by eighteen legs of sand-filled stockings, made for the central hall of Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen.
works.description_zh: 为博伊曼斯·范·伯宁恩博物馆中央大厅制作的大型柔软建筑：拉伸的织物由十八条装满沙子的长袜“腿”固定。
works.idea_en: Soft, weighted, body-scale sculpture makes visitors feel gravity, tension and softness with the whole body.
works.idea_zh: 柔软、有重量、与身体尺度相当的雕塑，让观众用整个身体感受重力、张力与柔软。
works.method: Stretch fabric and eighteen legs made of eight sand-filled socks each (about eight kilos per sock), installed from the artist's written instructions.
works.method_zh: 弹力织物与十八条“腿”，每条由八只装沙的袜子组成（每只约八公斤），依照艺术家的书面说明安装。

works.title: Eyeborg (Cyborg Antenna)
works.description: Neil Harbisson, born unable to see colour, wears an antenna implanted in his skull that turns the colours in front of him into tones he hears through bone.
works.description_zh: 天生无法看见颜色的 Neil Harbisson 戴着一根植入颅骨的天线，把眼前的颜色转成他通过骨传导听到的音调。
works.idea_en: After years of wearing it, colour-tones stopped being a translation and became perception, even in dreams; a new sense becomes part of the self, not an add-on.
works.idea_zh: 戴了多年之后，颜色音调不再是翻译，而成了知觉本身，甚至出现在梦里；新感官成为自我的一部分，而不是附加物。
works.method: A head-mounted camera sensor on an osseointegrated antenna maps light frequency to sound frequency and transmits it by bone conduction; it also receives colours over the internet.
works.method_zh: 骨整合天线上的摄像传感器把光的频率映射为声音频率，通过骨传导传给他；天线也能经互联网接收颜色。

works.title: Kick Ass Kung-Fu
works.description: Players fight virtual opponents with real kicks and punches, seeing their own video image on a large screen with slowed-down, exaggerated jumps.
works.description_zh: 玩家用真实的踢打与虚拟对手格斗，在大屏幕上看到自己的视频影像，跳跃被放慢和夸张。
works.idea_en: A full-body mirror with gentle 'cheats' like slow motion lets people feel like skilled martial artists and train real moves.
works.idea_zh: 带有慢动作等温和“作弊”的全身镜像，让人感到自己像熟练的武术家，同时练到真实的动作。
works.method: Camera-based silhouette tracking composited into a game world projected on two screens, with time-manipulation of jumps; tested with martial-arts practitioners.
works.method_zh: 基于摄像头的剪影追踪，把玩家合成进投影在两块屏幕上的游戏世界，并对跳跃进行时间处理；由武术练习者测试。

paper.title: Martial arts in artificial reality

works.title: PARO Therapeutic Robot
works.description: A furry baby harp seal robot that responds to being stroked, held and spoken to by moving its head and flippers, blinking and crying, used in hospitals and nursing homes, especially with people living with dementia.
works.description_zh: 一只毛茸茸的小竖琴海豹机器人，被抚摸、抱着或说话时会转头、摆动鳍肢、眨眼和鸣叫，用于医院与养老院，尤其是与失智症患者一起使用。
works.idea_en: A robot designed to be touched and held can calm the body the way animal contact does, without asking for any cognitive effort.
works.idea_zh: 一台为被触摸、被抱着而设计的机器人，可以像接触动物那样让身体安定下来，而不要求任何认知上的努力。
works.method: Tactile, light, sound, temperature and posture sensors under soft fur drive actuators and recorded harp seal cries; developed at AIST from 1993 and sold since 2004.
works.method_zh: 柔软毛皮下的触觉、光、声音、温度与姿态传感器驱动执行器与录下的竖琴海豹叫声；自 1993 年起在日本产业技术综合研究所开发，2004 年起销售。

works.title: Technology as Experience
works.description: McCarthy and Wright build a pragmatist account of experience with technology, naming four threads, the sensual, emotional, compositional and spatio-temporal, and six sense-making processes.
works.description_zh: McCarthy 与 Wright 建立了技术经验的实用主义解释，提出四条线索（感官的、情感的、构成的、时空的）与六个意义生成过程。
works.idea_en: Experience with technology is felt and lived as a whole; the sensual thread is as much part of it as function.
works.idea_zh: 与技术相处的经验是作为整体被感受和亲历的；感官线索与功能同样是它的一部分。
works.method: Theoretical framework drawing on Dewey and Bakhtin, illustrated with cases from online shopping to Internet banking.
works.method_zh: 以 Dewey 与 Bakhtin 为资源的理论框架，以从网购到网上银行等案例加以说明。

paper.title: Technology as Experience

works.title: The Hug Shirt
works.description: A shirt with sensors and actuators where a hug would land: a hug sent from a phone is replayed on the wearer's body as pressure, warmth and the sender's heartbeat.
works.description_zh: 一件在拥抱落点处嵌有传感器与执行器的衬衫：从手机发出的拥抱在穿着者身上重现为压力、温暖与发送者的心跳。
works.idea_en: A hug is a whole-body event of pressure, warmth and rhythm, so sending one means designing for where and how it lands on the skin.
works.idea_zh: 拥抱是一件关于压力、温度与节律的全身事件；要“发送”拥抱，就得设计它落在皮肤何处、以何种方式落下。
works.method: Sensors record the strength, duration and location of a hug; Bluetooth and a phone app relay it to actuators and heating elements in the partner's shirt.
works.method_zh: 传感器记录拥抱的力度、时长与位置，经蓝牙与手机应用传给伴侣衬衫里的执行器和加热元件。
exhibited: TIME Best Inventions of the Year 2006

works.title: Touching
works.description: Two dancers wrestle, lean and press their hands together, and every moment of skin-to-skin contact becomes audible: the harder or longer they touch, the more the sound changes.
works.description_zh: 两位舞者角力、倚靠、手掌相抵，每一次皮肤接触都变得可听：触碰越用力、越久，声音变化越大。
works.idea_en: Contact between bodies, not individual gestures, becomes the instrument.
works.idea_zh: 身体之间的接触，而非单人的手势，成了乐器。
works.method: A body-contact sensor worn by both dancers measures when and how firmly they touch and drives sound in real time (Palindrome's EyeCon-era systems, likely with Frieder Weiss).
works.method_zh: 两位舞者佩戴的身体接触传感器测量何时接触、接触多紧，并实时驱动声音（Palindrome 的 EyeCon 时期系统，很可能与 Frieder Weiss 合作）。

works.title: eMoto
works.description: eMoto is a mobile messaging service in which the sender expresses emotion by how they move and squeeze a stylus; the text is sent against an animated background of colours and shapes chosen that way.
works.description_zh: eMoto 是一种手机短信服务：发送者通过挥动、按压触控笔的方式表达情绪，文字连同由此选定的彩色动画背景一起发出。
works.idea_en: Emotion is not a label to select but a process that starts in the body; the interface should pull the user into it physically and leave the interpretation to them.
works.idea_zh: 情绪不是一个供挑选的标签，而是从身体开始的过程；界面应当在身体上把人卷入其中，并把解读留给使用者。
works.method: A pressure- and motion-sensing stylus maps effort and shape of gesture (from Laban analysis) to a circular space of animated colour backgrounds; tested with friends in everyday use.
works.method_zh: 带压力与运动传感的触控笔依据拉班动作分析，把动作的力度与形态映射到一个环形排列的彩色动画背景空间中；在朋友之间的日常使用中进行了测试。

paper.title: eMoto: emotionally engaging interaction

works.title: Baduanjin Qigong (Eight Pieces of Brocade)
works.description: Eight standing movements, such as 'holding up the heavens with both hands' and 'drawing the bow to shoot the eagle', done slowly with coordinated breath; the sequence dates back to the Song dynasty and was standardised as Health Qigong in 2003.
works.description_zh: 八个站立动作，如“两手托天理三焦”“左右开弓似射雕”，配合呼吸缓慢完成；这套功法可追溯至宋代，2003 年被整理为健身气功标准套路。
works.idea_en: A short daily sequence can join breath, stretch and attention so that the body is felt as one moving whole.
works.idea_zh: 一套简短的日常功法就能把呼吸、伸展与注意力连在一起，让身体被感受为一个整体在运动。
works.method: Twelve-minute routine of eight movements with preparatory and closing postures, each paired with slow nasal breathing and mental focus.
works.method_zh: 约十二分钟的套路，包括八个动作及起势、收势，每个动作都配合缓慢的鼻呼吸与意念集中。

works.title: Breakout for Two (Exertion Interfaces)
works.description: Two players in different cities kick a real ball against a wall that shows the other player life-size; hitting projected blocks scores points, like tennis across a video net.
works.description_zh: 身处不同城市的两名玩家把真实的球踢向墙面，墙上显示着真人大小的对方；击中投影方块得分，如同隔着视频网打网球。
works.idea_en: Physical effort itself creates social bonding; 'exertion interfaces' made tiring the body a design goal.
works.idea_zh: 身体的用力本身就能建立社交联结；“运动界面”把让身体累起来变成设计目标。
works.method: Life-size videoconference projected on a wall, with sensors detecting where a real soccer ball hits; compared with a keyboard version in a study.
works.method_zh: 墙上投影真人大小的视频会议画面，传感器检测真实足球的击中位置；并在研究中与键盘版本比较。

paper.title: Exertion interfaces: sports over a distance for social bonding and fun

works.title: Gaga
works.description: A teacher talks continuously, layering images such as 'float', 'shaking' or letting the body melt, while dancers or non-dancers keep moving for an hour without mirrors, attending to sensation, effort and pleasure.
works.description_zh: 教师不断说话，叠加“漂浮”“抖动”或让身体融化等意象，舞者或非舞者在没有镜子的房间里连续动一小时，关注感觉、用力与愉悦。
works.idea_en: Gaga puts listening to sensation before telling the body what to do, and keeps earlier instructions active while new ones arrive; it is a model for designing layered, continuous guidance rather than step-by-step commands.
works.idea_zh: Gaga 先倾听感觉，再告诉身体做什么，并在新指令到来时仍让先前的指令保持有效；这是设计“层叠、连续的引导”而非逐步命令的范例。
works.method: Improvised classes guided by layered verbal imagery, without mirrors, in Gaga/dancers and Gaga/people tracks; developed with Batsheva from the 1990s and named Gaga in 2003.
works.method_zh: 由层叠的语言意象引导的即兴课，不用镜子，分为 Gaga/舞者与 Gaga/大众两个方向；自 1990 年代在巴希瓦舞团发展，2003 年命名为 Gaga。

works.title: Natural-Born Cyborgs: Minds, Technologies, and the Future of Human Intelligence
works.description: Clark argues that humans are cyborgs by nature: our brains are built to fold pens, language, tools and devices into how we think and act, no implants needed.
works.description_zh: Clark 主张人天生就是赛博格：我们的大脑天生会把笔、语言、工具与设备纳入思考和行动之中，无需植入物。
works.idea_en: Augmentation is continuous with ordinary embodiment: a new tool is incorporated by the same plastic body schema that learns a tennis racket.
works.idea_zh: 增强与日常的具身性一脉相承：新工具被纳入身体的方式，与学会用网球拍的可塑身体图式相同。
works.method: Accessible book drawing on cognitive science, neuroscience of body schema and examples from Stelarc to wearable computing.
works.method_zh: 一部通俗著作，借鉴认知科学、身体图式神经科学，以及从 Stelarc 到可穿戴计算的案例。

paper.title: Natural-Born Cyborgs: Minds, Technologies, and the Future of Human Intelligence

works.title_zh: 天生的赛博格：心灵、技术和人类智能的未来

works.title: SenToy
works.description: SenToy is a plush doll with motion sensors that players move and squeeze to make game characters happy, sad, angry or afraid in the fantasy game FantasyA.
works.description_zh: SenToy 是一个装有运动传感器的毛绒玩偶。玩家在奇幻游戏 FantasyA 中挥动、挤压它，让游戏角色变得快乐、悲伤、愤怒或恐惧。
works.idea_en: Emotion can be entered into a system as a whole-body gesture, so the player has to act the feeling out to use it.
works.idea_zh: 情绪可以作为全身动作输入系统：玩家要把这份感受演出来，才能用上它。
works.method: Sensors in the doll's body and limbs (likely accelerometers and position switches) classify gesture patterns (e.g. bouncing for happy, covering the eyes for fear), derived from a Wizard of Oz study at SICS.
works.method_zh: 玩偶身体与四肢中的传感器（可能是加速度计与位置开关）识别动作模式（如上下跳动表示高兴、捂住眼睛表示害怕），这些模式来自 SICS 的“绿野仙踪”式实验。

paper.title: SenToy: an affective sympathetic interface

works.title: The Hug
works.description: A soft, arm-shaped robotic pillow for elders and their families: hugging it sends a hug to a matching pillow, which then vibrates, warms and plays the caller's voice.
works.description_zh: 一只手臂形状、柔软的机器人抱枕，面向老人与家人：抱紧它，就把拥抱传给另一只抱枕，后者随之振动、发热并播放来电者的声音。
works.idea_en: A robot for intimacy should first be shaped to be held; its form invites the embrace before any function does.
works.idea_zh: 为亲密而做的机器人首先要被塑造成可以被抱住的样子；在任何功能之前，形态先邀请了拥抱。
works.method: Pressure and stroke sensors in the pillow's arms connect over a phone line to vibration motors, heating pads and audio in the paired pillow.
works.method_zh: 抱枕手臂中的压力与抚触传感器经电话线与配对抱枕中的振动电机、加热垫与音频相连。

paper.title: The Hug: an exploration of robotic form for intimate communication

works.title: Understanding Contexts by Being There: Case Studies in Bodystorming
works.description: Case studies in which designers generated ideas while physically in the real setting — a bus, a home, a kindergarten — rather than in a meeting room.
works.description_zh: 案例研究：设计师身处真实情境——公交车、家中、幼儿园——而不是会议室里产生想法。
works.idea_en: Ideas come differently when the body is in the situation; being there is a way of thinking.
works.idea_zh: 身体置身情境中时，想法以不同方式出现；在场本身就是一种思考。
works.method: Four bodystorming case studies comparing idea quality and process with conventional brainstorming.
works.method_zh: 四个身体风暴案例，比较其与常规头脑风暴在想法质量与过程上的差异。

paper.title: Understanding contexts by being there: case studies in bodystorming

works.title_zh: 身临其境理解情境：身体风暴案例研究

works.title: Wave UFO
works.description: Three visitors lie inside a large teardrop-shaped pod wearing brainwave sensors; their brain activity becomes animations on the dome above, which merge as their minds settle together.
works.description_zh: 三位观众躺进一个巨大的泪滴形舱体，佩戴脑电传感器；他们的脑活动在头顶穹幕上化作动画，并在彼此平静下来时交融在一起。
works.idea_en: Biodata is used for shared attention, close to meditation, rather than for control: three bodies lying still become one visual rhythm.
works.idea_zh: 生物数据被用于共享的注意，接近冥想，而不是用于控制：三个静卧的身体化为同一个视觉节律。
works.method: EEG sensors record alpha, beta and theta activity, and a custom game engine made at Eyebeam renders it as real-time abstract animation on the domed ceiling.
works.method_zh: 脑电传感器记录 α、β、θ 波活动，Eyebeam 制作的定制游戏引擎把它实时渲染为穹顶上的抽象动画。

works.title: whisper[s]
works.description: A participatory performance in which visitors wear networked garments that sense their breath and heartbeat and pass them to each other as touch, sound and light.
works.description_zh: 一场参与式表演：观众穿上联网的衣物，衣物感知他们的呼吸与心跳，并以触碰、声音和光彼此传递。
works.idea_en: Somatic practice can be the design method: the garments grew from exercises in listening to one's own and others' inner rhythms.
works.idea_zh: 身体修习本身可以成为设计方法：这些衣物源自聆听自己与他人内在节律的练习。
works.method: Wireless wearables with breath and heart sensors plus vibration and sound outputs, developed through workshops of body-based listening; shown at DEAF03.
works.method_zh: 带呼吸与心跳传感器及振动、声音输出的无线可穿戴物，通过基于身体聆听的工作坊发展而来；在 DEAF03 展出。

works.title: Bodies in Technology
works.description: Ihde distinguishes 'body one', the felt, moving body, from 'body two', the body shaped by culture, and asks how technologies from VR to prostheses reshape both.
works.description_zh: Ihde 区分“身体一”（被感受、会运动的身体）与“身体二”（被文化塑造的身体），追问从虚拟现实到义肢的技术如何重塑两者。
works.idea_en: Virtual and augmented bodies are never complete substitutes: the full, multisensory lived body stays the reference against which every technical body feels thin.
works.idea_zh: 虚拟的与增强的身体从来不是完整的替代：完整的、多感官的生活身体始终是参照，任何技术身体在它面前都显得单薄。
works.method: Postphenomenological essays on VR, imaging, prosthetics and the 'technology body', written for the Electronic Mediations series.
works.method_zh: 关于虚拟现实、成像、义肢与“技术身体”的后现象学文集，收入 Electronic Mediations 丛书。

paper.title: Bodies in Technology

works.title: ComTouch
works.description: A sleeve on a mobile phone turns the pressure of each finger into vibration under the other caller's fingers, so a conversation carries squeezes as well as words.
works.description_zh: 套在手机上的装置把每根手指的按压转成对方手指下的振动，让一次通话既有话语也有“捏一下”。
works.idea_en: People invent their own tactile vocabulary, emphasis, turn-taking and play, as soon as touch is added to talk.
works.idea_zh: 一旦在话语之外加上触碰，人们会自己发明一套触觉词汇：强调、轮流与嬉戏。
works.method: Force-sensitive resistors under the fingers drive vibrotactile actuators on the remote device, tested with pairs of users in a lab study.
works.method_zh: 手指下的力敏电阻驱动远端装置上的振动触觉执行器，并以双人实验室研究检验。

paper.title: ComTouch: design of a vibrotactile communication device

works.title: How Do You Feel? Interoception
works.description: A review that redefines interoception as the sense of the physiological condition of the entire body, carried by a dedicated pathway to the insular cortex, and links it to feelings and emotional awareness.
works.description_zh: 一篇综述：把内感受重新定义为对全身生理状态的感觉，经由专门通路抵达脑岛皮层，并把它与感受及情绪觉知联系起来。
works.idea_en: Pain, temperature, itch, hunger and heartbeat belong to one sense of the body's inner state, and that sense is the stuff that subjective feeling is made of.
works.idea_zh: 疼痛、温度、瘙痒、饥饿与心跳同属一种对身体内部状态的感觉，而主观感受正是由这种感觉构成的。
works.method: Review of neuroanatomical and functional imaging evidence on the lamina I spinothalamocortical pathway and the insula (Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 2002).
works.method_zh: 综述关于脊髓丘脑皮层通路（I 层）与脑岛的神经解剖及功能成像证据（Nature Reviews Neuroscience，2002）。

paper.title: How do you feel? Interoception: the sense of the physiological condition of the body

works.title: Our Posthuman Future: Consequences of the Biotechnology Revolution
works.description: Fukuyama warns that genetic engineering, neuropharmacology and life extension could change human nature and undermine equal rights, and calls for regulation.
works.description_zh: Fukuyama 警告基因工程、神经药理学与寿命延长可能改变人性、动摇平等权利，并呼吁加以监管。
works.idea_en: A critic of enhancement who defends a shared human nature; soma design shares his caution but locates what matters in lived, felt bodies rather than in an abstract essence.
works.idea_zh: 一位捍卫共同人性的增强批评者；身体设计认同他的审慎，但把重要之处放在活生生的、被感受的身体上，而非抽象的本质。
works.method: Policy-oriented book drawing on political philosophy, biology and the history of eugenics.
works.method_zh: 一部面向政策的著作，借鉴政治哲学、生物学与优生学史。

paper.title: Our Posthuman Future: Consequences of the Biotechnology Revolution

works.title_zh: 我们的后人类未来：生物技术革命的后果

works.title: Dance for PD
works.description: Dance classes for people with Parkinson's disease taught by professional dancers, using live music, imagery and choreography rather than exercise drills.
works.description_zh: 由专业舞者教授的帕金森患者舞蹈课，使用现场音乐、意象与编舞，而不是训练式的动作操练。
works.idea_en: People with Parkinson's are addressed as dancers; music and imagery can unlock movement that effortful control cannot.
works.idea_zh: 帕金森患者被当作舞者对待；音乐与意象能唤起费力控制无法带出的动作。
works.method: Seated and standing dance classes with live music taught worldwide; teacher training programme run by the Mark Morris Dance Group with the Brooklyn Parkinson Group.
works.method_zh: 配现场音乐的坐姿与站姿舞蹈课，在全球开设；由 Mark Morris Dance Group 与布鲁克林帕金森组织运营教师培训。
works.title_zh: 帕金森舞蹈课（Dance for PD）

works.title: Where the Action Is: The Foundations of Embodied Interaction
works.description: Dourish draws on Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty, Schutz and Wittgenstein to define embodied interaction: meaning arises through engaged action in the physical and social world, which tangible and social computing should support.
works.description_zh: Dourish 借助 Heidegger、Merleau-Ponty、Schutz 与 Wittgenstein 定义了“具身交互”：意义在物理与社会世界中的投入行动中产生，有形计算与社会计算应当支持这一点。
works.idea_en: Interaction is not a mind operating a device but a body acting in a world; design for what people do, not what they represent.
works.idea_zh: 交互不是心智操作设备，而是身体在世界中行动；要为人们“做什么”设计，而不是为他们“表征什么”设计。
works.method: Theoretical synthesis of phenomenology with tangible and social computing research, closing with design principles for embodied interaction.
works.method_zh: 把现象学与有形计算、社会计算研究相综合，最后提出具身交互的设计原则。

paper.title: Where the Action Is: The Foundations of Embodied Interaction

works.title_zh: 行动之所在：具身交互的基础

works.title: Experience Prototyping
works.description: Describes IDEO's practice of letting designers and clients live through a situation — wearing a pager, carrying a heart-patient's load — to understand how a design would feel.
works.description_zh: 介绍 IDEO 的做法：让设计师与客户亲身经历某个情境——佩戴寻呼机、背负心脏病人的负担——以理解一个设计会带来怎样的感受。
works.idea_en: The quickest way to understand a felt experience is to have it, in your own body, with rough props.
works.idea_zh: 理解一种被感受的经验，最快的方法是用粗糙的道具，在自己身上经历它。
works.method: Case descriptions from IDEO projects using role-play, props and simulated situations at different design stages.
works.method_zh: 来自 IDEO 项目的案例描述，在不同设计阶段使用角色扮演、道具与模拟情境。

paper.title: Experience prototyping

works.title: EyesWeb
works.description: An open software platform that extracts expressive cues from video of dancers (contraction, fluidity, impulsiveness) and maps them to music and media in real time.
works.description_zh: 一个开放软件平台，从舞者视频中提取表现性线索（收缩、流畅、冲动）并实时映射为音乐与媒体。
works.idea_en: Expressive, emotional qualities of movement can be modelled directly, not only positions and gestures.
works.idea_zh: 动作中富有表现力的情感质感可以被直接建模，而不只是位置与手势。
works.method: Visual-programming environment with computer-vision modules for full-body motion features (quantity of motion, contraction index), developed at InfoMus Lab, Genoa.
works.method_zh: 可视化编程环境，带有提取全身运动特征（运动量、收缩指数）的计算机视觉模块，由热那亚 InfoMus 实验室开发。

paper.title: EyesWeb: Toward Gesture and Affect Recognition in Interactive Dance and Music Systems

works.title: I.K.U.
works.description: A Japanese sci-fi porn film in which replicant 'coders' collect orgasm data from people for a corporation that sells it as a chip.
works.description_zh: 一部日本科幻色情电影：复制人“编码者”为一家公司采集人们的高潮数据，公司再把它做成芯片出售。
works.idea_en: Pleasure imagined as extractable data: a queer, sex-positive cyborg story that also warns about the capture of intimate feeling.
works.idea_zh: 快感被想象为可提取的数据：一个酷儿的、性积极的赛博格故事，同时警示私密感受被捕获的危险。
works.method: Feature film shot in Tokyo, produced by Uplink, with a shape-shifting replicant whose arm acts as a data-collecting probe.
works.method_zh: 在东京拍摄、由 Uplink 制作的长片，片中可变形的复制人以手臂作为采集数据的探针。

works.title: My Body, The Buddhist
works.description: Nineteen short chapters with titles such as 'my body likes to rest' and 'my body is bored by answers', in which Hay reports what her dancing body taught her about attention and self.
works.description_zh: 十九个短章，标题如“我的身体喜欢休息”“我的身体对答案感到厌倦”，海在书中讲述跳舞的身体教给她的关于注意与自我的事。
works.idea_en: Hay gives the body agency in the creative process and treats perception as the dance; for designers it shows how to write from the body in the first person.
works.idea_zh: 海赋予身体在创作中的能动性，把知觉当作舞蹈本身；它为设计者示范了如何以第一人称从身体出发写作。
works.method: Short first-person essays linking choreographic practice and Buddhist ideas of the self, with a foreword by Susan Foster; Wesleyan University Press, 2000.
works.method_zh: 把编舞实践与佛教自我观联系起来的第一人称短文，苏珊·福斯特作序；卫斯理大学出版社，2000 年。

paper.title: My Body, The Buddhist

works.title: SnowWorld
works.description: An icy virtual canyon with snowmen, penguins and snowballs to throw, experienced in a head-mounted display by burn patients while their wounds are cleaned and dressed.
works.description_zh: 一个冰雪峡谷的虚拟世界，有雪人、企鹅和可以投掷的雪球；烧伤患者在清创和换药时通过头戴显示器进入其中。
works.idea_en: Pain is shaped by attention: when the mind is absorbed in a cold, playful world, the same wound hurts less. It is the classic case of VR as distraction, and a contrast to designs that teach people to attend to pain.
works.idea_zh: 疼痛受注意力塑造：当心神沉浸在一个寒冷而好玩的世界里，同一处伤口就没那么痛。它是“以 VR 分散注意”的经典案例，也与那些教人去注意疼痛的设计形成对照。
works.method: Head-mounted display VR used during burn wound care and physical therapy, compared with standard care in clinical studies; the first 2000 studies likely used an earlier VR world, with SnowWorld built for burn patients soon after.
works.method_zh: 在烧伤换药与物理治疗中使用头戴式 VR，并在临床研究中与常规照护比较；2000 年最早的研究可能使用的是更早的 VR 场景，SnowWorld 随后专为烧伤患者打造。

paper.title: Virtual reality as an adjunctive pain control during burn wound care in adolescent patients

works.title: How We Became Posthuman: Virtual Bodies in Cybernetics, Literature, and Informatics
works.description: Hayles traces how post-war cybernetics came to treat information as separable from its material body, and how that idea shaped fiction and fantasies of uploading.
works.description_zh: Hayles 追溯战后控制论如何把信息视为可与其物质载体分离的东西，以及这一观念如何塑造小说和心灵上传的幻想。
works.idea_en: The book names the dualism in posthuman dreams and argues for a posthuman that stays embodied: information is always carried and felt by some body.
works.idea_zh: 这本书点出了后人类梦想中的二元论，并主张一种保持具身的后人类：信息总是由某个身体承载、被某个身体感受。
works.method: Intellectual history of the Macy conferences and cybernetics read alongside science fiction by Philip K. Dick, Bernard Wolfe and others.
works.method_zh: 对梅西会议与控制论的思想史研究，并与 Philip K. Dick、Bernard Wolfe 等人的科幻小说对照阅读。

paper.title: How We Became Posthuman: Virtual Bodies in Cybernetics, Literature, and Informatics
