works.title_zh: 我们何以成为后人类：文学、信息科学和控制论中的虚拟身体

works.title: Improvisation Technologies
works.description: A video lecture series in which Forsythe demonstrates his improvisation principles while graphic lines drawn over the video show the imagined points, lines and planes his body moves through.
works.description_zh: 一套视频讲座：Forsythe 演示他的即兴原则，叠加在画面上的图形线条显示他身体所穿过的想象中的点、线和面。
works.idea_en: Dancers think with imagined geometry inside and around the body; making that inner imagery visible makes it teachable.
works.idea_zh: 舞者用身体内外想象的几何来思考；把这种内在意象变得可见，它就可以被教授。
works.method: Digitised lecture-demonstrations with line annotations, published as a CD-ROM by ZKM Karlsruhe for training Ballett Frankfurt dancers.
works.method_zh: 带线条注释的数字化讲座示范，由 ZKM 卡尔斯鲁厄以 CD-ROM 出版，用于法兰克福芭蕾舞团舞者的训练。

works.title: Philosophy in the Flesh: The Embodied Mind and Its Challenge to Western Thought
works.description: Lakoff and Johnson argue from cognitive science that the mind is inherently embodied, thought is mostly unconscious and abstract concepts are largely metaphorical, and re-read Western philosophy in that light.
works.description_zh: Lakoff 与 Johnson 依据认知科学主张：心智本质上是具身的，思维大多是无意识的，抽象概念主要是隐喻性的，并据此重读西方哲学。
works.idea_en: There is no disembodied reason: the same neural and bodily systems that let us move and perceive also structure how we think.
works.idea_zh: 不存在脱离身体的理性：让我们运动与知觉的神经与身体系统，同样结构着我们的思考方式。
works.method: Synthesis of cognitive linguistics and neuroscience, applied to concepts of time, causation, mind, self and morality.
works.method_zh: 综合认知语言学与神经科学，应用于时间、因果、心智、自我与道德等概念。

paper.title: Philosophy in the Flesh: The Embodied Mind and Its Challenge to Western Thought

works.title_zh: 肉身哲学：亲身心智及其向西方思想的挑战

works.title: Self-Cultivation as Education Embodying Humanity
works.description: Tu presents Confucian self-cultivation (xiushen) as learning to be human through the body: knowledge that is 'embodied' (tizhi) in comportment, ritual and relationships rather than held as propositions.
works.description_zh: 杜维明把儒家修身阐释为通过身体学做人：知识“体现”在举止、礼仪与人际关系中（体知），而不是作为命题被持有。
works.idea_en: To know is to embody: Confucian learning is judged by how one stands, speaks and relates, a first-person knowledge that lives in conduct.
works.idea_zh: 知即是体现：儒家的学问看的是一个人如何站立、说话与待人，这是一种活在行为中的第一人称知识。
works.method: Paper for the Twentieth World Congress of Philosophy (Boston, 1998), part of Tu's long work on tizhi and New Confucianism.
works.method_zh: 在第二十届世界哲学大会（1998 年，波士顿）上发表的论文，是杜维明长期研究“体知”与新儒学的一部分。

paper.venue: Proceedings of the Twentieth World Congress of Philosophy
paper.title: Self-Cultivation as Education Embodying Humanity

works.title: Somaesthetics: A Disciplinary Proposal
works.description: The essay that named and defined somaesthetics as the critical study and meliorative cultivation of the body as the site of sensory-aesthetic appreciation and creative self-fashioning.
works.description_zh: 为身体美学命名并下定义的文章：把身体作为感官审美鉴赏与创造性自我塑造的所在，对其进行批判性研究与改良性修养。
works.idea_en: The soma is a sentient, purposive body-mind; improving its felt awareness improves perception, thought and action together.
works.idea_zh: soma 是有感知、有意图的身心；提升对它的感受觉察，就同时提升了知觉、思考与行动。
works.method: Proposes three branches: analytic (theory of the body), pragmatic (methods such as Feldenkrais, yoga, Alexander) and practical (actually doing the disciplines).
works.method_zh: 提出三个分支：分析的（身体理论）、实用的（Feldenkrais、瑜伽、亚历山大技巧等方法）与实践的（亲身去修习）。

paper.title: Somaesthetics: A Disciplinary Proposal
paper.venue: The Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism 57(3)

works.title_zh: 身体美学：一个学科提议

works.title: The Expressiveness of the Body and the Divergence of Greek and Chinese Medicine
works.description: Kuriyama compares how Greek doctors learned to see muscles and anatomy while Chinese doctors learned to feel the pulse and read colours and qi, arguing that trained touch and sight produce different bodies.
works.description_zh: 栗山茂久比较古希腊医生如何学会看见肌肉与解剖结构，而中国医生如何学会诊脉、望色与感知气，论证不同训练的触觉与视觉会产生不同的身体。
works.idea_en: How a body feels depends on how the perceiver's senses have been trained: somatic sensitivity is a cultural skill, not a neutral reading.
works.idea_zh: 身体被感知成什么样，取决于感知者的感官如何被训练：身体感受力是一种文化技艺，而不是中性的读数。
works.method: Comparative history drawing on Greek medical treatises and Chinese pulse classics, with close attention to images and vocabulary of touch.
works.method_zh: 比较历史研究，材料来自古希腊医学论著与中国脉学经典，细致分析触觉的图像与词汇。

paper.title: The Expressiveness of the Body and the Divergence of Greek and Chinese Medicine

works.title_zh: 身体的语言：古希腊医学和中医之比较

works.title: The Feeling of What Happens: Body and Emotion in the Making of Consciousness
works.description: Damasio traces consciousness to the brain's ongoing mapping of the body's internal state: a proto-self from which core and extended selves arise as feelings of what happens.
works.description_zh: Damasio 把意识追溯到大脑对身体内部状态的持续映射：由“原我”生出核心自我与延展自我，也就是对所发生之事的感受。
works.idea_en: The sense of self begins as the felt body: consciousness is rooted in interoceptive feeling.
works.idea_zh: 自我感始于被感受的身体：意识扎根于内感受。
works.method: Neuroscientific theory built on lesion studies, neuroanatomy and clinical observation of disorders of consciousness.
works.method_zh: 基于脑损伤研究、神经解剖与意识障碍临床观察的神经科学理论。

paper.title: The Feeling of What Happens: Body and Emotion in the Making of Consciousness

works.title_zh: 感受发生的一切：意识产生中的身体和情绪

works.title: The Primacy of Movement
works.description: Sheets-Johnstone argues that animate movement is the origin of our sense of self, agency and concepts: we are first movers, and we learn ourselves by moving.
works.description_zh: Sheets-Johnstone 主张有生命的运动是自我感、能动性与概念的源头：我们首先是运动者，并在运动中认识自己。
works.idea_en: Thinking in movement is real thinking; kinesthetic experience comes before and shapes language and reflection.
works.idea_zh: “在运动中思考”是真正的思考；动觉经验先于语言与反思，并塑造它们。
works.method: Phenomenological and evolutionary analysis drawing on dance, infant development and comparative biology.
works.method_zh: 结合舞蹈、婴儿发展与比较生物学的现象学与进化分析。

paper.title: The Primacy of Movement

works.title: Cyborg series
works.description: White silicone sculptures of female cyborg bodies, headless and often missing limbs, hung from the ceiling like armour or anime figures.
works.description_zh: 白色硅胶雕塑，塑造女性赛博格身体，无头且常常缺失肢体，从天花板悬垂，像盔甲，也像动漫人物。
works.idea_en: The cyborg dream of a perfect technological body is shown as fragmented and gendered; enhancement fantasies carry old ideals of the female body.
works.idea_zh: 关于完美技术身体的赛博格梦想被呈现为破碎且被性别化的；增强幻想承载着对女性身体的旧有理想。
works.method: Cast silicone and polyurethane sculptures drawing on Japanese anime, classical statuary and mechanical armour; Cyborg W1–W4 were made in 1998.
works.method_zh: 以硅胶与聚氨酯铸成的雕塑，借鉴日本动漫、古典雕像与机械盔甲；《Cyborg W1–W4》作于 1998 年。

works.title: Ephémère
works.description: A breath-and-balance VR work in three layers (landscape, earth and the inside of the body), where organs and seeds appear and fade with the seasons.
works.description_zh: 一件以呼吸和平衡导航的 VR 作品，分为三层（地景、大地与身体内部），器官与种子随季节浮现又消失。
works.idea_en: Moving between landscape and body interior suggests that the felt body and the world share one living process.
works.idea_zh: 在地景与身体内部之间穿行，暗示被感受的身体与世界属于同一个生命过程。
works.method: Same breath-sensing vest and balance interface as Osmose, with time-varying generative imagery and spatial sound.
works.method_zh: 沿用 Osmose 的呼吸感应背心与平衡界面，配以随时间变化的生成图像和空间声音。

works.title: Exoskeleton
works.description: Stelarc stands on a six-legged pneumatic walking machine and steers it with arm gestures while its legs, sounds and his amplified body make a noisy choreography.
works.description_zh: Stelarc 站在一台六足气动行走机器上，用手臂动作操控它；机器的腿、声音和他被放大的身体构成一段嘈杂的编舞。
works.idea_en: Steering a much larger body shows how a new body schema forms: small gestures come to feel like steps of six legs.
works.idea_zh: 操控一个大得多的身体，让人看到新的身体图式如何形成：细小的手势逐渐被感受为六条腿的步伐。
works.method: Arm gestures, read by sensors on an upper-body exoskeleton, drive a pneumatic hexapod with ripple or tripod gaits; the left arm ends in an 11-degree-of-freedom pneumatic manipulator, and the machine's sounds are amplified.
works.method_zh: 上身外骨骼上的传感器读取手臂动作，驱动一台以波浪或三足步态行走的气动六足机器；左臂延伸为具有 11 个自由度的气动机械手，机器的声音被放大。

works.title: Moon Water
works.description: Cloud Gate dancers move in slow, continuous tai chi-based flows to Bach's cello suites while water gradually covers the stage and mirrors reflect their bodies; the company trains daily in tai chi daoyin, meditation and martial arts.
works.description_zh: 云门舞者伴随巴赫无伴奏大提琴组曲，以源自太极的缓慢而连绵的动作起舞，水渐渐漫上舞台，镜面映出舞者的身体；舞团每天以太极导引、静坐与武术训练。
works.idea_en: An Eastern somatic practice can become a stage language: the audience sees qi and breath moving through bodies trained from the inside.
works.idea_zh: 东方的身体修习可以成为舞台语言：观众看见气与呼吸在从内部训练出来的身体中流动。
works.method: Choreography built from tai chi daoyin (developed by Hsiung Wei) and meditation training, with water and mirror scenography.
works.method_zh: 以太极导引（熊卫创编）与静坐训练为基础编创，配合水与镜的舞台设计。
exhibited: New York Times best dance of 2003 (Anna Kisselgoff)

works.title: Project Cyborg
works.description: Kevin Warwick had an RFID chip implanted in 1998 and a 100-electrode array wired into his arm's median nerve in 2002, letting him move a robot hand and feel pulses from his wife's implant.
works.description_zh: Kevin Warwick 于 1998 年植入 RFID 芯片，2002 年又把 100 电极阵列接入手臂的正中神经，借此操控机械手，并感受来自妻子植入物的脉冲。
works.idea_en: The most striking result was felt, not technical: a nerve-to-nerve signal between two people, an early and crude form of shared bodily sensation.
works.idea_zh: 最动人的结果是被感受到的，而非技术性的：两人之间神经对神经的信号，一种早期而粗糙的共享身体感觉。
works.method: A Utah microelectrode array in the median nerve recorded and stimulated neural signals, linked over the internet to a robot hand and to electrodes in Irena Warwick's arm.
works.method_zh: 植入正中神经的犹他微电极阵列记录并刺激神经信号，经互联网连接到机械手和 Irena Warwick 手臂中的电极。

paper.title: The Application of Implant Technology for Cybernetic Systems

works.title: Rubber Hands 'Feel' Touch That Eyes See
works.description: A participant's hidden hand and a visible rubber hand are stroked in synchrony; after a few minutes the rubber hand feels like one's own and the real hand seems to drift toward it.
works.description_zh: 参与者被遮住的真手与眼前的橡胶手被同步抚摸；几分钟后，橡胶手感觉像是自己的，真手的位置仿佛也向它漂移。
works.idea_en: Ownership of the body is not given but continuously made from matching sight and touch, which is why a felt body can be extended or displaced.
works.idea_zh: 对身体的拥有感不是给定的，而是由视觉与触觉的吻合不断生成的；正因如此，被感受的身体可以被延展或挪移。
works.method: Synchronous versus asynchronous brush strokes on hidden real hand and visible rubber hand; questionnaires and proprioceptive drift measured.
works.method_zh: 用画笔对被遮住的真手与可见的橡胶手进行同步或不同步的抚触，测量问卷与本体感漂移。

paper.title: Rubber hands 'feel' touch that eyes see

works.title_zh: 橡胶手“感觉到”眼睛所见的触碰

works.title: The Extended Mind
works.description: Clark and Chalmers argue that when a notebook or tool plays the role memory would play, it is part of the mind, using the example of Otto and his notebook.
works.description_zh: Clark 与 Chalmers 主张，当笔记本或工具承担了记忆本应承担的角色时，它就是心灵的一部分，并以 Otto 和他的笔记本为例。
works.idea_en: Mind is not sealed inside the skull; but the paper still speaks of cognition, not felt experience, so soma design adds the question of how an extension feels.
works.idea_zh: 心灵并不封闭在颅骨之内；但这篇论文谈的仍是认知而非感受，因此身体设计补上一个问题：延伸被如何感受。
works.method: Philosophical argument using the parity principle and thought experiments (Tetris rotation, Otto's notebook).
works.method_zh: 以“对等原则”和思想实验（俄罗斯方块旋转、Otto 的笔记本）展开的哲学论证。

paper.title: The Extended Mind

works.title: Affective Computing
works.description: The book that named and founded affective computing: computing that relates to, arises from or deliberately influences emotion, including wearable sensing of physiological signals.
works.description_zh: 为情感计算命名并奠基的书：与情绪相关、源于情绪或有意影响情绪的计算，包括对生理信号的可穿戴感测。
works.idea_en: It put the body's signals at the centre of computing with emotion; soma design keeps that attention to the body but questions the idea that emotion can be read off it as a label.
works.idea_zh: 它把身体信号放到了与情绪相关的计算的中心；身体设计保留了对身体的关注，但质疑情绪可以作为标签从身体上被读出的想法。
works.method: A monograph combining emotion theory, signal processing, pattern recognition and early wearable prototypes from the MIT Media Lab.
works.method_zh: 一部结合情绪理论、信号处理、模式识别与麻省理工学院媒体实验室早期可穿戴原型的专著。

paper.title: Affective Computing

works.title: Primo Posthuman
works.description: A design concept for a future human body with upgradable senses, a 'metabrain', smart skin and replaceable parts, presented as images and texts.
works.description_zh: 一个未来人体的设计概念：可升级的感官、“元脑”、智能皮肤和可替换的部件，以图像与文字呈现。
works.idea_en: It shows the transhumanist image of the body as a product to redesign; the question soma design adds is who feels the upgrade and how it would be lived.
works.idea_zh: 它呈现了超人类主义把身体当作可重新设计的产品的形象；身体设计追加的问题是：谁来感受这次升级，它将如何被活出来。
works.method: Speculative design drawings and specifications drawing on nanotechnology, AI and cosmetic medicine, revised over the following decade.
works.method_zh: 思辨设计图与规格说明，借鉴纳米技术、人工智能与美容医学，在其后十年中不断修订。

works.title: Time Capsule
works.description: In a São Paulo gallery Eduardo Kac injected a microchip into his own ankle, then registered himself online in an animal-identification database, broadcast live on TV and the web.
works.description_zh: 在圣保罗的一家画廊，Eduardo Kac 把一枚微芯片注射进自己的脚踝，随后在网上把自己登记进动物识别数据库，并在电视和网络上直播。
works.idea_en: The body becomes a record in a database; the performance asks what happens to lived flesh once it is also an entry that others can read.
works.idea_zh: 身体成了数据库里的一条记录；这场表演追问：当活生生的血肉同时成为他人可读取的条目时，会发生什么。
works.method: A passive RFID identification chip for animals was implanted with a needle, scanned remotely over the web, and registered as both animal and owner.
works.method_zh: 用针头植入一枚用于动物的被动 RFID 识别芯片，经网络远程扫描，并以动物和主人的双重身份登记。

works.title: Waking the Tiger: Healing Trauma
works.description: Levine asks why wild animals, threatened constantly, rarely stay traumatised, and describes how humans can let frozen survival energy discharge through felt sensation.
works.description_zh: 莱文追问为何常受威胁的野生动物很少留下创伤，并描述人如何通过感受身体感觉，让冻结的生存能量得以释放。
works.idea_en: The book treats the body as healer and trauma as a physiological process, offering designers a cautious model for working with arousal and safety.
works.idea_zh: 此书把身体视为疗愈者、把创伤视为生理过程，为设计者处理唤醒与安全提供了一个需谨慎使用的模型。
works.method: Popular book in four parts (the body as healer, symptoms, transformation, first aid) with self-exercises; North Atlantic Books, 1997, with Ann Frederick.
works.method_zh: 分为四部分（身体作为疗愈者、症状、转化、急救）并附自我练习的大众读物；North Atlantic Books，1997 年，与安·弗雷德里克合著。

paper.title: Waking the Tiger: Healing Trauma

works.title_zh: 唤醒老虎：启动自我疗愈本能

works.title: inTouch
works.description: Two sets of three wooden rollers are linked by motors: when one person turns a roller, the matching roller under the other person's hand turns too, and both can push against each other.
works.description_zh: 两组各三根木质滚轴由电机相连：一人转动滚轴时，远方另一人手下对应的滚轴也随之转动，两人还能彼此“顶”住对方。
works.idea_en: Touch at a distance works best as a shared, two-way physical medium that both bodies can push and feel at once, not as a message sent from one to the other.
works.idea_zh: 远距离的触碰最好是一个双向共享的物理介质，两个身体能同时推动、同时感到，而不是一方发给另一方的讯息。
works.method: Force-feedback rollers with position sensors and motors synchronise two remote objects so that both users feel the same state and each other's resistance.
works.method_zh: 带位置传感器与电机的力反馈滚轴让两个远端物件保持同步，双方感到同一状态，也感到对方的阻力。

paper.title: Tangible interfaces for remote collaboration and communication

works.title: Bodymaps: Artifacts of Touch
works.description: A white velvet table shows a projected image of the artist's body; when visitors stroke, press or hover over it, the image and sound respond in ways that are hard to predict.
works.description_zh: 一张白色天鹅绒桌面上投影着艺术家的身体影像；观众抚摸、按压或悬手其上时，影像与声音以难以预料的方式回应。
works.idea_en: Touch is a two-way, intimate act: a surface that 'wants' contact makes visitors aware of how and why they touch.
works.idea_zh: 触摸是双向而私密的行为：一个“渴望”被触碰的表面，让人意识到自己如何触摸、为何触摸。
works.method: Fifteen electric-field sensors and eight force-sensitive resistors under the velvet sense proximity, touch and pressure and drive video and sound through a deliberately opaque rule set.
works.method_zh: 天鹅绒下的 15 个电场传感器与 8 个力敏电阻感知接近、触摸与压力，并通过刻意难以解读的规则驱动影像与声音。

paper.title: Bodymaps: artifacts of touch

works.title: Ping Body
works.description: Internet traffic moves Stelarc's body: network ping times are turned into electrical muscle stimulation, so his arms and legs jerk without his intention.
works.description_zh: 互联网流量驱动 Stelarc 的身体：网络 ping 值被转为肌肉电刺激，让他的手臂和腿不由自主地抽动。
works.idea_en: Being moved from outside makes the felt boundary between voluntary and involuntary movement vivid.
works.idea_zh: 被外部驱动，让主动与被动动作之间被感受到的界线变得鲜明。
works.method: Ping values to global internet domains are mapped to a muscle-stimulation system on his limbs; his own movements also drive a robotic Third Hand.
works.method_zh: 对全球互联网域名的 ping 值被映射到他四肢上的肌肉刺激系统；他自己的动作也驱动机械“第三只手”。

works.title: Bone, Breath, and Gesture: Practices of Embodiment
works.description: An anthology of first-hand writings by the founders of somatic practices, including Elsa Gindler, Charlotte Selver, Ida Rolf, Moshe Feldenkrais, F. M. Alexander, Bonnie Bainbridge Cohen and Emilie Conrad.
works.description_zh: 身心学实践创始人的第一手文字选集，收录 Elsa Gindler、Charlotte Selver、Ida Rolf、Moshe Feldenkrais、F. M. Alexander、Bonnie Bainbridge Cohen 与 Emilie Conrad 等人的文章。
works.idea_en: The somatic practices share one premise: attending to breath, bone and movement from within changes the whole person, not a body part.
works.idea_zh: 身体修习共享一个前提：从内部留意呼吸、骨骼与动作，改变的是整个人，而不是某个身体部位。
works.method: Edited collection with Johnson's introductions placing each practice in the history of the somatics movement.
works.method_zh: 编选文集，Johnson 为每种实践撰写导言，把它放入身心学运动的历史中。

paper.title: Bone, Breath, and Gesture: Practices of Embodiment

works.title_zh: 骨骼、呼吸与姿态：具身的实践

works.title: Mirror Box
works.description: A box with a mirror down the middle: an amputee places the intact arm beside the mirror, sees its reflection where the missing limb should be, and moves both, which can relieve cramping phantom pain.
works.description_zh: 一个中间立着镜子的盒子：截肢者把健全的手臂放在镜子一侧，看到它的倒影出现在缺失肢体的位置，并同时活动双臂，这可以缓解幻肢的痉挛性疼痛。
works.idea_en: The felt body is a living construction of vision, movement and expectation; changing what one sees can change what one feels.
works.idea_zh: 被感受的身体是由视觉、动作与预期活生生地建构起来的；改变看到的东西，就可能改变感受到的东西。
works.method: A vertical mirror in a cardboard box creates the visual illusion of two intact limbs; patients perform symmetric movements while watching the reflection.
works.method_zh: 纸盒中竖立的镜子制造出两只完整肢体的视觉错觉；患者一边看倒影，一边做对称动作。

paper.title: Touching the phantom limb

works.title: Osmose
works.description: An immersive virtual space of trees, clouds and code navigated by breath and balance: breathe in to float up, breathe out to sink, lean to drift.
works.description_zh: 一个由树木、云和代码构成的沉浸式虚拟空间，用呼吸和平衡来导航：吸气上浮，呼气下沉，倾身漂移。
works.idea_en: Tying navigation to breath and balance turns VR into a meditative, embodied experience instead of hand-and-eye control.
works.idea_zh: 把导航与呼吸、平衡绑定，让 VR 成为冥想式的具身体验，而不是手眼控制。
works.method: Head-mounted display with a vest that senses chest expansion (breath) and tilt sensors for balance, inspired by scuba diving; real-time graphics on SGI computers.
works.method_zh: 头戴显示器配合感知胸廓扩张（呼吸）的背心与感知平衡的倾斜传感器，灵感来自潜水；实时图形运行于 SGI 计算机。

paper.title: Osmose: towards broadening the aesthetics of virtual reality

works.title: Descartes' Error: Emotion, Reason, and the Human Brain
works.description: Damasio's somatic marker hypothesis shows that bodily feelings tied to emotion guide decisions, so patients who lose them reason badly despite intact logic.
works.description_zh: Damasio 的躯体标记假说表明，与情绪相连的身体感受引导着决策；失去这些感受的病人即使逻辑完好，也难以做出合理判断。
works.idea_en: Descartes' error was separating mind from body: reason depends on the body's felt signals.
works.idea_zh: 笛卡尔的错误在于把心与身分开：理性依赖身体被感受到的信号。
works.method: Neurological case studies (Phineas Gage, patient Elliot), the Iowa Gambling Task and skin conductance measures.
works.method_zh: 神经学个案研究（Phineas Gage、病人 Elliot）、爱荷华赌博任务与皮肤电测量。

paper.title: Descartes' Error: Emotion, Reason, and the Human Brain

works.title_zh: 笛卡尔的错误：情绪、推理和人脑

works.title: Epizoo
works.description: Audience members click on a screen to move the performer's nose, mouth, ears, buttocks and pectorals through a pneumatic exoskeleton he wears.
works.description_zh: 观众点击屏幕，通过表演者身上的气动外骨骼，牵动他的鼻子、嘴、耳朵、臀部和胸肌。
works.idea_en: Being moved by strangers makes the body's boundary felt from both sides: the audience enjoys control, the performer feels intrusion.
works.idea_zh: 被陌生人牵动，让身体的边界从两侧都被感受到：观众享受控制，表演者感受侵入。
works.method: A body-worn pneumatic exoskeleton with actuators on the face and torso is driven from a computer interface with animated images of his body.
works.method_zh: 身上穿戴的气动外骨骼在面部和躯干装有执行器，由带有其身体动画图像的电脑界面驱动。

works.title: In Plane (MidiDancer)
works.description: A solo in which dancer Dawn Stoppiello wears the MidiDancer suit: the bending of her own elbows, knees and hips controls the video image and music around her.
works.description_zh: 舞者 Dawn Stoppiello 身穿 MidiDancer 舞衣的独舞：她自己肘、膝、髋的弯曲控制着周围的影像与音乐。
works.idea_en: Sensing from inside the joints ties media to felt bending rather than to how the body looks from outside.
works.idea_zh: 从关节内部感知，让媒体与被感受到的弯曲相连，而不是与身体的外观相连。
works.method: Flex sensors on the joints transmit wirelessly to a computer that maps joint angles to MIDI-controlled video and sound.
works.method_zh: 关节上的弯曲传感器无线传输到计算机，把关节角度映射为由 MIDI 控制的影像与声音。

works.title: Technics and Time, 1: The Fault of Epimetheus
works.description: Stiegler argues that the human is born without fixed qualities and has always become human through tools, writing and other external technical memory.
works.description_zh: Stiegler 主张人生来没有固定的属性，一直是通过工具、书写和其他外在的技术记忆而成为人的。
works.idea_en: There is no pure natural body that technology later augments: body and technics co-evolve, so the question is which technics care for the body-mind and which exhaust it.
works.idea_zh: 不存在一个后来才被技术增强的纯粹自然身体：身体与技术共同演化，问题在于哪些技术照料身心，哪些消耗身心。
works.method: Philosophical reading of Leroi-Gourhan's paleoanthropology, Heidegger and the Greek myth of Epimetheus; French original La Technique et le temps 1 (1994).
works.method_zh: 对 Leroi-Gourhan 古人类学、海德格尔与希腊神话中 Epimetheus 的哲学解读；法文原著 1994 年出版。

paper.venue: Galilée, 1994; English trans. Stanford University Press, 1998
paper.title: Technics and Time, 1: The Fault of Epimetheus

works.title_zh: 技术与时间1：爱比米修斯的过失

works.title: Sensing, Feeling, and Action
works.description: A collection of Bainbridge Cohen's essays and interviews from Contact Quarterly (1980 onward) on organs, glands, fluids, reflexes, the senses and developmental movement, with explorations readers can try.
works.description_zh: 汇集了班布里奇·科恩自 1980 年起在《Contact Quarterly》发表的文章与访谈，涉及器官、腺体、体液、反射、感官与发育动作，并附有读者可以尝试的探索练习。
works.idea_en: The book argues that perception is an action: how we move shapes what we can sense and feel, so designing a sensation also designs a way of moving.
works.idea_zh: 书中认为知觉本身是一种行动：我们如何动，塑造了我们能感觉与感受到什么；因此设计一种感觉，也就是在设计一种动的方式。
works.method: Essays, interviews and experiential exercises on the body systems of Body-Mind Centering; Contact Editions, 1993.
works.method_zh: 关于 Body-Mind Centering 各身体系统的文章、访谈与体验练习；Contact Editions，1993 年。

paper.title: Sensing, Feeling, and Action: The Experiential Anatomy of Body-Mind Centering

works.title: Stomach Sculpture
works.description: A small gold, silver and steel capsule was pushed down Stelarc's oesophagus into his stomach, where it opened, extended, flashed and beeped while an endoscope filmed it.
works.description_zh: 一个金、银和钢制的小胶囊经食道被送入 Stelarc 的胃里，在那里展开、伸缩、闪光并发出声响，由内窥镜拍摄。
works.idea_en: It turns the hidden inside of the body into a site for art, but the inside is felt only as strain and risk; inner sensation stays mute on camera.
works.idea_zh: 它把身体隐藏的内部变成艺术的场地，但这内部只被感受为紧绷与风险；内在感觉在镜头前依然沉默。
works.method: A servo-driven worm-screw mechanism of biocompatible metals was inserted 40 cm into the inflated stomach and filmed with a medical endoscope over two days.
works.method_zh: 由生物相容金属制成、伺服电机驱动的蜗杆机构被送入充气后的胃中约 40 厘米，用医用内窥镜在两天内拍摄。

works.title: Attunement Through the Body
works.description: Nagatomo develops Yuasa's theory into an account of 'attunement': how a cultivated body comes into resonance with things, others and nature, drawing on Zen, Noh and Japanese aesthetics.
works.description_zh: 长友繁法在汤浅泰雄理论的基础上发展出“调谐”的说明：修炼过的身体如何与物、他人和自然共振，材料来自禅、能乐与日本美学。
works.idea_en: Attunement is a bodily skill of resonance that can be trained; designing for it means supporting the body's capacity to tune in, not delivering information.
works.idea_zh: 调谐是一种可以训练的身体共振能力；为调谐而设计，意味着支持身体去“调频”，而不是传递信息。
works.method: Philosophical study (SUNY Series in Buddhist Studies) combining phenomenology and Japanese Buddhist texts.
works.method_zh: 哲学研究（纽约州立大学出版社佛教研究丛书），结合现象学与日本佛教文献。

paper.title: Attunement Through the Body

works.title: Pragmatist Aesthetics: Living Beauty, Rethinking Art
works.description: Shusterman's first major book reads Dewey's aesthetics against analytic philosophy and ends by proposing that the body and its disciplines belong inside aesthetics, the seed of somaesthetics.
works.description_zh: Shusterman 的第一部重要著作，以 Dewey 的美学回应分析哲学，并在结尾提出身体及其修习应属于美学，这正是身体美学的萌芽。
works.idea_en: Aesthetic experience is lived and bodily, so cultivating how we feel and move is itself an art of living.
works.idea_zh: 审美经验是亲历的、身体的，因此培养我们如何感受与运动，本身就是一门生活的艺术。
works.method: Philosophical argument drawing on Dewey's pragmatism, popular arts (rap, dance) and the ethics of self-fashioning.
works.method_zh: 以 Dewey 的实用主义为基础，结合流行艺术（说唱、舞蹈）与自我塑造的伦理展开哲学论证。

paper.title: Pragmatist Aesthetics: Living Beauty, Rethinking Art

works.title_zh: 实用主义美学：生活之美，艺术之思

works.title: The vOICe
works.description: Free software that turns camera images into soundscapes, scanning left to right with pitch for height and loudness for brightness; some long-term blind users describe visual-like experiences from it.
works.description_zh: 免费软件，把摄像头画面转换为声音景观：从左向右扫描，音高表示高度，响度表示亮度；一些长期使用的盲人描述了类似视觉的体验。
works.idea_en: A sense can be learned through practice in another channel, and what it feels like may change as the skill deepens.
works.idea_zh: 一种感官可以通过另一个通道的练习来习得，而它的感受会随着技能加深而改变。
works.method: Image-to-sound mapping at about one scan per second, running on laptops, phones and camera glasses; studied in behavioural and brain-imaging work on sensory substitution.
works.method_zh: 每秒约一次扫描的图像到声音映射，可运行在笔记本电脑、手机与摄像眼镜上；在感官替代的行为与脑成像研究中被广泛使用。

paper.title: An experimental system for auditory image representations

works.title: Prosthetics, Robotics and Remote Existence: Postevolutionary Strategies
works.description: Stelarc's manifesto-essay argues that the human body is 'obsolete' and should be redesigned with prostheses, robotics and networks.
works.description_zh: Stelarc 的宣言式文章主张人体已经“过时”，应该用义体、机器人和网络重新设计。
works.idea_en: It treats the body as hardware to upgrade, yet his performances show the opposite: every extension had to be learned and felt from inside. Read the essay against the work.
works.idea_zh: 文章把身体当作待升级的硬件，但他的表演恰恰相反：每一次延伸都必须从内部学会、感受。请把文章与作品对照着读。
works.method: Essay in Leonardo drawing on his Third Hand, suspensions and remote-actuation performances.
works.method_zh: 发表于《Leonardo》的文章，基于他的“第三只手”、身体悬吊与远程驱动表演。

paper.title: Prosthetics, Robotics and Remote Existence: Postevolutionary Strategies

works.title_zh: 义体、机器人与远程存在：后进化策略

works.title: The Embodied Mind: Cognitive Science and Human Experience
works.description: The book that named enaction: cognition as embodied action that brings forth a world, joined with Buddhist mindfulness as a disciplined way to examine lived experience.
works.description_zh: 为“生成”（enaction）命名的著作：认知是带出一个世界的具身行动，并以佛教正念作为考察亲历经验的严谨方法。
works.idea_en: Mind is not inside the head but enacted by a living body in its world, and experience can be trained and studied from within.
works.idea_zh: 心智不在头颅之内，而是由活的身体在其世界中生成的；经验可以从内部被训练、被研究。
works.method: Brings together cognitive science, phenomenology and Madhyamaka and Abhidharma Buddhism, with mindfulness/awareness meditation as a method.
works.method_zh: 融合认知科学、现象学与中观、阿毗达磨佛学，以正念/觉知禅修为方法。

paper.title: The Embodied Mind: Cognitive Science and Human Experience

works.title_zh: 具身心智：认知科学和人类经验

works.title: Will the Real Body Please Stand Up? Boundary Stories about Virtual Cultures
works.description: Stone studies phone-sex workers and early online communities such as CommuniTree to show how bodies and identities are built through technology.
works.description_zh: Stone 研究电话性工作者和 CommuniTree 等早期在线社区，展示身体与身份如何通过技术被建构。
works.idea_en: Against the dream of leaving the body in cyberspace, she writes that 'forgetting about the body is an old Cartesian trick': virtual life still rests on real, mortal bodies.
works.idea_zh: 针对在赛博空间中离开身体的梦想，她写道“忘记身体是一个古老的笛卡尔把戏”：虚拟生活仍然建立在真实而会死亡的身体之上。
works.method: Essay combining ethnography of early virtual communities with performance-studies analysis, published in Benedikt's Cyberspace: First Steps.
works.method_zh: 结合早期虚拟社区民族志与表演研究分析的文章，收录于 Benedikt 编《Cyberspace: First Steps》。

paper.venue: In M. Benedikt (ed.), Cyberspace: First Steps, MIT Press, 1991
paper.title: Will the Real Body Please Stand Up? Boundary Stories about Virtual Cultures

works.title_zh: 真正的身体请站出来？关于虚拟文化的边界故事

works.title: Full Catastrophe Living
works.description: Kabat-Zinn's book lays out the MBSR program week by week, with the body scan, sitting meditation and mindful yoga, for people living with stress, pain and illness.
works.description_zh: 卡巴金在书中按周介绍正念减压课程，包括身体扫描、静坐与正念瑜伽，面向与压力、疼痛和疾病共处的人。
works.idea_en: The subtitle names its stance: using the wisdom of your body and mind together; it is the standard reference for the body scan used in HCI studies.
works.idea_zh: 副标题点明了立场：一起运用身体与心的智慧；它是人机交互研究中引用身体扫描时的标准文献。
works.method: Program description, guided practices and patient stories from the UMass Stress Reduction Clinic; Delacorte, 1990 (revised 2013).
works.method_zh: 来自马萨诸塞大学减压诊所的课程说明、引导练习与病人故事；Delacorte，1990 年（2013 年修订）。

paper.title: Full Catastrophe Living: Using the Wisdom of Your Body and Mind to Face Stress, Pain, and Illness

works.title: Technology and the Lifeworld: From Garden to Earth
works.description: Ihde's book describes the kinds of relations people have with technologies, starting with 'embodiment relations' in which glasses or a dental probe become part of how we perceive.
works.description_zh: Ihde 的书描述人与技术的几种关系，首先是“具身关系”：眼镜或牙科探针成为我们感知方式的一部分。
works.idea_en: A well-fitted tool withdraws into the felt body and extends it, while also amplifying some sensations and reducing others; augmentation always reshapes experience.
works.idea_zh: 一个合手的工具会隐退进被感受的身体并延伸它，同时放大一些感觉、削弱另一些；增强总会重塑体验。
works.method: Postphenomenological analysis of embodiment, hermeneutic, alterity and background relations, with historical and cross-cultural cases.
works.method_zh: 对具身关系、诠释关系、他异关系与背景关系的后现象学分析，辅以历史与跨文化案例。

paper.title: Technology and the Lifeworld: From Garden to Earth

works.title_zh: 技术与生活世界：从伊甸园到尘世

works.title: The Absent Body
works.description: Leder asks why the body, the ground of all experience, usually disappears from awareness, and shows how it 'dys-appears', returning as a problem, in pain, illness and breakdown.
works.description_zh: Leder 追问：作为一切经验基础的身体为何平时从意识中消失？他指出身体在疼痛、疾病与失灵时会“异常显现”，作为问题回到意识里。
works.idea_en: Dualism grows from the body's own tendency to recede; noticing the body without waiting for pain is a practice to cultivate.
works.idea_zh: 二元论源自身体自身的隐退倾向；不必等到疼痛才去觉察身体，这是一种需要培养的修习。
works.method: Phenomenological analysis of the surface body, the visceral depths and the body in pain, drawing on Merleau-Ponty and on Asian contemplative traditions.
works.method_zh: 借鉴 Merleau-Ponty 与亚洲沉思传统，对表层身体、内脏深处与疼痛中的身体进行现象学分析。

paper.title: The Absent Body

works.title: The Reincarnation of Saint-ORLAN
works.description: In nine surgery-performances (1990–1993) ORLAN had her face reshaped under local anaesthesia while reading texts, directing the scene and broadcasting it live.
works.description_zh: 在九场手术表演（1990–1993）中，ORLAN 在局部麻醉下接受面部改造，同时朗读文本、指挥现场并进行直播。
works.idea_en: Staying awake and speaking during surgery refuses the split between a passive body and a watching mind: she is author and material at once.
works.idea_zh: 在手术中保持清醒并说话，拒绝“被动的身体”与“旁观的心灵”的分裂：她同时是作者与材料。
works.method: Cosmetic surgeons operated under local anaesthesia in costumes she designed; the operations were filmed, and Omnipresence (1993) was broadcast by satellite to galleries.
works.method_zh: 整形外科医生在局部麻醉下为她手术，身穿她设计的服装；手术被拍摄，《Omnipresence》（1993）通过卫星直播到多家画廊。

works.title: Underscore
works.description: A long group improvisation, often three hours or more, that follows a shared map of phases: arriving alone, the 'small dance', expanding into space and contact with others, and slowly returning to stillness and reflection.
works.description_zh: 一场通常长达三小时以上的集体即兴，依循一张共享的阶段地图：独自抵达、“小舞”、扩展到空间并与他人接触，再缓慢回到静止与回顾。
works.idea_en: The Underscore gives structure to emergence: a common score of states lets many bodies improvise together without a leader, a model for designing open-ended collective somatic experiences.
works.idea_zh: Underscore 为“涌现”提供结构：一份关于状态的共同乐谱，让许多身体无需领导者即可一起即兴，是设计开放式集体身体体验的范例。
works.method: Scored group improvisation with named phases and graphic symbols, developed by Nancy Stark Smith from 1990 within the Contact Improvisation community.
works.method_zh: 带有阶段命名与图形符号的有谱集体即兴，由南希·斯塔克·史密斯自 1990 年起在接触即兴社群中发展。

works.title: Life Forms
works.description: A figure-animation program in which choreographers sketch and sequence body shapes on screen; Merce Cunningham used it from 1989 to compose dances such as Trackers (1991).
works.description_zh: 一个人体动画程序，编舞家可在屏幕上勾画身体姿态并编排顺序；Merce Cunningham 从 1989 年起用它创作了《Trackers》（1991）等舞蹈。
works.idea_en: Designing for choreographers meant building around how they think movement in the body, with dancers' bodies still testing every idea.
works.idea_zh: 为编舞家设计，就是围绕他们在身体里思考动作的方式来构建工具，而每个想法最后仍由舞者的身体来检验。
works.method: Keyframe animation of articulated human figures with a stance/body editor, timeline and spatial stage view, developed iteratively with choreographers at Simon Fraser University.
works.method_zh: 带有姿态编辑器、时间线与舞台空间视图的关节人体关键帧动画，在西蒙弗雷泽大学与编舞家迭代开发。

paper.title: The evolution of an interface for choreographers

works.title: Somatic Experiencing
works.description: A practitioner helps a client track small bodily sensations, such as warmth, trembling or the urge to push, and moves attention slowly between activation and resources so that stuck survival responses can complete.
works.description_zh: 治疗者帮助来访者追踪细小的身体感觉，如温热、颤抖或想推开的冲动，并让注意在激活与资源之间缓慢往返，使卡住的生存反应得以完成。
works.idea_en: Levine treats trauma as an incomplete bodily response rather than only a memory; his ideas of titration (small doses) and pendulation (swinging between states) are useful pacing rules for any design that stirs strong feeling.
works.idea_zh: 莱文把创伤看作未完成的身体反应，而不只是记忆；他的“滴定”（小剂量）与“摆荡”（在状态之间来回）是任何会激起强烈感受的设计都可用的节奏原则。
works.method: Talk-and-sensation sessions using interoceptive tracking, titration and pendulation, developed by Levine from the 1970s and formalised under this name in the late 1980s; clinical evidence is still limited.
works.method_zh: 以内感受追踪、滴定与摆荡为核心的对话与感觉疗程，莱文自 1970 年代起发展，1980 年代末以此名称确立；临床证据仍有限。

works.title: Mind Children: The Future of Robot and Human Intelligence
works.description: A roboticist predicts that machines will match human intelligence and that a person's mind could be scanned neuron by neuron and moved into a robot body.
works.description_zh: 一位机器人学家预言机器将达到人类智能，人的心灵可以被逐个神经元扫描，并转移到机器人身体里。
works.idea_en: This is the plainest dualist position in the field: the mind is a pattern that can leave its flesh. Soma design answers that thinking and feeling are done by a living body, not stored in it.
works.idea_zh: 这是该领域最直白的二元论立场：心灵是一种可以离开血肉的模式。身体设计的回应是：思考与感受由活着的身体完成，而不是储存在身体里。
works.method: Book-length argument from robotics and computing trends, including the thought experiment of gradual robotic 'transmigration' of the mind.
works.method_zh: 一部基于机器人学与计算趋势的专著，包括心灵经机器人逐步“转世”的思想实验。

paper.title: Mind Children: The Future of Robot and Human Intelligence

works.title_zh: 心智之子：机器人与人类智能的未来

works.title: Somatics: Reawakening the Mind's Control of Movement, Flexibility, and Health
works.description: Hanna explains 'sensory-motor amnesia', habitual muscle contractions we no longer feel, and gives a set of slow exercises to regain voluntary sensing and control.
works.description_zh: 汉纳解释了“感觉—运动失忆”，即我们已感受不到的习惯性肌肉收缩，并给出一组缓慢的练习，以重新获得主动的感知与控制。
works.idea_en: Hanna argues that many problems blamed on ageing are learned body-mind habits and can be unlearned from within, which puts first-person sensing at the centre of health.
works.idea_zh: 汉纳认为许多被归咎于衰老的问题其实是习得的身心习惯，可以从内部“去学习”，这把第一人称的感知放到了健康的中心。
works.method: Theory of the reflexes of stress (red light, green light, trauma) plus illustrated self-practice exercises; Addison-Wesley, 1988.
works.method_zh: 关于压力反射（红灯、绿灯、创伤反射）的理论，加上配图的自我练习；Addison-Wesley，1988 年。

paper.title: Somatics: Reawakening the Mind's Control of Movement, Flexibility, and Health

works.title_zh: 身体学：唤醒心对动作、柔韧与健康的掌控

works.title: The Body in the Mind: The Bodily Basis of Meaning, Imagination, and Reason
works.description: Johnson introduces image schemas, recurring patterns of bodily experience such as balance, containment, path and force, and shows how they structure imagination and reason.
works.description_zh: Johnson 提出“意象图式”——平衡、容器、路径、力等反复出现的身体经验模式，并说明它们如何结构想象与推理。
works.idea_en: Reason grows out of the felt patterns of a moving, balancing body.
works.idea_zh: 理性从一个运动着、保持平衡的身体所感受到的模式中生长出来。
works.method: Philosophical analysis of image schemas and their metaphorical projection, with examples from balance, force and containment.
works.method_zh: 对意象图式及其隐喻投射的哲学分析，以平衡、力与容器等为例。

paper.title: The Body in the Mind: The Bodily Basis of Meaning, Imagination, and Reason

works.title_zh: 心智中的身体：意义、想象与理性的身体基础

works.title: The Tree of Knowledge: The Biological Roots of Human Understanding
works.description: An accessible account of autopoiesis: living beings are self-producing systems, and knowing is the living process by which an organism brings forth a world with others.
works.description_zh: 对自创生理论的通俗阐述：生命体是自我生产的系统，认知是生命体与他者一起带出一个世界的生命过程。
works.idea_en: To live is to know: cognition is not a mind representing the world but the whole organism coupling with its environment.
works.idea_zh: 活着就是认知：认知不是心智表征世界，而是整个生命体与环境相互耦合。
works.method: Biological and philosophical argument illustrated with examples from cell biology, nervous systems, language and social coupling.
works.method_zh: 以细胞生物学、神经系统、语言与社会耦合为例展开的生物学与哲学论证。

paper.title: The Tree of Knowledge: The Biological Roots of Human Understanding

works.title_zh: 知识之树：人类理解的生物学根源

works.title: The Body, Self-Cultivation, and Ki-Energy
works.description: Yuasa's study of ki as it is used in acupuncture, meditation and the martial arts, with a four-layer model of the lived body that links sensory-motor circuits, emotion and the unconscious. Japanese edition 1986 (Ki, Shugyō, Shintai); English 1993.
works.description_zh: 汤浅泰雄研究针灸、冥想与武术中的“气”，提出一个四层的活的身体模型，把感觉运动回路、情绪与无意识联系起来。日文原版《气・修行・身体》1986 年出版，英译本 1993 年出版。
works.idea_en: Ki names the felt link between body, emotion and environment: an energy that practice makes perceptible rather than a hidden substance.
works.idea_zh: 气指的是身体、情绪与环境之间被感受到的联系：它是修行使之可被觉察的能量，而不是一种隐藏的物质。
works.method: Reads Chinese and Japanese research on ki, acupuncture meridian measurements and meditators' reports alongside Western psychology and physiology.
works.method_zh: 把中日两国关于气的研究、经络测量与冥想者的报告，与西方心理学和生理学放在一起阅读。

paper.title: The Body, Self-Cultivation, and Ki-Energy

works.title: Very Nervous System
works.description: Video cameras watch a person moving in an empty space and a computer answers every movement with sound, so the body plays the room like an instrument.
works.description_zh: 摄像头注视在空旷空间里移动的人，计算机以声音回应每一个动作，身体就像演奏乐器一样演奏整个房间。
works.idea_en: Rokeby: the loop is fast enough that control dissolves into 'encounter and involvement', a felt partnership rather than command.
works.idea_zh: Rokeby 说：回路快到控制感消融为“相遇与投入”，成为一种被感受的伙伴关系，而不是命令。
works.method: Custom video-motion analysis of camera images, mapped in real time to synthesised and sampled sound (developed 1982–1991).
works.method_zh: 自制的视频运动分析处理摄像头图像，实时映射为合成与采样声音（1982–1991 年间开发）。

works.title: A Cyborg Manifesto
works.description: Haraway's essay uses the cyborg, a hybrid of organism and machine, as a feminist figure that breaks the boundaries between human and animal, organism and machine, physical and non-physical.
works.description_zh: Haraway 的文章把赛博格——有机体与机器的混合——当作女性主义形象，打破人与动物、有机体与机器、物质与非物质之间的界限。
works.idea_en: Her cyborg is embodied and situated: technology is already in our flesh, so the task is to take responsibility for how bodies are built, not to escape them.
works.idea_zh: 她的赛博格是具身的、处境化的：技术早已进入我们的血肉，因此任务是为身体如何被建构负责，而不是逃离身体。
works.method: Essay first published in Socialist Review (1985) and revised as 'A Cyborg Manifesto' in Simians, Cyborgs, and Women (1991).
works.method_zh: 最初发表于《Socialist Review》（1985），修订版以《赛博格宣言》收入《Simians, Cyborgs, and Women》（1991）。

paper.venue: Socialist Review 80, 1985; Simians, Cyborgs, and Women (Routledge, 1991)
paper.title: Simians, Cyborgs, and Women: The Reinvention of Nature

works.title: Body Weather
works.description: Dancers train through farm labour, a demanding physical workout and 'manipulations', in which one partner, eyes closed, is moved and touched by another; Min Tanaka founded Body Weather Farm in 1985.
works.description_zh: 舞者通过农活、高强度的身体训练以及“操控”练习来训练：一人闭眼，由另一人移动和触碰其身体；田中泯于 1985 年创立身体气象农场。
works.idea_en: The body is weather: always changing and shaped by its environment, so training means becoming sensitive to forces rather than fixing a technique.
works.idea_zh: 身体就是天气：它不断变化，并被环境所塑造，因此训练意味着对各种力变得敏感，而不是固定一种技术。
works.method: Workshops and farm residencies combining 'MB' (muscles/bones) conditioning, partnered manipulations and image-based improvisation.
works.method_zh: 结合“MB”（肌肉/骨骼）体能训练、双人操控与意象即兴的工作坊和农场驻留。

works.title: The Structure of Mi (〈Mi〉 no kōzō)
works.description: Ichikawa builds a theory of the lived body on the everyday Japanese word mi, which can mean flesh, self, social position and heart at once. Kōdansha Gakujutsu Bunko edition 1993.
works.description_zh: 市川浩以日语日常词“身”为基础建立活的身体理论：“身”同时可以指肉体、自我、社会位置与心。1993 年收入讲谈社学术文库。
works.idea_en: Ordinary language already knows the soma: mi is the body as self in relation, extending into clothes, tools, other people and place.
works.idea_zh: 日常语言早已懂得身体：“身”就是处在关系中的身体-自我，延伸到衣服、工具、他人与场所。
works.method: Close reading of idioms built on mi (mi ni tsukeru, mi ni shimiru, mi o makaseru) as evidence of a relational, non-dualist body.
works.method_zh: 细读以“身”构成的惯用语（身につける、身にしみる、身をまかせる等），作为关系性、非二元身体的证据。

paper.title: 〈身〉の構造：身体論を超えて

works.title: Hakomi Method
works.description: The client settles into mindfulness and the therapist offers a small experiment, such as a phrase ('you are welcome here') or a light touch, then both study the spontaneous bodily and emotional reaction.
works.description_zh: 来访者进入正念状态，治疗者提供一个小实验，例如一句话（“这里欢迎你”）或轻微的触碰，然后两人一起研究随之出现的身体与情绪反应。
works.idea_en: Hakomi assumes that core beliefs are organised in the body and can be studied in mindful states; its gentle 'probes' are a template for designing stimuli that reveal rather than direct felt experience.
works.idea_zh: 哈科米假设核心信念组织在身体之中，可以在正念状态下被研究；它温和的“探针”为设计“揭示而非引导”亲身体验的刺激提供了模板。
works.method: Mindfulness-based assisted self-study with verbal and touch 'probes', built on principles of nonviolence, organicity and mind-body holism; developed by Ron Kurtz in the 1970s, taught by the Hakomi Institute since 1981.
works.method_zh: 基于正念的辅助式自我探索，使用语言与触碰“探针”，以非暴力、有机性与身心整体性为原则；由库尔茨在 1970 年代发展，1981 年起由哈科米学院教授。

works.title: Bartenieff Fundamentals
works.description: A set of floor-based movement sequences, the 'Basic Six' such as the thigh lift, pelvic shift and arm circles, that connect breath, core and limbs through developmental patterns like head-tail, upper-lower and cross-lateral connectivity.
works.description_zh: 一组在地面进行的动作序列，即“基础六式”，如抬大腿、骨盆移动与手臂画圈，经由头尾、上下、对侧等发育连接模式，把呼吸、核心与四肢连在一起。
works.idea_en: Bartenieff insisted that intention and spatial imagination drive physical recovery, so exercises are about where you are going, not muscle strength; for designers, a movement is always movement toward something.
works.idea_zh: 巴特尼夫坚持意图与空间想象驱动身体康复，练习关注的是“往哪里去”而不是肌力；对设计者而言，动作总是朝向某处的动作。
works.method: Breath-supported, spatially intended floor sequences based on six patterns of total body connectivity; set out in Body Movement: Coping with the Environment (1980, with Dori Lewis).
works.method_zh: 以呼吸支撑、带空间意图的地面序列，基于六种全身连接模式；在《身体动作：应对环境》（1980，与多丽·刘易斯合著）中系统阐述。

works.title: Metaphors We Live By
works.description: Lakoff and Johnson show that everyday thought is structured by conceptual metaphors grounded in bodily experience, such as HAPPY IS UP, AFFECTION IS WARMTH and ARGUMENT IS WAR.
works.description_zh: Lakoff 与 Johnson 指出，日常思维由扎根于身体经验的概念隐喻所结构，如“快乐是上”“亲密是温暖”“辩论是战争”。
works.idea_en: Abstract meaning is built from felt bodily experience of up and down, warm and cold, near and far.
works.idea_zh: 抽象意义由上与下、暖与冷、近与远等被感受的身体经验建构。
works.method: Linguistic analysis of systematic patterns in everyday English expressions.
works.method_zh: 对日常英语表达中系统模式的语言学分析。

paper.title: Metaphors We Live By

works.title: Rosen Method Bodywork
works.description: The client lies on a table while the practitioner rests hands on places where breath does not move and muscles are held, and gently names what they notice, so feelings connected to that holding can surface.
works.description_zh: 来访者躺在治疗床上，治疗者把手放在呼吸不流动、肌肉紧绷的位置，轻声说出所注意到的，让与这种“保持”相关的情感浮现。
works.idea_en: Rosen Method's touch listens rather than manipulates; it models how a device that touches the body could invite awareness instead of correcting posture.
works.idea_zh: 罗森疗法的触碰是聆听而非操控；它示范了一个触碰身体的装置如何可以邀请觉察，而不是纠正姿态。
works.method: Gentle 'listening' touch combined with dialogue about sensation and breath, rooted in Gindler's work via Lucy Heyer; the Rosen Institute was formed in 1980.
works.method_zh: 温和的“聆听式”触碰结合关于感觉与呼吸的对话，经由露西·海尔承接金德勒的工作；罗森学院成立于 1980 年。

works.title: Third Hand
works.description: A robotic right hand attached to Stelarc's arm is driven by muscle signals from his abdomen and legs; he spent years learning to write with three hands.
works.description_zh: 一只机械右手装在 Stelarc 的手臂上，由他腹部和腿部的肌肉信号驱动；他花了数年学会用三只手写字。
works.idea_en: An added limb has to be learned from inside: the body remaps which muscles 'mean' a hand, a slow first-person training of body schema.
works.idea_zh: 新增的肢体必须从内部学会：身体重新分配哪些肌肉“代表”一只手，这是对身体图式缓慢的第一人称训练。
works.method: Electromyographic (EMG) electrodes on abdominal and leg muscles control the grasp, rotation and release of a mechanical hand built in Japan.
works.method_zh: 腹部与腿部肌肉上的肌电电极控制一只在日本制造的机械手的抓握、旋转与松开。

works.title: Throwing Like a Girl: A Phenomenology of Feminine Body Comportment, Motility, and Spatiality
works.description: Young describes how women in a sexist society often move with hesitancy, use only part of the body and experience it as a thing, and traces this to social norms rather than biology.
works.description_zh: Young 描述了在性别歧视社会中女性常常迟疑地运动、只调用身体的一部分、并把身体当作物体来体验，并将此归因于社会规范而非生理。
works.idea_en: How we feel our own capacities is shaped by norms; the lived body is always a gendered, situated body.
works.idea_zh: 我们如何感受自身的能力受规范塑造；活的身体总是有性别、处在情境中的身体。
works.method: Feminist reading of Merleau-Ponty and Beauvoir, applied to everyday movements such as throwing, carrying and taking up space.
works.method_zh: 以女性主义视角解读 Merleau-Ponty 与 Beauvoir，并应用于投掷、搬运、占据空间等日常动作。

paper.title: Throwing like a girl: A phenomenology of feminine body comportment motility and spatiality

works.title_zh: 像女孩那样丢球：女性身体举止、动作与空间性的现象学

works.title: Body Scan
works.description: Lying down, a person moves attention slowly through the body, from the toes of one foot up to the crown of the head, noticing whatever sensations are present, including none, and breathing into each region.
works.description_zh: 人躺下来，让注意力从一只脚的脚趾开始，缓慢地移动到头顶，注意此刻存在的任何感觉（包括没有感觉），并向每个部位“呼吸”。
works.idea_en: The body scan is the simplest tool for turning inward and making the body available to design; KTH's Teaching Soma Design course (DIS 2019) used body scans with Feldenkrais to widen students' design space.
works.idea_zh: 身体扫描是向内转、让身体成为设计材料的最简单工具；KTH 的“教授身体设计”课程（DIS 2019）把身体扫描与费登奎斯结合，拓宽学生的设计空间。
works.method: A 30–45 minute guided sweep of attention through body regions, adapted in MBSR from the Burmese Vipassana tradition of U Ba Khin and S. N. Goenka.
works.method_zh: 30–45 分钟的引导练习，让注意逐区扫过身体；MBSR 将其改编自乌巴庆与葛印卡的缅甸内观传统。

works.title: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR)
works.description: An eight-week course in which participants learn the body scan, sitting meditation on the breath and gentle yoga, and bring non-judging attention to pain, stress and daily routines.
works.description_zh: 为期八周的课程，参与者学习身体扫描、以呼吸为对象的静坐和温和的瑜伽，并把不评判的注意带入疼痛、压力与日常生活。
works.idea_en: MBSR framed attention to bodily sensation as a secular clinical skill; its body-first practices became the default template that many biofeedback and wellbeing technologies imitate, often without the non-striving attitude.
works.idea_zh: 正念减压把对身体感受的注意发展为一种世俗的临床技能；它以身体为先的练习成为许多生物反馈与健康科技模仿的默认模板，但常常丢掉了“不强求”的态度。
works.method: Weekly group sessions, a day-long retreat and daily home practice with guided recordings; started at the University of Massachusetts Medical School in 1979.
works.method_zh: 每周团体课程、一日静修和每天的家庭练习（配合引导录音）；1979 年始于马萨诸塞大学医学院。

works.title: Focusing
works.description: Gendlin's popular book teaches the six Focusing steps for finding and staying with a bodily 'felt sense' of a problem until it shifts.
works.description_zh: 简德林的大众读物，教授聚焦的六个步骤：找到并停留在关于某个问题的身体“感觉感”上，直到它发生转变。
works.idea_en: It makes the felt sense practical: a designer can use the same steps to articulate what a prototype feels like before having words for it.
works.idea_zh: 它让“感觉感”变得可操作：设计者可以用同样的步骤，在找到词语之前表述一个原型给人的感觉。
works.method: A step-by-step manual with examples from therapy and everyday life; Everest House 1978, later Bantam.
works.method_zh: 附有治疗与日常例子的分步手册；Everest House 1978 年出版，后由 Bantam 再版。

paper.title: Focusing

works.title: Six Viewpoints
works.description: Performers practise noticing and working with six materials of performance, space, shape, time, emotion, movement and story, one at a time, in solo and group improvisations.
works.description_zh: 表演者在独舞与集体即兴中，一次只关注并运用一种表演材料：空间、形状、时间、情感、动作、故事。
works.idea_en: The Viewpoints treat attention as a skill that can be split into channels; designers use this to structure what participants notice in embodied ideation and bodystorming.
works.idea_zh: “观点”把注意力看作可以分频道训练的技能；设计者用它来组织参与者在具身构思与身体风暴中关注什么。
works.method: Improvisation exercises organised by six 'viewpoints', taught in NYU's Experimental Theater Wing since 1978 and later adapted by Anne Bogart and Tina Landau.
works.method_zh: 以六个“观点”组织的即兴练习，1978 年起在纽约大学实验剧场系教授，后被安妮·博加特与蒂娜·兰道改编。

works.title: Snoezelen
works.description: A multisensory room with soft light, bubble tubes, music, textures and scents where people with intellectual disabilities, autism or dementia can rest and explore without a task.
works.description_zh: 一间有柔光、气泡灯管、音乐、质感与气味的多感官房间，智力障碍者、自闭症者或失智者可以在这里无任务地休息与探索。
works.idea_en: A space that asks nothing lets a body settle and explore at its own pace; well-being comes through sensing, not performance.
works.idea_zh: 一个什么都不要求的空间，让身体按自己的节奏安定与探索；安适来自感受，而不是表现。
works.method: Controlled multisensory environment with an accompanying therapist; the name combines Dutch 'snuffelen' (to sniff, explore) and 'doezelen' (to doze).
works.method_zh: 由治疗师陪伴的可控多感官环境；名称结合了荷兰语 snuffelen（嗅探、探索）与 doezelen（打盹）。

works.title: Tamalpa Life/Art Process
works.description: Participants move a theme from their life, draw what they felt, speak or write about it, and dance again, cycling between body, image and word; Anna Halprin developed it from her own dances through cancer.
works.description_zh: 参与者把生活中的一个主题动出来，画下感受，说或写下来，再跳一次，在身体、图像与语言之间循环；安娜·哈普林从自己与癌症共处时的舞蹈中发展出它。
works.idea_en: The process assumes that body, feeling and imagination speak the same story in different languages, so moving between them (the 'psychokinetic visualisation' loop) deepens both; designers can borrow this loop for somatic reflection.
works.idea_zh: 这一历程假设身体、情感与想象用不同的语言讲述同一个故事，在它们之间转换（“心理动觉视觉化”循环）会让两者都更深；设计者可以借用这一循环做身体反思。
works.method: Movement, drawing and verbal reflection in a structured cycle, informed by the RSVP Cycles scoring method; taught by the Tamalpa Institute founded in 1978.
works.method_zh: 动作、绘画与口头反思组成的结构化循环，受 RSVP 循环乐谱方法影响；由 1978 年创立的塔玛帕学院教授。

works.title: Admiring La Argentina
works.description: A solo in which Ohno, then in his seventies, in a woman's dress and hat, evokes the Spanish dancer Antonia Mercé, whom he had seen in 1926, moving between trembling fragility and joy; directed by Hijikata.
works.description_zh: 年逾七十的大野一雄身着女装与帽子，追忆他在 1926 年看过的西班牙舞者 Antonia Mercé，在颤抖的脆弱与喜悦之间舞动；由土方巽导演。
works.idea_en: Memory lives in the body and can be danced: an old body becomes fully expressive when it moves from felt memory rather than technique.
works.idea_zh: 记忆活在身体里，并且可以被舞出来：当衰老的身体从被感受的记忆而非技术出发时，它可以充分地表达。
works.method: Solo butoh performance premiered in Tokyo in 1977 and toured internationally after its showing at the Nancy International Festival.
works.method_zh: 舞踏独舞，1977 年在东京首演，在南锡国际艺术节演出后开始国际巡演。

works.title: The Body: Toward an Eastern Mind-Body Theory
works.description: Yuasa reads Dōgen, Kūkai, Nishida, Watsuji and Noh theory to show how Japanese thought treats body and mind as something unified through practice. Published in Japanese in 1977 and in English (SUNY Press) in 1987.
works.description_zh: 汤浅泰雄通过解读道元、空海、西田几多郎、和辻哲郎与能乐理论，说明日本思想如何把身与心看作经由修行而统一的整体。日文原版 1977 年出版，英译本 1987 年由纽约州立大学出版社出版。
works.idea_en: Body-mind unity is an achievement of cultivation, not a starting fact: the more the body is trained, the less mind and body are felt as two.
works.idea_zh: 身心一如是修行的成就，而不是起点：身体越是受到修炼，身与心就越不再被感受为两个东西。
works.method: Comparative philosophy that pairs Japanese self-cultivation texts with Merleau-Ponty, Bergson and psychosomatic medicine, and describes a 'dark consciousness' of the body below awareness.
works.method_zh: 比较哲学：把日本修行文献与梅洛-庞蒂、柏格森和身心医学对读，并提出觉知之下的身体“暗的意识”。

paper.title: The Body: Toward an Eastern Mind-Body Theory

works.title: Zen Shiatsu
works.description: The giver uses relaxed body weight rather than muscle, keeping one 'mother hand' still while the other explores, and feels for kyo (empty) and jitsu (full) areas along extended meridians.
works.description_zh: 施术者以放松的体重而不是肌肉力量按压，一只“母手”保持静止，另一只手探寻，沿扩展的经络感知“虚”与“实”。
works.idea_en: Therapeutic touch is a two-way listening: the practitioner's own relaxation and attention are part of what the receiver feels.
works.idea_zh: 疗愈性的触摸是双向的倾听：施术者自身的放松与专注，也是接受者感受到的一部分。
works.method: Floor-based pressure and stretches on a futon, guided by Masunaga's meridian charts and hara (abdominal) diagnosis, set out in his book Zen Shiatsu (1977).
works.method_zh: 在地垫上进行的按压与伸展，依据增永静人的经络图与腹诊，整理于其著作《Zen Shiatsu》（1977）。

works.title: Estruturação do Self (Structuring of the Self)
works.description: A therapeutic practice in which Clark placed 'relational objects' (air bags, stones, shells, bags of water and seeds) on the body of a person lying down, in sessions lasting months.
works.description_zh: 一种治疗实践：Clark 在躺着的人身上放置“关系物件”（气囊、石头、贝壳、装水或种子的袋子），疗程持续数月。
works.idea_en: Objects exist only in relation to a body: weight, warmth and texture on the skin can reorganise body memory and sense of self.
works.idea_zh: 物件只在与身体的关系中存在：皮肤上的重量、温度与质地可以重组身体记忆与自我感。
works.method: Individual sessions with hand-made relational objects applied to the client's body, developed from 1976 until her death in 1988.
works.method_zh: 一对一的疗程，把手工制作的关系物件施于来访者身体上，从 1976 年一直发展到她 1988 年去世。

works.title: Hanna Somatic Education
works.description: Slow 'pandiculation' exercises, in which a person voluntarily contracts a habitually tight muscle group and then releases it very slowly, to regain sensation and control of muscles lost to what Hanna called sensory-motor amnesia.
works.description_zh: 缓慢的“伸展收放”（pandiculation）练习：主动收紧长期紧张的肌群，再非常缓慢地放开，以重新获得因汉纳所说“感觉—运动失忆”而失去的感觉与控制。
works.idea_en: Hanna defined soma as the body perceived from within by a first person, as distinct from the body seen from outside; soma design takes both its name and its first-person stance from this definition.
works.idea_zh: 汉纳把 soma 定义为由第一人称从内部感知的身体，区别于从外部看见的身体；身体设计的名称与第一人称立场都来自这一定义。
works.method: Guided voluntary contraction and slow release of muscle groups plus hands-on sessions, drawing on Feldenkrais; Hanna coined 'somatics' in 1976.
works.method_zh: 引导性的肌群主动收缩与缓慢放松，并配合手法课程，借鉴费登奎斯；汉纳于 1976 年提出“somatics”一词。

works.title: Suspensions
works.description: Between 1976 and 1988 Stelarc hung his body 25 times from hooks through the skin, over rocks, the sea, a New York street and a Copenhagen square.
works.description_zh: 1976 至 1988 年间，Stelarc 用穿过皮肤的钩子悬吊自己的身体 25 次，地点有礁石、海边、纽约街道和哥本哈根广场。
works.idea_en: Before any robot, his cyborg work started with the felt limits of skin, weight and gravity; he called the body 'obsolete' while testing it from inside.
works.idea_zh: 在任何机器人出现之前，他的赛博格创作始于皮肤、重量与重力被感受到的极限；他一边称身体“过时”，一边从内部检验它。
works.method: Steel hooks pierced the skin and were tied to ropes and pulleys; in some events amplified heartbeat and muscle (EMG) sounds made the stretched body audible.
works.method_zh: 钢钩穿过皮肤，连接绳索和滑轮；部分场次放大了心跳和肌电声音，让被拉伸的身体变得可听。

works.title: Mindful Breathing and Walking Meditation (Plum Village)
works.description: Walking slowly and matching steps to in- and out-breaths ('I have arrived, I am home'), and returning to the breath when a bell sounds; taught in The Miracle of Mindfulness (1975) and at Plum Village.
works.description_zh: 缓慢行走，让脚步与吸气、呼气相合（“我已到了，我已到家”），听到钟声时回到呼吸；这些方法记载于《正念的奇迹》（1975），并在梅村传授。
works.idea_en: Mindfulness is bodily: coming back to breath and feet reunites body and mind in the present moment.
works.idea_zh: 正念是身体性的：回到呼吸与双脚，就让身与心在当下重新合一。
works.method: Everyday practices of mindful breathing, walking, eating and bells of mindfulness, spread through books, retreats and the Plum Village community founded in 1982.
works.method_zh: 日常的正念呼吸、行禅、正念饮食与正念钟声，经由书籍、禅修营以及 1982 年创立的梅村社区传播。

works.title: The Body as Spirit (Seishin to shite no shintai)
works.description: Ichikawa's phenomenology of the body argues that human reality cannot be separated from the concrete body, and describes the body as subject, as object and as an 'entangled' whole that reaches into tools and others. First published by Keisō Shobō in 1975; Kōdansha Gakujutsu Bunko edition 1992.
works.description_zh: 市川浩的身体现象学主张人的现实无法与具体的身体分离，并把身体描述为主体、对象以及延伸到工具与他人之中的“错综体”。1975 年由劲草书房出版，1992 年收入讲谈社学术文库。
works.idea_en: The body is already spirit: thinking, feeling and acting are one body extending itself into the world, so design shapes the mind by shaping how the body reaches.
works.idea_zh: 身体本身就是精神：思考、感受与行动都是同一个身体向世界的延伸，因此设计通过塑造身体的延伸方式来塑造心灵。
works.method: Phenomenological analysis in dialogue with Merleau-Ponty, Gestalt psychology and physiology, organised as the body as phenomenon, as structure and as action.
works.method_zh: 与梅洛-庞蒂、格式塔心理学和生理学对话的现象学分析，分为“现象的身体”“结构的身体”“行动的结构”三部分。

paper.title: 精神としての身体

works.title: Videoplace
works.description: Visitors see their live silhouettes on a large screen, where they can play with graphic creatures, draw with their fingers and touch the silhouettes of people in another room.
works.description_zh: 观众在大屏幕上看到自己的实时剪影，可以与图形生物玩耍、用手指作画，并触碰另一房间里其他人的剪影。
works.idea_en: The whole, unencumbered body can be the interface; no gloves, goggles or controllers are needed to feel present.
works.idea_zh: 不穿戴任何设备的整个身体就可以是界面；无需手套、眼镜或控制器也能感到在场。
works.method: Real-time camera silhouette extraction on custom hardware, composited with graphics and linked between separate rooms.
works.method_zh: 在自制硬件上实时提取摄像头剪影，与图形合成，并连接不同的房间。

paper.title: VIDEOPLACE—an artificial reality

works.title: Body-Mind Centering
works.description: Students embody one body system at a time (bones, organs, fluids, glands, cells) and the developmental movement patterns of infancy, moving and vocalising from it until they can feel how that system shapes mood and attention.
works.description_zh: 学员一次“体现”一个身体系统（骨骼、器官、体液、腺体、细胞）以及婴儿期的发育动作模式，从这个系统出发去动、去发声，直到能感受到它如何塑造情绪与注意力。
works.idea_en: In Body-Mind Centering the mind is found in each tissue: every body system has its own quality of feeling and moving, so a designer can ask which system an interaction speaks to, not just which muscle.
works.idea_zh: 在 Body-Mind Centering 里，心就在每一种组织之中：每个身体系统都有自己的感受与运动质感，因此设计者可以追问一个交互在与哪个系统对话，而不只是哪块肌肉。
works.method: Experiential anatomy: touch, imagery, sound and movement explorations of body systems and developmental patterns, taught through the School for Body-Mind Centering founded in 1973.
works.method_zh: 体验式解剖学：用触碰、意象、声音与动作探索身体系统和发育模式，经由 1973 年创立的 Body-Mind Centering 学校教授。

works.title: Awareness Through Movement
works.description: Feldenkrais's book explains why we act according to our self-image and gives twelve lessons, such as lifting the head or coordinating flexors and extensors, that readers do lying on the floor.
works.description_zh: 费登奎斯在书中解释了人为何按照自我意象行动，并给出十二节课，例如抬头、协调屈肌与伸肌，读者躺在地上即可练习。
works.idea_en: Its core claim, that every action involves moving, sensing, feeling and thinking together, is the practical non-dualism soma designers adopt when they design from Feldenkrais lessons.
works.idea_zh: 书的核心主张是每一个动作都同时包含运动、感觉、感受与思考，这正是身体设计者从费登奎斯课出发设计时所采纳的实践性非二元论。
works.method: Theory chapters on self-image and learning followed by twelve scripted Awareness Through Movement lessons; Harper & Row, 1972.
works.method_zh: 关于自我意象与学习的理论章节，加上十二节有脚本的“动中觉察”课程；Harper & Row，1972 年。

paper.title: Awareness Through Movement: Health Exercises for Personal Growth

works.title: Contact Improvisation
works.description: Two or more dancers keep a rolling point of physical contact, sharing weight, falling, lifting and following momentum; the 'Small Dance' of standing still and sensing the reflexes that keep you upright is its basic exercise.
works.description_zh: 两名或更多舞者保持一个滚动的身体接触点，分担重量、跌落、托举、顺着动量走；静立并感受维持站立的反射的“小舞”是它的基本练习。
works.idea_en: Contact Improvisation shows that two bodies can think together through touch, faster than conscious decision; for designers of social touch it offers a trained vocabulary of listening through skin and weight.
works.idea_zh: 接触即兴表明，两个身体能通过触碰一起“思考”，比有意识的决定更快；对社交触觉的设计者而言，它提供了一套经由皮肤与重量去“聆听”的训练有素的词汇。
works.method: Duet improvisation through shared weight, rolling contact and reflexes, practised in classes and open jams; initiated by Steve Paxton in 1972 (Magnesium) and documented in the Videoda film Fall After Newton (1987).
works.method_zh: 以分担重量、滚动接触与反射为基础的双人即兴，在课程与开放“即兴会”中练习；1972 年由帕克斯顿发起（Magnesium），并由 Videoda 影片《牛顿之后的坠落》（1987）记录。

works.title: Pencil Mask
works.description: A mask of fabric straps with pencils sticking out from the face; by rocking her head in front of a wall, Horn draws marks that record the rhythm of her movement.
works.description_zh: 一副布带面罩，脸前伸出许多铅笔；Horn 在墙前摆动头部，画下记录自己动作节奏的痕迹。
works.idea_en: The body becomes a drawing instrument; the drawing is a trace of how the head and neck felt their way across the wall.
works.idea_zh: 身体成了绘画工具；画面是头颈摸索着划过墙面时的感受痕迹。
works.method: Wearable mask of straps and pencils, used in a filmed performance; the mask is in the Tate collection.
works.method_zh: 由绑带与铅笔构成的可穿戴面罩，用于一段拍摄下来的表演；面罩现藏于泰特美术馆。

works.title: Deep Listening
works.description: Groups perform text scores that ask them to listen to everything, including their own body sounds and the room, and to sound or stay silent in response; workshops mix body work, dreams and listening walks.
works.description_zh: 团体演绎文字乐谱，被要求聆听一切，包括自身的身体声音和房间，并以发声或沉默回应；工作坊还结合身体练习、梦境与聆听漫步。
works.idea_en: Oliveros distinguished hearing from listening: listening is a bodily, relational attention that can be trained, which invites designers to treat sound as something the whole soma takes part in.
works.idea_zh: 奥利维罗斯区分了“听见”与“聆听”：聆听是可以训练的身体性、关系性注意；这邀请设计者把声音当作整个身体参与其中的事。
works.method: Listening and sounding exercises, text scores (Sonic Meditations, 1971) and group retreats; named Deep Listening after a 1988 recording in the Fort Worden cistern.
works.method_zh: 聆听与发声练习、文字乐谱（《声音冥想》，1971）和团体静修；因 1988 年在沃登堡蓄水池的录音而得名“深度聆听”。

works.title: Rolfing Structural Integration
works.description: A series of ten hands-on sessions in which a practitioner works slowly and deeply on connective tissue and gives movement prompts, aiming to reorganise how the whole body stands and moves in gravity.
works.description_zh: 由十次手法课程组成：治疗者缓慢而深入地处理结缔组织并给出动作提示，意在重组整个身体在重力中站立与运动的方式。
works.idea_en: Rolf treated posture as an organisation of the whole person in gravity, with emotional and bodily holding inseparable; its health claims are not supported by evidence, but it shaped how somatics thinks about fascia and touch.
works.idea_zh: 罗尔夫把姿态看作整个人在重力中的组织方式，情绪与身体的“保持”不可分；其健康功效缺乏证据支持，但它影响了身体学对筋膜与触碰的理解。
works.method: Ten-session manual therapy protocol ('the recipe') on fascia combined with movement education, developed from the 1940s and taught by the Rolf Institute founded in 1971.
works.method_zh: 针对筋膜、为期十次的手法治疗方案（“配方”），结合动作教育；自 1940 年代发展，由 1971 年成立的罗尔夫学院教授。

works.title: Bodies in Revolt: A Primer in Somatic Thinking
works.description: Hanna's manifesto for 'somatic thinking' argues that Western culture is shifting to treat humans as living somas, bodies experienced from within, rather than as minds carried by machines.
works.description_zh: Hanna 的“身心思维”宣言，认为西方文化正在转向把人看作活的 soma——从内部被经验的身体，而不是被机器承载的心智。
works.idea_en: A soma is the body perceived from within by first-person perception: one self-sensing, self-moving process, not a mind plus a body.
works.idea_zh: soma 是以第一人称从内部感知的身体：一个自我感受、自我运动的过程，而不是心加上身。
works.method: Philosophical essay drawing on Darwin, Nietzsche, Merleau-Ponty and phenomenology; Hanna later defined the term in 'What Is Somatics?' (1986) and built Hanna Somatic Education on it.
works.method_zh: 以达尔文、尼采、Merleau-Ponty 与现象学为资源的哲学论著；Hanna 后来在《What Is Somatics?》（1986）中界定了这个词，并据此创立 Hanna 身心教育。

paper.title: Bodies in Revolt: A Primer in Somatic Thinking

works.title_zh: 身体的反叛：身心思维入门

works.title: Einhorn (Unicorn)
works.description: A woman walks slowly through fields and woods wearing a tall white horn strapped to her head with bandages around her upper body.
works.description_zh: 一位女性头上用绑带固定着一只高高的白色角，绷带缠绕上身，缓慢地穿过田野和树林。
works.idea_en: A small addition to the head changes posture, balance and pace completely; extension makes the whole body newly felt.
works.idea_zh: 头上的一点添加就彻底改变了姿态、平衡与步伐；延伸让整个身体被重新感受到。
works.method: Wearable body sculpture of wood and fabric straps, performed outdoors and recorded on 16 mm film.
works.method_zh: 由木材与织物绑带构成的可穿戴身体雕塑，在户外表演并以 16 毫米胶片记录。

works.title: Focusing
works.description: A person turns attention to the middle of the body and waits for a vague 'felt sense' of a situation, then tries words or images against it until one fits and the body registers a 'felt shift'.
works.description_zh: 人把注意转向身体中部，等待关于某个处境的模糊“感觉感”（felt sense），再用词语或意象去对照，直到有一个契合、身体出现“感觉转变”（felt shift）。
works.idea_en: Gendlin showed that meaning is bodily before it is verbal: the felt sense knows more than we can say, which grounds first-person methods where designers articulate what a design feels like.
works.idea_zh: 简德林表明，意义在成为语言之前是身体性的：感觉感知道的比我们能说出的更多，这为设计者表述“设计感觉如何”的第一人称方法提供了基础。
works.method: Six steps (clearing a space, felt sense, handle, resonating, asking, receiving), practised alone or in listening partnerships; first described in a 1969 paper from Gendlin's psychotherapy research with Carl Rogers.
works.method_zh: 六个步骤（清理空间、感觉感、把手、共鸣、询问、接收），可独自或在“聆听伙伴”中练习；最早见于简德林 1969 年基于与罗杰斯合作的心理治疗研究发表的论文。

paper.title: Focusing

works.title: Tactile Vision Substitution System (TVSS) and BrainPort
works.description: Blind people sat in a dental chair fitted with 400 vibrating pins on the back, fed by a camera they could move; with practice they located and recognised objects 'out there', not on the skin. The later BrainPort moves the image to an electrode grid on the tongue.
works.description_zh: 盲人坐在背部装有 400 个振动针的牙科椅上，振动针由他们可以移动的摄像头驱动；经过练习，他们能定位并辨认“在外面”的物体，而不是觉得刺激在皮肤上。后来的 BrainPort 把图像转移到舌头上的电极阵列。
works.idea_en: Perception is something the whole acting body learns: once people could move the camera themselves, touch on the back became a kind of seeing located in the world.
works.idea_zh: 知觉是整个行动着的身体习得的：一旦人们能自己移动摄像头，背上的触觉就变成了一种定位在世界中的“看”。
works.method: A TV camera image converted to a 20 x 20 array of vibrotactile stimulators on the back (1969); BrainPort uses a head-worn camera and electrotactile stimulation of the tongue.
works.method_zh: 电视摄像头图像被转换为背部 20 x 20 振动触觉刺激阵列（1969）；BrainPort 使用头戴摄像头和舌部电触觉刺激。

paper.title: Vision Substitution by Tactile Image Projection

works.title_zh: 触觉视觉替代系统（TVSS）与 BrainPort

works.title: Vipassana Meditation (as taught by S. N. Goenka)
works.description: In a silent ten-day residential course, meditators first watch the breath at the nostrils (Anapana) and then sweep attention systematically through bodily sensations, observing them without reacting.
works.description_zh: 在为期十天的禁语住宿课程中，禅修者先观察鼻孔处的呼吸（安那般那），再系统地让注意扫过全身感受，只观察而不反应。
works.idea_en: The technique treats mind and body as one flow of changing sensation and trains equanimity towards it; it is a direct source of the clinical body scan that soma design workshops use.
works.idea_zh: 这一方法把身与心视为一股不断变化的感受之流，并训练对它的平等心；它是身体设计工作坊所用的临床身体扫描的直接来源。
works.method: Ten-day silent retreats with fixed timetables, recorded instructions and evening discourses, offered free worldwide since Goenka began teaching in India in 1969.
works.method_zh: 按固定作息进行的十日禁语静修，配合录音指导与晚间开示；葛印卡 1969 年在印度开始教学，此后在全球免费开设。

works.title: Éden
works.description: A walk-through environment of sand, straw, water, leaves and small shelters where visitors go barefoot, lie down and rest.
works.description_zh: 一个可穿行的环境，铺着沙子、稻草、水和树叶，还有小小的棚屋，观众赤脚行走、躺下、休息。
works.idea_en: Oiticica called it a place for 'crelazer' (creative leisure): sensing with the whole body, slowly, is the work.
works.idea_zh: Oiticica 称之为“创造性闲暇”（crelazer）的场所：用整个身体、缓慢地感受，就是作品。
works.method: Installation of natural materials and enclosures (Ninhos, Bólides) first built for his exhibition at the Whitechapel Gallery, London.
works.method_zh: 由自然材料和围合空间（Ninhos、Bólides）构成的装置，最初为伦敦 Whitechapel 画廊的展览搭建。
exhibited: To Organize Delirium, Carnegie Museum of Art 2016

works.title: Continuum
works.description: Practitioners lie or sit and combine breaths and sounds with very small wave-like movements, then rest and sense the aftermath, often discovering spiralling motions that feel more like water than muscle.
works.description_zh: 练习者躺或坐，把呼吸与发声结合非常细小的波浪状动作，然后休息并感受余韵，常会发现一种更像水而非肌肉的螺旋运动。
works.idea_en: Conrad saw the body as fluid, continuous with the oceans and with early life forms; designing from this view means working with undulation and resonance instead of discrete commands.
works.idea_zh: 康拉德把身体看作流体，与海洋和早期生命形态相连；从这一视角设计，意味着以波动与共振而非离散指令来工作。
works.method: Breath and sound sequences, micro-movement, and 'open attention' rests between explorations; founded by Emilie Conrad in 1967.
works.method_zh: 呼吸与发声序列、微动作，以及探索之间的“开放注意”休息；1967 年由艾米莉·康拉德创立。

works.title: Máscaras Sensoriais (Sensorial Masks)
works.description: Cloth hoods that cover the whole head, fitted with small bags of herbs at the nose, sound devices at the ears and lenses at the eyes, change how the wearer smells, hears and sees.
works.description_zh: 覆盖整个头部的布质头罩，鼻前有装着香草的小袋，耳边有发声装置，眼前有镜片，改变佩戴者的嗅觉、听觉与视觉。
works.idea_en: Blocking and altering the everyday senses turns the wearer inward and makes perception itself felt.
works.idea_zh: 阻断并改变日常感官，把佩戴者转向内部，让感知本身被感受到。
works.method: Fabric masks in different colours, each with its own combination of scent sachets, ear devices and optical eyepieces.
works.method_zh: 不同颜色的织物面罩，各自组合了香料包、耳部装置与光学目镜。

works.title: O Eu e o Tu (The I and the You)
works.description: Two people, hooded and unable to see, wear heavy suits joined by a tube; zippers on each suit open onto textures the other can explore by touch.
works.description_zh: 两个人戴着头罩、看不见，穿着以一根管子相连的厚重连体衣；每件衣服上的拉链打开后露出可供对方触摸探索的材质。
works.idea_en: Knowing another person through touch alone reorganises the felt sense of self and other, including gendered expectations.
works.idea_zh: 只通过触摸去认识另一个人，会重组对自我与他人的感受，也包括性别化的预期。
works.method: Industrial plastic overalls lined with materials such as foam, rubber and water bags, with hoods and a connecting tube.
works.method_zh: 工业塑料连体衣，内衬泡沫、橡胶、水袋等材料，配有头罩与连接管。

works.title: Iyengar Yoga
works.description: Students hold yoga postures with exact attention to alignment, using belts, blocks, blankets and chairs so that each person can feel the intended action of the pose in their own body.
works.description_zh: 学员以对排列的精确注意保持瑜伽体式，借助带子、砖、毯子和椅子，使每个人都能在自己身体里感受到体式要求的动作。
works.idea_en: Iyengar used precise alignment to bring awareness into every part of the body, down to the skin and the breath; his props show how external objects can help a body feel from within, a precedent for supportive soma design artefacts.
works.idea_zh: 艾扬格借助精确的排列把觉察带到身体的每一处，直至皮肤与呼吸；他的辅具表明外部物件可以帮助身体从内部去感受，是支持性身体设计物件的先例。
works.method: Detailed alignment instruction, long holds, sequencing and props, set out in Light on Yoga (1966); yoga as practised in Western studios.
works.method_zh: 细致的排列指导、长时间停留、序列编排与辅具，阐述于《瑜伽之光》（1966）；即西方瑜伽馆中的练习方式。

works.title: Respire Comigo (Breathe with Me)
works.description: A rubber tube, closed at both ends, is stretched and released by the participant's hands so that it rhythmically 'breathes' next to their ear.
works.description_zh: 一根两端封闭的橡胶管，被参与者双手拉伸又放开，在耳边有节奏地“呼吸”。
works.idea_en: An object can lend the body a breath to follow; noticing its rhythm turns attention to one's own breathing.
works.idea_zh: 一个物件可以借给身体一种可以跟随的呼吸；注意它的节奏，注意力就转向自己的呼吸。
works.method: A length of diving-hose rubber tube; its air sound and elasticity respond to hand pressure.
works.method_zh: 一段潜水用橡胶软管；它的气声与弹性回应手的压力。
exhibited: Lygia Clark: The Abandonment of Art, 1948–1988, MoMA 2014

works.title: Skinner Releasing Technique
works.description: Dancers are led through poetic images, such as being suspended by threads or moving like seaweed, often with a partner's hands-on support, until held tension releases and movement becomes spontaneous.
works.description_zh: 舞者被诗意的意象引导，例如被细线悬起、像海草一样摆动，常配合同伴的手把手支持，直到保持的紧张释放、动作变得自发。
works.idea_en: In Skinner Releasing, technique and creativity are the same act: alignment is found through imagination rather than correction, a stance close to soma design's joining of craft and felt experience.
works.idea_zh: 在斯金纳释放技巧中，技术与创造是同一件事：通过想象而非纠正找到排列，这与身体设计把手艺与亲身体验结合的立场相近。
works.method: Image-guided classes, partner 'hands-on' studies and improvisation, first shared with students at the University of Illinois in 1966–67.
works.method_zh: 以意象引导的课程、同伴手把手练习与即兴，1966–67 年首次在伊利诺伊大学与学生分享。

works.title: The Perceptible Breath (Der Erfahrbare Atem)
works.description: Sitting or lying, people let the breath come and go by itself and sense where it moves in the body, using pressure points, stretches, vowel sounds and a teacher's touch to explore breath 'spaces'.
works.description_zh: 人们坐着或躺着，让呼吸自己来去，并感受它在身体何处流动，借助按压点、伸展、元音发声和教师的触碰去探索呼吸的“空间”。
works.idea_en: Middendorf's rule 'I let my breath come, I let it go, and wait until it comes by itself' contrasts with breath-pacing technology: the designer's job may be to make breath perceptible rather than to control it.
works.idea_zh: 米登多夫的原则“我让呼吸来，让它走，并等待它自己再来”与呼吸节拍类技术形成对照：设计者的任务或许是让呼吸可被感知，而不是控制它。
works.method: Breath sensing with pressure points, movement, vowel resonance and hands-on work; Middendorf founded her breath-therapy institute in Berlin in 1965.
works.method_zh: 结合按压点、动作、元音共鸣与手法的呼吸感知练习；米登多夫 1965 年在柏林创立呼吸治疗学院。

works.title: Cut Piece
works.description: Ono kneels motionless on stage with a pair of scissors in front of her, and audience members come up one by one to cut away pieces of her clothing; first performed in Kyoto in 1964.
works.description_zh: 小野洋子一动不动地跪在舞台上，面前放着一把剪刀，观众一个接一个上前剪下她衣服的碎片；1964 年在京都首演。
works.idea_en: Stillness and exposure make the audience feel their own agency: the work is felt as much by those who cut as by the one who is cut.
works.idea_zh: 静止与暴露让观众感到自己的能动性：剪的人与被剪的人都同样在身体上感受这件作品。
works.method: Event score that Ono performed six times between 1964 and 2003; the 1965 New York performance was filmed by Albert and David Maysles.
works.method_zh: 事件乐谱式作品，小野洋子在 1964 至 2003 年间共表演六次；1965 年的纽约演出由 Albert 与 David Maysles 拍摄。

works.title: Noguchi Taisō
works.description: Practitioners hang, sway and ripple the body, imagining it as 'a leather bag filled with water' in which bones and organs float, and let weight and momentum do the moving; taught at Tokyo University of the Arts and in Noguchi's own classes from 1964.
works.description_zh: 习练者悬垂、摇荡、波动身体，把身体想象成“装满水的皮袋”，骨骼与内脏漂浮其中，让重量与惯性带动动作；在东京艺术大学以及野口自 1964 年起开设的课堂中传授。
works.idea_en: Ask the body rather than command it: Noguchi's motto 'karada ni kiku' (listen to the body) makes sensing weight the basis of moving well.
works.idea_zh: 问身体而不是命令身体：野口的格言“からだに貞く”（问身体）把感知重量作为良好运动的基础。
works.method: Relaxation and wave exercises (nyoro-nyoro, hanging forward bends), taught without fixed goals, alongside Noguchi's writings such as Genshi Seimeitai to shite no Ningen (1972).
works.method_zh: 放松与波动练习（如蠕动、前屈悬垂），不设固定目标，辅以野口的著作《作为原初生命体的人》（1972）。

works.title: Parangolé
works.description: Layered capes, banners and tents of fabric and plastic that only come alive when worn and danced in, first by samba dancers of the Mangueira community in Rio.
works.description_zh: 用织物和塑料叠成的斗篷、旗帜与帐篷，只有被穿上并随之起舞时才活起来，最初由里约 Mangueira 社区的桑巴舞者穿着。
works.idea_en: Colour and structure are completed by the dancing body; the wearer is at once artwork, performer and viewer.
works.idea_zh: 色彩与结构由舞动的身体完成；穿戴者同时是作品、表演者与观看者。
works.method: Wearable fabric constructions with painted colour fields and written phrases, activated through samba movement.
works.method_zh: 带有色块和文字的可穿戴织物结构，通过桑巴动作被激活。

works.title: The Visible and the Invisible
works.description: Merleau-Ponty's unfinished last work introduces 'the flesh', a single element of which perceiver and perceived, body and world, are both made, and the reversibility of touching and being touched.
works.description_zh: Merleau-Ponty 未完成的遗作提出“肉身”（la chair）：感知者与被感知者、身体与世界都由这同一元素构成；以及触摸与被触摸的可逆性。
works.idea_en: Body and world are of one flesh; to feel is always also to be felt, which dissolves the line between subject and object.
works.idea_zh: 身体与世界同属一块肉身；感受总同时是被感受，这消解了主体与客体的界线。
works.method: Manuscript and working notes edited by Claude Lefort after Merleau-Ponty's death in 1961.
works.method_zh: Merleau-Ponty 于 1961 年去世后，由 Claude Lefort 编辑出版的手稿与工作笔记。

paper.title: The Visible and the Invisible
paper.venue: Gallimard 1964; Northwestern University Press (trans. Alphonso Lingis, 1968)

works.title: Caminhando (Walking)
works.description: The participant cuts a paper Möbius strip lengthwise with scissors, again and again, choosing where to go until the strip becomes too thin to cut.
works.description_zh: 参与者用剪刀沿纵向一次次剪开纸质莫比乌斯带，自己选择走向，直到纸条细得无法再剪。
works.idea_en: The work is the act: meaning lives in the time and attention of the participant's hands, not in an object.
works.idea_zh: 作品就是行为本身：意义存在于参与者双手的时间与注意之中，而不在某个物件里。
works.method: A paper strip, glue and scissors; instructions invite anyone to perform it.
works.method_zh: 一条纸带、胶水和一把剪刀；说明邀请任何人来完成它。

works.title: Experiencing and the Creation of Meaning
works.description: Gendlin's philosophical work describes 'experiencing', the bodily felt flow that is always richer than words, and how new meaning forms when we attend to it and let it be carried forward.
